articles.title: Arrested at the hospital where he worked, he turned the prison into a pulpit
articles.summary: 🇪🇷Eritrea· 2010s
articles.summary_zh: 🇪🇷厄立特里亚·21世纪10年代
articles.title_zh: 他在自己工作的医院被捕，并将监狱变成了讲坛。
articles.content: Dr Berhane was a new believer in Jesus, working in a hospital in Eritrea, when the secret police came for him. His crime was his faith. They put him in prison for eleven months, in one of the harshest systems on earth, a place designed to make Christians disappear and go quiet. He did the opposite. "Every day I was clapping my hands," he said, "and prisoners would come forward and I shared the gospel." A man who had only recently met Jesus decided his cell was simply the next place to introduce Him. Three Bibles and a valley of death The authorities took his Bible. He smuggled another in. They took that one too, and he smuggled a third. He leaned hard on the Psalms, and when fellow prisoners were taken out and executed, the old line about walking through the valley of the shadow of death stopped being poetry and became the thing that held him upright. Eleven months of that did not break him. It made him a preacher. The guards meant to silence a new Christian and instead handed him a congregation with nowhere to go. Wherever they put you, Jesus goes with you, and He is not intimidated by the walls. Dr Berhane found that out in an Eritrean prison. You can trust it wherever you are.
articles.content_zh:
Berhane博士是耶稣的新信徒,在厄立特里亚的一家医院工作,当时秘密警察来找他。 他的罪行是他的信仰。 他们把他关进监狱11个月,在地球上最严酷的系统之一,一个旨在使基督徒消失和安静的地方. 他做的恰恰相反。

"每天我拍手,"他说:"囚犯会站出来,我分享福音". 一个刚认识耶稣的人决定 他的牢房只是下一个介绍他的地方 三个圣经和一个死亡之谷 当局拿走了他的圣经。 他又偷渡进来了 他们也拿走了那个 他走私了三分之一

他极力倚靠"诗经",当狱友被带出处死时,关于走过死亡阴影谷的老台词不再是诗歌,成为了扶他站直的东西. 11个月没有打倒他。 这让他成了传教士。 守卫们打算让新基督徒安静下来,反而给了他一个无处可去的会众.

无论他们把你放在哪里,耶稣都跟着你,他不受墙壁的恐吓. Berhane博士在厄立特里亚的一所监狱发现了这一点。 你可以相信它 无论你在哪里。

articles.title: A construction engineer in Madagascar became convinced the Bible was true
articles.summary: 🇲🇬Madagascar· 2013
articles.summary_zh: 🇲🇬马达加斯加·2013年
articles.title_zh: 一位在马达加斯加的建筑工程师确信圣经是真的
articles.content: Melias was building things for a living in Madagascar, a construction engineer with a steady trade and, by his own account, no particular expectation that God would interrupt him. In 2013, at twenty-one, God did. It was not dramatic thunder. It was quieter and harder to argue with. "The Holy Spirit convinced my heart that the Bible is true," Melias said. "I found new joy and excitement learning about Jesus through the Scriptures." The book he might have dismissed became the most alive thing in his life. From building houses to building the church He could have kept his new faith as a private comfort and gone on with engineering. Instead he gave it everything. In 2015 he trained for six months as a missionary, and since then he has planted churches and discipled new believers among the Tanala people in Ikongo and the Sakalava in Nosy Be, some of the least reached corners of the island. Now he is training three more Malagasy missionaries to do the same. Madagascar is not a footnote in what God is doing. He is raising up local people like Melias, engineers and tradesmen and ordinary workers, and sending them to their own unreached neighbours. When the Holy Spirit convinces your heart that this is all true, it does not stay a hobby. It becomes the thing you build your life around. He is ready to convince yours.
articles.content_zh:
梅利亚斯在马达加斯加为生计而建东西,他是一位稳定的建筑工程师,据他自己说,他并不特别期望上帝会打断他。 2013年,21时,上帝做到了. 这不是戏剧性的雷声。 更安静,更难争论 "圣灵使我的心相信圣经是真的,"梅利亚斯说.

"我发现新的快乐和兴奋 通过圣经学习耶稣。" 他可能放弃的书 成为他一生中最活的 从建房到建教堂 他本可以保持他作为私人慰藉的新信仰,继续从事工程工作. 相反,他给了它一切。

2015年,他作为传教士接受了半年的训练,此后他在伊孔戈的塔纳拉人和诺西贝的萨卡拉瓦人中种植了教堂和门徒新信徒,其中部分到达的岛角最少. 现在他正在训练另外三名马达加斯加传教士, 马达加斯加不是上帝所作所为的一个脚注。

他正在培养梅利亚斯,工程师和商人以及普通工人等当地人,并将他们送到他们自己无法接触到的邻居那里. 当圣灵说服你的心脏 这一切都是真的, 它不仍然是爱好。 它成为你围绕你生活的东西。 他准备说服你

articles.title: A New Testament sat in his welding workshop until a teenager finally read it
articles.summary: 🇳🇪Agadez· 2000s
articles.summary_zh: 🇳🇪阿加德兹·21世纪初
articles.title_zh: 一本新约圣经一直放在他的焊接车间里，直到一位少年终于读了它。
articles.content: Someone left a New Testament in Pierre's welding workshop in Niger, and for a while it just sat there. He was a teenager, and eventually he picked it up. What he read did not match what he had been told about Christians. It was full of tenderness, of nearness to the poorest, exactly the kind of world his young heart had been quietly hoping was real. Years later he moved to Agadez, out toward the desert, and there he found the thing the book had described. A church family drawn from Benin, Togo, Burkina Faso, France, and Niger, living out what he had only read about. No regret, not for a single day Pierre became a lay missionary, and he does not hedge when he talks about it. "I have never regretted converting to the Christian faith," he says, "not even for a single day." That is a bold thing to say in Niger, where jihadist groups make following Jesus dangerous and his own children have stayed Muslim, something he carries with love and without pressure. Still, no regret. Not one day. He read about a God who is tender toward the poor, and he found that God to be exactly as advertised. Whatever you have heard about Jesus secondhand, He holds up when you finally meet Him yourself. Pierre would tell you to open the book and see.
articles.content_zh:
有人在尼日尔的皮埃尔焊接车间留下了一份新约, 他少年时期,最终他捡到了. 他所读的内容与他被告知的基督徒的情况不符。 它充满了温柔,与最贫穷的人的亲近, 正是他年轻时所希望的世界是真实的。

多年后,他搬到阿加德兹, 向着沙漠, 在那里他发现了书上描述的东西。 一个来自贝宁、多哥、布基纳法索、法国和尼日尔的教会家庭,靠他只读过的东西生活。 没有遗憾,没有一天,皮埃尔成为了一名非专业的传教士,他谈论这件事时不设套.

"我从未后悔过皈依基督教信仰",他说:"即使是一天也没有". 在尼日尔,这是一件大胆的事,在那里,圣战团体追随耶稣,而他自己的孩子则留在穆斯林手中,他带着爱,没有压力。 不过,没有遗憾。 一日不见.

他曾诵读了真主--对于贫民是温和的--他发现真主确是彻知的。 无论你听到什么关于耶稣的二手消息 当你们终于亲眼见到他时 他都挺过来了 Pierre会告诉你打开书看看

articles.title: He was taught Christians do not pray. Then he watched his uncle pray before a meal
articles.title_zh: 他被教导说基督徒不祷告。然后，他看到叔叔在饭前祷告。
articles.content: Charles Yabaga Diarra grew up in a strict Muslim family in Lere, Mali, where Christians were mocked and misunderstood. His father, a headmaster and politician, ran the house like a school. As a boy, Charles fled about a hundred and fifty miles to stay with an uncle, and there he ran straight into something he had been told did not exist. His uncle, a Christian pastor, bowed his head and prayed before the meal. Charles was stunned. "Because we are Christians, we pray before meals," the uncle explained. Charles had been taught that Christians do not pray at all. That simple prayer, in his own language, lodged in him and would not leave. Just show me the way His father pulled him back and forced him into Quranic school, but the seed was planted. Years later, back with his uncle, tired and searching, Charles finally prayed his own prayer. "Lord, I'm really tired of seeking the truth. Just show me the way." A verse he had heard at a Vacation Bible School came back to him, and in November 1981 he gave his life to Jesus. The cost has been real. Charles is a preacher now, displaced by Mali's conflict and facing daily pressure. But he did not go alone. Of his fourteen siblings, most now follow Jesus, and around a hundred Christians gather at his extended family events. One uncle praying over dinner turned a whole family toward Jesus. Your quiet, ordinary faithfulness may be planting more than you know.
articles.content_zh:
查尔斯·亚巴加·迪亚拉(Charles Yabaga Diarra)在马里勒尔一个严格的穆斯林家庭长大,在那里基督徒受到嘲笑和误解. 他的父亲是一名校长和政治家,他像学校一样管理着房子. 童年时,查尔斯逃离了大约一百五十英里,与一个叔叔住在一起,在那里,他直接遇到了他被告知的东西并不存在.

他的叔叔,一位基督教牧师,低头祷告,在饭前祷告. 查尔斯被惊呆了 "因为我们是基督徒,我们吃饭前祈祷",叔叔解释道. 查尔斯被告知基督徒根本不祷告 用他自己的语言祈祷,他不会离开。

只要告诉我他父亲把他拉回来的方式 强迫他进入古兰经学校 但种子是种的 多年之后,与他的叔叔一起回来,疲惫和寻找,查尔斯终于自己祈祷. "主啊,我真的厌倦了寻找真相. "给我带路" 他在一所假期圣经学校听到的一首诗回到了他身边,1981年11月他把生命献给了耶稣.

代价是真实的。 查尔斯现在是一名传教士,因马里的冲突而流离失所,每天都面临压力。 但他没有一个人去。 他的十四个兄弟姐妹中,大多数现在都跟随耶稣,大约一百名基督徒聚集在他的大家庭活动中. 一个叔叔为晚餐祷告 整个家庭都向耶稣倾斜 你安静的,普通的忠诚 可能是种更多 比你知道。

articles.title: A widow heard the good news from a travelling salesman and could not unhear it
articles.summary: Laos· 2022
articles.title_zh: 一位寡妇从一位推销员那里听到了好消息，从此念念不忘。
articles.content: Pei was a fifty-two-year-old widow in Laos, raised the way her whole village was raised, worshipping ancestors and local spirits in a place where the government pushes atheism and neighbours warn that following the God of foreigners will offend the gods of home. Then a salesman came through and, somewhere between selling his goods, told her about Jesus. Salvation as a gift, not a payment. Pei believed it. She let go of the ancestor worship she had carried her whole life and quietly followed Jesus instead. The cost at her own front door She was discipled in secret for four months, growing strong enough to speak. The first people she told were her daughter and her son-in-law, who happens to be a policeman. They did not celebrate. He threatened her, saying that if she did not stop believing in Jesus, they would report her, jail her, or throw her out. In June they made good on it, tossing her clothes into the yard and telling her to go live with the people who gave her this Jesus. She went. She did not go back. A widow with nothing chose Jesus over a roof, because she had found something no one could evict from her heart. Following Jesus is not always safe, but it is always worth it. What Pei found is worth more than what it cost her, and it is offered to you too.
articles.content_zh:
裴 was在老挝是一位52岁的寡妇,养大了整个村庄的养殖方式,在政府推崇无神论的地方崇拜祖先和地方灵灵,邻居警告说,追随外国人神会冒犯家乡神灵. 然后一个推销员走过来,在出售他的商品之间,告诉她耶稣的事. 救世是礼物,不是报酬

裴 believed信之. 她放弃了她毕生怀念的祖先的崇拜,悄悄地跟随耶稣. 在她自己的前门付出的代价 她被秘密地关了四个月, 变得足够强大,可以说话。 她告诉的第一个人是她的女儿和女婿,她们碰巧是一名警察。 他们没有庆祝。

他威胁她,说如果她不停止相信耶稣,他们会告发她,监禁她,或者把她赶出去. 6月,他们在上面做得很好,把她的衣服扔到院子里,并告诉她去和给她这个耶稣的人一起生活. 她去了 她去了吗? 她没有回去。 一个什么都没有的寡妇选择了耶稣 而不是一个屋顶, 因为她已经发现了一些没人能从她的心脏里赶走的东西。

追随耶稣并不总是安全的,但总是值得的. 裴氏发现的比付出的代价更值钱,也是献给你的.

articles.title: After his daughter was killed, he prayed for a Bible no one could take from him
articles.summary: Uzbekistan and Tajikistan· 2020s
articles.summary_zh: 乌兹别克斯坦和塔吉克斯坦·2020年代
articles.title_zh: 女儿被杀后，他祈祷能拥有一本无人能夺走的圣经
articles.content: Rashid Kadirov was a Muslim in Central Asia when the worst thing happened. His six-year-old daughter Azizza was killed by a drunk neighbour driving a tractor. In his grief he went looking for something the ache could rest on, and he went to the Koran. There he read a line, in Surah 5:70, that pointed back to the Gospels as holy scripture. So he prayed a strange, specific prayer. He asked God for an Injil, a New Testament. His friends brought him one. It was a stolen Gideon Bible, taken from a vandalised car. It did not last. When the friends took it back, Rashid prayed again, this time for a Bible no one could take away from him. The book that stayed Then a couple arrived from Tajikistan, sent by a former classmate of his who had himself come to Christ. They carried a Bible and a copy of the JESUS Film. Rashid and his wife Aleka watched it, and as the good news was explained, each of them, without telling the other, quietly prayed to receive Jesus. Aleka barely understood it all. "She had very little understanding of the Gospel," she said later, "and yet peace flooded her heart." They were baptised in Tajikistan, and Rashid started telling others what he had found. A grieving father asked for a book, and God gave him a Person. The peace Rashid could not manufacture arrived the moment Jesus did. He is close to the brokenhearted, and He is near to you.
articles.content_zh:
拉希德·卡迪罗夫(Rashid Kadirov)是中亚穆斯林,当时最糟糕的事情发生了. 他的六岁女儿Azizza被驾拖拉机喝醉的邻居杀死. 在悲痛中,他去寻找可以安息的东西,他去了可兰经. 在那里,他读到了一行,在苏拉5:70中,指向福音书作为圣经. 所以他祈祷了一个奇怪的,具体的祈祷.

他向上帝祈求"印吉尔","新约". 他的朋友给他带来了一个。 是一辆被偷来的吉迪恩圣经 从被破坏的汽车上拍下来的 它没有持续。 当朋友们收回它时,拉希德再次祈祷,这次要一本圣经,没有人能夺走他. 留下来的书 之后一对夫妇从塔吉克斯坦赶来,他们是由自己来到基督的前同学派来的.

他们携带了圣经和JESUS电影的拷贝. 拉希德和他的妻子阿莱卡观看了,正如好消息被解释的那样,他们每个人都在不告诉对方的情况下悄悄地祈祷要接受耶稣. 阿莱卡根本不懂这些

"她对福音几乎没有什么了解,"后来她说,"然而和平却淹没了她的心. 他们在塔吉克斯坦接受洗礼,拉希德开始告诉其他人他发现了什么. 一个悲伤的父亲要求一本书,上帝给了他一个人. 和平拉希德无法在耶稣到达的时候制造。 他与心碎者密不可分,他与你们密不可分。

articles.title: 35 priests could not help her. In a church she saw Jesus crush what was choking her
articles.summary: 🇱🇰North Central Province· 2021
articles.summary_zh: 北中央省
articles.title_zh: 35位神父都无法帮助她。在教堂里，她看到耶稣粉碎了正在扼住她喉咙的东西。
articles.content: Chandra lived in a rural village in Sri Lanka's North Central Province, and she was slowly falling apart. Pain, weakness, a heart that raced for no reason doctors could name. She and her family were Hindu, so they did what they knew to do. They went to priest after priest. Thirty-five of them. Nothing changed. In July 2021 they walked into a church instead. As people prayed for her, Chandra saw something. Demons were trying to strangle her, and then Jesus Christ stepped in and stamped on them. She felt the pain and the sickness drain out of her body as they were defeated. In the vision Jesus spoke Scripture over her, from Psalm 34. "They looked to Him and were radiant," He said, and told her she would be radiant too if she trusted Him. The prayer a father prayed Her husband Dinesh, a day labourer, watched his wife come back to life and made God a promise. "God, if you will heal my wife, I will dedicate my daughter for your service." The whole family, who had barely heard the name of Jesus, gave their lives to Him. Their daughter Tenusha told her class what had happened, that her mother was free and that Jesus forgives sinners and makes them new. They did not keep it to themselves. A house church started in their home with four people. By now it is forty-six. Jesus is still stronger than whatever is choking the life out of you. He steps in, He stamps it down, and He calls you radiant.
articles.content_zh:
钱德拉住在斯里兰卡中北部省的一个乡村,她慢慢地分崩离析. 痛苦,软弱,一个无缘无故的心脏 医生无法命名 她和她的家人是印度教徒,所以他们做了他们知道的事。 他们跟随牧师去了牧师那里. 三十五门. 什么都没有改变。 2021年7月,他们走进了一座教堂。

当人们为她祈祷时,钱德拉看到了一些东西. 恶魔试图掐死她,然后耶稣基督介入并盖在他们身上. 她感到痛苦和疾病 排出她的身体 当他们被打败。 在视觉中,耶稣说圣经 超过她,从Psalm 34。 他说:他们崇拜他,而且赞颂他超绝万物。他说:她也超绝万物,如果她信任他。

一个父亲祈祷她的丈夫迪尼什(Dinesh),一个白天的劳工,看着他的妻子复活,并给上帝一个承诺. "上帝,如果你能治愈我的妻子, 我将奉献我的女儿为你服务。" 几乎听不到耶稣之名的全家都为他献出了生命.

他们的女儿特努沙告诉了班上所发生的事情,她的母亲是自由的,耶稣宽恕了罪人,使他们成为新人. 他们没有保守秘密。 一所房屋教堂在他们家中开始,共有4人. 时已四十六. 耶稣仍然比任何 扼杀你生命的东西更强大 他走进来,他把它印下来,他叫你光辉。

articles.title: He prayed for his mother's infected leg. Then his Muslim neighbours started coming
articles.summary: 🇸🇩El Hasahisa· 2022
articles.summary_zh: 🇸🇩哈萨希萨·2022年
articles.title_zh: 他为母亲感染的腿祈祷。然后，他的穆斯林邻居开始前来
articles.content: Pastor Abdalla Haron Sulieman gathered his small church in El Hasahisa, Sudan, to pray for his mother. Aisha Adam was sixty, and a leg infection had worn her down. They prayed, and she recovered. What looked like a private family mercy did not stay private for long. Word of the healing moved through the town, which is mostly Muslim. And people started showing up at the church. Not to argue. To ask if the God who healed Aisha might heal them too. When a healing becomes a door That is exactly the kind of thing that makes some people afraid. Local extremists pressed the police to arrest Sulieman, and they did, charging him under an old law with claiming to be a witch doctor, as if the love of Jesus were a kind of sorcery. Believers across Sudan shared his name and called for his release. "This is a serious violation against Christians in Sudan," said one, an evangelist named Francis Ismail. But notice what the fear could not undo. A mother was well. A Muslim town had seen the name of Jesus do something real, and neighbours who had never entered a church walked in looking for Him. God still heals, and He still uses one ordinary answered prayer to open a door no one can shut. He can open one where you are too.
articles.content_zh:
Abdalla Haron Sulieman牧师在苏丹El Hasahisa聚集了他的小教堂,为其母亲祈祷。 艾莎·亚当六十岁 腿部感染使她疲惫不堪 他们祈祷,她恢复了。 看起来像一个私人家庭的怜悯 并没有长期保持私人。 关于治愈的传言传遍了大部分是穆斯林的城镇。 人们开始出现在教堂。 不为辩才.

问治愈艾莎的神能否治愈他们 当治愈变成一扇门 这正是那种让人害怕的东西。 当地的极端分子逼迫警察逮捕苏利曼,他们确实如此,根据旧法指控他自称巫医,仿佛对耶稣的爱是一种巫术.

苏丹各地的信徒都认同他的名字,要求释放他。 "这是对苏丹基督徒的严重侵犯",一位名叫弗朗西斯·伊斯梅尔的福音者说. 但请注意恐惧无法消除 一个母亲很好 一个穆斯林城镇看到了耶稣的名字做一些真实的事情,从未进入教堂的邻居走进教堂寻找他.

上帝仍然痊愈,他仍然使用一个普通的应答祷告来打开一个没人能关闭的门. 他可以打开一个你的地方。

articles.title: Karma said he had to earn heaven. At 17 he heard he could be forgiven
articles.summary: Rakiraki· 1990s
articles.summary_zh: 拉基拉基·1990年代
articles.title_zh: 因果报应说他必须修功德才能上天堂。17岁时，他听说自己可以得到宽恕。
articles.content: Simon Gounder was born into a strict Hindu family in Fiji. His great-grandfather had been shipped from India as a contract labourer after the British took the islands in 1874, and the family settled in a small village in the north of Viti Levu. Simon grew up inside a system with clear rules. "As a Hindu, we believed in karma," he said. "If you do good karma, you get to heaven. If you do bad karma, you will be punished." It was a ledger he could never quite balance. He knew his own wrongs too well. The night the ledger closed At seventeen, a friend invited him to a Christian youth meeting in another town. There he heard something that did not fit anything he had been taught. That Jesus Christ could simply forgive sins. Not offset them, not average them out over lifetimes. Forgive them. Simon felt the weight of his own failures and, for the first time, an offer to be free of them. "I gave my life to Jesus that night," he said. He hid it from his parents at first. When they found out, they were not happy. But the son who came home changed did not stop there. In time he led his whole family to Christ, and he went on to plant a ministry that carries the same forgiveness to others. Karma keeps a running tab you can never clear. Jesus tears the tab up. Whatever you are carrying tonight, He is still in the business of forgiving it all at once.
articles.content_zh:
西蒙·古德出生于斐济一个严格的印度教家庭. 他的曾祖父在1874年英国人攻占群岛后,作为合同工从印度被运走,全家定居在维提莱武北部的一个小村庄. 西蒙在一个有明确规则的系统中长大. "作为一个印度教徒,我们相信因果报应,"他说. "若作善因缘即得上天.

若作恶报果报果报果. " 这是他无法平衡的分类账 他对自己的错误太了解了 结账的那一晚 17岁时,一位朋友邀请他到另一个城镇的一次基督教青年会议. 在那里,他听到一些不符合他所教过的东西。 耶稣基督可以宽恕罪过

不抵消它们, 也不平均出一生。 原谅他们 西蒙感受到了自己失败的轻重,并首次提出摆脱这些失败. "当晚我把生命交给耶稣,"他说. 起初他瞒着父母 当他们发现, 他们不高兴。 但回家的儿子变了 并没有停下来。

时他带领全家来到基督身边,他继续栽培一个对别人同样怀有宽恕的部. 卡玛一直有追踪器 你永远无法清除 耶稣撕开标签。 无论你今晚携带什么 他现在仍然要马上原谅这一切

articles.title: A soldier who should have died in battle walked into a demon's shrine
articles.summary: 🇲🇲Myanmar· 2010s
articles.title_zh: 一名本应死于战斗的士兵走进了恶魔的神殿
articles.content: Pastor Dano was a soldier before he was a pastor. He came out of the battlefield alive when he had no reason to, and he never shook the sense of why. "I believe God preserved my life from death on the battlefield for a purpose," he said. The purpose showed up in a Buddhist village that wanted nothing to do with him. The vice chief's son was tormented, demon-possessed, and no one could help. Dano fasted and prayed for three days. Then, near midnight, he went to the shrine where the boy was and did the only thing he knew to do. "I called upon the name of the Lord," he said, "and the demon left the young man." The night the shrines fell silent Villagers said every evil spirit left the village at once. Dano went from shrine to shrine, praying against the darkness that had ruled the place for generations. The vice chief's family, who had braced for his anger, found grace instead. They gave their lives to Jesus, and four more families followed. The people who once opposed him now follow his lead. There is a church in that village today where there used to be shrines. The name of Jesus is still stronger than every dark thing that has ever frightened you. One believer, praying at midnight, was enough to set a whole village free.
articles.content_zh:
牧师达诺在担任牧师之前是一名军人. 他毫无理由地活着走出战场,从未动摇过为什么的感官. "我相信上帝为了某种目的在战场上拯救了我的生命". 宗旨现于一佛村中欲与他无相. 副宰相的儿子被折磨,妖魔吞噬,无人能助.

达诺斋戒祈祷三天. 然后,近午夜,他去了男孩所在的神殿,做了他唯一知道该做的事. "我呼唤天主之名,"他说:"妖魔离开了少年. 夜神社失声村民说 每一个邪恶的灵魂 立刻离开村庄

达诺从神社到神社,祈祷反抗历代统治这个地方的黑暗. 副局长的家族,他为愤怒而坚韧不拔,却找到了恩典。 他们把生命献给了耶稣,还有四个家庭随行. 曾经反对他的人现在遵循他的路线。 今天村里有一座教堂 曾经有神社

耶稣的名字仍然比每件令你害怕的黑暗事物更强大. 一个信徒在午夜祈祷 足以让整个村庄自由

articles.title: Sustained giving to Lottie Moon offering helps provide gospel access for Deaf communities in Middle East
articles.summary: Every dollar you give to the Lottie Moon offering goes to support missionaries like Noah Lewis who live and serve among the lost. Will you consider giving today? Noah Lewis couldn’t help signing along with a worship song playing in the background as Deaf friends gathered in his home for dinner. The International Mission Board missionary was sitting in the living room with his roommate and two friends while others prepared food nearby. As a young, single adult, simply opening the doors to his hom
articles.summary_zh:
你给洛蒂·穆恩的每块钱 都用来支持像诺亚·刘易斯这样的传教士 在迷路者中生存和服役 你会考虑今天给钱吗? 当聋人朋友聚集在家中吃饭时,

国际传教委员会传教士与室友和两名朋友坐在客厅里,而其他人则在附近准备食物。 作为一个年轻,单身的成年人, 只要打开门给他的妈妈
articles.title_zh: 持续向慕拉第献金奉献，有助于为中东的失聪群体提供福音传播的机会
articles.content: An IMB missionary among the Deaf records a Bible story in sign language. IMB Photo Every dollar you give to the Lottie Moon offering goes to support missionaries like Noah Lewis who live and serve among the lost. Will you consider giving today? Noah Lewis couldn’t help signing along with a worship song playing in the background as Deaf friends gathered in his home for dinner. The International Mission Board appoints missionaries who are both Deaf and hearing to serve among the global Deaf. Many missionaries learn sign language for the first time, while others use their American Sign Language to more quickly learn global sign languages. IMB Photo The International Mission Board missionary was sitting in the living room with his roommate and two friends while others prepared food nearby. As a young, single adult, simply opening the doors to his home in the Middle East has created some of his most fruitful opportunities for gospel conversations. That evening, Lewis was stirred to worship the Lord. “I just love worshiping in sign language because it’s a full-body experience,” Lewis said. Lewis, who is hearing, began signing the song in American Sign Language. Across the room, one of his Muslim friends watched intently. When the song ended, his friend told him it was beautiful and asked to see another. Lewis explained that Christians use songs to worship God. His friend compared what he had seen to hearing the Islamic call to prayer. The exchange opened an opportunity for Lewis to explain Christian worship and why Christians worship Jesus. When his friend asked to see more, Lewis continued signing songs from the playlist. “He was just really captivated by it,” Lewis said. “It really felt like in that moment the Spirit was working in his heart.” The conversation did not end with a profession of faith. Instead, it became another step in a friendship where Lewis has watched spiritual curiosity grow over time. During Ramadan, the same friend asked about fasting. On another night, he asked how Christians pray. Each question has allowed Lewis to explain what Christians believe and why he follows Jesus. Those conversations reflect much of Lewis’ ministry. He has served in the Middle East for nearly a year and a half, spending much of his time learning sign language and building relationships in the local Deaf community. Learning sign language, like learning any language, requires time, practice and immersion in the community that uses it. For Lewis, that process has looked different from the experience of missionaries who can spend several hours each day in a formal language school. There are no comparable sign language centers where he serves, so much of his language learning happens through relationships with Deaf friends. Although Lewis has not had a dedicated language tutor since arriving on the field, personal relationships help him develop a strong conversational understanding of the sign language used where he serves. The process has also drawn him more deeply into the Deaf community he came to reach. “I want to genuinely learn about their language,” he said. “I want to be friends with them. I want to know who they are.” As Lewis’ ability to communicate grows, relationships deepen and opportunities to share the gospel follow. Even when he doesn’t know the exact sign he needs, friends help him find ways to communicate biblical truths. Lewis has learned to faithfully use the language he has while continuing to grow in his ability to communicate the gospel clearly. An IMB worker among the Deaf records a Bible story. 国际代表团委员会任命聋人和听力传教士在全球聋人中任职。 许多传教士首次学习手语,而其他传教士则使用他们的美国手语更快地学习全球手语.

IMB照片 国际传教委员会传教士与他的室友和两个朋友坐在客厅里,而其他人则在附近准备食物. 作为一个年轻、单身的成年人,只要打开通往他在中东的家的大门,就为他的福音对话创造了一些最富有成果的机会。 当晚,刘易斯被激起崇拜主.

「我只是喜欢手语崇拜, 正在听话的刘易斯开始用美国手语签署歌曲. 在房间里,他的一个穆斯林朋友故意观看。 歌曲结束的时候,他的朋友告诉他这很美丽,并请求见另一首. 刘易斯解释说,基督徒使用歌曲来崇拜上帝.

他的朋友比较了他所看到的听到的伊斯兰祈祷的呼声. 这次交流为刘易斯解释基督教崇拜和基督徒为何崇拜耶稣提供了机会. 当他的朋友要求看到更多时,刘易斯继续从播放列表上签名歌曲. 刘易斯说:“他只是被它迷住了。”

“在那个时刻,精神确实在他心中发挥作用。” 对话没有以信仰职业结束。 相反,它成为友谊的又一个步骤,刘易斯目睹了精神好奇心随时间推移而增长. 斋月期间,同友问斋事. 在另一个晚上,他问基督徒如何祈祷.

每个问题都让刘易斯解释基督徒相信什么,为什么他跟随耶稣. 这些谈话反映了刘易斯部的许多情况。 他在中东服务了近一年半,花了很多时间学习手语,在当地聋人社区建立关系.

学习手语,就像学习任何语言一样,需要时间,练习和沉浸在使用手语的社区中. 对刘易斯来说,这一进程与传教士的经历不同,传教士可以每天在一所正式语言学校中度过几个小时。

他所服务的手语中心并不存在类似的手语中心,所以他的许多语言学习都是通过与聋人朋友的关系发生的. 虽然刘易斯自到达球场后便没有专门的语言辅导员,但个人关系帮助他发展出对他所服务的手语的强烈的对话理解.

这一过程还使他更深入地融入了他所接触的聋人社区。 他说:“我想真正了解他们的语言。” “我想与他们成为朋友。 我想知道他们是谁。” 随着刘易斯沟通能力的增长,关系加深,分享福音的机会随之而来。

即使他不知道自己需要什么具体标志, 刘易斯学会了忠实使用他拥有的语言,同时继续增强他明确传达福音的能力. 一个IMB工人在聋人中记录了一个圣经故事. 慷慨地给洛蒂月亮圣诞节 提供全球聋人中的支持任务

articles.content: How old were you when you first learned that Jesus loves you? Perhaps you’ve always known it and can’t remember a day when you didn’t know the song “Jesus Loves Me” or couldn’t recite John 3:16 by heart. Maybe you were a teenager and learned about Jesus’ love through a friend or church summer camp. Or were in college and went to a concert where the gospel was clearly articulated. Maybe you were in the trenches of the workforce, and a coworker boldly shared with you about the God who radically changed their life. Regardless of how old you were, each of us who has chosen to follow Jesus has an origin story — a moment in our lives when the knowledge that “Jesus loves me, this I know, for the Bible tells me so” moved from head knowledge to heart belief. And from then on, our lives were transformed forever. This is the truth of the gospel and the power of understanding that Jesus loves you. People around the world are discovering the personal truth of John 3:16 for themselves in a language and format they clearly understand. Explore why understanding that “God so loved the world” transforms entire communities → A Changing Reality Throughout Christian history, the gospel has spread from one community to the next. Stories were told and retold, Scripture was translated, churches were planted, and discipleship deepened as people learned more about Jesus. Bible translation is foundational to all ministries of the church. It fuels evangelism, church planting, discipleship and more. It equips people to move from a blurry picture of who God is to a clear understanding and personal encounter with Jesus as Lord. Through Scripture, people are able to read, hear or see the love of God on display. Just two decades ago, most of the world’s language communities still needed Bible translation work to begin , let alone be completed. But praise God, in the last few years, we’ve seen tremendous progress made, with Bible translation underway in more languages than ever before . While the change in numbers is exciting, what’s more important is what they signify: Every number represents a person who has a story that matters to God. For these communities, the stories of future generations are being completely rewritten as children will now grow up never remembering a day when they didn’t have access to God’s Word in a language and format they clearly understand. That statement bears repeating: There will now be people who never remember a day when they didn’t have access to God’s Word in a language and format they clearly understand. From the first word of Genesis to the last word of Revelation, the Bible tells one incredible story: God’s love for the world and His invitation for people from every nation and language to know Him. Get a glimpse of how God continues writing this story today as more and more people are experiencing the power of His Word. Watch the video → A New Generation Growing Up With God’s Word Let’s take a look at some of the recent communities that are experiencing not only life transformation but generational transformation as they encounter Jesus personally through Scripture. Jakalteko | Guatemala The Jakalteko Bible was dedicated in July 2026 in Guatemala! During the celebration, John 1:1-18 was read aloud — a passage that focuses on Christ, the eternal Word and our Redeemer. Early on, many women in the community memorized Job 19 . Like Job, they had faced various hardships in their lives and identified with his suffering. The book reminded them that God remains in control and that, in the midst of difficult circumstances, their Redeemer will deliver them and comfort them in their pain. Today, they have the full counsel of God’s Word and can now see this Redeemer fulfilled in Jesus in the New Testament. They are overjoyed that the Bible has arrived in the language they were born into! When the Bible was distributed, one mother who is raising her family alone said with joy and tears: “Thank God we have the Bible in our language. Now

你第一次得知耶稣爱你时多大了? 或许你一直都知道, 也不记得有一天你不知道“耶稣爱我”的歌曲, 或许你还是个少年, 或者在大学时,去参加一个音乐会,其中福音被明确表达出来.

也许你在劳动力的战壕里, 一个合作者大胆地与你分享上帝 谁彻底改变了他们的生活。 无论你多大,选择跟随耶稣的我们每个人都有一个起源故事——在我们生活中的这一刻,“耶稣爱我,我知道,因为圣经如此告诉我”的知识从头知识转移到心信。

从那时起,我们的生活就永远改变了 这是耶稣爱你的福音和理解的力量的真理. 世界各地的人们正在用他们明白的语言和格式,为自己发现约翰3:16的个人真理.

探讨为什么“上帝如此热爱世界”会改变整个社区? 基督教历史上不断变化的现实,福音从一个社区传播到另一个社区。 故事被讲述和重播,圣经被翻译,教堂被种植,随着人们更多地了解耶稣,门徒身份加深. 圣经翻译是教会所有各部的基础.

它为福音派,教会的种植,门徒活动等等提供了燃料. 它使人们能够从模糊的上帝是谁的画面走向一个明确的理解和与耶稣作为主的个人交锋. 通过圣经,人们能够阅读,听到或看到上帝的爱在展示.

就在20年前,世界上大多数语言社区仍然需要开始圣经翻译工作,更不用说完成了。 但赞美上帝, 在过去几年里, 我们看到了巨大的进步,

当越来越多的人正在经历着他的话语的力量时, 让我们看看最近的一些社区,

这本书提醒他们,上帝仍然在控制之中,在困难的情况下,他们的救赎者会将他们送去,并在他们的痛苦中安慰他们. 今天,他们有充分的神话的劝告,现在可以看到这个救世主在新约中的耶稣实现了. 他们太高兴了 圣经已经用他们生下来的语言传下来了!

articles.summary_zh:
我丈夫和我20多岁时 从田纳西州的家搬到南亚 上帝召我们通过国际使命委员会为海外服务,我们激动地与那些还没有机会听的人分享福音。 随着我们开始将生活植根于世界另一边的一个城市,我们很快意识到我们面前的任务是巨大的.

我们被数百万人包围着,其中绝大多数是精神上的损失,并走上了一条通往人类的轨道。
articles.title_zh: 第一人称：我们为什么请您祷告
articles.content: April Bunn, IMB director of global prayer strategies, shows messengers at an SBC annual meeting the latest Loving the Lost prayer resource. IMB Photo April Bunn directs global prayer strategies for the IMB. IMB Photo My husband and I moved from our home in Tennessee to South Asia when we were in our 20s. God called us to serve overseas through the International Mission Board, and we were excited to share the gospel with those who had not yet had an opportunity to hear it. As we began to plant our lives in a city on the other side of the world, we quickly realized the task before us was massive. We were surrounded by millions of people, the vast majority of whom were spiritually lost and on a trajectory to an eternity separated from Christ. We were grappling with a new language, a different culture, unfamiliar foods, homesickness and the list went on. We were overwhelmed. The reality of the lostness around us felt too much to carry. As we turned to God for help, He reminded us that we were not meant to carry this task alone. We had been sent as laborers to the nations, but the Great Commission was given to the whole Church. The Church was our partner in this work. As we began intentionally inviting brothers and sisters in the U.S. to walk with us regularly in prayer, we saw God move in unmistakable ways. They carried the burden of lostness with us, and they also rejoiced with us as we saw God work. We had been sent as laborers to the nations, but the Great Commission was given to the whole Church. The Church was our partner in this work. Today, after two decades in South Asia, I have the privilege of encouraging and equipping believers to pray for people and places around the world through my work with the IMB. In doing so, I’m continually reminded that God’s mission is His work, and we are utterly dependent on Him to accomplish it. Missionaries can faithfully go, learn languages, share the gospel and disciple believers, but they cannot change hearts. God can. That is why we ask you to pray. Prayer is strategic to the Great Commission, and e very believer can take part in it. As the Church, we are living between the giving of the Great Commission and its culmination in the great multitude we see in Revelation 7:9, where people from every nation, tribe, people and language will stand before the throne worshiping God together. Until that day, we go to take the good news to a world in need. And we pray, asking God to do what only He can do. Through prayer, every believer, regardless of age or location, can intercede for places we may never be able to go ourselves. No country or people group is closed to the work of the Spirit through the prayers of God’s people. We may not see every answer to those prayers in our lifetime; some will only become visible when we stand before the throne and see the faces of those God drew to Himself. articles.title_zh: 创作者的心
articles.content: Holly Neal loves people, and she loves making things. And when something catches her interest, she dives in. “I’m a maker,” she said simply. But making has become more than just a hobby for Holly. Through some of her family’s hardest seasons, it has offered them comfort and connection. And eventually it became an unexpected way to give back to what God is doing around the world. When Holly’s adult daughter Julia was being treated for leukemia, a friend invited them to learn how to quilt. The creative process gave Holly something to focus on as their family walked through a difficult season. It became a way to work through hard things alongside her daughter. Years later, when Holly’s grandson Graham was born during the COVID-19 pandemic, she reached for another familiar project: cross-stitching. Graham spent his first four months in the hospital. And because of visitation restrictions at the time, Holly spent long hours waiting in the cafeteria. So she brought her cross-stitch. Being busy helped calm Holly’s mind. Cross-stitching was a small, practical way to make the waiting a little easier. Holly and her husband, Steve, have continued to navigate some unique family circumstances as they’ve cared for their daughter and grandson. So when Chris and Lindsay Beals, Holly and Steven’s daughter and son-in-law, invited the couple to a Wycliffe event, they were especially excited. After a season of isolation, they looked forward to reconnecting with other Christians and hearing stories about what God was doing through Bible translation. One part of the work specifically stayed with Holly: sign language Bible translation. Curious about what sign language Bible translation actually looks like? See for yourself when you visit our interactive Bible Translation Experience! You’ll go on a global journey where you’ll meet some of the hardworking Deaf translators bringing the Bible to their people in a language and format that capture their hearts. Start your journey! → As a grandmother of a child with unique needs, Holly has a special place in her heart for communities and families who navigate specific challenges and contexts. Learning about the work of making God’s Word accessible to Deaf communities worldwide gave Holly a personal connection to a ministry she’d never fully understood before. Holly and Steve had already talked and prayed about a financial gift they wanted to make to Wycliffe. But as she continued thinking about the ministry and Bible translation projects for sign languages, another question kept coming to mind: “Steve and I had already come up with a number that we felt like to donate, but the Lord kept speaking to me. And I kept thinking, ‘But what can I do? … That’s our money, but how can I make an impact?’” So Holly began thinking about how much she had invested — in supplies, patterns, fabric and tools — over the years in her love of crafting. She wondered if some of those things could become part of her gift to Bible translation. And what if Holly passed some of those supplies along to other makers and used the proceeds to support Bible translation for sign languages? See how one couple in Alabama also creatively used their gifts and skills to give back to Bible translation → Giving in Community Holly decided to hold what the stitching community calls a “destash” — an opportunity for her to sell supplies she already owned to other stitchers who could put them to good use. She shared the idea through her YouTube channel and social media, where she had already connected with a community of people who love cross-stitch. So when Holly told her stitching community about Wycliffe and her desire to support sign language Bible translation, she invited them into partnering with something that mattered to her. And people responded with generosity! Some people paid more for supplies and projects than the asking price, wanting to give a little extra toward the cause. articles.title_zh: 值得铭记的波兰感恩节
articles.content: In 2018, God provided food for more than 70 people, double the expected number, at a Thanksgiving celebration Cal and Erin Hiebsch helped to host in order to share the gospel by telling the story of God’s provision for the Pilgrims on the first Thanksgiving. IMB Photo For Cal and Erin Hiebsch and their family, Thanksgiving is more than a cherished American holiday. Living and serving in Poland as International Mission Board missionaries, it has become one of their most effective opportunities to build relationships, share their culture and ultimately point people to Christ. While Poland celebrates Christmas and Easter on a grand scale, Thanksgiving is uniquely American. Many Poles are familiar with the holiday and curious about its traditions. Over the years, the Hiebsch family has learned to use that curiosity as a bridge for ministry. “Thanksgiving is probably one of our bigger entrées into American culture,” Cal explained. Each year, they invite friends, neighbors and participants from their English conversation clubs to experience a traditional Thanksgiving meal. For many guests, this is their first encounter with foods such as stuffing, green bean casserole, sweet potato casserole and roasted turkey. Even finding a whole turkey in Poland can be a challenge, since stores more commonly sell turkey breasts and other cuts rather than the whole bird. One Thanksgiving, in particular, is especially memorable for the family. With the help of volunteers, Erin and the culinary crew carefully planned a special celebration. “We had people in four or five different kitchens across the city cooking,” she said. A generous spread of traditional American dishes filled the tables, and invitations had been extended throughout their community. Based on past events, they expected 20 to 30 people to attend. Erin said they planned for “double batches” of each dish with the intention of everybody trying a little of everything that was served. Servers fill up plates as IMB missionaries Cal and Erin Hiebsch and their friends host a Thanksgiving meal in Poland. They planned for 20 or 30 people to show up, but nearly 70 people filled the house. Thankfully, everyone had a full meal and heard the gospel message. IMB Photo As the evening began, guests kept arriving. More came through the doors. Then more. Soon the room was packed. Instead of the anticipated crowd of a few dozen, nearly 70 people showed up. The gathering became standing-room only. “I quietly asked a couple of the volunteer ladies to be praying that there would be enough for everyone,” Erin recalled. Cal was serving as emcee for the event, welcoming guests and sharing the Thanksgiving story. Meanwhile, others were distributing plate after plate of food. Every time someone entered the room, the challenge seemed to grow. How could the food possibly stretch far enough? Yet somehow, it did. People continued to receive full plates. Everyone ate. Conversations flourished around the tables. “The pumpkin pie was especially popular,” Erin said. Guests learned about the history of Thanksgiving and heard how God had provided for the Pilgrims during difficult circumstances. Most importantly, they heard the gospel woven naturally into the evening’s program. When the event finally concluded, the team compared notes and realized an astonishing experience occurred. “We doubled our crowd and had enough food for everyone to have a good Thanksgiving feast,” Cal recalled. To this day, Cal and Erin still talk about that evening. The experience remains difficult to explain, outside of God’s provision. They prepared for one number of guests and served more than twice as many. Whether miraculous or simply an extraordinary provision, the outcome was undeniable. More people than expected were welcomed, fed and exposed to the hope of Christ. An American holiday became a platform for meaningful conversations and gospel witness in a place far from home. 在波兰生活和担任国际传教委员会传教士,已经成为他们建立关系、分享其文化并最终指向基督的最有效机会之一。 虽然波兰在大尺度上庆祝圣诞节和复活节,但感恩节是独特的美国人. 许多波兰人对节日很熟悉,对其传统很好奇.

多年来,Hiebsch家族学会了利用这种好奇心作为部委的桥梁。 Cal解释道, “感恩大概是我们美国文化中一个更大的参与者。 每年,他们都会邀请他们英语对话俱乐部的朋友,邻居和参与者体验传统的感恩节餐.

对于许多嘉宾来说,这是他们第一次遇到填料,绿豆砂锅,甜薯砂锅和烤火鸡等食物. 即使是在波兰找到整只火鸡也可能是一个挑战,因为商店更常出售火鸡乳房和其他切口,而不是整只鸟. 特别是感恩节对家庭来说特别值得纪念。

在志愿者的帮助下,艾琳和烹饪船员精心策划了一场特别的庆祝活动. 她说:「我们有四五个不同的厨房, 美国传统菜肴的慷慨推广为餐桌填满了餐桌,在他们的社区内发出了邀请。 根据过去的事件,他们预计有20至30人参加。

Erin说,他们计划将每道菜“分两批”使用,目的是让每个人都尝试一下所服务的东西。 服务器在IMB传教士卡尔和艾琳·希布希及其朋友在波兰举办感恩节晚宴时填满了盘子. 他们计划有20到30人出现,但将近70人填满了房子.

谢天谢地,每个人都吃过一顿饭,听到了福音的信息. IMB 图片 随着夜晚的开始, 客人不断到达。 更多人从门进来了 再来 很快房间就收拾好了. 而不是预期的几十人的人群,近70人出现了. 聚会变成了只有站着的房间。

Erin回忆道, “我悄悄地要求几位女志愿者祈祷, 卡尔当时担任了该活动的代表,欢迎嘉宾并分享感恩节的故事. 与此同时,其他人在分发盘子后再分发食物。 每次有人进入房间,挑战似乎越来越大。 食物怎么够长?

然而,不知何故,它确实如此。 人们继续收到满板。 每个人都吃了。 围绕桌子的议论蓬勃发展. 艾琳说,“南瓜派特别受欢迎。” 嘉宾们了解感恩节的历史,并听说上帝在艰难的情况下为朝圣者提供了什么. 最重要的是,他们听到了晚间节目中自然编织的福音。

当活动最终结束时,团队比较了笔记,意识到发生了惊人的经历. Cal回忆道, “我们的人口增加了一倍, 直到今天,卡尔和艾琳仍在谈论那个晚上. 除了上帝的规定之外,这些经历仍然难以解释。

他们为1位客人做准备,服务人数为2倍以上. 无论是神奇的还是简单的特别的规定,结果都是不可否认的。 更多的人受到基督的欢迎、食物和希望。 一个美国节日成为了在远离家的地方进行有意义的交谈和福音见证的平台.

articles.title_zh: 为巴基斯坦基督徒的释放而进行的呼吁工作变得更加紧迫
articles.content: Shahzad Masih has been praying for justice since 2017. He was just 16 years old when he was arrested on false charges, and has been waiting to be hanged since 2022. Nine years later, the American Center for Law and Justice (ACLJ), through its Pakistani counterpart, the Organization for Legal Aid (OLA), is continuing to advocate for his release, Christian Daily International reported. In 2017, Masih was working as a janitor at a hospital when a Muslim coworker asked him about his belief in Jesus. As he explained his faith, he mentioned a comment made by a family friend that was spoken against the Prophet Muhammad, which offended the coworker and ended the conversation. The coworker belonged to Tehreek-e-Tahfuz-e-Islam, a conservative Islamic group in Pakistan. Members of the group heard about their conversation and confronted the Masih. Though he tried to clarify the situation, he was handed over to the police on July 13, 2017, and was questioned without legal representation before being imprisoned. In November 2022, according to Section 295C of the Pakistan Penal Code, he was sentenced to death for the “use of derogatory remarks, etc. in respect of the Holy Prophet.” Since then, he has been waiting to be hanged for his unjust sentence. The United Nations has called for his immediate release, stating that these decisions deny his right to “freedom of expression.” OLA has supported him and filed an appeal for his freedom four times, but the Lahore High Court has yet to hear his case. “Shahzad Masih was just 16 years old when he was arrested, and nine years later, he remains on death row for allegedly reporting someone else’s words,” said CeCe Heil, senior counsel and international legal director for the ACLJ. “We urge Pakistani authorities to uphold fundamental human rights, overturn this unjust conviction, and bring Shahzad Masih home to his family.” One of Many As more stories of Christians being imprisoned for false blasphemy accusations arise this year — including Amir Peter , who was tried before by a Lahore court in 2024 and died in custody in July — ACLJ is committed more than ever to fighting for the life of this young Christian. “This is the ultimate abominable human rights violation, and we’ll take this case all the way to Pakistan’s Supreme Court,” the advocacy group wrote . Open Doors ranks Pakistan as the eighth most dangerous place to be a Christian in the world. They are constantly subjected to persecution through discrimination, death threats, mob violence, imprisonment, and death, through its Pakistani counterpart, the Organization for Legal Aid (OLA), continues. Story by Bella Agnello To read more news stories, visit the ICC Newsroom . For interviews, please email us . To support ICC’s work around the world, please give to our Where Most Needed Fund . articles.title_zh: 越南在教会土地纠纷中拆除历史悠久的天主教建筑
articles.content: Vietnamese authorities demolished a historic building belonging to the Redemptorist Catholic community in the central city of Huế on Tuesday, escalating a decades-long dispute over church property and raising renewed concerns about religious freedom in the communist-governed country. The demolition of the L’Accueil building followed the deployment of police by local authorities to block roads surrounding the Redemptorist monastery and Our Lady of Perpetual Help Church. Electricity to the area was also cut, preventing some parishioners from reaching the church to attend Mass or express solidarity with the religious community. According to the Redemptorists, heavy machinery began demolishing the structure while priests, religious brothers, and parishioners gathered nearby in prayer. The demolition continued through Nov. 18, leaving the property leveled and fenced off. The Redemptorist Provincial Chapter of Vietnam condemned the operation, arguing that authorities proceeded despite unresolved legal questions and repeated requests to review the property’s ownership. “Justice cannot be established through force, and the truth cannot be erased along with the structures that have been demolished,” the congregation said in a Nov. 17 statement as the demolition was proceeding. Communist Land Takeover The dispute centers on land that the Redemptorists purchased in 1930. According to historical documentation cited by the religious order, Huế municipal authorities formally recognized the congregation’s ownership in 1971. The L’Accueil complex was subsequently developed on the property between 1938 and 1943. It served as a center for educational, cultural, and community activities, housing a library, auditorium, and reading room. A sawmill was also established on the grounds in the 1950s, providing local employment. Following the communist takeover of South Vietnam in 1975, the government’s relationship with religious institutions changed significantly. Church properties throughout the country came under increasing state control, with religious communities frequently losing access to land and buildings they had previously owned. The Redemptorists maintain that they never voluntarily surrendered their rights to the L’Accueil property. They acknowledge that the congregation transferred assets associated with a sawmill to the state in 1978, but argue that the transfer did not include the land itself. Authorities subsequently assigned the property to government-controlled institutions. The remaining parcel, measuring about 2,550 square meters, is currently managed by a local sports vocational school. Recent Efforts The congregation has sought the property’s return since 1994. Its most recent formal complaint, submitted to the Huế People’s Committee on Oct. 24, requested recognition of its land-use rights and clarification of the property’s legal status. Authorities reportedly rejected the complaint in a Nov. 8 response, stating that it had no basis for consideration. A notice posted at the property in October announced plans to develop a public park and parking lot on the site. Local authorities have defended the project as serving public interests, including improving traffic conditions and providing additional green space in a densely populated area. Vietnamese law establishes that land is collectively owned by the people and administered by the state. Government authorities have also invoked a 2003 National Assembly resolution that generally prevents reconsideration of certain land and housing arrangements established before July 1, 1991. The Redemptorists, however, dispute the government’s interpretation of the property’s history and say authorities have not adequately explained the legal grounds for demolishing the building. They have asked officials to publicly disclose the documentation supporting their decision and review the historical records presented by the congregation. The dispute illustrates the difficulties religious communitie

在L ' Accueil大楼被拆除之前,地方当局部署了警察,封锁救赎会修道院和永生圣母助教周围的道路。 该地区的电力也被切断,使一些教区人士无法前往教堂参加弥撒或表示对宗教界的声援.

据救赎派说,重型机械开始拆除该建筑,而祭司,宗教兄弟,以及教区教徒聚集在附近祈祷. 拆除工作一直持续到11月18日,财产被夷为平地和围起来。

越南救赎主义省分会谴责了这次行动,认为当局不顾尚未解决的法律问题和一再要求审查该财产的所有权而继续行动. “正义不能通过武力建立,真理不能与被拆除的建筑物一起抹去。”

它作为教育、文化和社区活动中心、图书馆、礼堂和阅览室。 1950年代还在当地建立了锯木厂,提供当地就业。 1975年共产党接管南越后,政府与宗教机构的关系发生了重大变化.

全国各地的教会财产受到越来越多的国家控制,宗教社区往往失去获得其以前拥有的土地和建筑物的机会。 救赎者坚持认为,他们从未自愿放弃对L ' Accueil财产的权利。

他们承认教会在1978年将与锯木厂有关的资产转移到了国家,但辩称转让不包括土地本身. 当局随后将财产分配给政府控制的机构。 其余部分占地约2,550平方米,目前由当地体育职业学校管理.

最近的努力 自1994年以来,教会一直要求归还财产。 它最近于10月24日向胡瓦克人民委员会提出正式申诉,要求承认其土地使用权并澄清财产的法律地位。 据报告,当局在11月8日的答复中驳回了申诉,称申诉没有审议依据。

10月在该地产张贴了一份通知,宣布计划在该地开发一个公共公园和停车场. 地方当局捍卫该项目是为了公共利益,包括在人口稠密地区改善交通条件和提供更多的绿色空间。 越南法律规定,土地属于人民集体所有,由国家管理。

政府当局还援引了2003年国民议会的一项决议,该决议一般禁止重新审议1991年7月1日之前确定的某些土地和住房安排。 但救赎者质疑政府对该地产历史的解释,

他们要求官员公开公布支持其决定的文件,并审查教会提出的历史记录。 争议说明了宗教共产主义的困难

articles.title_zh: 特朗普、习近平和普京在宗教自由状况恶化之际会晤
articles.content: U.S. President Donald Trump, Chinese President Xi Jinping, and Russian President Vladimir Putin met Thursday in Shenzhen, China, for an unprecedented trilateral summit, projecting an image of cooperation among three of the world’s most powerful nations but offering few concrete agreements on the conflicts and international issues facing them. The roughly 80-minute meeting produced a joint statement addressing United Nations reform, energy production, international legal authority, and nuclear risks. However, the statement offered no clear breakthroughs on the wars in Ukraine or Iran and made no public reference to religious freedom or the persecution of religious communities in China and Russia. The gathering underscored the importance of direct engagement among world leaders as they seek to manage competing interests, global conflicts, and questions about the future of international order. The summit also offered an opportunity to address concerns affecting millions of people who face persecution for their faith, particularly in countries governed by authoritarian regimes. A Summit Focused on Global Stability The three leaders presented themselves as sharing responsibility for maintaining international peace and security. Their joint statement called for United Nations reform, increased production and supply of petroleum products, and further dialogue on reducing nuclear risks. The leaders also emphasized state sovereignty and the immunity of government officials, declaring that the International Criminal Court and similar bodies should not abuse their authority. The language reflects a shared interest among the three governments in limiting the reach of international institutions, although their respective political, economic, and security priorities remain distinct. Concerningly, this language is similar to that used by China in pushing back on American calls to respect human rights and ensure citizens can freely practice religion. Claiming that these are internal affairs, China rejects what it considers to be overly zealous policing by the U.S. and continues on its path of persecution. Putin described the summit as a new chapter in diplomatic history and praised the opportunity for direct engagement with Trump and Xi. The Russian president also invoked the 1945 Yalta Conference, which helped shape the postwar European order, arguing that international conflicts eventually require countries to recognize realities on the ground. While the leaders expressed interest in dialogue and international stability, their meeting did not produce publicly announced agreements to resolve major conflicts or address underlying tensions between their governments. Religious Freedom Remains a Global Concern For religious freedom advocates, high-level diplomatic meetings represent an important opportunity to raise the plight of prisoners of conscience and religious communities facing government persecution. China, in particular, continues to impose severe restrictions on religious practice. Christians in unregistered churches face surveillance, detention, church closures, and pressure to submit to government oversight. The Chinese Communist Party’s campaign to bring religious institutions under its control has affected Protestant house churches, Catholic communities, Tibetan Buddhists, Uyghur Muslims, and other religious minorities. In recent months, international advocates have urged the Trump administration to raise the cases of imprisoned religious leaders with Xi. Earlier this year, Trump raised the case of Pastor Ezra Jin Mingri, founder of Beijing’s Zion Church, during a meeting with Xi. Chinese authorities subsequently released Jin, who later relocated to the United States. However, other Zion Church leaders arrested during the same crackdown remain detained, and no such direct advocacy seems to have occurred at this most recent meeting. The case demonstrated how direct presidential engagement can potentially influence the circumstances
articles.content_zh:
美国总统唐纳德·特朗普,中国国家主席习近平,俄罗斯总统弗拉基米尔·普京星期四在中国深圳举行前所未有的三边峰会,展现出世界三大强国之间合作的形象,但很少就它们面临的冲突和国际问题达成具体协议.

大约80分钟的会议产生了关于联合国改革、能源生产、国际法律权威和核风险的联合声明。 然而,该声明对于乌克兰或伊朗的战争没有提出明确的突破,也没有公开提及中国和俄罗斯的宗教自由或对宗教团体的迫害.

会议强调了世界领导人直接参与的重要性,因为他们寻求管理相互竞争的利益、全球冲突和有关国际秩序未来的问题。 首脑会议还提供了一个机会,解决影响到数百万因信仰而面临迫害的人的关切,特别是在专制政权统治的国家。

以全球稳定为重点的首脑会议 三位领导人自称分担维护国际和平与安全的责任。 他们的联合声明呼吁联合国改革、增加石油产品的生产和供应,以及就减少核风险进一步进行对话。

各国领导人还强调国家主权和政府官员的豁免权,宣布国际刑事法院和类似机构不应滥用其权力。 其措辞反映了三国政府对限制国际机构的影响力的共同利益,尽管它们各自的政治、经济和安全优先事项仍然不同。

关于这一点,这种语言类似于中国在抵制美国尊重人权和确保公民可以自由信奉宗教的呼声时所使用的语言。 中国声称这是内政,反对美国过于狂热地维持治安,继续走迫害的道路。

普京将峰会描述为外交史上的新篇章,并称赞与特朗普和习近平直接接触的机会. 俄罗斯总统还援引了1945年雅尔塔会议,会议帮助塑造了战后的欧洲秩序,认为国际冲突最终需要各国承认当地的实际情况.

虽然领导人对对话和国际稳定表示兴趣,但他们的会议没有达成公开宣布的协议,以解决重大冲突或解决政府之间的紧张关系。

宗教自由仍然是全球关注的问题 对于宗教自由倡导者来说,高级别外交会议是一个重要的机会,可以提高良心犯和宗教界面临政府迫害的困境。 特别是中国继续严格限制宗教活动.

在未登记的教堂的基督徒面临监视,拘留,教堂关闭,以及服从政府监督的压力. 中国共产党将宗教机构置于其控制之下的运动影响了新教住宅教堂,天主教社区,藏传佛教,维吾尔穆斯林等宗教少数派.

最近几个月,国际倡导者敦促特朗普政府向习近平提出被囚禁宗教领袖的案件. 今年早些时候,特朗普在北京锡安教会创始人伊兹拉·金明里牧师会见习近平时提出这个案例. 中国当局随后释放了后来移居美国的金.

然而,在同一次镇压中被捕的其他锡安教会领导人仍然被拘留,在最近的这次会议上似乎没有进行这种直接的宣传。 该案表明,总统直接参与会如何影响局势

articles.title: In the Darkness, Christmas Shines a Light
articles.summary: The general revelation of God’s created order—darkness and light, night and day—primes every created thing to know they need light, a salvation from outside themselves.
articles.summary_zh: 神所创造的秩序——黑暗与光明、黑夜与白昼——的普遍启示，使每一受造物都认识到自己需要光明，需要来自自身之外的拯救。
articles.title_zh: 在黑暗中，圣诞节照亮光明
articles.content: Read For behold, darkness shall cover the earth, and thick darkness the peoples; but the LORD will arise upon you, and his glory will be seen upon you. And nations shall come to your light, and kings to the brightness of your rising. (Isa. 60:2–3) Reflect There’s something about a sunrise. It wakes the world. Unlike the jarring blare of an alarm clock, a sunrise quietly whispers “Wake, O sleeper” with the graceful love of a parent rubbing a sleeping child’s back. When the sun rises, the slumbering stir to life. We’ve just spent seven or eight hours dead to the world. Then the sunrise triggers in us what looks like a resurrection. We rise. Certain flowers—daisies, poppies, and the aptly named morning glories—open their blossoms at the sun’s rising. Little by little, empty streets fill and quiet houses stir. Drawn to the warmth and energy of the just-unveiled sun, we transition from rest to work, stillness to activity. Drawn to the warmth and energy of the just-unveiled sun, we transition from rest to work, stillness to activity. It’s not surprising that the sun is an oft-used metaphor for God. For he, too, resurrects the dead. He, too, is the Giver of life and growth. He, too, draws all things to himself—such as the trees, which by nature grow upward, toward the sun, their branches like arms raised in perpetual worship. This is the created order. All things were made to be drawn to and sustained by the sun. We were made to be alive insofar as we live, grow, and flourish by solar energy. So too with God. We’re in darkness and death without him. As he bestows his grace on us, we rise to new life. We’re able to grow. Like the sunflower blossom, which turns to follow the sun wherever it’s positioned in the sky, we’re created to look to the Lord, who “will arise upon [us], and his glory will be seen upon [us]” (Isa. 60:2). In a world of darkness, we ache for the light. We wait for the sunrise. All nations, all kings, all people share this in common. The horizon each of us looks to—the nature of the “new day” we await—may be different: A new job. A remodeled home. A regime change. But only the sunrise of Christ will eternally satisfy. His is “the true light, which gives light to everyone” (John 1:9). Isaiah’s prophecy was fulfilled in him. Only the sunrise of Christ will eternally satisfy. The general revelation of God’s created order—darkness and light, night and day—primes every created thing to know they need light, a salvation from outside themselves. The special revelation of Christ reveals a truer light than even the sun: the light that is our eternal life, the light the darkness will never overcome (v. 5), the light that will one day end night as we know it (Rev. 22:5). Respond How is God’s glory seen in your life? How are you reflecting his beauty? In contrast to those who dwell in darkness, how does your life reflect 1 Thessalonians 5:5: “You are all children of light, children of the day. We are not of the night or of the darkness”?

日出与闹钟不同, 当太阳升起时,沉睡会激起生命. 我们刚刚花了七八个小时去世界。 然后日出触发了我们 看起来像复活。 我们升起。

某些花朵——日出、罂粟和有名的晨光, 空荡荡的街道 安静的房屋被搅动 我们从休息到工作 静静到活动 我们从休息到工作 静静到活动

太阳是上帝常用的比喻, 他也会复活死者 他也是生命和成长的源泉 他也将万物引到自己身上,如那些自然而然地向着太阳生长的树木,他们的枝条,犹如在永恒的崇拜中竖起的手臂一样。 这是创造出来的秩序。 万物皆为太阳所牵引及支撑.

我们被太阳能所制成活生生的 故与神为也. 我们身处黑暗和死亡之中, 当他赐予我们恩典时 我们走向新生活 我们有能力成长。

和向日葵花一样,它会随太阳而来,无论太阳位于何处,我们都是为了仰望主而创造的,主"将出现[我们],他的荣耀将出现[我们]"(Isa. 60:2)。 在一个黑暗的世界里,我们渴望光明。 我们等待日出。 所有国家,所有国王,所有人民都拥有这个共同点.

我们每个人期待的地平线——我们等待的 " 新日 " 的性质——可能不同:新的工作。 一座重修的故乡. 政权更迭. 但只有基督的日出才能永远满足. 他的作品是“真正的光,它为每个人带来光明”(约翰1:9)。 以赛亚的预言在他身上得到了实现. 只有基督的日出才能永远满足

真主所创造的秩序——黑暗和光明,昼夜——的启示,使每一个被创造的事物都明白,他们需要光明,这是外部的拯救。 基督的特别启示揭示出比太阳更真实的光芒:即我们永恒生命的光芒,黑暗永远不会战胜的光芒(v. 5),即我们所知道的一天末夜的光芒(Rev.22: 5).

响应 上帝的荣耀在你的生活中是如何显现的? 你怎么反映他的美丽? 与那些生活在黑暗中的人不同,你的生活如何反映一个塞萨洛尼亚人5:5:“你们都是光明的孩子,是白天的孩子。 我们不是在黑夜中,也不是在黑暗中。”

articles.title_zh: 蝠鲼带领海洋科学家找到失去的鳍
articles.content: By Mark Ellis — Amber Sparks (Blue Latitudes Foundation Facebook page) Growing up in Laguna Beach, California, Amber Sparks developed a deep love for the ocean, which led her to study marine science at UC Berkeley and earn a master’s degree at Scripps Institute in San Diego. As co-founder of Blue Latitudes Foundation, she works with industry to find opportunities for conservation, especially with the Rigs-to-Reefs program, when oil drilling platforms are decommissioned. “We work with the oil companies to repurpose certain parts of the platform, retrofit it so that it can remain in place and continue to function as an artificial reef,” she told God Reports. Amber’s work has taken her around the world, with many dive experiences and encounters in the ocean with marine life. But there is one story she will never forget. It happened in the Gulf of Mexico shortly after Amber graduated from Scripps Institute and was invited on a research industry cruise with oil company representatives, scientists, and regulators on a liveaboard vessel. At the Flower Garden National Banks, a marine protected area 200 miles offshore, Amber was excited about her first dive, but slightly nervous. “You don’t know what you’re going to see or what this experience is going to be like,” she recalls. Dropping in (Blue Latitudes Foundation Facebook) Each diver had to jump off the vessel to get in the water. “We’re all geared up with our snorkel, our buoyancy control device, our wetsuit, and fins are the last thing you put on. So, I put on my fins and I jumped off the side of the boat.” “The second that I hit the water, one of my fins fell off, and I looked down and watched as it slowly descended to the bottom.” Amber glanced over at her dive buddy, and said, “I’m gonna go down. I’m going down.” Normally she would wait for her dive partner and they would go down together, but in this case, she thought, “I can’t (wait). I gotta go get my fin.” So Amber slowly began to descend to the bottom, about 60 feet below the ocean surface. “I felt completely lost. I was in a completely new area. I never dove before, and now I only had one fin.” She realized there were major currents that could have moved her fin in any direction. “I realized I can’t really swim with just one fin. So now not only am I at depth, but I’m handicapped with just one fin, and I started to feel pretty nervous.” It would probably take her 10 minutes to get back the surface, with safety stops. At the moment before panic set in, she looked upward and saw an amazing sight. It was a giant manta ray, with wings extending at least 10 feet. “Its wingspan was double mine. Its arms were out, and it was coming up over the side of a reef. “I’ve never seen a manta ray like this before. It totally took my breath away, it was so magnificent.” Another manta ray (Blue Latitudes Foundation Facebook page) She noted that manta rays are known in the ocean community to be “majestic, God-connected creatures with an understanding maybe beyond what humans can fully comprehend. They see the world and feel it in another way,” she notes. Mantas have the largest known brain of any fish. Their brains are large in absolute terms and relative to body size, which is also true of elephants, dolphins, and people. Their brains have enlarged areas associated with intelligence, vision, and motor coordination, and some of their brain cells are more like those in birds and mammals than in other fish.(1) As the manta ray drew close to Amber, she had an unusual communication experience. “I felt this sense where it said, ‘I want you to follow me. I’m going to help you find your fin.’ Amber Sparks Amber’s diving partner had just descended next to her, and they both began to swim after the manta. “I was barely making it, following this manta ray across the reef. At this point, I was so excited to see a manta ray. I kind of forgot about being handicapped, and I was just trying to go as fast as I can to keep up with it. Then Amber got the sur

articles.summary: By Brian Nixon — While sitting in the John Warwick Montgomery Study Center at the Lanier Library and Study Center in Houston, Texas, awaiting a meeting, I turned to librarian Sharon Cofran and Executive Director Dr. David Fleming and remarked, “John Warwick Montgomery would be very pleased with what Lanier has accomplished on his behalf.” […]  The post  Lanier’s Sixth Annual John Warwick Montgomery Lecture Series: A Grand Success  first appeared on  God Reports .
articles.summary_zh:
布莱恩·尼克松(Brian Nixon)——在德克萨斯州休斯敦拉尼尔图书馆和研究中心的约翰·沃里克·蒙哥马利研究中心等会议时,我转而请图书管理员莎伦·克夫兰(Sharon Cofran)和执行主任Dr.

David Fleming说,“约翰·沃里克·蒙哥马利对拉尼尔代表他取得的成就将感到非常高兴。” Lanier的第六届年度John Warwick Montgomery讲座系列:大成功首次出现在"上帝的报告"上。
articles.title_zh: 拉尼尔第六届年度约翰·沃里克·蒙哥马利系列讲座：圆满成功
articles.content: John Warwick Montgomery By Brian Nixon — While sitting in the John Warwick Montgomery Study Center at the Lanier Library and Study Center in Houston, Texas, awaiting a meeting, I turned to librarian Sharon Cofran and Executive Director Dr. David Fleming and remarked, “John Warwick Montgomery would be very pleased with what Lanier has accomplished on his behalf.” From Montgomery’s framed correspondence with C. S. Lewis and his barrister gowns to the thousands of books that comprise his remarkable personal collection, Lanier has provided the Christian world with a marvelous tribute to one of the great Christian intellectuals of the twentieth and twenty-first centuries. Born in 1931, John Warwick Montgomery (d. 2024) was a distinguished Christian apologist, theologian, attorney, and scholar whose extraordinary career spanned several disciplines. Holding numerous academic degrees, including doctorates in theology, philosophy, and law, Montgomery became internationally recognized for his defense of Christianity through historical evidence, legal reasoning, and philosophical argumentation. His influential books, including History and Christianity , Faith Founded on Fact , and The Shape of the Past , helped establish a rigorous approach to Christian apologetics. Whether lecturing in universities, debating skeptics, or practicing law, Montgomery maintained that Christianity was not merely a matter of subjective belief but a faith grounded in historical reality and rational inquiry. Yet to stop at the library would be to understate Lanier’s remarkable work. The sixth annual John Warwick Montgomery Lecture Series was a tour de force of distinguished thinkers, passionate Christians, and intellectually engaging presentations. More than a commemoration of Montgomery’s life, the gathering represented a continuation of his intellectual legacy: the conviction that Christianity can withstand serious scrutiny and offer compelling answers to life’s most profound questions. Mark Lanier, Nancy Pearcey, Paul Gould, Adam Francisco, and Michael Horton From the opening panel discussion hosted by attorney and philanthropist Mark Lanier to Dr. Paul Gould’s thoughtful presentation on worldviews, followed by attorney Craig Parton’s lecture on jurisprudential apologetics, one theme emerged with unmistakable clarity: Christianity is a reasonable faith. The presentations reflected Montgomery’s own interdisciplinary approach to apologetics: the Christian faith and intellectual inquiry need not be adversaries. Indeed, the Christian tradition has long insisted that faith and reason are complementary avenues in the pursuit of truth. The following day continued this rich intellectual exploration. Professor Nancy Pearcey addressed questions surrounding truth, dismantling various modern ideologies, while Dr. Adam Francisco offered an informative overview of Islamic history and belief, helping participants better understand one of world’s biggest religions. The keynote address by Dr. Michael Horton examined the challenge of reaching those who identify as “spiritual but not religious,” a growing segment of contemporary society. Horton’s presentation underscored the importance of communicating historic Christian truth in a culture increasingly suspicious of religious institutions yet often deeply interested in spiritual meaning. Dr. Michael Horton On Sunday morning, Lanier founder, Mark Lanier, hosted many participants during his Biblical literacy class, where he continued the dialogue with Michael Horton. Taken together, the lectures, discussions, and interviews demonstrated the breadth of Christian scholarship and the continuing relevance of thoughtful apologetics in an age of skepticism, religious pluralism, and cultural uncertainty. As I reflected on the weekend, I was reminded of the Festschrift Christianity for the Tough-Minded , a collection of scholarly essays honoring Montgomery’s life and ministry. Like that volume, the Lanier lecture series brought together
articles.content_zh:
约翰·沃威克·蒙哥马利·由布赖恩·尼克松(John Warwick Montgomery By Brian Nixon)——在德克萨斯州休斯敦拉尼尔图书馆和研究中心的约翰·沃威克·蒙哥马利研究中心等会议时,我转而请图书管理员莎伦·克夫兰(Sharon Cofran)和执行主任Dr.

大卫·弗莱明(David Fleming)说道,“约翰·沃里克·蒙哥马利(John Warwick Montgomery)将非常满意拉尼尔代表他取得的成就。” 蒙哥马利与C.S.的书信

刘易斯和他的大律师礼服为他杰出的个人收藏的上千本书所提供,莱尼尔为基督教世界提供了令人赞叹的敬意,他是20世纪和21世纪伟大的基督教知识分子之一。 1931年生于约翰·沃里克·蒙哥马利(d.

2024年是一位杰出的基督教道歉学家,神学家,律师和学者,他的非凡生涯跨越了多个学科. 蒙哥马利拥有众多学术学位,包括神学,哲学和法学等博士学位,他通过历史证据,法律推理,和哲学论证,为基督教辩护而获得国际承认.

他的有影响力的著作,包括"历史与基督教"(History and Christian, Faith Founded on Fact),以及"过去的形状"(The Shape of the Past)等,帮助确立了对基督教古典主义的严格处理方法. 无论是在大学里讲道,辩论怀疑论,还是实践法律,蒙哥马利都坚持认为基督教不仅仅是主观信仰的问题,而是建立在历史现实和理性调查基础上的信仰.

在图书馆停留, 第六期年度约翰·沃里克·蒙哥马利讲座系列是一次由杰出的思想家,充满热情的基督徒,以及智力参与演讲的巡回演出.

这次集会不仅是纪念蒙哥马利的生平,还代表着他思想遗产的延续:坚信基督教能够经受住严肃的审视,并为人生最深刻的问题提供令人信服的答案.

马克·拉尼尔,南茜·皮尔西,保罗·古尔德,亚当·弗朗西斯科,和迈克尔·霍顿 从律师和慈善家马克·拉尼尔主持的开场小组讨论到保罗·古尔德博士关于世界观的深思熟虑的介绍,然后是克雷格·帕通律师关于法学学说讲座,一个主题以明确无误的方式出现: 基督教是一种合理的信仰.

这些演讲反映了蒙哥马利自己对道具的跨学科方法:基督教信仰和知识调查不必是对手。 事实上,基督教传统长期以来一直坚持认为,信仰和理性是追求真理的补充途径。 次日继续进行这种丰富的知识探索.

Nancy Pearcey教授谈到了围绕真理的问题,摧毁了各种现代意识形态,而Adam Francisco博士则对伊斯兰历史和信仰提供了翔实的概述,帮助参与者更好地了解了世界上最大的宗教之一。 由Dr.A.先生作主旨发言。

迈克尔·霍顿研究了帮助那些认为是“精神上而非宗教上”的当代社会日益扩大的阶层的挑战。 Horton的演讲强调了在一种对宗教机构越来越有怀疑的文化中传播历史性的基督教真理的重要性,而这种文化往往对精神意义很感兴趣。 医生

迈克尔·霍顿 星期天早上,拉尼尔的创始人马克·拉尼尔(Mark Lanier)在圣经扫盲班期间接待了许多参与者,在那里他继续与迈克尔·霍顿进行对话.

讲座、讨论和访谈共同显示了基督教奖学金的广度,以及深思熟虑的学说在怀疑主义、宗教多元化和文化不确定性的时代的持续相关性。

正如我在周末所回顾的那样,人们提醒我为强硬派而信奉费斯奇里夫基督教,这是一本纪念蒙哥马利生平和部的学术论文集。 和那卷一样,拉尼尔系列讲座也聚集在一起

articles.summary_zh: 文：查尔斯·加德纳（Charles Gardner）——在第二次世界大战南太平洋的一场海战中，一名日本水兵所在的驱逐舰被美国人击沉，他的大多数战友都淹死了。令人惊奇的是，尽管鱼雷官新谷通晴与其他人一起被卷入波涛之下，随着战舰的沉没，但他却奇迹般地在这场1942年的灾难中幸存下来。（只有18名……）  这篇文章《二战日本战俘在战俘营中找到“自由”》最初发表在《上帝报道》上。
articles.title_zh: 二战日本战俘在战俘营中找到“自由”
articles.content: By Charles Gardner — When a Japanese sailor’s destroyer was sunk by the Americans in a World War II South Pacific battle, most of his companions drowned. Amazingly, even though he was sucked underneath the waves with others as the ship went down, torpedo officer Michiharu Shinya somehow survived this 1942 disaster. (Only 18 of the 200-strong crew did). But he would rather have died at that point as his people had been indoctrinated to believe that it was shameful to be captured. Nevertheless, he was badly wounded but nursed back to health by medics. In time, he was picked up and eventually taken to a Prisoner-of-War camp at Featherston, near Wellington, in New Zealand, where he was to spend the next three years, as Don Stephens records in his inspirational book War and Grace (Evangelical Press, an imprint of 10Publishing). Shinya and his fellow inmates were treated with much kindness (in sharp contrast to the torture often experienced by Allied prisoners at the hands of the Japanese). Being showered with gifts at Christmas, a feast he knew nothing about, seemed especially strange. However, he was determined not to be ‘taken in’ by the Christian teaching offered after some of the prisoners requested spiritual help and a Japanese Bible was made available. That is until he chanced upon an article entitled ‘Sorrow in Victory’ in which the author quoted a ‘Hebrew prophet’ as saying: “Those who hope in the Lord will renew their strength. They shall soar on wings like eagles; they will run and not grow weary; they will walk and not be faint.” It made a deep impression on him, and he was determined to find out where it came from. Assuming it was from the Old Testament, he began reading the Bible, starting at Genesis chapter 1. Eventually, to his joy, he discovered that the profound words were from the Book of the prophet Isaiah (chapter 40, verse 31). After flagging somewhat in his search, he found himself hospitalised with malaria when a friend brought him a booklet called The Reason Why explaining the way to salvation. It so happened that the camp’s chaplain, Pastor Hessell Troughton, had been a missionary to Japan and spoke the language. Shinya joined others in his Bible studies and came to know and love Jesus as his Saviour. So much did this “complete freedom” now rule his life that prison had morphed into what he described as “a unique paradise on earth”. He never looked back after that and became convinced that his post-war calling would be in service of his Lord. When he finally returned home, his family were shocked to see him alive for he had been reported as killed in action. He had also given a false name to his captors because of the supposed shame of falling into enemy hands. Shinya subsequently became a pastor and prolific writer and translator following years of theological study both in Tokyo and the US. The Old Testament, he came to believe, demonstrated that sin is “the ultimate problem of mankind” and clearly pointed to Christ as the answer. On seeking to understand why so few Japanese became Christians, he felt it was partly due to their pride borne of believing they were a superior race. As for those three Christmases he spent in New Zealand, author Don Stephens writes: “Of all the gifts he received, the one he valued most was ‘the boundless and deep grace and peace of God in the Lord Jesus Christ’.” The post WWII Japanese POW found ‘freedom’ in camp first appeared on God Reports .
articles.content_zh:
查尔斯·加德纳编著: 当一艘日本水手的驱逐舰在二战南太平洋战役中被美国人击沉时,大部分同伴溺毙. 令人惊奇的是,尽管随着船只的下沉,他与其他人一起被吸在海浪下,但鱼雷军官Michiharu Shinya却不知何故幸免于1942年的灾难。 (200人的船员中只有18人这样做).

但他宁愿死在那个时候,因为他的族人被灌输相信被俘虏是可耻的. 然而,他受了重伤,但被医护人员喂养。

在时间上,他被接了起来,最终被带到新西兰惠灵顿附近的费瑟斯顿(Featherston)的战俘营,在那里他将度过接下来的三年,正如唐·斯蒂芬斯在他的励志书"战争与格蕾丝"(福音出版社,10Publishing的印记)中记载的那样.

信也和同狱囚犯受到很大程度的善待(与盟军囚犯经常在日本人手中遭受的酷刑形成鲜明对比). 在圣诞节用礼物淋浴 一个他一无所知的宴会 看起来特别奇怪

然而,在一些囚犯要求精神帮助和提供日本圣经后,他决心不再接受基督教教义的 " 接纳 " 。 直到他看到一篇题为“为胜利而悲伤”的文章,作者在文章中引用了一位“赫布鲁先知”的话:“那些希望主复活的人。 他们将像鹰一样飞翔,

他们将奔驰,而不会疲倦,他们将走路,而不会晕倒。 这给他留下了深刻的印象,他下定决心要找出它来自何处. 假设它来自旧约,他开始阅读圣经,从创世纪第一章开始. 最终,在他的喜悦中,他发现深刻的文字来自先知以赛亚的经典(第40章第31节).

在搜索中略微浮出水面后,他发现自己患上了疟疾,一位朋友给他带了一本小册子,名为《原因》,解释救世之路。 难民营的牧师Hessell Troughton牧师曾是日本的传教士, 信也加入了其他人的圣经研究,来到了了解和热爱耶稣作为他的救世主.

这种“完全自由”现在统治了他的生活,监狱变成了他所称的“地球上独一无二的天堂”。 他从此之后再也没有回头看,并且确信他的战后召唤将会为他的主服务. 当他最终回家时,家人震惊地看到他活着,因为他被报道为阵亡.

他还给抓捕者取了一个假名,因为被假定是落入敌人手中的耻辱。 在东京和美国多年的神学研究之后,信也后来成为一名牧师和多产作家和翻译。 他逐渐相信,《旧约》表明了罪恶是“人类的最终问题”,并明确指出基督是答案。

在试图理解为什么如此少的日本人成为基督徒时,他感到部分是由于他们的自豪感,因为他们相信他们是优越的种族。

至于他在新西兰度过的三个圣诞节,作者Don Stephens写道:"在他收到的所有礼物中,他最珍视的一件是`上帝在耶稣基督中无限和深厚的恩惠与和平 ' 。 日本战俘在营地发现「自由」,

articles.title_zh: 在西部明星的阴影下：格罗弗·刘易斯、拉里·麦克默特里和文字的胜利
articles.content: With The Grover Lewis Reader: Splendor in the Short Grass and Western Star , the newest biography of Larry McMurtry, in hand, I load my truck and head toward Archer City, Texas, accompanied by my wife, Melanie, and our friend Eliott. Archer City is, of course, McMurtry country, a small Texas town made famous through the literary imagination of one of America’s most celebrated novelists. Having written about McMurtry’s faith—or lack thereof—in a previous article , following an earlier visit to Archer City, I’m returning with a somewhat different interest. This time, my attention turns to Grover Lewis, the gifted journalist, critic, and poet whose life intersected with McMurtry’s during their college years. Lewis’ story, however, begins not with literary achievement but with almost unimaginable tragedy. As a child, he experienced the devastating loss of both parents when his father murdered his mother and was subsequently shot with the same gun, either by his dying wife or another person present. Lewis was only eight years old. It is difficult to imagine a more horrific beginning. Yet rather than allowing that tragedy to become the entirety of his story, Lewis eventually found a voice through literature. Perhaps the cards life dealt him gave him plenty to write about. Or perhaps writing became his way of making sense of a world that had revealed its cruelty far too early. In his autobiographical poem “Hillbilly Song,” Lewis writes: “You asked me once, Ann/Over coffee gone cold with talk/In your mother’s rain-drowsy/House, who they were, how it/Was with them in their breathless/Time in the wilds of years.” For Lewis, those early years were indeed wild. But they were also the soil from which his literary imagination would eventually grow. A Life in Words Born in Texas in 1934, Grover Lewis emerged as a distinctive voice in American journalism, particularly through his cultural criticism and reporting on the rapidly changing landscape of the 1960s and 1970s. He became known for his sharp observations, literary flair, and ability to capture the personalities and contradictions of American culture, even if he occasionally stretched the truth in the telling. His work appeared in prominent publications, including Rolling Stone , where his reporting helped establish his reputation as an insightful, sometimes cutting observer of popular culture. Lewis was more than a journalist, however. He was a poet and literary craftsman, someone who understood that words could do more than convey information. They could illuminate the human condition, expose its contradictions, and perhaps even provide a measure of healing. Grover Lewis (ChatPGT) Continuing “Hillbilly Song,” Lewis ponders: “At last, breathless and dry-mouthed/With private desire in the blue,/Swollen dark, we all lie down together—/My mother, my father, their perishing/Dreams, and I this unborn prisoner son…” There is something haunting about these lines. The dead remain present. The past refuses to disappear. And the poet, even as an adult, seems to wrestle with the circumstances that shaped his entrance into the world. Yet the very act of writing suggests something else: a refusal to remain silent. Two Texans, Two Literary Paths Lewis and Larry McMurtry crossed paths as students at North Texas State College, now the University of North Texas, during the 1950s. Both were young Texans drawn to literature and the possibilities of the written word. Their friendship developed within a shared intellectual environment, one that encouraged reading, conversation, and the pursuit of literary ambitions. Although their careers eventually followed different paths—McMurtry toward novels, screenplays, and literary fame, Lewis toward journalism, poetry, and cultural criticism—they shared an interest in the complexities of American life. articles.content_zh:
与《格罗弗·刘易斯读者:短草中的辉煌与西部之星》,拉里·麦克默特里的最新传记, 手持,我装载我的卡车并前往德克萨斯州阿彻城, 由我的妻子梅兰妮和我们的朋友埃利奥特陪同。 阿彻城当然是麦克默特里国家,一个通过美国最著名的小说家之一的文学想象而成名的德克萨斯小镇.

在之前访问Archer城后, 我对McMurtry的信仰(或缺乏信仰)有一番兴趣, 这一次,我转而关注有天赋的记者、评论家和诗人格罗弗·刘易斯,他在大学时代的生活与麦克默特里的生活交织在一起。

然而,刘易斯的故事并非从文学成就开始,而是从几乎难以想象的悲剧开始. 他从小就经历了父母的惨痛损失,当时他的父亲谋杀了他的母亲,随后被他即将死亡的妻子或在场的其他人用同一把枪射杀。 刘易斯才八岁 很难想象一个更可怕的开端。

然而,刘易斯最终没有让这场悲剧成为他的全部故事,而是通过文学找到了声音. 也许他命中注定的卡片 给他写了很多东西 或写作成为他理解世界的方式, 这个世界已经揭示了它的残酷性,还为时过早。

刘易斯在自传诗“Hillbilly Song”中写道 : “ 你曾经问过我,Ann/Over咖啡随着谈话而变得冷淡,在你妈妈的雨滴/住所里,他们是谁,他们在无气息的年代/在野外时如何。 ” 对刘易斯来说,那些早年的确很狂野. 但它们也是他的文学想象最终会成长的土壤.

1934年出生于德克萨斯州的"言语生活"(A Life in Words Born in Texas),格罗弗·刘易斯(Grover Lewis)成为美国新闻业中一个有特色的代言人,特别是通过他对1960年代和1970年代迅速变化的地貌的文化批评和报道.

他以尖锐的观察,文学的才华,以及能够捕捉美国文化的个性和矛盾而闻名,即使他偶尔在讲述中伸张真理. 他的作品出现在包括滚石公司在内的著名出版物中,他的报道帮助他树立了自己作为有见地,有时剪切流行文化观察者的声誉.

然而,刘易斯不只是一名记者。 他是一位诗人和文学家,一个懂得文字可以比传递信息更有用的人. 它们可以揭示人类的状况,暴露其矛盾,甚至可能提供某种治疗方法。

Grover Lewis (ChatPGT) 继续“Hillbilly Song,” 刘易斯思考道:“最后,无气息和干燥的嘴唇/在蓝色的暗处私欲下,我们都躺在一起——/我的母亲、父亲、他们的死亡/梦想,我这个未出生的囚犯儿子......” 这些台词有些困扰。 死者仍然在场。 过去拒绝消失。

而诗人,即使作为一个成年人,似乎也与塑造他进入世界的环境相搏. 然而,写作本身就暗示了另一种情况:拒绝保持沉默。 两德克萨斯州立大学,两条文学道路刘易斯州立大学和拉里·麦克默特里(英语:Larry McMurtry)在1950年代作为北德克萨斯州立学院,即现在的北德克萨斯大学的学生跨过道路.

两人都是年轻的德克萨斯人,被吸引到文学和写字的可能性. 他们的友谊是在共同的知识环境中发展起来的,这种环境鼓励阅读,对话,追求文学野心.

尽管他们的职业生涯最终走的是不同的道路——小说、剧本和文学名人、刘易斯新闻、诗歌和文化批评——但他们对美国生活的复杂性有着共同的兴趣。 麦克默特里和刘易斯在大学期间(ChatGPT)都拥有超越德克萨斯州和美国西部神话的能力,认识到孤独,凝视
