시편 51편 라틴어 구절에서 유래 루오 작품, 전쟁 사실 기록 넘어 비극 인간 실존 심연 정면 응시 치유와 구속 갈망 인간 신앙고백 캄캄한 잿더미 속 그리스도 상처 응시하며 새벽을 대망했던 루오

인류 역사상 전쟁이 멈추었던 평화의 시기는 다 합쳐도 고작 수십 년에 불과하다고 한다. 이는 인류의 연대기가 피와 폭력으로 얼룩져 왔음을 방증하는 테이터이다.

두 차례 세계대전을 거치며 괴멸적인 비극을 겪은 인류는 ‘다시는 전쟁을 되풀이하지 않겠다’고 맹세했으나, 올바른 길을 잃고 캄캄한 정글을 헤매는 인간의 어리석음은 이에 아랑곳없이 오늘날에도 지구촌 도처에서 포성을 멈추지 않고 있다.

미학자 테오도어 아도르노(Th. W. Adorno)는 전쟁의 야만을 목도한 후 “이제 예술에 관해서는 그 어떤 것도 자명하지 않다는 사실만이 자명해졌다”고 탄식했다. 시대의 비극은 인간의 삶에 충격을 주고 그것은 곧 예술로 이어진다.

프랑스 화가 조르주 루오(Georges Rouault, 1871–1958) 역시 참혹한 전쟁의 광기 앞에서 침묵하는 대신, 분노와 연민을 화폭에 아로새긴 예술가다. 제1차 세계대전의 참상 속에서 루오는 그의 필생의 역작인 ‘미제레레(Miserere)’ 연작을 구상하기에 이른다.

‘미제레레’는 시편 51편 1절의 라틴어 구절 “하나님이여, 주의 인자를 따라 내게 은혜를 베푸시며(Miserere mei, Deus, secundum magnam misericordiam tuam)”에서 가져온 제목이다. 전반부 33점은 하나님의 자비와 긍휼을 간구하는 내용을, 후반부 25점(34-58번)은 전쟁의 비극을 테마로 삼아 구성되었다.

그런데 루오의 화면에는 통상적인 전쟁화에서 흔히 볼 수 있는 군인들의 스펙터클한 전투 장면이나 피비린내 나는 살육의 현장이 등장하지 않는다. 대신 잿더미가 된 폐허 속에서 오열하는 여인들, 전장으로 떠나는 아들과 고개 숙인 아버지, 가난한 어머니와 눈을 맞추는 아이, 그리고 온갖 조롱과 모욕 속에서 묵묵히 십자가를 지신 그리스도의 형상이 화면을 채운다.

루오의 판화는 전쟁에 대한 사실적 기록을 넘어, 어둡고 비극적인 인간 실존의 심연을 정면으로 응시하며 치유와 구속을 갈망하는 양심적인 인간의 신앙적 고백이다.

토머스 홉스(Thomas Hobbes)의 ‘만인에 대한 만인의 투쟁’을 환기하는 ‘인간은 인간에게 늑대이다(Homo Homini Lupus)’는 전쟁의 광기가 빚어낸 참혹한 주검을 그로테스크하게 폭로한다. 바닥에 뒹구는 해골과 황폐한 거리는 인간이 인간을 증오하고 도륙한 결과가 결국 공멸의 절망뿐임을 가감없이 표출한다.

반면 ‘아버지, 이제 마지막입니다’는 전쟁터로 징집돼 떠나는 아들과 늙은 아버지의 비통한 작별을 담은 흑백 동판화다. 아버지는 흐느끼며 고개를 떨구고, 작별을 고하는 아들의 곁에는 불길한 해골의 형상이 드리워져 있어 청년의 죽음을 예고한다.

전자는 폭력과 증오가 휩쓸고 지나간 폐허를 정면으로 고발하며 인간의 죄성과 파멸의 실상을 적나라하게 증언하는 반면, 후자는 피할 수 없는 비극적 운명 앞에서 서로를 부둥켜 안는 부자(父子)의 내밀한 비탄을 통해, 차가운 역사의 폭력에 희생되는 개별 인간의 존엄과 애끓는 연민을 일깨운다.

니콜라스 월터스토프(Nicholas Wolterstorff)는 2017년 듀크 대학교에서 열린 루오의 ‘미제레레’ 기념 강연에서 그의 작업을 ‘사회적 저항 예술(Social Protest Art)’로 규정했다. 월터스토프는 20세기 판화의 정점인 ‘미제레레’를 피카소의 ‘게르니카’, 벤저민 브리튼의 ‘전쟁 레퀴엠’, 존 스타인벡의 소설 『분노의 포도』와 어깨를 나란히 하는 대표적 저항 예술의 기념비로 꼽았다.

그는 강연에서 루오의 작품이 “사회적 불의에 맞서는 저항에 활력을 불어넣고 이를 조형적으로 증언함으로써”, 짓밟힌 인간의 존엄성을 회복하고 고통받는 사람들의 신음을 가시화했다는 점에 주목했다.

이 작품들이 비록 100년 전 시공간에 뿌리를 두고 있지만, 작품 속 ‘투사된 세계(projected world)’와 마주하는 감상자 사이에 강력한 도덕적·정서적 상호 작용을 촉발해, 예술 속 인물의 고통이 오늘 우리가 살아가는 ‘실제 세계(actual world)’로 전이(transference)되는 심오한 윤리적 힘을 발휘한다고 보았다.

‘미제레레’ 연작은 전쟁을 통해 명백히 드러난 사회적 불의와 인간의 타락, 비참한 실존을 거침없이 노출시킴으로써, 세상을 지배하는 폭력의 구조에 저항한다. 루오 스스로도 억압받는 사람들을 대변하는 것을 예술가의 천직으로 여겼으며, 자신의 삶을 ‘그림자의 포로(prisonnier des ombres)’로 규정할 만큼 희생자와 가난한 자들의 편에 서기를 주저하지 않았다.

조르주 루오가 이 연작에서 가장 깊은 영적 에너지를 쏟아부은 대목은 단연 ‘그리스도의 수난’이다. ‘미제레레’ 연작의 서막을 “예수 곤욕을 당하시다(2번)”로 열고, 대단원을 “그가 상처를 입음으로 우리가 나음을 입었도다(58번, 사 53:5)”로 마감한 것은 대단히 상징적이다. 그는 인간의 절망과 부조리에 대한 궁극적인 해법이 오직 고난받으신 그리스도의 십자가에 있음을 고백한 것이다.

“일어나라 죽은 자들이여(54번)”에서는 에스겔 골짜기의 마른 뼈들을 일으키신 하나님의 숨결(겔 37장)처럼, 죽음의 잿더미 속에서 부활하는 생명들을 묘사했다. 비록 피부가 덮이고 살이 차오르는 가시적 묘사는 생략됐을지라도, 이 흑백의 판화는 “그리스도 안에서 모든 사람이 삶을 얻으리라(고전 15:22)”는 종말론적 소망을 길어 올린다.

이 연작에서 주목하고 싶은 점은 인간 실존의 근원적 비극을 응시하기 위해 루오가 선택한 조형적 태도다. 전쟁의 참화를 표현하기 위해 그는 부르주아적 살롱 미술의 화려한 색채나 매끄러운 아름다움을 배격했다. 아픈 현실을 표현하는데 기본의 방식은 어울리지 않는다고 판단한 것이다.

그는 대신에 거칠고 투박한 검은 윤곽선과 칙칙하고 짓이겨진 채색법을 동원했다. 당대에 풍미했던 안이한 유미주의적 전통에 안주하기를 거부하고, 스스로를 비판적 저항 예술의 자리에 고수한 것이다.

지하 카타콤의 암흑 속에서 걸어나온 듯한 인물들의 처연한 형상은, 구원에 목말라 하던 당대의 병사들과 피난민들의 얼굴이자, 오늘날에도 미사일과 무인 드론의 포화 아래 신음하는 지구촌의 무고한 생명들을 정면으로 직시하게 만든다.

루오는 전쟁의 한복판에서 인간의 궁극적 구원과 하나님의 공의를 간구하는 기도의 심정으로 ‘미제레레’의 동판을 깎아냈다. 월터스토프가 통찰했듯, 폭력에 짓밟힌 진리를 향해 온몸으로 저항했던 루오의 몸부림은 단순한 감상적 미화를 넘어 불의를 폭로하고 상처 입은 자들을 품으시는 하나님의 긍휼을 증언하고 있다.

생애 말년에 조르주 루오는 “나는 평생을 ‘황혼’을 그리는 데 바쳤다. 이제부터는 ‘새벽’을 그리고 싶다”는 함축적인 말을 남겼다. 인간의 비참함과 상흔을 정면으로 마주하며 어둠의 긴 터널을 통과해 온 노작가가 마침내 구원과 회복의 여명을 갈망한 것이다.

하지만 불행하게도 지구촌 곳곳에서 폭력과 파괴의 비극이 되풀이되는 오늘의 현실은, 인류가 여전히 짙게 드리운 ‘황혼’의 그늘을 벗어나지 못했음을 일깨운다.

캄캄한 잿더미 속에서도 그리스도의 상처를 응시하며 새벽을 대망했던 루오의 시선은, 오늘날 이 부서진 세계를 향해 깊은 애통을 품고 치유와 위로의 손길을 내미는 일의 의미를 되새기게 한다.

서성록 명예교수(안동대 미술학과)

articles.content:
삼위일체, 구속사 성패 좌우 반석 추상적 변증법, 심리학 모델 아냐 존재론적·경륜적 핵심 구분 필요 언약신학과 예배 통해 구체화 돼 박진영, 양태론·영지주의적 편향

한국장로교신학회(회장 박응규 교수) 제42회 학술발표회가 11월 21일 오전 경기 용인 웨스트민스터신학대학원대학교 그레이스홀에서 ‘장로교회의 전통과 역할’이라는 주제로 개최됐다.

박진영 JYP 대표의 주장 등으로 ‘삼위일체 교리’에 다시 관심이 모아지는 가운데, 이날 신학회에서는 안명준 박사(한국성서대)를 좌장으로 본지 칼럼니스트 이금석 교수(수도국제대학원대학교)가 ‘개혁주의 관점의 정통 삼위일체론과 세상적 관점 비교’라는 제목으로 정통 개혁주의 삼위일체론에 대해 발표했다.

이금석 교수는 “정통 개혁주의 삼위일체론은 계시된 하나님의 초월성과 내재성, 본질의 단일성과 위격의 다양성을 온전히 보존하는 기독교 신앙의 심장”이라며 “세속 철학이 이를 추상적 변증법이나 심리학적 모델로 환원시키고, 박진영과 같은 자의적 강해자들이 이를 기능적 구원 메커니즘과 지적 확신론으로 왜곡할 때, 기독교의 하나님은 인격을 상실하거나 단순한 법률적 집행자로 전락할 수 있다”고 밝혔다.

그러면서 “삼위일체 하나님은 인간의 죄 문제를 처리하기 위해 고안된 ‘기계 장치’가 아니라, 영원한 사랑과 영광의 교제 속에 우리를 ‘아들의 자녀 됨’으로 부르시는 참 하나님”이라며 “교회는 성부의 영원한 작정과 성자의 온전한 대속, 성령의 주권적 갱신으로 이어지는 정통 삼위일체론의 부요함을 확고히 붙들고, 변질된 대중주의적 신학 운동에 대해 명확한 성경적·교의학적 분별력을 발휘해야 한다”고 강조했다.

구체적으로는 “기독교 신학 역사에서 삼위일체론(Trinitas)은 단지 하나의 사변적 명제에 머물지 않고, 교회 정체성과 구원론, 예배의 기틀을 결정지어 온 신앙의 가장 핵심적 기초(fundamentum fidei)였다”며 “개혁주의 교의학은 하나님을 ‘본체에 있어서는 한 분이시며, 위격에 있어서는 세 분이신 영원한 자존자’로 고백하며(웨스트민스터 신앙고백서 II.3), 삼위일체 교리를 구속사의 성패를 가르는 중심 반석으로 삼아왔다”고 말했다.

이 교수는 “정통 개혁주의 삼위일체론의 신학적 정체성은 고대 공교회적 정통성(Catholic Orthodoxy)의 충실한 계승, 성경 계시에 기초한 사변적 이성주의 극복, 하나님의 단일 주권과 위격적 구속 사역의 조화를 이룬 ‘성경적·변증학적 삼위일체주의’에 자리하고 있다”며 ““개혁주의 삼위일체론 이해에 핵심적 구분은 존재론적 삼위일체(Immanent·Ontological Trinity)와 경륜적 삼위일체(Economic Trinity)의 관계성”이라고 소개했다.

그는 “존재론적 삼위일체는 시간 이전 영원 안에서 삼위 하나님이 스스로 거하시는 본질적 관계와 내적 생명을 의미한다. 성부·성자·성령은 완전한 동등성(aequalitas)과 동일본질(homoousios)을 공유하신다”며 “경륜적 삼위일체론은 창조-섭리-구속이라는 역사적 시공간 속에서 삼위 하나님이 자신을 계시하시고 사역하시는 질서를 의미한다. 정통 개혁주의는 ‘외부로 향하는 하나님의 사역은 나뉠 수 없다(opera Trinitatis ad extra indivisa sunt)’는 고전적 명제를 강력히 지지한다. 다만 각 위격의 고유한 관계에 따른 ‘사역의 특정성(appropriatio)’이 경륜 속에서 드러날 뿐”이라고 풀이했다.

그러면서 “개혁신학에서 삼위일체 교의는 특히 ‘구속 경륜의 영원한 기초(언약신학)’와 ‘교회의 공적 예배 및 기도 구조(예배학)’ 안에서 가장 선명하게 구체화된다”며 “개혁주의 언약신학(Covenant Theology)에서 인간의 구원은 타락 이후 역사 속에서 임기응변으로 고안된 즉흥적 계획이 아니다. 구원은 창세 전 삼위 하나님 사이의 영원한 내재적 합의인 ‘구원 협약(Pactum Salutis)’에 굳건히 뿌리를 두고 있다. 구원의 근거가 인간의 가변적 감정이나 불완전한 결단이 아니라 삼위일체 하나님의 불변하는 영원한 언약적 합의에 기초해 있기에, 성도의 구원은 결코 취소될 수 없는 절대적 확실성과 견인의 보증을 획득한다”고 했다.

또 “개혁주의 예배학(Liturgics)과 영성은 인간 중심적 감정의 배설이나 심리적 위안의 통로가 아니라, 삼위일체 하나님의 영원한 교제 안으로 초대받는 성례적·교제적 사건이다. 참된 기독교 예배와 기도는 철저하게 상향적·하향적 삼위일체 구조를 띤다”며 “성령의 도우심 없는 예배는 열광주의로 변질되기 쉽고, 그리스도의 중보 없는 기도는 교만한 율법주의에 빠지기 쉬우며, 성부의 영광을 지향하지 않는 영성은 자기 만족적 주관주의로 전락하기 쉽다. 따라서 개혁주의 예배는 그 시작인 ‘삼위일체적 송영과 기원’부터 마침의 ‘축도’에 이르기까지, 삼위일체 하나님의 이름 안에서 전개되는 거룩한 역사”라고 전했다.

이에 대해 “정통 삼위일체론은 ‘한 본질(una substantia) 안에 계신 세 위격’의 영원한 내적 관계와 외적 사역을 설명하며, 본질의 단일성과 위격의 실재성을 상호 내주 원리로 정립한다”며 “반면 세속적 삼위일체 이해는 주로 헤겔식 정-반-합의 변증법적 원리, 융의 심리학적 원형, 기능주의적 양태론으로 왜곡된다. 특히 박진영의 삼위일체와 구원 이해는 지적 동의 중심의 ‘단번에 받는 구원’ 논리와 결합, 성령의 독립적 위격성과 성화 사역을 축소시키거나 그리스도의 사역을 기능적 메커니즘으로 환원시키는 양태론적·영지주의적 편향을 노출한다”고 분석했다.

박진영 신론 및 삼위일체론 오류 성경, 논리적·수학적 계약서 접근 구원사, 채무 변제 계약서로 환원 탈문맥화, 기계적 성경 실증주의 성령의 주권적 중생 사역 배제돼 성령 하나님 인격적 사역도 약화

특히 그는 “박진영 신학의 가장 근본적인 신론적 오류는 ‘영·혼·몸’이라는 인간의 삼분법적 구조를 삼위일체 하나님께 그대로 대입하는 ‘범주 혼동(Category Mistake)’에서 출발한다”며 “박진영은 성부와 성자에게 각각 독립된 ‘혼’이 존재한다고 주장함으로써, 성부와 성자를 분리하는 ‘삼신론적 경향’을 갖는다. 곧 두 분을 서로 다른 본질을 지닌 두 신적 존재로 나눈다. 이는 하나님을 ‘몸이나 부분이 없으신 가장 순수한 영’으로 고백하는 웨스트민스터 신앙고백서(WCF II.1)와 하나님의 단순성(Simplicitas Dei) 교리에 정면으로 위배된다”고 지적했다.

이금석 교수는 “박진영의 강해에서 두드러지는 특징은 성경을 일종의 ‘논리적·수학적 계약서’로 접근한다는 점이다. 그는 하나님의 자기 계시(Self-revelation)이자 구속사적 언약 문서인 성경을 ‘수학적 공식과 법률적 조항으로 규격화된 채무 변제 계약서’로 환원한다”며 “그는 성경 텍스트를 인격적 삼위일체 하나님과 맺는 언약적 교제의 매개체로 대하기보다, 누구나 논리적 추론을 거치면 필연적으로 동일한 결론에 도달할 수밖에 없는 ‘닫힌 연역 체계’로 취급한다. 이러한 접근은 성경 저자의 역사적·문맥적·신학적 의도를 왜곡하고, 개별 구절들을 법조문처럼 탈문맥화해 기계적으로 조립하는 ‘성경 실증주의(Scriptural Positivism)’의 전형”이라고 했다.

이에 대해 “박진영이 규정하는 ‘믿음과 거듭남’은 역사적 개혁신학이 규정해 온 구원하는 믿음의 구조를 심각하게 훼손하고, 초대교회 영지주의(Gnosticism)적 지식주의와 18세기 스코틀랜드 신학자 로버트 샌더만(Robert Sandeman, 1718–1771)의 ‘샌더만주의(Sandemanianism)’인 ‘지적 동의 중심의 구원론’의 궤적을 따른다”며 “박진영의 강해에서 구원은 지식을 듣고, 그것이 논리적으로 타당함을 이성적으로 동의해 ‘아, 내 죄가 미래의 것까지 이미 다 갚아졌구나!’라는 사실을 깨닫는 찰나에 즉각 완성된다. 성령의 주권적 중생 사역이 배제되는 것”이라고 전했다.

이 교수는 “이로써 참된 회개는 실종되고, 죄에 대한 영적 자각과 슬픔, 자기를 부인하고 하나님께로 돌이키는 전인격적 회개가 사라진다”며 “그 결과 ‘구원받은 날짜와 시각을 지적으로 특정할 수 있다’는 식의 확신 지상주의로 치닫게 되고, 이는 역사적 구원파(권신찬·이요
articles.content_zh:
三位一体，决定救赎史成败的磐石，不是抽象的辩证法，也不是心理学模型，需要区分本体论和神经营理学的核心，通过立约神学和敬拜具体化，朴振英，形态论和诺斯替主义倾向

11月21日上午，韩国长老会神学学会（会长朴应圭教授）在京畿道龙仁市威斯敏斯特神学研究生大学的格雷斯厅举办了第42届学术研讨会，主题为“长老会的传统与作用”。随着JYP娱乐公司代表朴振英的言论等再次引发人们对“三位一体教义”的关注，在当天的神学学会上，由安明俊博士（韩国圣经大学）担任主席，本刊专栏作家李金锡教授（首尔国际大学院大学）以“从改革宗视角看正统三位一体论与世俗观点的比较”为题，就正统改革宗三位一体论发表了演讲。

李金锡教授表示：“正统改革宗三位一体论是基督教信仰的核心，它完整地保留了启示的神的超越性和内在于万物性、本质的统一性和位格的多样性。”他还指出：“当世俗哲学将其简化为抽象的辩证法或心理学模型，而像朴振英这样的主观主义解经者将其扭曲为一种功能性的救赎机制和理性的确信论时，基督教的神就可能失去其位格性，或沦为单纯的法律执行者。”

他还强调说：“三位一体的神不是为了解决人类的罪的问题而设计的‘机械装置’，而是呼召我们‘成为祂的儿女’，与祂在永恒的爱和荣耀的团契中的真神。”他还强调：“教会必须坚定地坚持正统三位一体论的丰富性，即由圣父的永恒旨意、圣子的完全救赎和圣灵的主权更新所组成的丰富性，并对变质的民粹主义神学运动展现出明确的圣经和教义辨别力。”

他具体指出：“在基督教神学的历史上，三位一体论（Trinitas）不仅是一个纯粹的思辨命题，更是决定教会身份、救恩论和崇拜基础的信仰最核心的基石（fundamentum fidei）。”他还表示：“改革宗神学主张上帝是‘在本体上是一位，在位格上是三位的永恒自存者’（《威斯敏斯特信条》II.3），并将三位一体教义视为决定救赎史成败的中心基石。”

李教授介绍说：“正统改革宗三位一体论的神学身份在于忠实地继承古代公教会正统（Catholic Orthodoxy）、克服基于圣经启示的思辨理性主义，以及实现上帝的单一主权与位格救赎工作和谐统一的‘圣经辩证三位一体论’。”他还表示：“理解改革宗三位一体论的关键区分在于本体论三位一体（Immanent·Ontological Trinity）与经纶三位一体（Economic Trinity）之间的关系。” 他说：“本体论三位一体指的是三位一体的神在时间之前的永恒中自己所拥有的本质关系和内在生命。

圣父、圣子、圣灵具有完全的平等性（aequalitas）和同一本质（homoousios）。”他还解释说：“经纶性三位一体论指的是三位一体的神在创造-护理-救赎这一历史时空里启示自己并施行祂的旨意的秩序。正统改革宗神学强烈支持这样一个古典命题：“上帝向外的作为是不可分割的（opera Trinitatis ad extra indivisa sunt）”。只是根据每个位格的独特关系，‘工作的特殊性（appropriatio）’会在经纶中显明出来。”

他还表示：“在改革宗神学中，三位一体教义尤其在‘救赎经纶的永恒根基（圣约神学）’和‘教会的公共敬拜与祷告结构（礼拜学）’中得到最清晰的体现。”“在改革宗圣约神学（Covenant Theology）中，人类的救赎并不是在堕落后的历史中临时应变而制定的即兴计划。救恩牢牢地植根于‘救恩契约（Pactum Salutis）’，这是三位一体的神在创世之前达成的永恒的内在协议。由于救恩的基础不是人类多变的情感或不完美的决定，而是基于三位一体的神永恒不变的立约性约定，因此圣徒的救恩获得了绝对的确定性和坚守的保证，这是绝不会被撤销的。”

他还表示：“改革宗礼仪学（Liturgics）和灵性并不是宣泄以人为中心的情感或获得心理安慰的途径，而是受邀进入三位一体神的永恒团契的圣礼性、团契性事件。真正的基督教礼拜和祷告具有彻底的自下而上、自上而下的三位一体结构。”他还表示：“没有圣灵帮助的礼拜很容易蜕变为狂热主义，没有基督中保的祷告很容易陷入骄傲的律法主义，不以父神的荣耀为目标的灵性很容易沦为自我满足的主观主义。因此，改革宗的崇拜是从其开头的‘三一颂赞和祷告’到最后的‘祝福’，都是以三一神的名为中心展开的神圣工作。”

对此，他分析道：“正统三位一体论解释了‘一个本质（una substantia）内的三个位格’的永恒内在关系和外在工作，并将本质的单一性和位格的实在性确立为相互内住的原则。”“另一方面，世俗的三位一体理解主要被黑格尔式的正-反-合辩证法原理、荣格的心理学原型和功能主义的模式论所扭曲。他分析道：“特别是朴振英对三位一体和救恩的理解与以理性认同为中心的‘一次得救’的逻辑相结合，暴露出了模式论和灵知主义的偏向，这种偏向要么削弱了圣灵的独立位格和圣化工作，要么将基督的工作简化为一种功能性机制。”

朴振英的神论和三位一体论的谬误
将圣经、救赎史以逻辑和数学的方式，当作契约来对待
将救赎史简化为偿还债务的契约
脱离语境、机械式的圣经实证主义
排斥圣灵的主权重生工作，削弱圣灵上帝的人格性工作

他特别指出：“朴振英神学最根本的神论谬误源于‘范畴混淆（Category Mistake）’，即将‘灵、魂、体’这一人类的三分法结构原封不动地套用在三位一体的神身上。”他还表示：“朴振英主张圣父和圣子各自拥有独立的‘魂’，从而表现出将圣父和圣子分开的‘三神论倾向’。也就是说，他将父与子分为两个具有不同本质的神性存在。

他指出：“这与《威斯敏斯特信仰告白》（WCF II.1）中将上帝称为‘没有身体或肢体的最纯粹的灵’的表述，以及上帝的单纯性（Simplicitas Dei）的教义是完全相悖的。” 李金锡教授指出：“朴振英的解经中一个突出的特点是将圣经视为一种‘逻辑与数学的契约’。他将圣经——神的自我启示和救赎史的约章——简化为‘以数学公式和法律条款规范的债务偿还契约’。”他还指出：“他并不将圣经文本视为与位格的三一神建立约章性关系的媒介，而是将其视为一个‘封闭的演绎系统’，即任何人只要经过逻辑推理，都必然会得出相同的结论。”

这种方法歪曲了圣经作者的历史、语境和神学意图，并将个别经文像法律条文一样脱离语境，机械地拼凑起来，是‘圣经实证主义（Scriptural Positivism）’的典型。”

articles.title_zh: 您的休息习惯揭示了您的内心
articles.content: “Hey, honey, you’re not going to be able to sleep tonight if you don’t start shutting things down soon!” After 36 years of marriage, my husband knows me well. He’s absolutely right, but I still sometimes want to keep pushing until bedtime. The way of wisdom is to stop consciously, set the work aside, and engage in the repetitive, mundane wind-down of the day. The work will still be there tomorrow, and I can trust God for new mercies to finish when morning comes (Lamentations 3:22–23). Our habits of rest reveal what we trust. While our need for sleep, recreation, and downtime weighs on our very physical, very finite bodies, we often resist submitting to our limitations. Substituting entertainment for true rest, we become passive consumers of endlessly streaming content that devours our time. Paradoxically, we crave rest and engage in ceaseless striving after things we hope will satisfy the desires of our heart. This is an ongoing battle for me, and I know I’m not alone. Our society values activity and busyness. We spend our hours and days going and doing, always with one eye on the clock. We reward tireless resilience with job promotions and earnest admiration. In our fervor for achievement, we may forget that rest is necessary for quality work to continue — and that rest can teach our hearts to trust God. Rest Reveals the Heart Psalm 127:1–2 is a reminder for our caffeinated and sleep-deprived souls that progress depends not solely on the work of our own hands but on God’s gracious provision: Unless the L ORD builds the house, those who build it labor in vain. Unless the L ORD watches over the city, the watchman stays awake in vain. It is in vain that you rise up early and go late to rest, eating the bread of anxious toil; for he gives to his beloved sleep. Note that the psalmist illustrates a right and a wrong way to work. He makes three important points for the restless. 1. The Lord builds the house. God builds the ministry, the family, and the career. We work in cooperation with the Lord, and he watches over us and our work. The point is not that we shouldn’t work heartily at whatever we do (Colossians 3:23). Rather, our security is found in God, not in our efforts. Knowing our frame, remembering that we are dust, God commands us to observe regular patterns of rest, not only for our physical health but also as an acknowledgment of our dependence upon him (Psalm 103:14). 2. The Lord watches over the city. Whether we’re closing our eyes or closing our laptop and office door at the end of the day, when we leave the results of our work in God’s hands, we demonstrate trust in him. “He who keeps Israel will neither slumber nor sleep,” the psalmist writes (Psalm 121:4). God is your keeper, too. Entrusting our work to the Lord prevents it from becoming an idol. In our glad contemplation of work well done, we remember that he is both giver and gift. Our work is evidence of his power and goodness. 3. The Lord gives sleep to his beloved. Anyone who has spent a night sleepless from worry knows our bodies are not designed to run on anxious adrenaline. Insomnia has many causes and may not indicate a spiritual problem, but God often uses physical symptoms to reveal our spiritual condition. A steady diet of “the bread of anxious toil” (Psalm 127:2) starves us of what we need most: the ability to rest in God. When we rest, we accept our God-given limits. We hand the controls over to him. We lay aside our disordered loves, and we choose to believe the Father’s delight in Christ is also for us, his treasured children: “This is my beloved Son, with whom I am well pleased” (Matthew 3:17). Because it can feel entirely unnatural, we may need to approach rest as a learned behavior, a habit of holiness, a spiritual discipline that we “put on” in the same way Paul exhorted the Colossians to clothe themselves with compassion, kindness, humility, gentleness, and patience (Colossians 3:12). Such discipline is worth the effort; when we rest, we proclaim

“嘿,亲爱的,你今晚不能睡觉了, 经过36年的婚姻,我丈夫很了解我. 他说得对, 但我还是想继续推到睡觉。 智慧之道在于自觉停止,把工作搁置一边,从事日常的反复,无常的风化.

工作明天仍然会到来,我可以相信上帝会在早晨完成新的慈悲(3:22-23号纪念日)。 我们的休息习惯揭示了我们所信任的东西。 虽然我们对睡眠、娱乐和休息时间的需求影响着我们身体,非常有限的身体,但我们常常不愿屈从于我们的局限性。

以娱乐来代替真正的休息, 我们成为被动的消费者 无限流畅的内容 吞噬我们的时间。 矛盾的是,我们渴望休息,在我们希望能够满足我们内心愿望的事情之后,进行不懈的努力。 这是一场持续的斗争, 我们的社会重视活动和繁忙。

我们花我们的时间和时间去和做, 总是一眼钟。 我们以工作晋升和真诚的钦佩来奖励不懈的韧性。 在我们追求成就的热情中,我们可能忘记,为了继续开展高质量的工作,休息是必要的——休息可以教导我们相信上帝。

安息吧 127:1–2 提醒我们吃咖啡和失眠的灵魂 进步不仅取决于我们自己的工作 也取决于上帝的恩赐: 除非LORD建造房子,否则建造房子的人会白费力气。 除非LORD监视整个城市,否则守望者会白白地保持清醒.

你早起,晚去休息,吃急劳的面包,那是徒劳的。他使他所爱的睡眠。 请注意,诗人表明了一种正确和错误的工作方式。 他为不安的人提出了三个重要点. 1. 主建房屋。 神造部,家人,事业.

我们与上帝合作,他监视着我们和我们的工作。 关键不是我们不应该在做任何事情时勤奋工作(3:23)。 相反,我们的安全在于上帝,而不是我们的努力。

上帝知道我们的框架,记得我们是尘土,命令我们观察正常的休息模式,这不仅是为了我们的身体健康,也是为了承认我们对他的依赖(第103:14段)。 2. 主观城.

无论是闭眼还是关闭手提电脑和办公门, " 保住以色列的人既不睡也不睡, " 诗人写道(第121:4段)。 上帝也是你的守护者 将我们的工作托付给主,防止它成为偶像.

在我们愉快地看待出色的工作时,我们记得,他既是馈赠者,也是天赋。 我们的工作证明了他的力量和善良。 3,主让他的爱人睡觉. 任何因忧愁而睡不着夜的人都知道 我们的身体不是想靠焦虑的肾上腺素运行的

失眠有很多原因,可能没有表明精神问题,但上帝经常使用身体症状来揭示我们的精神状况. 稳定的“焦急劳累的面包”(第127:2段)使我们无法满足我们最需要的:在上帝中安息的能力。 当我们休息时,我们接受上帝赐予我们的限制。 我们把控制权交给他

我们抛下我们无序的爱,我们选择相信父亲对基督的喜悦也是对我们,他珍贵的孩子们:“这是我所爱的儿子,我很高兴与他们在一起”(Matthew 3:17)。

由于它会感到完全不自然,我们可能需要将休息视为一种有学问的行为,一种圣洁的习惯,一种我们以同样方式“寄托”的精神纪律,保罗劝说科洛斯人以慈悲、善良、谦逊、温柔和耐心为己任(科洛斯人3:12)。 这种纪律值得我们努力;当我们休息时,我们宣布

articles.title_zh: 墨西哥主教们在基督徒抵抗运动发起一百周年之际发表的牧函——Infovaticana博客
articles.content: A cien años del inicio de la resistencia cristera, los obispos mexicanos proponen leer aquel doloroso episodio histórico desde la verdad, la libertad de conciencia, la reconciliación y el compromiso de una fe dispuesta a hacerse servicio A cien años del inicio de la resistencia cristera, los obispos de México han dirigido al país una carta pastoral que busca recuperar uno de los episodios más dolorosos, complejos y controvertidos de la historia nacional sin convertirlo en instrumento de revancha, polarización o legitimación de la violencia. Bajo el título ¡Viva Cristo Rey! Su fe, nuestra memoria; su testimonio, nuestra misión, el documento propone una lectura histórica, teológica, espiritual, jurídica y pastoral de aquellos acontecimientos, pero, sobre todo, formula una pregunta dirigida a los creyentes de nuestro tiempo: ¿Qué significa hoy mantener viva una fe por la que otros estuvieron dispuestos a entregar la existencia? La carta no celebra la guerra ni presenta la resistencia armada como modelo de acción cristiana para el presente. Su punto de partida es otro, recordar la fidelidad de un pueblo que, en medio de la persecución, continuó rezando en sus hogares, bautizando a sus hijos, protegiendo a sus sacerdotes, celebrando clandestinamente los sacramentos y defendiendo la libertad de conciencia frente a un Estado que pretendió administrar las convicciones religiosas como si fueran una concesión del poder. Los obispos establecen desde el comienzo una diferencia indispensable entre el conflicto bélico, con sus errores, excesos, responsabilidades y heridas, y el testimonio de quienes murieron sin renunciar a su fe. Los mártires, subraya el documento, no son recordados porque hubieran matado por Cristo, sino porque murieron por Él y, en numerosos casos, perdonaron a sus verdugos. No se trata de recuperar un grito de guerra, sino la fuerza espiritual de una conciencia que se negó a ser sometida. El episcopado propone un triple ejercicio de memoria histórica, valoración del martirio y compromiso cristiano con la vida, la dignidad humana y la paz. Al recorrer la carta aparece una convicción transversal, la memoria solo es auténticamente cristiana cuando conduce a la conversión, ayuda a sanar las heridas, impide la repetición de las injusticias y se transforma en misión. Ese propósito exige comenzar por “un breve recuento del conflicto religioso”, título del primer capítulo y punto de entrada para entender que la confrontación no surgió repentinamente en 1926. Sus antecedentes se remontan a la formación del Estado mexicano después de la Independencia, cuando comenzaron a enfrentarse dos proyectos de nación. Uno reconocía al catolicismo como fundamento del orden social; el otro pretendía limitar la influencia institucional de la Iglesia para consolidar un Estado liberal, soberano y progresivamente secular. La Constitución de 1857 y las Leyes de Reforma representaron un momento decisivo en ese proceso. Establecieron la separación entre la Iglesia y el Estado, limitaron la propiedad eclesiástica y modificaron la presencia de la institución religiosa en la educación y la vida civil. Para sus promotores fueron disposiciones indispensables para modernizar al país; para la Iglesia y numerosos católicos significaron una intervención hostil sobre espacios que consideraban esenciales para su identidad y misión. La carta reconoce, sin embargo, que la secularización no ocurrió de manera inmediata ni eliminó el profundo arraigo del catolicismo en la vida nacional. La fe continuó presente en las costumbres, las familias, la educación, las fiestas y las formas comunitarias de organización. En ese contexto cobró fuerza el catolicismo social, inspirado en buena medida por la encíclica Rerum novarum de 1891. Surgieron organizaciones obreras, asociaciones juveniles y femeninas, cajas de ahorro para campesinos, escuelas nocturnas, centros de ayuda mutua, medios de comunicación y proyectos de participación política. Los católicos no se limitaron a re

articles.title: RED WEEK PER RICORDARE I CRISTIANI PERSEGUITATI
articles.summary: Anche quest’anno, nonostante il disinteresse dei media, dal 15 al 22 novembre la Fondazione Pontificia Aiuto alla Chiesa che Soffre ha dato vita al Red Week per ricordare che in tutto il mondo milioni
articles.summary_zh: 今年，尽管媒体不感兴趣，但教宗基金会“援助受苦教会”仍于11月15日至22日举办了“红色周”活动，以提醒人们在全球范围内有数百万
articles.title_zh: 红色周，纪念受迫害的基督徒
articles.content: Anche quest’anno, nonostante il disinteresse dei media, dal 15 al 22 novembre la Fondazione Pontificia Aiuto alla Chiesa che Soffre ha dato vita al Red Week per ricordare che in tutto il mondo milioni di persone sono discriminate o perseguitate per la loro fede, in particolare le tante comunità cristiane che vivono in contesti dove la loro libertà religiosa subisce gravi violazioni. Per farlo, luoghi di culto, monumenti ed edifici pubblici in questa settimana si sono illuminate di rosso in tante nazioni contemporaneamente in occasione della Red Week, Dal 2015, sono stati illuminati luoghi di culto e monumenti fra i più iconici del mondo: dalla Fontana di Trevi a Roma al monumento del Cristo Redentore di Rio de Janeiro, dalla Basilica della Sagrada Familia di Barcellona a quella del Sacro Cuore di Parigi. La libertà religiosa in pericolo. Il Rapporto sulla libertà religiosa nel mondo 2025 di Aiuto alla Chiesa che Soffre evidenzia come in 62 Paesi si siano verificate violazioni sistematiche della libertà religiosa: 24 Paesi rientrano nella categoria più grave, ovvero quella di “persecuzione”, e 38 in quella di “discriminazione”. Complessivamente, oltre 5,4 miliardi di persone vivono in contesti in cui la libertà di religione è seriamente compromessa. 413 milioni di cristiani vivono in Paesi in cui la libertà religiosa è gravemente violata; di questi, circa 220 milioni risiedono in nazioni in cui sono direttamente esposti a persecuzioni. Regimi autoritari, violenza jihadista, nazionalismi religiosi e criminalità organizzata rappresentano oggi le principali minacce. Voci dimenticate: due serate tra musica e testimonianza a Milano e Roma Tra gli appuntamenti centrali della Red Week 2026 si sono svolte due serate di Voci dimenticate, il 16 novembre a Milano nella Basilica di Santa Maria delle Grazie, e il 21 novembre a Roma nella Basilica di San Saba. Chi lo desidera potrà contribuire, con una donazione libera, ai progetti di Aiuto alla Chiesa che Soffre a beneficio dei cristiani perseguitati. A Milano il pubblico ha assistito al concerto del Coro Filarmonico G.B. Pergolesi e dell’Orchestra Filarmonica Amadeus, diretti dal Maestro Gianmario Cavallaro; in programma brani del repertorio barocco, con musiche di Vivaldi, Torelli e Händel. Nella capitale il Coro Città di Roma, diretto dal Maestro Mauro Marchetti, ha proposto invece un percorso musicale con musiche di Mozart, Bach e Pergolesi. Ospite di entrambi gli appuntamenti è stata una donna che ha vissuto personalmente il dramma della persecuzione. La giovane sarà accompagnata da Don Joseph Fidelis Bature, sacerdote della diocesi nigeriana di Maiduguri e direttore del Trauma Center. La struttura, sostenuta dai benefattori di ACS, offre assistenza psicologica, spirituale e sociale alle vittime del gruppo terroristico islamista Boko Haram, accompagnandole in un percorso di guarigione e reinserimento nella comunità. Le loro toccanti testimonianze hanno raccontato la violenza che continua a colpire migliaia di persone e le occasioni di rinascita rese possibili dalla solidarietà di numerosi benefattori, italiani e internazionali. Le donazioni raccolte durante i due eventi di Milano e Roma sosterranno in particolare un progetto finanziato da ACS nella diocesi nigeriana di Minna, nel cui territorio le comunità cristiane vivono sotto la minaccia di attacchi armati, sequestri e violenze. L’iniziativa aiuterà 200 donne, uomini e bambini sopravvissuti alla violenza a ricostruire la propria vita attraverso il sostegno psicologico, il rafforzamento dei legami con la comunità e, per gli adulti, il recupero dell’autonomia economica. Il progetto prevede inoltre la formazione di circa 60 figure di riferimento delle comunità locali, tra cui sacerdoti e autorità, affinché sappiano riconoscere i bisogni delle persone più vulnerabili e offrire loro un sostegno adeguato. articles.title: México abre un año de memoria y reconciliación a cien años de la Cristiada – Infovaticana Blogs
articles.summary: Con un emblema concebido como relicario de la memoria y con convocatorias que comienzan a traducirse en disposiciones concretas dentro de las diócesis, la Iglesia católica en México abre este domingo
articles.content: Con un emblema concebido como relicario de la memoria y con convocatorias que comienzan a traducirse en disposiciones concretas dentro de las diócesis, la Iglesia católica en México abre este domingo 22 de noviembre el Año Jubilar por el centenario del inicio de la resistencia cristera. La celebración comenzará en la solemnidad de Jesucristo, Rey del Universo, y se prolongará hasta el 21 de noviembre de 2027. El Jubileo lleva como lema “Su fe, nuestra memoria y su testimonio, nuestra misión”. Su propósito no consiste únicamente en recordar los acontecimientos que sacudieron la vida religiosa del país entre 1926 y 1929, sino en recuperar el testimonio de los mártires, promover la reconciliación y reafirmar la libertad religiosa como un derecho de toda persona. La presentación del emblema oficial, presidido por la proclamación “¡Viva Cristo Rey!”, ofrece una síntesis visual de esa finalidad. El diseño adopta la forma de un medallón o relicario en cuyo interior aparecen la Iglesia y el pueblo congregados bajo Cristo Rey. La Virgen de Guadalupe, la Eucaristía radiante, las coronas real y de espinas, así como las figuras del clero, la vida consagrada, los jóvenes y los fieles laicos, articulan una composición construida alrededor de tres conceptos: fe, memoria y testimonio. El color guinda remite a la sangre derramada por los mártires y las estrellas evocan el manto de la Virgen de Guadalupe. El emblema, por tanto, no constituye solamente la identificación gráfica de una efeméride, pretende expresar la continuidad histórica de una experiencia religiosa y transmitirla a las generaciones que conocen la cristiada como un episodio cada vez más distante. El Año Jubilar fue anunciado el 9 de noviembre durante la misa de apertura de la CXXI Asamblea Plenaria de la Conferencia del Episcopado Mexicano, celebrada en la Basílica de Guadalupe. En ese contexto, el obispo de Cuernavaca y presidente de la CEM, Ramón Castro, subrayó que recordar la persecución religiosa no significa reabrir heridas, alimentar resentimientos ni señalar enemigos. La memoria cristiana de la resistencia cristera, explicó el Episcopado, debe conducir al reconocimiento del sufrimiento, la reconciliación y la construcción de la paz. Esta precisión resulta indispensable para evitar que el centenario sea utilizado como exaltación de la violencia o como argumento para trasladar al presente las confrontaciones políticas y religiosas del pasado. El Jubileo cuenta con un decreto de la Penitenciaría Apostólica, fechado el 6 de noviembre de 2026, mediante el cual se concede indulgencia plenaria a los fieles que cumplan las condiciones establecidas por la Iglesia y peregrinen a los santuarios dedicados a los mártires mexicanos o a los templos jubilares designados por los obispos. La Conferencia del Episcopado Mexicano pidió que el decreto sea proclamado en las Iglesias particulares este 22 de noviembre y que cada diócesis disponga los lugares, celebraciones y actividades pastorales correspondientes. La apertura nacional comienza así a adquirir características propias en las comunidades diocesanas. Entre las convocatorias más amplias se encuentra la del arzobispo de Guadalajara, cardenal José Francisco Robles Ortega. El prelado convocó a toda la Iglesia que peregrina en esa arquidiócesis a celebrar el Jubileo del centenario del inicio de la resistencia cristera. El documento señala que la solemnidad de Cristo Rey de este año coincide con la celebración de los beatos mártires mexicanos, el Día del Laico y la Jornada Mundial de la Juventud. Sin embargo, sostiene que la fecha adquiere una profundidad particular por cumplirse cien años del comienzo de la resistencia. La arquidiócesis de Guadalajara propone vivir el Jubileo como una experiencia de comunión eclesial, memoria agradecida y renovación de la fe. La convocatoria recuerda a quienes permanecieron fieles a Jesucristo y a la Iglesia hasta entregar su vida y reafirma el derecho del pueblo a celebrar, transmitir y vivir su fe tant

articles.title_zh: 基督徒运动与禧年 – Infovaticana博客
articles.content: Este 22 de noviembre, solemnidad de Cristo Rey, el Episcopado Mexicano da a conocer su Carta Pastoral con motivo del centenario del inicio de la resistencia cristera y del Año Jubilar concedido por el Papa León XIV. Tras un prolongado silencio en materia de pastorales colectivas, donde han predominado mensajes y la pastoral de los comunicados y declaraciones puntuales, el documento recupera el valor de una instrucción eclesial capaz de orientar una reflexión profunda, más allá del mero posicionamiento coyuntural. La carta no pretende soliviantar ánimos ni azuzar conciencias contemporáneas. Como subrayan los obispos desde el preámbulo, no se celebra el conflicto bélico ni se buscan venganzas. Se recuerda la fidelidad de un pueblo que, en medio del miedo, siguió rezando en las casas, bautizando a escondidas y protegiendo a sus sacerdotes; el testimonio de los mártires que no mataron por Cristo, sino que murieron por Él perdonando a sus verdugos y la lección de que la libertad religiosa no es privilegio clerical, sino derecho de toda persona, cuya negación termina costando sangre. Se trata de recuperar y actualizar la memoria desde el ámbito de la fe y de la pastoral, precisamente en un México que vive una convulsión que se nos ha vendido como “transformación”. Esa actualización resulta especialmente urgente cuando se lee el capítulo V, particularmente el apartado “Del fratricidio a la construcción de la paz: una Iglesia reconciliadora”. Los obispos reconocen con claridad que la persecución religiosa fue real y que la guerra enfrentó a mexicanos contra mexicanos. Por ello, advierten que no es posible reducir la memoria a una historia simplista de buenos contra malos. Exigen reconocer causas, responsabilidades, sufrimientos, errores y excesos, sin renunciar a la verdad, pero sin convertirla en pretexto para el odio o la confrontación. Una Iglesia que guarda la memoria de sus mártires está llamada a ser reconciliadora. Y esa responsabilidad, afirman, resulta especialmente urgente hoy, en un país herido por la violencia, la inseguridad, la desconfianza y el debilitamiento de los vínculos comunitarios. México padece un fratricidio cotidiano que no se agota sólo en la violencia. Se expresa en la polarización política que convierte al adversario en enemigo absoluto, en la erosión del tejido social por el crimen organizado y la impunidad, en la pobreza que deshumaniza, en la corrupción que mina la confianza institucional y en la fragmentación de las familias. La “transformación” oficial ha prometido paz y justicia; sin embargo, la realidad entrega, en demasiados territorios, miedo y abandono. Frente a ello, la carta no propone venganza armada ni revancha confesional. Propone la reconstrucción del tejido social, la justicia, la fraternidad y la paz como aprendizajes del presente. Esa orientación se refuerza en los compromisos éticos, comunitarios y eclesiales del mismo capítulo, defender la libertad religiosa y de conciencia sin reclamar soberanía absoluta sobre la persona, rechazar el recurso a la violencia como medio de reivindicación, fortalecer redes de apoyo y participación cívica desde una ética cristiana, visibilizar el papel de mujeres y jóvenes en la construcción de la paz e impulsar una formación histórica que evite la manipulación ideológica del pasado. La memoria martirial solo es fecunda cuando se convierte en examen de conciencia y en compromiso renovado por la vida, no en polarización. Cristo es Rey. México debe reconocer el profundo arraigo de esas raíces en su historia y en su presente, no para imponer una confesión de Estado, sino para afirmar que la dignidad de la persona, la libertad de conciencia y la construcción de la paz no son concesiones revocables del poder, sino exigencias de una tradición que, a precio de sangre, defendió que ningún poder humano es absoluto. En un país convulso que se nos presenta como transformado, esa memoria actualizada puede ser, si se vive con verdad y caridad, semilla de reconciliación

articles.title_zh: 一位爱上耶稣的年轻女王
articles.content: Continua il mio studio sui Santi piemontesi, da alcuni definiti “Santi sociali”, da altri “Santi della carità”. Ho appena finito di leggere l’ottima biografia del giornalista Luciano Regolo, “Maria Cristina di Savoia. La regina innamorata di Gesù”, Kogoi edizioni (2014; pagine 526). Apprendo dalla rete che Regolo ha pubblicato una nuova edizione aggiornata con le Edizioni Ares di Milano nel 2025. Maria Cristina, è una figura particolare che meriterebbe molta attenzione non solo nella Chiesa, ma anche nella società civile, nelle cosiddette istituzioni. Una figura straordinaria, unica, che potrebbe ispirare registi, attori per realizzare film per la televisione o per il cinema. La Storia ufficiale, quella che viene proposta nelle nostre scuole o la ignora totalmente, oppure viene considerata come una donna “bigotta”, per via della sua troppa insistenza nelle cose religiose. Ma studiandola bene come ha fatto Regolo ed altri studiosi, è qualcos’altro, nei soli tre anni di vita da regina delle Due Sicilie è riuscita a fare cose straordinarie che riguardano soprattutto l’elevazione sociale delle donne napoletane. E in quel periodo storico non era facile, non solo nel regno di Napoli. Beatificata nel 2014 nella Basilica di Santa Chiara a Napoli, Maria Cristina rappresenta ancora oggi un modello di santità vissuta nel mondo, capace di coniugare responsabilità pubbliche, vita familiare e profonda fede cristiana. Il libro di Luciano Regolo ricostruisce la vicenda umana e spirituale della sovrana, inserendola nel contesto storico dell’Europa del XIX secolo e mostrando come la sua eredità morale continui a parlare agli uomini e alle donne del nostro tempo. Una sovrana amata dal popolo, una donna di profonda spiritualità e una madre che visse la regalità come servizio. A quasi due secoli dalla sua morte, la figura di Maria Cristina di Savoia continua a suscitare interesse e ammirazione, tanto da essere ricordata ancora oggi come la “Reginella Santa”. Il libro di Regolo si compone di tredici corposi capitoli, corredato da alcune foto a colori. Ho letto altri testi sulla giovane regina di Casa Savoia, questo di Regolo mi sembra abbastanza completo soprattutto per quanto riguarda i diversi aneddoti proposti. Nata a Cagliari il 14 novembre 1812, da Vittorio Emanuele I e da Maria Teresa d’Asburgo d’Este. Maria Cristina è stata amata e addirittura venerata dall’Italia meridionale, condensando in sé tutti i connotati italiani: «innanzitutto il Credo cattolico; un’ampia cultura umanistica e scientifica; l’amore per l’arte e le cose belle; una femminilità dolce e forte: cioè mite, ma risoluta; inoltre, onestà di vita; fedeltà nelle relazioni con le persone; uso della sana prudenza, che permette di non cadere nelle trappole e nei pettegolezzi». Sposò il 21 novembre 1832 Ferdinando II di Borbone re delle Due Sicilie. Nonostante la breve esistenza – morì a soli ventitré anni il 31 gennaio del 1836, pochi giorni dopo aver dato alla luce il futuro Francesco II – lasciò un’impronta profonda nella storia religiosa e sociale del suo tempo. La figura di Maria Cristina di Savoia occupa un posto particolare nella storia della santità laicale. Cresciuta in un ambiente profondamente cristiano, interpretò il proprio ruolo di regina come una missione al servizio dei poveri, dei malati e delle persone più fragili. “Non è una novità che un sovrano possa essere elevato alla gloria degli altari – scrive Padre Gianni Califano, postulatore – La lunga storia della santità è costellata di esempi di questo tipo, basti pensare a san Luigi dei Francesi, a santa Elisabetta del Portogallo o, in epoca più recente, all’ultimo imperatore d’Austria, Carlo I d’Asburgo […]”. Tuttavia, questi esempi ci dicono che la santità o la beatitudine non conoscono confini di classe e ruolo sociale. Numerose testimonianze raccontano di Maria Cristina della sua attenzione verso gli ultimi, della sua intensa vita di preghiera e della sua capacità di influenzare positivamente la corte napoletana

articles.title_zh: 你就不能帮我吗?
articles.content: Several times now, I have been out in creation with unbelievers, speaking to them of eternal matters, and, passing by a dying branch at the base of a tree, I have picked it up and said, “This is your life apart from Christ.” Speaking about their souls, Jesus’s illustration is irresistible. The conversation goes something like this: Jesus gives us this illustration. He looks you in the eye and says that he is the tree (to augment the illustration slightly), and you are the branch. Look up and see the branches above us, beautiful leaves waving, healthy in their vibrant greens, bearing evidence of life. And then there is this branch. Dry. Leafless. Withered. Why? Because it is detached from the source of its life. Cut off from the one it was made to have communion with. And so, it lies here, detached from its purpose and severed from the only thing that can make it flourish. Jesus claims to be man’s source. He claims to be the Tree to whom you belong. In relationship with him, you have life. Apart from him, he teaches, you spend life withering. I usually pause to let the claim have its proper space. I ask what they think of such an assertion. I give them an opportunity to respond. I have often expected indifference or offense, but I have consistently been met with quiet consideration or outright acknowledgment that such an illustration made sense to them. Or at least they would like to hear more. So I go on to wonder aloud with them. What is it like to be a branch fallen from the tree that is, as Jesus says, withering ? Don’t you know? Need we ask? The restlessness, the fatal dryness, the looming death. The reaching out to anything and everything for life — except for the tree standing beside and over us. Him we do not want. Him we can do without. We can make it our own way. The adverb is different, but the end is the same — restless withering, drunken withering, religious, secular, or thoughtless withering . Some overdose on pleasure. Others get high on their own morality. Still others distract themselves from death’s shadow creeping over them with fantasy football and rounds of golf. But for all that, withering. But Jesus himself asserts that he is the Tree. He is the one we were made for; in him alone can we find the life that haunts us in still and sober moments. Be grafted to him through repentance and faith, be attached to him by the Spirit of the living God, have his words live in you, direct you, amaze you, and dead things will come to life. And what will it be on that day, I am compelled to continue, for those dry and fruitless branches who refused life in him? They will be gathered and thrown into the fire and burned as useless things. But Jesus came that you might have otherwise. He told us his mission was to bring life — life abundantly . Imagine the branch grafted to the tree, suddenly infused with life and purpose and the vital sap of God’s own Spirit. We are as branches; the Father, Son, and Spirit are the source of everlasting life. With him, we flourish though all may seem to go poorly. Without him, only sapped wood remains. Would you like to know more about this Jesus? Now, I tell you this to highlight one of many places where the Bible addresses the interiority of man and its solution: God. I want you to see how dangerous the alternative answers found in modern therapeutic culture are to our souls and our churches. It is a scourge, especially to this inward age, not because a therapeutic culture takes distresses of the heart seriously, but because it too often sends branches reaching out for anything but the Tree. Ingrown Toenails The problem comes not from a focus on the inner man. Anyone who says the Bible has little to say about internal battles, demons, depressions, anxieties, doubts, and the despairs of human life should not air his ignorance. The Scriptures abound with stories of the faithful brought into all the perplexities and pains of life in a fallen world. The Psalms, as one profound example, give u

articles.title_zh: 我们对耶稣的眼泪有什么误解
articles.content: Audio Transcript “Jesus wept” (John 11:35). It’s the shortest verse in the Bible. We read it together in the Navigators Bible Reading Plan yesterday. But it’s so brief we can pass it too quickly. Maybe we pass over it because we think we know what it means. Jesus’s friend Lazarus died. Jesus wept because his friend was gone. But what if we got that wrong? Or, what if we mistakenly thought his emotions were simple when they were complex? What if Jesus wept not simply in the loss of death but from a frustration with the living? Today on Ask Pastor John: what we get wrong about the tears of Jesus. Henry, a listener, writes in with a timely question on John 11:35. “Pastor John, thank you for taking my question today. I’d like to ask you about John 11:35. Why do you think Jesus wept at the tomb of Lazarus? One way to read this account is that he’s simply sharing in Mary and Martha’s sorrows over his death. But I wonder if something deeper is going on here. Jesus already planned to raise Lazarus, and he even told his disciples he was going to do it in John 11:11–15. “So, my questions are these two: First, why does Jesus ask, ‘Where have you laid him?’ Was he simply asking to be taken to the tomb? When they answer, ‘Lord, come and see,’ it’s almost like they still don’t appreciate who he is as the Messiah. And that is my second question: This whole event leaves me wondering if this weeping is more like Jesus’s weeping over Jerusalem in Luke 19:41 — weeping because he is heartbroken over the city’s unbelief. Is it a stretch to connect these two moments? Is Jesus grieving the dead Lazarus? Or is he grieving the unbelief of the living?” Jesus’s Mingled Emotions I doubt that any of Jesus’s emotions were simple. I think they were always complex. We finite creatures have emotions that respond to one or two, maybe three, happy or painful aspects of a situation. So, we may feel sorrow and joy mingled because, say, a very old saint has just gone to be with the Lord, and we will miss him, and yet we’re so happy for him. But Jesus could see every angle, every imaginable aspect of a situation, some of which called for very different emotions. So, I doubt that he ever had a simple emotion. For example, in Mark 3:1–5, there’s this man with a withered hand in the synagogue, and the people are watching to see if Jesus would heal him so that they could accuse Jesus. Can you imagine? They don’t give a hoot about this man’s pain. All they want is to accuse Jesus if he heals him. And in verse 5, it says, “He looked around at them with anger, grieved at their hardness of heart.” And that’s what I mean by complex emotions: anger and grief perfectly mingled in the sinless heart of Jesus. Another example would be that he looked on unbelieving Jerusalem and wept: “Would that you, even you, had known on this day the things that make for peace! But now they are hidden from your eyes” (Luke 19:42). But in Luke 10:21, it says Jesus “rejoiced in the Holy Spirit and said, ‘I thank you, Father, Lord of heaven and earth, that you have hidden these things from the wise and understanding and revealed them to little children; yes, Father, for such was your gracious will.’” He could weep and rejoice over the wise and bitter providence of God. So, we come to John 11 and the death of Lazarus. And I think Henry, who’s sending us this question, is right when he says Jesus’s tears in John 11 aren’t just about sharing our human grief — that maybe he is genuinely mourning their spiritual blindness. Yes, and I’m going to say not just mourning — he’s indignant. Divine Love and Wisdom The story begins in John 11:1–6 with Mary and Martha sending words to Jesus that their brother Lazarus is very sick. Jesus waits two more days before going and intentionally lets Lazarus die. He says in John 11:14–15, “Lazarus has died, and for your sake I am glad that I was not there, so that you may believe.” That’s an amazing statement: “I let him die for the sake of your faith.” “They needed to

articles.title: Who or What? A Continuum for Using AI Wisely
articles.summary: From AI as god to AI as assistant. Here is a continuum of nine roles that can help Christians tell legitimate uses of AI from illegitimate ones, and wise from unwise. See Also A Christian’s Guide to AI Technology is Fast, Sanctification Is Slow, and Claude Can’t Do It For You A La Carte (October 16)
articles.summary_zh: 从AI为神到AI为助手。这里有九个角色的连续体，可以帮助基督徒区分人工智能的合法使用和非法使用，以及明智和不明智的使用。另请参阅基督徒的人工智能指南：人工智能技术快，成圣慢，克劳德无法为你点菜（10 月 16 日）
articles.title_zh: 谁或什么？明智使用人工智能的连续体
articles.content: It is sometimes hard to believe that it has been only four years since AI became widely available. Few technologies have made so massive and rapid a leap into our daily lives, to the extent that AI now exists in the background of all of our lives and, for many of us, in the foreground as well. Few technologies have evolved as quickly, so that the latest ChatGPT model bears about as much resemblance to its debut as the latest MacBook does to a Commodore 64. If all this has happened in just four years, imagine what the next four—or the next fourteen—might hold. As AI’s capabilities have increased, so too have the ways we can use it in our homes, churches, and workplaces. It seems like every month or two we read of a feature that can make a difference to our lives by adding a new ability or taking on work that used to be done by a person. The latest trend is the rise of agents—AI tools like Meta’s Muse or xAI’s Grok Bot that can carry out tasks, routines, and duties on an ongoing basis. With all of the tools available to us and all of their capabilities, it can be difficult to know which uses are legitimate and which are not. We all know that just because AI can do a task doesn’t mean that it should . So how can we determine the legitimate roles AI can play in our lives? I think sketching out a continuum of some of AI’s potential roles can help us. At the beginning are roles that most of us would agree are illegitimate, and at the end roles that most of us would agree are legitimate. Between them are roles that may be illegitimate in some cases and perfectly fine in others. These demand that we approach them thoughtfully to determine whether integrating them into our lives would be an act of wisdom or folly. As you will see, illegitimate roles tend to be those that require a who whereas legitimate roles tend to be those that require a mere what . The Continuum AI as God . There are some people, most of them deeply engaged in the tech industry, who ascribe to AI god-like qualities and who relate to it accordingly. They may believe it is an evil god that is likely to destroy humanity or a benevolent god that is likely to redeem humanity, but in either case, they treat AI as something far more than software. These people go too far and commit idolatry as they attribute to tech what rightly belongs to God. AI as Friend . There are some people who relate to AI as a friend, and even a few troubled people who relate to it as a lover. While AI is capable of mimicking the kind of relationship one might enjoy with a fellow human being, it can only ever mimic it. To relate to AI as a friend is to anthropomorphize a mere technology and worse, to deprive oneself of actual friendship. Though AI can imitate friendship, it cannot be a friend in any legitimate sense of the word, for friendship depends upon personhood. Not only that, but friendship depends upon mutuality and both the blessings and risks that come with relationship. You cannot be friends with AI any more than you can be friends with a tree, a PlayStation, or any other non-being. AI as Counselor . Many people today relate to AI as a counselor—a confidant who will listen patiently and counsel them with a trusted voice. Yet because AI is a what , not a who , it cannot offer answers based on a true understanding of their circumstances, true wisdom that comes from learning and experience, or true compassion that comes from sharing their humanity. It cannot empathize with them, pray for them, or plead with the Holy Spirit for wisdom in helping them. AI is capable of advising in many ways, but not of counseling, for counseling is inherently personal. AI as Pastor . Increasingly, people bring to AI the matters of spiritual health, growth, and well-being that in the past would have been addressed to a pastor. Every Christian needs to be under the loving oversight of a pastor who will care for their soul, and such crucial matters must be entrusted not to AI, but to a pastor who is called and
articles.content_zh:
有时很难相信,自AI广泛提供至今才四年。 很少有技术使我们的日常生活如此巨大和迅速地跃入,以至于AI现在存在于我们所有生活的背景中,对我们许多人来说,也存在于前景中。

很少有技术发展得这么快,因此最新的ChatGPT模型与其首发版的相近程度与最新的MacBook对准将64的相近程度相同. 如果这一切在短短的四年内就发生了,想象下四年,或下十四年可能发生的情况。 随着AI能力的增强,我们在家里、教堂和工作场所使用它的方式也一样。

我们似乎每个月或两个月都读到一个特点,通过增加新的能力或从事过去由一个人完成的工作,可以改变我们的生活。 最近的趋势是,诸如Meta的Muse或xAI的Grok Bot等能够持续执行任务、例行公事和职责的代理-AI工具的兴起。

有了我们可以利用的所有工具及其所有能力,就很难知道哪些用途是合法的,哪些用途不是。 我们都知道, 我们如何确定AI在生活中可以扮演的合法角色? 我认为勾画出AI的一些潜在角色可以帮助我们。

开始时,我们大多数人都认为这种角色是非法的,最后,我们大多数人都认为这种角色是合法的。 两者之间是在某些情况下可能是非法的,而在另一些情况下则完全正确。 这些要求我们深思熟虑地对待他们,以确定将他们融入我们的生活是明智还是愚蠢。

你会看到,非法角色往往是那些需要谁的角色,而合法角色往往是那些只需要什么的角色。 连续AI作为上帝。 有一些人,其中大多数人深入从事技术产业,他们把AI的神性描述为"类似"的特质,并与之相应相通.

他们可能相信是邪恶的神有可能毁灭人性或者仁慈的神有可能赎回人性,但无论在哪种情况下,他们都把AI视为远远超出软件的东西. 这些人太过分了 以偶像为神 因为他们把属于上帝的东西归为技术 作为朋友的AI.

有些人以朋友身份与AI有关,甚至有少数人以恋人身份与之有关系. 虽然AI能够模仿人们可能享受的那种与人类同胞的关系,但它只能模仿它. 作为朋友与AI的关系就是人类化,将一种简单的技术变成更糟糕的技术,剥夺了自己的实际友谊。

虽然大赦国际可以模仿友谊,但它不能是任何合法意义上的朋友,因为友谊取决于人性。 不仅如此,友谊还取决于相互以及关系带来的幸福和风险。 你不可能成为AI的朋友 也不可能成为树上的朋友,PlayStation,或者其他的不幸福. 作为律师的AI.

今天,许多人都把大赦国际当作一个顾问——一个会耐心地倾听他们的意见并以一个值得信赖的声音给他们提供建议的告密者。 然而,由于大赦国际是一个什么人,而不是谁,它不能根据对他们情况的真正理解、来自学习和经验的真正智慧或来自分享其人性的真正同情来提供答案。

它不能同情他们,不能为他们祈祷,也不能恳求圣灵的智慧帮助他们。 大赦国际能够在许多方面提供咨询,但不能提供咨询,因为咨询本质上是针对个人的。 作为牧师的AI. 人们越来越多地将精神健康、成长和福祉等问题带到大赦国际,这些问题过去本来是交给牧师的。

每个基督徒都需要接受一位会关心自己灵魂的牧师的慈爱监督,这种关键事项必须不委托给大赦国际,而委托给一位被叫作"和"和"的牧师".

articles.content: Le christianisme mondial change, peu à peu, de visage. D’ici à 2070, le nombre de chrétiens dans le monde pourrait approcher les 3 milliards, contre 2,27 milliards en 2020.  Une progression de 30% qui devrait être particulièrement spectaculaire en Afrique subsaharienne, où le nombre de chrétiens pourrait bondir de 129% en cinquante ans. Publiées le mercredi 18 novembre, les nouvelles projections du Pew Research Center dessinent ainsi une géographie religieuse en pleine évolution, dans laquelle le continent africain prendra une place toujours plus importante. Le christianisme devrait conserver sa place de première religion mondiale jusqu’en 2035, avant d’être dépassé par l’islam en nombre de fidèles. Selon le Pew Research Center, la population musulmane devrait ainsi augmenter de 80% entre 2020 et 2070, contre 30% pour la population chrétienne. Cette différence de rythme ne signifie toutefois pas que le christianisme recule. Au contraire, ses fidèles devraient être près de 700 millions supplémentaires à l’échelle mondiale d’ici à cinquante ans. Cette progression Tout lire… The post Pourquoi l’Afrique va bouleverser la carte des croyants appeared first on Aleteia .
articles.content_zh:
全球基督教的面貌正在逐渐发生变化。到 2070 年，全球基督徒人数可能接近 30 亿，而 2020 年为 22.7 亿。这一30%的增长在撒哈拉以南非洲地区尤为显著，该地区的基督徒人数在50年内可能激增129%。

皮尤研究中心于11月18日（星期三）发布了最新预测，勾勒出一幅不断变化的宗教版图，其中非洲大陆将占据越来越重要的位置。预计基督教将保持其世界第一大宗教的地位直至2035年，此后伊斯兰教的信徒人数将超过基督教。

皮尤研究中心的数据显示，2020年至2070年间，穆斯林人口预计将增长80%，而基督教人口的增长率则为30%。然而，这种增长速度的差异并不意味着基督教正在衰落。相反，预计在未来五十年内，基督教信徒人数将在全球范围内增加近7亿。

Derrière ce chiffre, des hommes et des femmes qui continuent de vivre leur foi malgré les menaces. Ce jeudi 19 novembre, des centaines de fidèles se pressent devant l’église saint Sulpice à Paris, pour la Nuit des Témoins. Organisée chaque année par l’AED depuis 16 ans, cette veillée mêle prière et témoignages pour rendre hommage aux chrétiens persécutés et faire entendre leur voix. Pour cette édition, deux témoins venus du Burkina Faso et du Mexique ont raconté leur quotidien, marqué par la violence et l’épreuve. Devant l’autel, des photographies de chrétiens assassinés au cours de l’année sont disposées. Nigeria, Haïti, Mexique, Burkina Faso, Mozambique, Pakistan… Un à un, leurs noms sont égrenés. Des bougies sont ensuite distribuées aux fidèles, qui viennent les déposer devant les portraits. articles.title_zh: 随着马来西亚压制良心自由，绝望和恐惧与日俱增
articles.content: A wave of viral social media videos featuring Malaysian citizens publicly declaring their departure from state-sanctioned Sunni Islam has cast a harsh spotlight on the severe lack of religious freedom in the Southeast Asian nation. While state authorities have scrambled to investigate and suppress the footage, international religious freedom advocates warn that the phenomenon highlights a much deeper, systemic crisis: the complete criminalization of apostasy for ethnic Malays and the intense persecution faced by those who desire to follow other faiths, including Christianity. Under Article 160 of the Constitution of Malaysia, all ethnic Malays are legally defined as Muslims. This constitutional binding leaves no legal avenue for a Malay individual to officially change their religion. For those who experience a personal crisis of faith or choose to embrace Christianity, the path forward is fraught with state-sponsored surveillance, social ostracism, and severe legal penalties. Central to this machinery of suppression is the powerful federal agency JAKIM (Department of Islamic Development Malaysia) and state-level enforcers like JAIS (Selangor Islamic Religious Department). Together, they operate a rigid, dual-track legal system where Shariah courts hold near-absolute jurisdiction over Muslims. Requests by individuals to officially exit Islam are systematically rejected. Instead of granting freedom of conscience, JAIS and other state bodies actively weaponize mandatory detention in state-run Islamic rehabilitation centers (pusat pemurnian akidah). These centers function as forced re-education camps. Converts who are caught or who attempt to petition the courts for apostasy are routinely sentenced to months of involuntary confinement. Inside, they are subjected to intense psychological pressure, isolation, and compulsory doctrinal lectures designed to break their resolve and force a recantation. Recently, JAIS publicized a court-ordered Istitabah (forced repentance ritual) for a social media figure, signaling that the state will use its full administrative weight to enforce religious compliance. Recent landmark legal battles from 2025 and 2026 expose a devastating reality: born-Muslims face a structural wall of total rejections. In an Oct. 2, 2025 ruling, the Federal Court — Malaysia’s highest civil judiciary — completely shut down a final appeal from a 47-year-old Christian convert who spent years fighting the Shariah court system just to return to his original faith following a divorce. The apex court reaffirmed that civil courts have zero jurisdiction to override Shariah rejections, leaving the believer legally trapped. Similarly, on Jan. 6, 2025, a Selangor woman who was unilaterally converted to Islam as a child saw her final legal challenge collapse at the Federal Court, cementing the precedent that her state identity card (MyKad) must permanently brand her as a Muslim. Even elderly believers who have secretly practiced their faith for decades are being hunted through bureaucracy. In June 2026, a 58-year-old mother filed a prominent judicial review against the National Registration Department (JPN) after they flatly refused to remove the “Islam” label from her identification card — despite her having formally converted out of Islam via a deed poll more than 30 years ago. JPN continues to trap her under state custody, demanding a clearance letter from the Shariah court that officials refuse to grant. The statistics highlight how tightly the trap is wound. Historical data shows that out of 863 formal applications submitted nationwide to leave Islam during a 10-year period, only 168 were granted. Legal analysts emphasize that nearly 100% of those rare exceptions were administrative clerical corrections in East Malaysia — such as a Jan. 7 Kota Kinabalu High Court ruling where a father and three children successfully proved they were raised Christian and that an NRD officer had made a data-entry error. articles.title_zh: 食堂大屠杀4天后遇害
articles.content: Just days after the deadly massacre in Cantine, where at least 33 civilians were reportedly killed, suspected Allied Democratic Forces (ADF) fighters have struck again in Beni Territory, claiming four more lives and burning several houses in Mabalako, in the Democratic Republic of Congo. At about 12:20 a.m. on Thursday, Nov. 12, Mabalako once again faced ADF violence , with a fresh overnight attack in the Kamahume neighborhood. According to local civil society representatives, the death toll rose from an initial three to four, while more than seven houses were also set ablaze during the deadly incursion. The attack has renewed fears among civilians already traumatized by the violence that struck Cantine-Aloya less than a week earlier. The proximity of these two attacks in time and location has heightened concerns about the continuing threat posed by the ADF to civilian populations across Beni. “We are living in constant fear,” said Mulwahali, a survivor. “We have not yet recovered from the pain of what happened in Cantine, where innocent people were brutally killed and homes reduced to ashes. Now the violence has reached Mabalako, and once again we are mourning our loved ones and watching our homes burn. We do not know who will be next or where these attackers will strike again. We are even tired of burying our people without heads. All we want is to live in peace and sleep in our homes without fearing that we may never see another morning.” A Need for Security Local civil society representatives have appealed to security services to take full responsibility for protecting civilians, strengthen security operations, and prevent further attacks. Residents of Runzayi, Malondo, Ngazi, and Kibunamaru have also been urged to remain vigilant, maintain calm, and cooperate with security forces by reporting suspicious movements. “We cannot continue living at the mercy of armed attackers,” a local Catholic bishop said. “Although the intervention of the FARDC helped limit the destruction in Mabalako, the fact that the attackers could strike and disappear without their direction being known leaves us deeply frightened. We want security, not another massacre.” To read more news stories, visit the ICC Newsroom . For interviews, please email us . 据报道,在坎廷发生了至少33名平民被杀的致命屠杀事件,几天后,疑似民主同盟军(民主同盟军)战斗人员再次袭击了贝尼县,在刚果民主共和国的马巴拉科又造成4人死亡,几所房屋被烧毁。 11月,星期四上午12点20分左右.

马巴拉科再次面临民主同盟军的暴力, 据当地民间社会代表说,死亡人数从最初的3人增加到4人,而在致命的入侵中,还有七座房屋被点燃。

袭击使已经因不到一周前袭击Cantine-Aloya的暴力而受到创伤的平民再次感到恐惧。 这两起袭击在时间和地点上接近,使人们更加担心民主同盟军对贝尼各地平民继续构成威胁。 幸存者穆尔瓦哈利说:“我们生活在持续的恐惧之中”。

“我们尚未从坎廷发生的痛苦中恢复过来,在那里,无辜者惨遭杀害,家园沦为灰烬。 现在,暴力已蔓延到马巴拉科,我们再次哀悼我们的亲人,并观看我们的家园被烧毁。 我们不知道下一个是谁,也不知道这些袭击者将在哪里再次袭击。 我们甚至厌倦了无头埋葬我们的人民。

我们只想在家中过上和平的生活和睡觉,而不必担心再有早晨。” 地方民间社会代表呼吁安全部门全面负责保护平民,加强安全行动,防止进一步的袭击。

还敦促Runzayi、Malondo、Ngazi和Kibunamaru的居民保持警惕,保持平静,并与安全部队合作,报告可疑行动。 一位当地天主教主教说,“我们不能继续受武装袭击者的摆布”。

“虽然刚果(金)武装部队的干预有助于限制对马巴拉科的破坏,但袭击者可能袭击并消失而不了解他们的方向这一事实使我们深感恐惧。 我们要的是安全,而不是另一次屠杀。” 阅读更多新闻, 请给我们发电子邮件

articles.summary_zh: 11月6日，一名名叫阿贾克·马比奥尔（Ajak Mabior）的18岁基督徒女孩在南苏丹琼莱州因拒绝接受家人包办的强迫婚姻而被殴打致死。她本应嫁给一位年长的穆斯林男子——由于她的基督教信仰以及不愿意被强迫结婚，她反对这桩婚事。此后……   这篇题为《因拒绝强迫婚姻而被杀害的女孩》的文章  最初发表在  国际基督徒关注组织  网站上。
articles.title_zh: 因拒绝强迫婚姻而被杀害的女孩
articles.content: On Nov. 6, an 18-year-old Christian girl named Ajak Mabior was beaten to death in Jonglei, South Sudan, after refusing to enter a forced marriage arranged by her family. She was expected to marry an older Muslim man — a marriage she opposed because of her Christian faith and her unwillingness to be forced into it. After attempting to escape, she was killed by her own brother and cousin. Days later, police in Bor arrested the two men but released them without charges after family members demanded their freedom, arguing that “there was no case” because they were relatives. A Common Problem The killing has raised serious concerns among Christian leaders about the pressure Christian girls face when their faith and personal convictions conflict with family expectations. “When a young girl is killed for refusing a forced marriage, and the killers walk free because they are family, the message is clear: Tradition is stronger than the law, and stronger than the value of a life,” a local pastor said. “Many of our Christian daughters live under this same shadow.” For Christian girls in South Sudan , forced marriages can become a matter of religious persecution when they are pressured to marry outside their faith and abandon their Christian convictions. Those who refuse may face rejection, threats, intimidation, and violence from their own families. Mabior’s death highlights the vulnerability of young Christian women who seek to remain faithful to Christ while facing pressure to submit to marriages that violate their faith and conscience. “The church teaches that every life is precious because it is created in the image of God,” the pastor added. “Yet when a Christian girl refuses a marriage that would bind her against her will, she can be treated as a traitor to the community. We have buried too many who paid that price.” Seeking Justice The authorities’ response has added to the church’s concerns. Police reportedly released the suspects without the consent of the Jonglei State Caretaker Commissioner. The justification that the suspects were relatives raises serious questions about the protection available to Christian girls facing forced marriages and violence. When perpetrators are released without facing justice, vulnerable Christian women are left with little confidence that the authorities will protect their right to practice their faith and make decisions according to their conscience. “We preach freedom in Christ, but our young people still live in fear of the consequences of that freedom,” the pastor said. “If the police and local authorities remain quiet, the church becomes the only place left where these girls and boys can find a voice. We need courage to speak, and we need the wider Body of Christ to stand with us.” Mabior’s case raises concerns about forced interfaith marriages, religious pressure, and violence against young Christian women in South Sudan. “We call on the wider Body of Christ to pray for Ajak’s justice, and for the protection of Christian girls facing forced marriages because of their faith,” an International Christian Concern (ICC) staffer said. “Pray that the church will have the courage to speak against religious coercion and violence, and that the authorities will uphold the law and protect vulnerable believers.” To read more news stories, visit the ICC Newsroom . For interviews, please email us . To support ICC’s work around the world, please give to our Where Most Needed Fund . articles.content_zh:
11月6日,一名名叫Ajak Mabior的18岁基督教女孩在南苏丹琼格莱州因拒绝参加家庭安排的强迫婚姻而被殴打致死。 她被期望嫁给一个年长的穆斯林男子——她反对这种婚姻,因为她的基督教信仰以及她不愿意被迫加入. 在试图逃跑后,她被自己的哥哥和表妹杀死.

几天后,Bor的警察逮捕了这两名男子,但在家属要求他们自由后,在没有指控的情况下将他们释放,他们辩称“没有案件”,因为他们是亲属。 常见问题 杀害事件引起了基督教领袖的严重关切,基督教女孩在信仰和个人信念与家庭期望相冲突时面临压力。

“当一名年轻女孩因拒绝强迫婚姻而被杀害,而杀人者因是家人而自由行动时,信息是明确的:传统比法律更强大,比生命的价值更强大。” 一位当地牧师说。

“我们许多基督教女儿生活在这种阴影下。” 对于南苏丹的基督教女孩来说,当她们被迫在信仰之外结婚并放弃基督教信仰时,强迫婚姻就可能成为宗教迫害的问题。 拒绝者可能面临自己家庭的排斥、威胁、恐吓和暴力。

Mabior的死亡凸显了基督教青年妇女的脆弱性,她们试图保持对基督的忠诚,同时面临压力,迫使她们向违反其信仰和良心的婚姻屈服。 牧师补充说,“教会教导每一条生命都是宝贵的,因为它是以上帝的形象创造的。”

“当一个基督教女孩拒绝违背她意愿而束缚她的婚姻时,她可以被当作一个叛徒对待。 我们埋葬了太多付出这一代价的人。” 寻求正义 当局的反应增加了教会的关注。 据报告,警方未经琼格莱州看守专员同意释放了嫌疑人。

关于嫌疑人是亲属的理由,令人对面临强迫婚姻和暴力的基督教女孩获得的保护提出严重问题。 当肇事者在没有受到法律制裁的情况下被释放时,脆弱的基督教妇女对当局将保护其信仰和根据其良心作出决定的权利缺乏信心。

牧师说,“我们在基督中宣扬自由,但我们的年轻人仍然生活在对这种自由的后果的恐惧之中。” “如果警察和地方当局保持安静,教堂就成了这些女孩和男孩能够发表意见的唯一地方。

我们需要勇气说话,我们需要更广泛的基督与我们站在一起。” Mabior案引起了人们对南苏丹境内强迫不同信仰间婚姻、宗教压力以及针对基督教青年妇女的暴力的关注。

“我们呼吁广大的基督机构为阿贾克的正义祈祷,并保护因信仰而面临强迫婚姻的基督教女孩。” 一位国际基督教关注组织的工作人员说。

“祈祷教会有勇气反对宗教胁迫和暴力,并祈祷当局将维护法律,保护脆弱的信徒。” 阅读更多新闻, 请给我们发电子邮件 支持电算中心在世界各地的工作,

articles.title: The Festive Attire We Really Need
articles.summary: Even in our finest clothes we can still be dirty on the inside. Advent reminds us that Jesus dresses us in his righteousness.
articles.summary_zh: 即使穿着我们最好的衣服 内心还是可以脏的 基督提醒我们,耶稣穿戴我们的正义。
articles.title_zh: 我们真正需要的节奏
articles.content: Read He will sit as a refiner and purifier of silver, and he will purify the sons of Levi and refine them like gold and silver, and they will bring offerings in righteousness to the LORD. Then the offering of Judah and Jerusalem will be pleasing to the LORD as in the days of old and as in former years. (Mal. 3:3–4) Reflect My grandmother always made going to church a special event. She helped me pick the right dress, made sure my shoes were shiny and clean, and withstood burns from the curling iron to perfect my hairdo. I know church attire can vary. But I still get dressed up for corporate worship because, no matter how cliché it sounds, I want to wear my Sunday best for Jesus. Yet even in our finest clothes, we can still be dirty on the inside. Hidden sins are, after all, hidden. We can sing hymns at max volume, forgetting the way we treated our coworkers last week. We can kneel in prayer, easily dismissing what we posted on the internet earlier that morning. We can take the bread and wine even if we lost it with our kids in the car. People at church only see what’s on the outside, but God looks on the heart (1 Sam. 16:7). And unless we come clean, we can’t come into his presence at all. Even in our finest clothes, we can still be dirty on the inside. Purity in God’s presence is a major theme in Scripture. In Leviticus, we learn how Israel was to distinguish between the clean and unclean. These categories extended to foods and animals. Even people could be defiled by disease or by touching unclean things such as a dead body. The temple was off-limits for the unclean. Only ritual washings and animal sacrifices made reentry into God’s presence achievable. But even this wasn’t permanent—for the blood of bulls and goats couldn’t fully atone for sin (Heb. 10:4). Like Israel, we dare not present ourselves before God in our sinful condition. As the psalmist asks, “Who shall stand in [God’s] holy place? He who has clean hands and a pure heart” (Ps. 24:3–4). While soap and water might wash our filthy hands, what can purify our sin-stained hearts? In today’s verses, the prophet Malachi announced the coming of One who would refine his people as gold and silver. Later, the author of Hebrews clarified the refiner’s identity: If the blood of goats and bulls . . . sanctify for the purification of the flesh, how much more will the blood of Christ, who through the eternal Spirit offered himself without blemish to God, purify our conscience from dead works to serve the living God. (Heb. 9:13–14) During Advent, we remember that Jesus is the great Refiner. He came to shed his purifying blood to cover our sins and forgive us. Then, like a refiner who heats metal to remove impurities, the Lord sanctifies us so that on judgment day we’ll be an unblemished offering to God. On that day, because of Jesus, we’ll wear white robes of righteousness (Rev. 6:11). Grandma made sure I looked pretty for church, but I wasn’t truly clean. Jesus, the great Purifier of sinners, is the only One who can wash away every stain and remove every impurity. When he dresses us in white robes, we’ll enter God’s presence because we’ll be clean—not just on the outside but on the inside too. Respond Sometimes the Lord refines us through trials and difficult circumstances. How have you experienced his refining process this year? Write a prayer thanking God for Christ who cleanses, purifies, and refines us so we’ll one day be holy and acceptable in his presence.
articles.content_zh:
读取 他必坐作炼银的精炼者,他必洗涤利未之子,并如金银般精炼,他们必以善报主耶和华. 犹大和耶路撒冷的供奉,将像往年和往年一样,为耶和华所喜悦。 (3:3-4) 反映 我奶奶总是把去教堂做成一件特殊的事

她帮我选合适的裙子 确保我的鞋子光亮洁洁 从卷曲的铁里烧伤 我知道教堂的服装会有所不同 但我还是穿好衣服去参加公司礼拜 因为不管这听起来多么陈词滥调 我想穿我的星期天最好的耶稣。 即便穿着我们最好的衣服 我们内心仍然可以肮脏

隐藏的罪恶毕竟是隐藏的。 我们可以用最高音量唱颂歌 忘记上周我们对待同事的方式 我们可以跪在祷告中, 轻易地放弃我们当天早晨在互联网上发布的内容。 我们可以拿走面包和酒 即使我们失去了它与我们的孩子在车里。 人们在教堂只看到外面的东西,但上帝看着心脏(1Sam. 16:7).

除非我们坦白,否则我们根本无法进入他的存在。 即使穿着我们最好的衣服, 我们内部仍然可以脏。 上帝面前的纯洁是圣经中的一个主要主题。 在利维提库斯,我们了解到以色列如何区分干净和不干净。 这些类别扩大到食物和动物。

甚至人们也可能因疾病或触摸尸体等不干净的东西而受到玷污。 该寺对不洁者禁入. 只有仪式洗涤和动物牺牲才能使重返上帝的存在。 但即使是这也不是永久的 — — 因为公牛和山羊的血无法完全赎罪(Heb. 10:4)。

与以色列一样,我们不敢在罪恶的条件下站在上帝面前。 正如诗人所问的, " 谁会站在[上帝]的圣地? 手清净而心清净者”(第24:3-4页)。 虽然肥皂和水可能洗我们的脏手,但什么能净化我们的罪恶的心? 先知马拉奇在今天的诗文中宣布,

后来,希伯来人的作者澄清了提炼者的身份: 如果山羊和公牛的血... ...为净化肉体而神圣化, 基督的血会有多少, 他通过永恒的灵献给自己 没有污垢上帝, (Heb. 9:13-14)在"启示录"中,我们记得耶稣是伟大的炼油者.

他为了掩盖我们的罪孽 并原谅我们而来 然后,像精炼者一样,他用金属加热去除杂质,主使我们圣洁,这样,在审判日,我们将成为向上帝献礼的无瑕疵者。 因为耶稣的缘故, 外婆确保我看起来很适合教堂,

耶稣,罪人的伟大净化者,是唯一可以洗去每一个污点,去除每一个杂质的人. 当他穿白袍时, 我们将进入上帝的面前, 有时主会通过考验和困难的环境来完善我们 你今年是怎么经历他的提炼过程的?

感谢上帝净化、净化、精炼我们,

articles.title: Don’t Be Afraid of the Alien Question
articles.summary: ‘Faith in Space’ shows that many Americans throughout history have already taken the question of extraterrestrial life seriously, but they’ve done so from outside an orthodox Christian framework.
articles.summary_zh: ”“宇宙信仰”表明, 历史上许多美国人已经认真对待地球外生命问题,
articles.title_zh: 不要害怕外星人的问题
articles.content: Have you ever wondered whether other worlds exist, and, if they do, whether they’re filled with intelligent life? If so, you’ve tapped into a deeply human instinct. Americans have long looked up at the night sky and asked that question. For Christians, though, the answers can feel unnerving. We already believe in nonhuman intelligence. We call them angels and demons. But aliens would be something else—material, embodied, literally otherworldly . In 2016, NASA started a conversation among religious scholars at the Center of Theological Inquiry in Princeton about what the existence of extraterrestrial life would mean for religion. Paul Gutjahr, Ruth N. Halls professor of English at Indiana University, has been wrestling with that question for years. Faith in Space: American Religious Belief in Extraterrestrial Life is his considered answer. He thinks we need to look back at existing “extraterrestrial cosmologies” in American religions rather than merely pondering future possibilities (7). Faith in Space is ultimately a history of what happens when religious communities take extraterrestrial life seriously. Many minority religions have, and it has shaped their cosmology and even their soteriology. But for many evangelical Christians, Gutjahr’s history raises a more uncomfortable question: What happens when we don’t take seriously the possibility of extraterrestrial life? Alien Religion Early Americans didn’t need much help imagining inhabited worlds. According to Gutjahr, many Americans “believed there to be life elsewhere in the universe” (19). By the end of the 19th century, “every stratum of American society had been exposed” to this belief (43). For example, Emanuel Swedenborg taught that the universe is populated with humans bearing God’s image and claimed to have conversed with them. His American followers never numbered more than a few thousand, and yet his ideas traveled across the young nation; Helen Keller held them, as did John Chapman (a.k.a. Johnny Appleseed). What happens when we don’t take seriously the possibility of extraterrestrial life? Andrew Jackson Davis, the father of American Spiritualism, was similarly inspired, convinced that “if life is to be found on other planets, it is human life.” He arranged extraterrestrial humans in “a progression of degrees that move from less to more spiritual” (64). Then Joseph Smith took things further. Latter-day Saints (Mormons) took an “aggressive extraterrestrial cosmological stance,” linking all worlds under one governing structure (79). God created many inhabited worlds arranged in “a hierarchy where some worlds rule over others” (89). Among these many worlds, Earth holds the least desirable title of “the most wicked, and thus most in need of a savior” (86). God himself is an enfleshed exalted man dwelling on a planet near the star Kolob. I’d add that the Salt Lake Temple bears the Big Dipper, and early Latter-day Saint temple iconography is thick with suns, moons, and stars. Next came the founder of Seventh-day Adventism, Ellen G. White. Where William Miller’s followers read comets and meteor showers as signs of Christ’s return, White gave Seventh-day Adventists “a far more complex understanding of their relationship with the stars” (124). Ours “was the only wicked world” (125). White distinguished strongly between the righteous and unrighteous worlds, and put Earth on the wrong side of that distinction. By the 20th century, the heavens were packed and theories about the heavens were part of salvation. Then comes Helena Blavatsky (Theosophy), L. Ron Hubbard (Scientology), Wallace Fard Muhammad and Louis Farrakhan (Nation of Islam), Malachi Z. York (Nuwaubian Nation), Ashtar Command, and Heaven’s Gate. All these figures or groups saw extraterrestrial life as part of the human story, whether for our good or our ill, or both. While the subtitle promises to cover American religions broadly, Gutjahr sets aside Catholics, Jews, and native traditions. The only “Protestants” h

articles.title: Young Adults Are Hungry. Here Are 3 Ways to Feed Them.
articles.summary: Gen Z’s hunger for food, people, and the Word gives the church a magnificent opportunity in this moment.
articles.summary_zh: Gen Z对食物的渴望, 人们,
articles.title_zh: 年轻的成年人是饿了。 这里有3种喂食方法。
articles.content: When we opened the century-old church doors on the corner of Whaley Street and Wayne Street, we figured we’d have about 50 folks step through them that night. It was a Bible class for Gen Z, after all. How many Gen Zers actually want to learn about the Bible? Apparently, more than 50. We had to scramble for more chairs. It quickly became obvious that this generation—my generation—is hungry for the Bible, and we’ll starve if we don’t get fed. How are you feeding the hungry young adults in your context? My church has learned key lessons about feeding college students and young adults. These aren’t novel, but I hope they can help your people as much as they’ve helped ours. 1. Food (Like, Actual Food) I was sitting across from a leader at a major university recently and asked him how we could influence the students on that campus. He looked at me and said the plainest thing: “Food wins.” To win the heart of a man, you go through the stomach. If you want to feed people the gospel, consider first feeding them a sandwich. This is why my brother (“Chef Chunk” as they call him) has been serving an incredible amount of pancake batter out of a four-foot plastic storage container, complete with chocolate chips, blueberries, and a few other cheap toppings. We start pancake-flipping before 7 p.m. and don’t stop until we start class at 8:03 p.m., to keep up with the demand. Apparently breakfast for dinner is a fan favorite. Eating meals with others is one of the greatest indicators of personal well-being—the more we eat with our families (whether spiritual or biological), the more likely we are to be satisfied with our lives and filled with love, joy, and peace. Yet we’re eating fewer meals together than ever. What if the church was one of the great combatants of this damaging trend? 2. Friends (Like, Actual Friends) Speaking of loneliness, our culture is increasingly lacking “third spaces” where lonely people can find and build community. Robert Putnam described and predicted this decades ago in Bowling Alone —but these days we don’t just bowl alone. We shop alone, eat alone, entertain alone. We even tend to date or do friendship “alone,” as in virtually rather than in person. What few third spaces remain—the gym, sports environments, coffee shops—aren’t ideal for making meaningful connections. In gyms, we have our headphones on; at sports games, the music is so loud you get hoarse when you speak; and coffee shops are great but usually filled with headphones-on, screened-off people (and $7 lattes). Fresh-out-of-college Jimmy has nowhere to meet potential-best-friend Johnny or potential-love-of-his-life Jessica. That leaves Jimmy feeling hopeless in one of the most foundational needs of life: relationships. Our culture is increasingly lacking ‘third spaces’ where lonely people can find and build community. Yet this is a hole best filled by the new humanity God created called the church. Amid a growing cultural hunger for embodied friendships, maybe one of the major ways our church can “seek the welfare” of our cities (Jer. 29:7) is to build environments where a wide variety of folks can congregate. Maybe that looks like creating spaces for line-dancing, pick-up basketball, or weekly pickleball nights. But I have a hunch that one of the most interesting third spaces we can create might not need to be about entertainment. 3. Knowledge (Like, Spiritual Knowledge) “Do you know what Christmas is about?” “Um—not sure. What do you mean?” “Like, do you know the story behind it?” “Hmm. I feel like it’s about a guy . . .” “YES! Do you know his name?” “Mmm. Nah man.” “Jesus. His name is Jesus.” This is a real conversation I had with an average high school student in the South, the heart of the so-called Bible Belt. I could tell you of dozens of other conversations just like it. Here’s the truth: The Bible is the most interesting story in the world, and no one knows it anymore. 当我们在Whaley街和Wayne街的拐角打开一个世纪以来的教堂大门时, 我们以为当晚会有大约50个人走进它们。 毕竟是Gen Z的圣经课 有多少Zers将军真正想学习圣经? 显然,超过50个。 我们不得不找更多的椅子

食物(如实际食物),我最近坐在一所大大学的领袖对面,问他我们如何影响那个校园的学生。 他看着我,并说出最简单的话:“粮食获胜”。 欲胜人心则通于胃. 如果你想给人们吃福音 考虑先喂他们三明治

因此,我的兄弟(“Chef Chunk”)从一个四英尺高的塑料储存容器中,提供了令人难以置信的煎饼击打器,并配有巧克力片、蓝莓和一些其他廉价的顶料。 我们晚上7点开始煎饼,

晚餐早餐显然是粉丝最喜欢的 与他人一起吃饭是个人福祉的最大指标之一——我们与家人一起吃得越多(无论是精神的还是生理的),我们就越有可能满足于生活,充满爱、欢乐与和平。 我们一起吃的食物比以前少。

如果教会是这种破坏性趋势的伟大战士之一呢? 2. 朋友(如实际朋友) 说到孤独,我们的文化越来越缺乏“第三空间”,人们可以在那里找到和建设社区。 罗伯特·普特南(Robert Putnam)在几十年前, 我们单独购物 单独吃饭 单独娱乐

我们甚至倾向于“单独”约会或进行友谊,实际上而不是当面进行。 体育馆、体育环境、咖啡店等仅剩的第三个空间, 在健身房里,我们开着耳机;在体育比赛里,音乐响得那么响亮,说话时会变得粗糙;
