articles.title: El papa León XIV ya está en Argentina y el campo tuvo protagonismo en su primer discurso
articles.summary: Tras pasar por Uruguay, el papa León XIV inició este domingo su histórica gira de cuatro días por Argentina, que constituye la primera llegada de un líder de la Iglesia Católica mundial a nuestro país
articles.summary_zh: 在访问乌拉圭之后，教宗利奥十四世于本周日开启了为期四天的历史性阿根廷之行，这是全球天主教会领袖首次踏上我国的土地。
articles.title_zh: 教宗方济各已抵达阿根廷，他在首场讲话中重点谈及乡村问题。
articles.content: Tras pasar por Uruguay, el papa León XIV inició este domingo su histórica gira de cuatro días por Argentina, que constituye la primera llegada de un líder de la Iglesia Católica mundial a nuestro país desde Juan Pablo II en 1987. En ese marco, la primera actividad del Sumo Pontífice fue un discurso en el Palacio Libertad de la Ciudad Autónoma de Buenos Aires (CABA), frente al presidente de la Nación, Javier Milei. Y aunque sus palabras lógicamente estuvieron apuntadas hacia toda la sociedad, hubo numerosos pasajes que encontraron especial sintonía con el mundo agropecuario. Esto, en la previa de la reunión que León XIV mantendrá el lunes con representantes empresariales, sindicales y de organizaciones sociales, entre los que estarán los presidentes de las cuatro entidades de la Mesa de Enlace. EL PAPA LEÓN XIV EN ARGENTINA Puntualmente, el jefe mayor del Vaticano destacó el valor del esfuerzo cotidiano de los argentinos, con una mención expresa a quienes trabajan en el campo, y reivindicó la importancia de generar oportunidades, estimular la iniciativa privada y aprovechar responsablemente los recursos naturales. “Esta tierra conoce bien el valor del esfuerzo de quienes se ganan la vida en el campo y en las ciudades”, expresó León XIV, al destacar también el papel de los emprendedores y de las familias que sostienen sus hogares a través del trabajo. Asimismo, el Papa reconoció el enorme potencial productivo del país, al señalar que la Argentina cuenta con una extraordinaria riqueza natural, desde sus campos y reservas de agua hasta sus fuentes de energía, minerales y biodiversidad. Así, su mensaje combinó la posibilidad de aprovechar esos recursos para generar desarrollo y bienestar con la responsabilidad de preservar el ambiente y las condiciones de vida de las futuras generaciones. También dedicó un espacio a la innovación, la investigación y las nuevas tecnologías, incluida la inteligencia artificial, destacando su capacidad para transformar la producción y mejorar la vida de las personas. Por otro lado, al expresar una mirada sobre América del Sur, mencionó además a los alimentos, la energía y el conocimiento como elementos que vinculan a los países y abren oportunidades para fortalecer la cooperación regional. LEON XIV, EL MARTÍN FIERO Y EL MATE Asimismo, León XIV ofreció referencias cargadas de simbolismo para la identidad argentina. Por ejemplo, mencionó al Martín Fierro de José Hernández, a Jorge Luis Borges, al tango y a las tradiciones del interior del país. Y no faltó una de las costumbres más arraigadas entre los argentinos: el mate compartido, al que presentó como un gesto cotidiano que favorece la conversación y la cercanía. Por último, hacia el final de su intervención, León XIV evocó a Nuestra Señora de Luján, patrona de la Argentina y figura de especial significado para las comunidades rurales y para generaciones de familias de todo el país. También recordó al papa Francisco, citó a Carlos Gardel y alentó a los argentinos a valorar el patrimonio recibido de las generaciones anteriores y trabajar para dejar un país mejor a quienes vendrán. De esta manera, sin ser un discurso específicamente dirigido al agro, las palabras de León XIV dejaron un reconocimiento al trabajo rural, a la producción, a la iniciativa emprendedora y a las tradiciones que forman parte de la identidad argentina. Un mensaje que también llegó al corazón del campo argentino. EL DISCURSO COMPLETO DEL PAPA LEÓN XIV Señor Presidente de la República, distinguidas autoridades y miembros del cuerpo diplomático. Señoras y señores, me alegra profundamente encontrarme hoy en esta querida tierra argentina. Agradezco, señor Presidente, las cordiales palabras que ha tenido a bien dirigirme y la acogida que por medio de usted me brinda su pueblo. Saludos también a los miembros del cuerpo diplomático y a las demás autoridades aquí presentes, y extiendo con afecto mi saludo a todos los argentinos. articles.title_zh: 《国家报》/圣洛伦索教区迎来新主教
articles.content: El papa León XIV nombró a monseñor Pierre Jubinville como nuevo obispo de la diócesis de San Lorenzo en reemplazo de monseñor Joaquín Robledo, quien presentó renuncia al cargo. La Nunciatura Apostólica en Paraguay comunicó el sábado 7 de noviembre que el santo padre aceptó la renuncia de Robledo y designó en su reemplazo a monseñor Pierre Laurent Jubinville, quien se desempeñaba como obispo de San Pedro y es el actual presidente de la Conferencia Episcopal Paraguaya (CEP). La decisión fue anunciada por la CEP, conforme a lo establecido en el Código de Derecho Canónico, que contempla la renuncia de los obispos al alcanzar los 75 años de edad. No obstante, monseñor Robledo continuará al frente de la diócesis como administrador apostólico hasta la toma de posesión canónica de su sucesor. La Conferencia Episcopal Paraguaya agradeció a monseñor Robledo por su servicio pastoral y dedicación a la Iglesia, al tiempo que encomendó en oración al nuevo obispo, deseándole un fecundo ministerio episcopal en su nueva misión. El nuevo obispo Monseñor Pierre Laurent Jubinville nació el 5 de agosto de 1960 en Ottawa, Canadá. Tras algunas experiencias laborales, ingresó en la Congregación del Espíritu Santo y estudió Teología en la Universidad de Montreal. Emitió los votos solemnes en 1988 y fue ordenado presbítero el 17 de setiembre de 1988. Tras algunas experiencias misioneras en África, realizó estudios académicos en Montreal y París. Llegó a Paraguay en 1991, desarrolló diversas tareas pastorales y formativas; entre ellas, se desempeñó en la pastoral indígena de la parroquia San José Obrero, en la Diócesis de San Pedro; fue párroco de San Francisco de Asís y formador de la Congregación del Espíritu Santo en Asunción. En 2013 fue nombrado obispo de San Pedro y recibió la ordenación episcopal el 21 de diciembre de ese mismo año. Además, ejerció la vicepresidencia de la Conferencia Episcopal Paraguaya entre 2018 y 2024 y, desde noviembre de 2024, ocupa la presidencia de dicha institución. La Diócesis de San Lorenzo comprende varias localidades del departamento Central, entre ellas Capiatá, San Lorenzo, Ñemby, Itá, Ypané, Guarambaré, Villeta, Nueva Italia, San Antonio, J. Augusto Saldívar, Ypacaraí y Thompson.

articles.title: Why Did Prosecutors Agree To Omit References to Katy Perry From the Opening Statements at Trial ?
articles.summary: Prosecutors agreed to remove references to Katy Perry from their opening statement at Russell Brand's London rape trial after objections from his lawyers. The decision emerged on Thursday, 5 November
articles.summary_zh: 在拉塞尔·布兰德的伦敦强奸案庭审中，经其律师提出异议，检方同意从开庭陈述中删除提及凯蒂·佩里的内容。该决定于11月5日星期四公布。
articles.title_zh: 为什么检察官同意在庭审开场陈述中省略对凯蒂·佩里的提及？
articles.content: Prosecutors agreed to remove references to Katy Perry from their opening statement at Russell Brand's London rape trial after objections from his lawyers. The decision emerged on Thursday, 5 November 2026, after a jury returned verdicts at Southwark Crown Court. Brand, 51, was convicted of one count of rape and three counts of sexual assault involving four women. Jurors acquitted him of two further rape charges and one count of attempted indecent assault. He had denied all seven charges, which concerned six women. Details of the pretrial discussions became public after reporting restrictions ended. They showed how Brand's former marriage was kept out of the prosecution's opening address, although he later mentioned Perry while giving evidence. Why Katy Perry References Were Removed From the Opening Lead prosecutor Riel Karmy-Jones KC acknowledged in written submissions that references to Brand's relationship with Perry after 2009 'may be sensitive'. According to Sky News' court reporting, prosecutors were 'content to remove these from the opening' following defence submissions. The agreement was limited to the opening statement. It did not prevent every mention of Perry during the proceedings or establish that the relationship itself was evidence of wrongdoing. Perry was not accused of any offence. Prosecutors also agreed to leave out references to Brand's earlier religious beliefs and his 2024 baptism. His Christian conversion was nevertheless mentioned during questioning of his wife, Laura, showing that the restrictions on the opening did not cover all subsequent testimony. Other arguments before the trial concerned references to Brand's past drug and alcohol use. His lawyers challenged their relevance to the allegations, and material about treatment at a sex addiction clinic was omitted from a former assistant's evidence. Those disputes were separate from the agreement concerning Perry. The Crown Prosecution Service confirmed that investigators had not asked Perry for a witness statement. Senior Crown Prosecutor David Roberts said reasonable lines of inquiry relevant to the charges had been pursued. There is no basis in that statement to suggest Perry refused to cooperate. Katy Perry's Marriage Still Entered the Courtroom Perry and Brand began dating in 2009 and married in Rajasthan, India, in 2010. They separated in December 2011, and their divorce was finalised in 2012. The offences for which Brand was convicted took place between 2004 and 2009. During his evidence, Brand referred to the marriage and said it had brought him 'staggering fame'. The comment arose from his own testimony, not the prosecution's opening statement. It did not turn Perry into a witness or complainant. The Crown Prosecution Service said the women whose cases resulted in convictions came forward independently after a television investigation aired in September 2023. Prosecutors relied on their accounts and testimony from other witnesses to present evidence of Brand's conduct. Following the verdict, Roberts said Brand had 'used his celebrity status to commit sexual crimes'. The agency thanked the women for coming forward and stressed that sexual offences can be prosecuted years after they occur. The complainants have lifelong anonymity. Mr Justice Joel Bennathan refused Brand bail and remanded him in custody ahead of sentencing on Monday, 9 November. The judge warned that he faced a 'significant custodial term'. Rape carries a maximum penalty of life imprisonment in England and Wales. © Copyright IBTimes 2026. All rights reserved.

articles.content: Antes de escribir la biografía de Jorge Bergoglio, que llamó El gran Reformador, Austen Ivereigh ya era un experto en la historia de la Iglesia argentina. “Mi tesis de doctorado [en Oxford], que terminé en el 92, fue sobre catolicismo y política en la Argentina”. Y hay más: “Debo mi fe a la Iglesia Argentina, leyendo artículos de monseñor (Gustavo) Franceschi, volví a la fe”, dice. Ese conocimiento de nuestro país y de su fe mayoritaria representó una ventaja a la hora de escribir sobre Bergoglio, ya que cada etapa de la trayectoria del futuro Papa está debidamente contextualizada en la época que atravesaba el país. Desde aquel marzo de 2013, cuando la novedad de un pontífice argentino y jesuita impactó al mundo entero, Ivereihg siempre pensó que vendría cuando Francisco visitara la Argentina, viaje que finalmente no se concretó. “Ahora vengo con León”, comenta. En efecto, este escritor, historiador, periodista y analista de asuntos religiosos y políticos estará en nuestro país contemporáneamente con la visita del papa León XIV, invitado por la Universidad del Salvador (USAL), donde dictó, el pasado viernes 6, una clase magistral sobre “El giro latinoamericano Francisco-León: la Iglesia misionera sinodal y el cambio de época”. Ivereigh también es co-autor de Let Us Dream (Soñemos Juntos, 2020), un libro escrito en colaboración con Francisco. Su trabajo más reciente es First Belong to God: On Retreat with Pope Francis (Lo primero es pertenecer a Dios: Un retiro con el Papa Francisco, 2024), basado en los escritos y charlas de Bergoglio como director espiritual de un retiro ignaciano de 8 días. De 2004 a 2006, Ivereigh fue colaborador del entonces arzobispo de Westminster, cardenal Cormac Murphy-O’Connor, uno de los más activos promotores de la candidatura de Jorge Mario Bergoglio al papado. Ivereigh considera que el papado de Francisco inició un giro latinoamericano hacia una iglesia misionera y sinodal, cuyo primer paso fue la exhortación apostólica Evangelii Gaudium (noviembre de 2013), sobre “el anuncio del Evangelio en el mundo actual”, con la cual, dice, “Francisco inaugura una hoja de ruta de su Papado que también es la del pontificado de León”. Pero esa hoja de ruta tenía una génesis anterior: el ya famoso documento de Aparecida, la V Conferencia General del Episcopado Latinoamericano y del Caribe (Celam), redactado por Bergoglio. De esta manera, “América Latina pasó a ser la iglesia fuente”, señala, porque “siempre hay una parte de la Iglesia de la cual brota un dinamismo teológico”. Antes, ese rol lo cumplía Europa, pero a partir del Concilio Vaticano II eso cambia porque es en América Latina donde mejor se lo pone en práctica. Aclara que “fuente” no quiere decir centro; de hecho, “Francisco quería una Iglesia multipolar”. — ¿Hasta qué punto Aparecida refleja a Bergoglio como individualidad y hasta dónde es la Iglesia latinoamericana, que usted define como “fuente”? — El proceso de preparación de esa conferencia general, fue muy sinodal, de mucha consulta, y el papel de Bergoglio en esa conferencia general es muy conocido. Creo que influyó la recepción del Concilio Vaticano II en el Río de La Plata, que tuvo un matiz distinto al resto de América Latina. Tal vez, cuando llegó a Aparecida esa visión sobre la religiosidad popular estaba ya madura. Es decir, una teología de espiritualidad latinoamericana, distinta a anteriores teologías latinoamericanas. Bergoglio tenía muchas cosas que eran de él. Pero también llevaba en su forma de ser y de pensar muchos aportes de la iglesia argentina, la influencia de Lucio Gera y de Rafael Tello y toda esa tradición. — ¿Cómo vio el impacto de su papado en la Argentina? — Creo que una de las razones por las que no vino, sobre todo al principio, fue que tenía horror del triunfalismo. Y sabía que tal vez los argentinos tenían —todos los países lo tienen— una cierta tentación de decir: “El Papa es argentino”. articles.title_zh: 教皇警告人工智能会导致非人性化
articles.content: Pope Leo XIV waves to faithful from the popemobile upon his arrival for a prayer vigil at the Centenario Stadium in Montevideo on November 7, 2026. (AFP Photo) Pope Leo XIV warned students on Nov. 7 of “dehumanization” through the use of AI in education, and urged schools and university to place the “person before the algorithm.” “The process of dehumanization we are experiencing poses a challenge,” the pope, who has warned repeatedly about the need to ensure AI is used ethically, said in a speech at the Catholic University of Uruguay. Just three weeks after undergoing surgery for lung cancer, the 71-year-old pontiff is on a 12-day tour of South Africa where he served nearly two decades as a missionary. On Nov. 7, he visited the crime-blighted Montevideo neighborhood of Casavalle. The murder rate in the impoverished district is four times the national average and residents spoke movingly of the dangers they faced, like commonplace gun violence. Katherine Silva’s voice cracked with emotion as she told the pope about the violence and abuse she had suffered as a child. After ending up homeless at 15, the young mother said she “went through very dark times” and “nearly died.” “There are children in Uruguay who do not go to school for fear of never returning home,” Leo said. “In a country as rich in resources as this, children should never have to go to bed hungry... Much less should they have to suffer violence to the point of losing their lives,” he added. As police helicopters flew overhead, locals waved and cheered to welcome the head of the world’s 1.4 billion Catholics, who blessed 12 new low-income houses financed by the Church.

articles.title_zh: 世界各地的地标建筑将在2026年红色周期间亮灯
articles.content: About 130 cathedrals, thousands of churches, and over 125,000 people around the world are expected to take part in Red Week this month, with the European Parliament in Strasbourg, France, honoring the occasion by lighting up in red on Nov. 23. Red Week 2026 will take place from Nov. 15–22, with Red Wednesday falling on Nov. 18 in most regions, although it will be observed on Nov. 25 in the Philippines. The observance began in 2016 by Aid to the Church in Need (ACN), an international Catholic aid organization and Pontifical Foundation of the Church that supports Christians who are persecuted, oppressed, or in material need. The week includes illuminating monuments in red, prayer vigils, testimonies, and seminars on Christian persecution around the world. Designed to raise awareness of the ongoing Christian persecution in countries particularly in Africa and Asia, Red Week brings together those who are persecuted and those who are working to end violence and hatred against people of faith. At various events, testimonials from survivors of religious persecution will provide powerful moments of reflection about the suffering and human rights violations happening around us that go unnoticed. According to the latest figures provided by ACN, 413 million Christians live in countries where serious violations of religious freedom occur, and around 220 million Christians worldwide are directly exposed to persecution. "Faced with this reality, the pontifical foundation is once again promoting the Red Week this November, an international mobilization of prayer, witness, and awareness-raising to draw attention to the deterioration of religious freedom and remember the millions of Christians who suffer discrimination and persecution because of their faith," said Regina Lynch, executive president of ACN International. Red is more than a color According to ACN's "Religious Freedom in the World Report 2025," more than 5.4 billion people — almost two-thirds of humanity — live in countries where religious freedom is not fully guaranteed. The color red is used to symbolize the blood of martyrs and all those who suffer for their faith. In 33 countries Christians have been forced to leave their homes because of their faith while in 57 countries Christians suffer physical violence or even detention because of their faith. Each church and monument taking part in Red Week serves as a reminder of Christians who cannot freely practice their religion. In line with article 18 of the Universal Declaration of Human Rights, every individual has the freedom of thought, religion, and conscience with the right to practice their beliefs, free from persecution and violence. Through this weeklong initiative, ACN aims to promote one shared goal of making visible the shared suffering of the Christian people and defend everyone's fundamental rights to religious freedom.

根据澳大利亚基督教联合会提供的最新数字,有4.13亿基督徒生活在严重侵犯宗教自由的国家,全世界约有2.2亿基督徒直接受到迫害。

阿尔。 根据ACN的"2025年世界报道中的宗教自由",红色不止一种颜色,超过54亿人——几乎占人类的三分之二——生活在宗教自由得不到充分保障的国家. 颜色红色用来象征烈士和所有因信仰而受苦的人的鲜血.

在33个国家,基督教徒因信仰而被迫离开家园,而在57个国家,基督教徒因信仰而遭受暴力甚至拘留。 每个参加红周的教堂和纪念碑都提醒不能自由信奉其宗教的基督徒。

根据《世界人权宣言》第18条,每个人都有思想、宗教和良心自由,有权信奉自己的信仰,不受迫害和暴力。

通过这一为期一周的倡议,基督教大会旨在促进一个共同目标,即使基督教人民共同遭受苦难,并捍卫人人享有宗教自由的基本权利。

articles.summary: Sharing your faith, or evangelising, is not always an easy experience. For those of us who are not naturally extroverted or confident in public speaking, talking about our faith with people close to u
articles.summary_zh: 分享信仰或传福音并不总是那么容易。对于我们当中那些天生不外向或不善于公开演讲的人来说，与亲近的人谈论我们的信仰
articles.title_zh: 分享您的信仰：传福音的实用建议
articles.content: Sharing your faith, or evangelising, is not always an easy experience. For those of us who are not naturally extroverted or confident in public speaking, talking about our faith with people close to us, let alone complete strangers, can be nerve-wracking. Nonetheless, sharing the gospel is something all Christians have been called to participate in through the Great Commission (Matthew 28:19-20), regardless of our personality, intellectual knowledge or position within the church. As someone who regularly participates in street evangelism and teaches the Bible to young people, I have learnt a few lessons along the way. Here are some practical tips that may help you grow in confidence and approach evangelism with greater love, wisdom and faith. 1. Prepare yourself spiritually First and foremost, it is important to remember that someone’s spiritual growth or acceptance of Christ is ultimately not within our control. Faith is a gift from God, and it is by His grace that hearts are transformed (Ephesians 2:8-9; John 6:44). Our responsibility is to faithfully share the gospel while humbly entrusting the outcome into His hands (Romans 10:14-15). So, pray. Pray for the people you will encounter, for wisdom in your conversations and for the Holy Spirit to guide you (Colossians 4:3-4; James 1:5; Luke 12:12). Read your Bible regularly, not simply to accumulate knowledge or prepare answers, but to know God more deeply through His Word (2 Timothy 3:16-17; Psalm 119:11). The more His Word dwells in your heart, the more naturally it will flow into your conversations (Colossians 3:16; Matthew 12:34). Above all, learn to rely on the Holy Spirit rather than your own intellect, eloquence or comfort. As Paul reminds us in 1 Corinthians 3:6, one person plants, another waters, but it is God who gives the growth. 2. People are not as scary as they seem One thing I have learnt through evangelism is that people are often not as intimidating as we imagine. Despite our different backgrounds and beliefs, we are all human beings searching for something, whether that is meaning, love, belonging or purpose. If a friend, colleague or family member comes to you for advice or shares something they are struggling with, this can be a natural opportunity to explain how your faith has helped you through similar experiences. And when approaching strangers, you may be surprised by how open some people are to conversations about faith. Many actually know very little about the Bible beyond what they have encountered through popular culture, the media or secular perspectives. Others may have genuine questions but hesitate to ask them for fear of sounding ignorant or offensive. Rather than assuming someone will be hostile or uninterested, approach them with openness and a willingness to listen. You may discover that they are more curious than you expected. 3. Help people understand why they need Jesus and the Church A common response I encounter is something along the lines of, “If Christianity makes you happy, that's great, but it’s just not for me.” Others may say that they are not religious but respect all religions because they encourage people to do good. These responses offer opportunities to explain that Christianity is not simply about personal happiness, moral improvement or following another set of religious rules. At its heart, the Christian faith is about a relationship with God, founded on His love and truth (John 17:3; 1 John 4:9-10). The gospel is for everyone because we all fall short and need God’s grace (Romans 3:23). Jesus did not come merely to make our lives more comfortable, but to reconcile us to God and give us new life (2 Corinthians 5:18-19; John 10:10). Some people may argue that life has no ultimate meaning and that they do not need one to live. Yet even this outlook often involves living according to certain values, purposes or convictions. This can open a thoughtful conversation about where we find meaning and what ultimately gives our live
articles.content_zh:
分享你的信仰,或传福音,并不总是容易的经历。 对于我们当中那些不自然地对公开演讲感到放荡或自信的人来说,与我们身边的人谈论我们的信仰,更不要说完全陌生的人了,可能会让人神经崩溃.

然而,分享福音是所有基督徒通过大委员会(Matthew 28:19-20)被要求参与的事情,无论我们的个性、知识或教会中的地位如何。 作为经常参加街头福音仪式,向年轻人讲授《圣经》的人,我从中吸取了一些教训。

这里有一些实用的提示,可能有助于你充满信心地成长,并以更大的爱、智慧和信心来对待福音派。 1. 首先,从精神上准备自己,必须记住,一个人的精神成长或对基督的接受最终不在我们的控制范围之内。 信仰是真主所赐的,是他的恩典所赐的。

约翰6:44。 我们的责任是忠实地分享福音,同时谦卑地将结果交给他(罗姆人10:14-15)。 所以,祈祷。 祈祷你们将遇到的人,祈祷你们谈话中的智慧,祈祷圣灵指引你们(科洛斯人4:3-4;詹姆斯1:5;卢克12:12).

经常阅读你的圣经,不仅仅是积累知识或准备答案,而是通过他的言语更深入地了解上帝(Timothy 3:16-17;Psalm 119:11). 他的话越是停留在你的心中,就越自然地会流进你的谈话中(Clossians 3:16;Matthew 12:34). 最重要的是,学会依靠圣灵 而不是你自己的智慧,言辞或安慰。

正如保罗在科林斯3: 6中提醒我们的那样,一个人种植物,另一个水域,但生长的却是上帝。 2.人们没有看起来那么可怕 我从福音传道中学到的一件事是,人们往往不像我们想象的那样害怕。

尽管我们有不同的背景和信仰,但我们都是在寻找某种东西的人,无论是意义、爱情、归属还是目的。 如果一个朋友、同事或家庭成员来找你寻求建议或分享他们正在挣扎的东西,这可以是一个自然的机会来解释你的信仰如何帮助你通过类似的经验。

当接近陌生人时,你可能会对有些人对谈论信仰的开放性感到惊讶。 许多人实际上对圣经了解甚少,超出了他们通过流行文化,媒体或世俗观点所遭遇的. 其他人可能会有真正的问题,但由于害怕听上去无知或冒犯而犹豫不决。

与其假设有人会怀有敌意或不感兴趣,不如公开和愿意倾听他们的意见。 你可能会发现他们比你想象的更好奇 3个

帮助人们理解为什么他们需要耶稣和教会。 我遇到的一个共同反应是,“如果基督教让你快乐,那就太好了,但对我来说却不是。 ” 其他人可能说他们不是宗教,而是尊重所有宗教,因为他们鼓励人们做好事。

这些回应为解释基督教不仅仅是个人幸福,道德改善或遵循另一套宗教规则提供了机会. 基督教信仰的核心是和上帝的关系,建立在他的爱与真理之上(John 17:3; 1 John 4:9-10). 福音是给每个人的,因为我们都不足,需要上帝的恩惠(罗姆人3:23)。

耶稣的到来不仅仅是为了使我们的生活更加舒适,而是使我们与上帝和解,给我们新的生活(2科林斯人5:18-19;约翰10:10). 有些人可能认为生命没有最终意义,他们不需要一个人来生活. 然而,即使这种前景也往往涉及按照某些价值观、宗旨或信念生活。

这可以打开一个深思熟虑的谈话 关于我们在哪里找到意义 并最终给我们的生活

articles.summary_zh: É a maior comunidade religiosa, mas também a mais perseguida do mundo. Os cristãos são notícia quase diariamente por serem alvo de ataques ou assassínios ； ou por as suas instalações e símbolos terem s
articles.title_zh: Félix Lungu ： É muito difícil ser cristão em países fundamentais
articles.content: É a maior comunidade religiosa, mas também a mais perseguida do mundo. Os cristãos são notícia quase diariamente por serem alvo de ataques ou assassínios; ou por as suas instalações e símbolos terem sido danificados. Só em setembro, o Observatory on Intolerance and Discrimination against Christians dá conta de 30 casos na Europa, entre atos de vandalismo a igrejas, cemitérios, ataques a sacerdotes - um foi assassinado - ou mesmo a discriminação profissional por se ser cristão. Se a Nigéria é considerada o país mais perigoso para os católicos, o México é o inferno para padres, pois é aí que mais são assassinados. O Nascer do SOL entrevista Félix Lungu, um romeno a viver em Portugal há 31 anos, porta-voz, em Portugal, da fundação Ajuda à Igreja que Sofre (AIS). Esta organização faz relatórios sobre a liberdade religiosa no mundo, e tenta explicar onde as religiões são mais perseguidas e quais os desafios que enfrentam, com especial ênfase na Igreja Católica. Félix Langu, à semelhança dos seus chefes - a organização tem sede na Alemanha -, procura não alimentar divisões, mas é impossível fugir a factos: no Paquistão, só muito recentemente é que os empresários do lixo deixaram de recrutar obrigatoriamente cristãos; não faltam países fundamentalistas onde meninas de 10 anos são violadas e obrigadas a casar, ‘adquirindo’ automaticamente a religião islâmica; e são ainda muitas as nações onde os católicos não podem desempenhar cargos na função pública. O Vaticano calcula que, anualmente, são mortos cerca de cinco mil cristãos, mas a liberdade religiosa afeta também os muçulmanos moderados, que são alvo da ira dos fundamentalistas, acabando muitos deles assassinados. Qual o papel da Fundação Ajuda à Igreja que Sofre? A Ajuda à Igreja que Sofre, fundação Pontifícia, é uma organização que tem quase 80 anos e foi criada na Alemanha. Nasceu no final da Segunda Guerra Mundial para ajudar os refugiados alemães que se deslocavam pela Europa. Depois, pouco a pouco, ajudou cristãos dos países do Leste, por causa do comunismo, do ateísmo, de toda essa situação. Ou seja, não somos como a Cáritas, ou outras ONGs, no sentido de dar ajuda social, ou educação, ou saúde. Também chegamos a estas áreas, o foco, contudo, é a ajuda pastoral, ajudar a Igreja, ajudar sacerdotes, construir igrejas, formação de seminaristas, ajudar nas missões os missionários, com carros, com rádios, televisões, bíblias, o que é necessário para fazer a evangelização. Basicamente é isso e estamos em 24 países. A sede é na Alemanha, onde se faz a gestão de tudo isso. E nos outros 24 secretariados fazemos a angariação de fundos. Para fazer a angariação de fundos é preciso saber por que se pede dinheiro, por que se pede esta ajuda. Temos três pilares, digamos assim, da nossa missão: informar, rezar e ajudar. Informar é tentar dizer qual é a situação no mundo, sobretudo onde há carências, que tipo de carências, sempre com foco nesta dimensão pastoral ou de evangelização. Nos últimos anos, a Ajuda à Igreja que Sofre dedica-se ao estudo ou análise da situação da liberdade religiosa no mundo. Porque se nós somos uma organização da Igreja, e se temos parceiros em todo o mundo, em 186 países, é importante saber onde há carências, que tipo de carências são. E temos percebido que, por exemplo, no Médio Oriente, junto com as carências materiais, falta de escola, de saúde, da alimentação, há também esta dimensão da perseguição. Falta algo que valorizamos muito, que é a questão da liberdade religiosa, dos direitos, que estão valorizados no ocidente. O que fazem nesses países onde os cristão são perseguidos? Na Arábia Saudita, por exemplo, não há hipótese de haver uma igreja? Não, na Arábia Saudita não temos uma presença. A única presença nesses países é através da representação consular. É na capela de uma embaixada, por exemplo, de França ou de Itália, que se pode celebrar a missa, porque não há possibilidade de ter uma igreja na Arábia Saudita. Considerado o país do profeta, terra sagrada

articles.title: Calendar creștin ortodox joi , 22 octombrie 2026 . Rugăciunea către Sfinții șapte tineri din Efes , rostită pentru liniște sufletească și somn odihnitor
articles.summary: Calendarul creștin ortodox pentru joi, 22 octombrie 2026, îi pomenește pe Sfinții șapte tineri din Efes, cunoscuți și sub numele de „cei șapte adormiți”. Aceștia sunt sărbătoriți de Biserica Ortodoxă
articles.summary_zh: Calendarul creștin ortodox pentru joi, 22 octombrie 2026, îi pomenește pe Sfinșii șapte tineri din Efes, cunoscuźi și sub numele de "cei șapte adormiźi". Aceștia sunt sărbătoriźi de Biserica Ortodoxă
articles.title_zh: Calendar creștin ortodox joi, 22 octombrie 2026. Rugăciunea către Sfinźii șapte tineri din Efes, rstită pentru liniște sufletească și somn odihnitor
articles.content: Calendarul creștin ortodox pentru joi, 22 octombrie 2026, îi pomenește pe Sfinții șapte tineri din Efes, cunoscuți și sub numele de „cei șapte adormiți”. Aceștia sunt sărbătoriți de Biserica Ortodoxă de două ori pe an, pe 22 octombrie și pe 4 august. Povestea lor este legată de o peșteră din Muntele Ohlonului, unde, potrivit tradiției creștine, au dormit vreme de mai multe sute de ani. Credincioșii se pot ruga către aceștia pentru liniște sufletească și odihnă. Cine sunt Sfinții șapte tineri din Efes Sfinții șapte tineri din Efes sunt Maximilian, Exacustodian, Iamvlih, Martinian, Dionisie, Ioan și Constantin. Potrivit tradiției creștine, aceștia au trăit în vremea împăratului Deciu, când creștinii erau persecutați pentru credința lor. Pentru a se adăposti de prigoană, cei șapte tineri s-au retras într-o peșteră din Muntele Ohlonului, unde au adormit pentru mai multe sute de ani. Tot joi, 22 octombrie, Biserica Ortodoxă îl pomenește și pe Sfântul Averchie, episcopul cetății Ierapole din Frigia. În aceeași zi mai sunt pomeniți Sfântul Kukșa din Odesa, Sfântul Mucenic Alexandru episcopul, Mucenicul Iraclie, Anna, Elisaveta, Teodota și Glicheria, Sfântul Mucenic Zaharia, Sfântul Ruf și Cuviosul Lot. Rugăciunea către Sfinții șapte tineri din Efes, pentru liniște sufletească și odihnă Credincioșii care se confruntă cu griji și lipsa somnului pot rosti rugăciunea către Sfinții șapte tineri din Efes, cerând ajutor pentru dobândirea păcii sufletești. „Sfinților 7 tineri din Efes, care bine v-ați nevoit și cununa Împăratului Hristos ați dobândit, ne rugăm vouă, ca unii care multă îndrăzneală înaintea Domnului ați câștigat. Sfinților Maximilian, Exacustodian, Iamvlih, Martinian, Dionisie, Ioan şi Constantin, izbăviți-ne de lipsa somnului și puținătatea sufletului. Citește și: Carmen Harra, mesaj pentru populație! Ce s-ar putea întâmpla în 2027: “Nimeni nu spune adevărul!” Citește si: Andreea Pirui a fost prinsă de oamenii legii! Unde a fost găsită Voi, care în vremea împăratului Deciu, prigonitorul, ați fost pregătiți să luați cununa muceniciei, mărturisind dreapta credință și împotrivindu-vă tiranului celui fără de omenie, însă, din rânduială dumnezeiască, peștera în care v-ați adăpostit nu v-a fost vouă mormânt, ci s-a făcut vouă sân al lui Avraam, în care ați dormit somn adânc mai multe sute de ani şi, ca nişte prunci ce se încălzesc la sânul maicii lor, nu ați suferit nicio stricăciune. Iar în vremea binecredinciosului împărat Teodosie, din încredințarea Mântuitorului și pentru adeverirea Învierii celei de obște, v-ați trezit și v-ați arătat oamenilor, dând mărturie despre puterea lui Dumnezeu, apoi ați adormit cu adevărat întru odihna cea veșnică. O, preaslăvită minune, încât pretutindeni oamenii o au cunoscut. Deci, și acum, când gânduri negre vin asupra noastră, văzând cum slăbim cu duhul și cum ne descurajăm din lipsa somnului, acestea ne rod și ne macină sufletește, ca un vierme neadormit. Grijile cele apăsătoare, ca niște ulii la pradă, ne covârșesc și nu mai știm ce sunt pacea și odihna încrederii în Dumnezeu. Știm că toate acestea pentru păcatele noastre sunt. Știm că, pentru puțina noastră iubire de Dumnezeu și de aproapele, în astfel de mâhniri se afundă sufletul nostru. Cu pocăință ne rugăm și cerem ajutorul vostru, Sfinților din Efes, somn binecuvântat și mângâietor, spre pacea sufletului și odihna cea trupească, dăruiți-ne. Așadar, Sfinților ai lui Dumnezeu, prin ajutorul vostru, luminare și împăcare întru Hristos să găsim și cerul să îl dobândim. Amin.”

articles.title_zh: 十字架：所有基督徒被称为的苦难
articles.content: By Bradlee Dean October 21, 2026 “For unto you it is given on behalf of Christ, not only to believe in Him, but also to suffer for His sake…”-Philippians 1:29 When it comes to suffering, there is not a genuine Christian who is not appointed to it. Why? For His sake. “For we preach not ourselves, but Christ Jesus the Lord; and ourselves your servants for Jesus’ sake. For God, who commanded the light to shine out of darkness, hath shined in our hearts, to give the light of the knowledge of the glory of God in the face of Jesus Christ. But we have this treasure in earthen vessels, that the excellency of the power may be of God, and not of us. We are troubled on every side, yet not distressed; we are perplexed, but not in despair; Persecuted, but not forsaken; cast down, but not destroyed; Always bearing about in the body the dying of the Lord Jesus, that the life also of Jesus might be made manifest in our body. For we which live are always delivered unto death for Jesus’ sake, that the life also of Jesus might be made manifest in our mortal flesh. So then death worketh in us, but life in you. We having the same spirit of faith, according as it is written, I believed, and therefore have I spoken; we also believe, and therefore speak; Knowing that he which raised up the Lord Jesus shall raise up us also by Jesus, and shall present us with you. For all things are for your sakes, that the abundant grace might through the thanksgiving of many redound to the glory of God.” –2 Corinthians 4:5-15 I also realize that no one spoke of, or endured, suffering more than Christ, though ours are light in comparison (Isaiah 53), who told us before His ascension that as the Father sent Him, so He would send us (John 20:21). I have personally suffered, including fellowship with His sufferings, afflictions, trials, and testings, so that I might learn and grow from the lessons the Lord gives in the process (Psalm 119:71). Oftentimes we think we are in control of our own world; we may even deceive ourselves into believing we are trusting the Lord and are being led by His Spirit (Romans 8:14) when we are not, only to find that in the end we were all the while limiting Him through our means of control. For example, we can pray, Lord, increase our faith, or, Lord, oh, that I would grow in grace more so I might be just like you, and then, when He brings us through the process to learn the lessons, we lose control, and there it is: we find out who it is that we really are, and who it is that we really trust (John 3:6). We have heard some say that the Lord will never give us more than we can handle, and I have to say, this is not true whatsoever, because in many cases He brings us to the place of more than we can handle to show us what we cannot handle, to show us what it is that He can handle, and this with ease. This is done so that we trust not in ourselves (2 Corinthians 1: 5-10). In other words, our extremity is the Lord’s opportunity. You see, the root of fear is control, and throughout our lives we are taught to control every aspect of our lives so that we do not have to trust in the Lord (avoid suffering) that we may grow, though we claim that we are doing so. Then, when we lose that control, we have to trust the Lord in ways that we never have before, this where we suffer through our unbelief (though we hold to His Word) until we transition (by the Holy Ghost – Titus 3:5) into what it is that He means for us to be, and to see outside of our own limited controls in order to bring us into a larger place (Psalm 4:1). Isaiah 55:8-9 says, “For my thoughts are not your thoughts, neither are your ways my ways, saith the LORD. For as the heavens are higher than the earth, so are my ways higher than your ways, and my thoughts than your thoughts.” In conclusion: Through suffering, the Lord introduces us to His workings, so that we might see His faithfulness, to see His wonderful works which are His righteous operations in and through Christ, as we are confo
articles.content_zh:
2026年10月21日 布莱德利·迪恩 “为了你们,不仅为了信仰基督,而且为了他而受苦受难。” 关于受苦,没有一个真正的基督徒没有被任命。 为什么? 为他故. " 我们不是为自己而传教,而是为主而传教;我们是你们的仆人;

因为上帝命令光从黑暗中闪出,已经照亮了我们的心,在耶稣基督面前赋予了上帝的荣耀知识之光. 但我们有这个宝藏在地上, 权力的卓越可能来自上帝,而不是我们。 我们每边都忧心忡忡,却不忧愁;我们感到困惑,但不是绝望;我们受到迫害,但不是被遗弃;

我们有着同样的信仰精神,按照它所写的,我相信,因此我说过话;我们也相信,因而也说出话来;我们知道,复活主耶稣的人,也要由耶稣来养育我们,并将我们与你一同呈现.

万事都是为你着想的,丰厚的恩典,可以通过许多为上帝所荣耀而赞颂的恩惠来达到。” ——2 科林斯人4:5-15 我也意识到,没有人会说出或忍受比基督更痛苦的事,尽管我们的比喻是轻的(以赛亚53),在他升天之前,他告诉我们,正如父亲派遣他那样,他将派遣我们(约翰20:21)。

我个人遭受了痛苦,包括同他的痛苦、苦难、考验和试验的友谊,以便我能够从上帝在这一过程中提供的经验教训(第119:71段)中吸取并成长。 我们常常认为我们控制着自己的世界;

我们甚至可以欺骗自己,使我们相信我们信任主,并且正被他的精神所引导,而我们不是那样的,我们只是发现,我们最终通过我们的控制而限制他。

例如,我们可以祈祷,主,增加我们的信仰,或者,主, 哦,我将会在恩典中成长得更多,这样我或许就和你一样,然后,当他带我们走进吸取教训的过程时,我们失去控制,这就是:我们发现我们真正是谁,我们真正信任谁(John 3:6)。

我们听到有人说,上帝永远不会给我们 超过我们所能处理, 我必须说,这不是真的,因为在许多情况下, 他带我们到我们无法处理的地方 向我们展示我们无法处理的事 向我们展示他能处理的事 以及轻松处理的事 这样做是为了让我们不信任自己(2个哥林多1:5-10).

换句话说,我们的极限是上帝的机会。 你看,恐惧的根源是控制,在我们一生中,我们被教导要控制我们生活的方方面面,这样我们不必相信主(避免痛苦),以便我们成长,尽管我们声称我们这样做了.

然后,当我们失去这种控制时,我们必须以我们以前从未有过的方式信任上帝,这是我们通过不信而受苦的地方(尽管我们坚持他的话),直到我们(由圣灵-提图斯3:5)过渡到他对我们意味着什么,并且看到我们自己有限的控制之外,以便把我们带入更大的地方(Psalm 4:1).

以赛亚55:8-9说:"耶和华说,我的想法不是你们的,你们的道路也不是我的。

因为天比地高,我的道路也比地高;我的思想也比地高。” 最后:主通过苦难向我们介绍他的工作,以便我们看见他的忠诚,看到他的出色的作品,这是他在基督中和通过基督的正义行动,就像我们聚集在一起一样。

articles.title: De la pesadilla de Gaza al sueño de Fatma : cómo podemos seguir creyendo en la humanidad en medio del horror
articles.summary: “I have a dream”, decía Martin Luther King en 1963, cuando agitaba las conciencias desde las escalinatas del monumento a Lincoln en Washington, en uno de los discursos más emblemáticos de la historia.
articles.summary_zh: “我有一个梦想” ， decía Martin Luther King en 1963, cuando agitaba las conciencias desde las escalinatas del monumento a Lincoln en Washington, en uno de los discursos más emblemáticos de la historia。
articles.title_zh: De la pesadilla de Gaza al sueño de Fatma: cómo podemos seguir creyendo en la humanidad en medio del horror
articles.content: “I have a dream”, decía Martin Luther King en 1963, cuando agitaba las conciencias desde las escalinatas del monumento a Lincoln en Washington, en uno de los discursos más emblemáticos de la historia. Hoy, sin embargo, sólo siento ganas de decir: I have a nightmare. O mejor dicho: We have a nightmare, porque la pesadilla no sólo afecta a los palestinos, sino a todos nosotros, a cualquiera que cree que la “justicia” no es una palabra vacía. La vida de los palestinos es una pesadilla interminable. En Gaza oyes el ruido de los aviones, sientes el miedo de los bombardeos, el acecho de los drones –cada vez más traicioneros y sofisticados– que te siguen, te espían, te ensordecen y disparan. La vida cotidiana consiste en sobrevivir en tiendas de campaña desgarradas por el viento y llenas de barro. Compartir un baño con tanta gente que usarlo se vuelve imposible. Volver a una casa medio destruida por las bombas con el riesgo de que el techo se derrumbe y mate a tu familia. Afrontar el rigor del invierno –ya es el tercero desde que comenzó el genocidio–, sin ni siquiera unos libros que poder quemar para mantener a tus seres queridos, al menos a los niños y ancianos, en un lugar cálido y seguro. Sólo tiendas, frías en invierno, sofocantes en los tórridos veranos. Cuántos muertos, desplazados, huérfanos, heridos, mutilados… Y los que aún no han sucumbido al asedio total que impera desde hace más de dos años están condenados a sufrir hambre y sed, a no tener derecho a una asistencia sanitaria y a una supervivencia digna. En Cisjordania y en Jerusalén Este, los palestinos viven con el terror de despertarse en plena noche con un soldado que los apunta con un fusil a la cara, que destruye sus casas, que los amenaza, los humilla delante de sus hijos o se los lleva consigo, con sus pijamas manchados de pipí porque se han orinado encima de miedo. Mientras tanto, los colonos están cada vez más furiosos: los ataques a los pueblos, comunidades rurales, tierras, coches, ganado, están a la orden del día. Incluso en las cárceles hay casos documentados en los que se ha autorizado a periodistas y civiles israelíes a presenciar –e incluso a grabar con sus teléfonos móviles– los abusos infligidos a prisioneros palestinos, a quienes deberíamos llamar “rehenes”, dada la falta de garantías mínimas legales que caracteriza las detenciones israelíes en el territorio palestino ocupado. Esta fragmentación territorial, legal y política es la institucionalización de la excepción; es la transformación de la precariedad en condiciones permanentes; es un sistema en el que la ocupación militar y la colonización ya no son sucesos aislados, sino un régimen consolidado en el que el control no sólo se ejerce con las armas sino también mediante la planificación urbanística, la burocracia, la segmentación administrativa, con la creación de categorías jurídicas diferenciadas para personas que viven en el mismo espacio pero no bajo los mismos derechos. Y después de décadas, la violencia de esta época nos indica que hemos llegado a la fase final: la del genocidio, la de la guerra de Israel contra un pueblo que hasta ahora ha resistido como ha podido. La mujer que amasa el pan bajo los drones, el maestro que sigue enseñando bajo las tiendas, la familia que planta un limonero donde el día antes había una casa, las parejas que siguen casándose y –también en el infierno de Gaza– trayendo hijos al mundo. Es ahí donde la esperanza se vuelve radical: el sueño de un mundo que persiste y que, si nos esforzamos, puede mejorar. Este sueño es el corazón palpitante de la resistencia palestina En los últimos dos años las cosas han ido todavía a peor: el terror se ha vuelto omnipresente, cotidiano. Se trata de una pesadilla que ha alcanzado dimensiones delirantes a los ojos del mundo. Pero es cuando todo se derrumba a nuestro alrededor, entre el horror y la esperanza, que resulta indispensable comenzar a soñar. Para no sucumbir a la oscuridad de esos días, para intentar imaginar o al menos e

articles.title: Revd Beilieü Shüya : The Pioneer of Christian Revival Church in Arunachal Pradesh
articles.summary: Revd Beilieü Shüya (15.8.1928 to 18.9.2026), remembered as the first CRC woman to be ordained, passed away at the age of 98 in Kohima, leaving behind a remarkable legacy of Christian faith, missionary
articles.content: Revd Beilieü Shüya (15.8.1928 to 18.9.2026), remembered as the first CRC woman to be ordained, passed away at the age of 98 in Kohima, leaving behind a remarkable legacy of Christian faith, missionary commitment, education, and service. Her life was a testimony to perseverance, spiritual conviction, and obedience to the call of GOD, extending her influence beyond Nagaland into Arunachal Pradesh. The eldest of ten children of Lhousuohie Shüya and Zeno Dolie Shüya of Meriema village, she belonged to a family closely connected with the region’s Christian history. Her maternal grandfather was reportedly the second person from Khonoma village to embrace Christianity. Her mother was also the sister of Angami Zapu Phizo, the legendary Naga nationalist leader. An Exceptional Educational Journey Revd Shüya received her early education at Mission School, Kohima, before continuing her studies at Mission School, Golaghat, Government High School, Kohima, and Cotton College, Guwahati. She completed the first two years of her Bachelor of Arts degree at Scottish Church College, Calcutta, and her final year at Tribhuvan University, Nepal. Her academic achievements extended across several disciplines. She obtained a diploma from the International Montessori Association, Kolkata, completed a Perspective Course in Education at William Carey University, California, earned a Bachelor of Education degree from Utkal University, Bhubaneswar, and pursued a Master of Theology at Los Angeles University. She also earned a Master of Arts in Tenyidie from Ura Academy. Her educational background reflected a lifelong commitment to learning, teaching, and the development of people through knowledge and faith. A Life Transformed By The Holy Spirit A defining moment in her spiritual journey came in 1946, when she experienced what she described as the filling of the Holy Spirit. From then on, her life became increasingly devoted to Christian ministry rather than earthly popularity or recognition. In 1978, she was ordained at the World Mission Conference in Chennai, becoming the first CRC woman to receive ordination, according to accounts of her life. Her ordination represented a significant milestone for CRC women in Christian ministry and demonstrated her determination to serve despite the social and institutional challenges of her time. Her Christian convictions also brought hardship. She was imprisoned for her faith and reportedly imprisoned again in 1956 because of her family connection with A. Z. Phizo. During periods of imprisonment in Kohima, Nagaon, and Guwahati, she translated numerous passages of the Bible. Even confinement could not silence her commitment to GOD’S Word. Bringing The Revival Movement To Arunachal Pradesh Among her most significant contributions was her involvement in introducing the Christian revival movement to Arunachal Pradesh. Along with a few fellow believers and missionary friends, she helped bring a new spiritual impetus to Christian communities in the state. According to personal recollections, the early team undertook three days of fasting in a forest, seeking GOD’S guidance and spiritual empowerment. This pioneering work contributed to the establishment of the Christian Revival Church in Arunachal Pradesh. Her missionary journeys were not without opposition. There were occasions when the police reportedly attempted to arrest her for preaching the gospel in the state. Nevertheless, she continued her mission, demonstrating courage and perseverance in the face of persecution. I still vividly remember the excitement surrounding the visits of Miss Beilieü Shüya and Miss Rose, a missionary from Goa, to Jipu. People would say that GOD was going to perform signs, wonders, and miracles through their ministry. In Siji, where the community had embraced Christianity, the atmosphere within our families and the wider village was filled with spiritual enthusiasm and expectation. featured.title: Maxym Abramov: From Occupied Sloviansk to Army Chaplain
featured.summary: 🇺🇦Sloviansk· 2014 (came to faith); 5 May 2022 (wounded)
featured.summary_zh: 🇺🇦斯洛维扬斯克·2014年（归信）；2022年5月5日（受伤）
featured.title_zh: 马克西姆·阿布拉莫夫：从被占领的斯洛维扬斯克到军队牧师
featured.content: A City Struck In 2014 Maxym Abramov was a 16-year-old schoolboy in Sloviansk, in eastern Ukraine, getting ready to finish school. On 12 April that year Russia first struck his hometown, and the city was occupied. The occupation shattered the way he saw life. Depression closed in, and it drove him to the edge of suicide. That was when he found Christ. "My material world simply collapsed like a house of cards," he says. Two Metres Away Before he joined the army, Maxym volunteered at a rehabilitation centre for people struggling with addiction. Later he signed a contract with the army. On 5 May 2022, in the third month of the full-scale war, his unit held a stretch of front line under a barrage that lasted more than 12 hours. A fellow soldier sitting two metres behind him was hit in the neck by shrapnel and died instantly. Maxym was wounded in the arm. He was ordered to reach the evacuation point about a kilometre away, and he ran, fell, got up and ran again under fire. At the hospital in Bakhmut the doctors looked at his arm and said things looked grim. "The damage was so severe, I still don't know how God saved it. But He did." A Chaplain Who Listens In December 2024 Maxym became a certified military chaplain. He studies at Kremenchuk Seminary and the Ostroh Academy, and he cares for soldiers, veterans and the families of the fallen, the captured and the missing. "I've earned the right to speak to them about hope," he says. "But more often, my job is simply to listen." God met a teenager at the edge of his life in an occupied city. Eight years later, in a hospital in Bakhmut, He saved the arm the doctors said looked grim. "Even though I walk through the valley of the shadow of death, I will fear no evil, for You are with me" (Psalm 23:4).
featured.content_zh:
A City Struck 2014 Maxym Abramov是乌克兰东部斯洛维安斯克的16岁在校生,准备完成学业. 当年4月12日,俄罗斯首次袭击他的家乡,该城被占领. 占领摧毁了他对生活的看法。 抑郁症收缩了,使他陷入了自杀的边缘. 那时他发现了基督。

他说:“我的物质世界就像一栋牌屋一样崩溃了。” 在他入伍前,两个梅特雷斯·阿威(英语:Two Metres Away)志愿在一个康复中心为那些为瘾君子挣扎的人服务. 后来他与军队签订了合同. 2022年5月5日,在全面战争的第三个月中,他的部队在长达12小时以上的炮火下保持了前线的伸展.

一名坐在他身后两米的士兵被弹片击中颈部,当场死亡。 Maxym手臂受伤。 他被命令到达约一公里外的疏散点,他跑,倒,起来,又在火力下跑. 在Bakhmut的医院,医生看着他的手臂,说事情看起来很惨淡。 "损失如此严重,我仍然不知道上帝是如何挽救的.

但是,他做到了。" 2024年12月,马克西姆成为一名经认证的军事牧师。 他在克勒门丘克神学院和奥斯特罗学院学习,他关心士兵,退伍军人和阵亡者家属,俘虏和失踪者. "我赢得了跟他们谈论希望的权利,"他说.

"但更常见的是,我的工作只是倾听。" 上帝在被占领城市遇到一个少年 八年后,在Bakhmut的一家医院里,他救了医生说看起来很惨的手臂。 "即使我走过死亡之阴谷,我也不会害怕邪恶,因为你与我同在"(第23:4段)。

featured.title: 35 priests could not help her. In a church she saw Jesus crush what was choking her
featured.summary: 🇱🇰North Central Province· 2021
featured.summary_zh: 北中央省
featured.title_zh: 35位神父都无法帮助她。在教堂里，她看到耶稣粉碎了正在扼住她喉咙的东西。
featured.content: Chandra lived in a rural village in Sri Lanka's North Central Province, and she was slowly falling apart. Pain, weakness, a heart that raced for no reason doctors could name. She and her family were Hindu, so they did what they knew to do. They went to priest after priest. Thirty-five of them. Nothing changed. In July 2021 they walked into a church instead. As people prayed for her, Chandra saw something. Demons were trying to strangle her, and then Jesus Christ stepped in and stamped on them. She felt the pain and the sickness drain out of her body as they were defeated. In the vision Jesus spoke Scripture over her, from Psalm 34. "They looked to Him and were radiant," He said, and told her she would be radiant too if she trusted Him. The prayer a father prayed Her husband Dinesh, a day labourer, watched his wife come back to life and made God a promise. "God, if you will heal my wife, I will dedicate my daughter for your service." The whole family, who had barely heard the name of Jesus, gave their lives to Him. Their daughter Tenusha told her class what had happened, that her mother was free and that Jesus forgives sinners and makes them new. They did not keep it to themselves. A house church started in their home with four people. By now it is forty-six. Jesus is still stronger than whatever is choking the life out of you. He steps in, He stamps it down, and He calls you radiant.
featured.content_zh:
钱德拉住在斯里兰卡中北部省的一个乡村,她慢慢地分崩离析. 痛苦,软弱,一个无缘无故的心脏 医生无法命名 她和她的家人是印度教徒,所以他们做了他们知道的事。 他们跟随牧师去了牧师那里. 三十五门. 什么都没有改变。 2021年7月,他们走进了一座教堂。

当人们为她祈祷时,钱德拉看到了一些东西. 恶魔试图掐死她,然后耶稣基督介入并盖在他们身上. 她感到痛苦和疾病 排出她的身体 当他们被打败。 在视觉中,耶稣说圣经 超过她,从Psalm 34。 他说:他们崇拜他,而且赞颂他超绝万物。他说:她也超绝万物,如果她信任他。

一个父亲祈祷她的丈夫迪尼什(Dinesh),一个白天的劳工,看着他的妻子复活,并给上帝一个承诺. "上帝,如果你能治愈我的妻子, 我将奉献我的女儿为你服务。" 几乎听不到耶稣之名的全家都为他献出了生命.

他们的女儿特努沙告诉了班上所发生的事情,她的母亲是自由的,耶稣宽恕了罪人,使他们成为新人. 他们没有保守秘密。 一所房屋教堂在他们家中开始,共有4人. 时已四十六. 耶稣仍然比任何 扼杀你生命的东西更强大 他走进来,他把它印下来,他叫你光辉。

featured.title: Rakthai Sophia Loibl: Sold as a Child, Brought Back to Life by Jesus
featured.summary: 🇹🇭Bangkok· Over many years before 2025 (published March 2025)
featured.summary_zh: 🇹🇭曼谷·2025 年之前的许多年（2025 年 3 月发布）
featured.title_zh: Rakthai Sophia Loibl：被卖掉的童年，因耶稣而重获新生
featured.content: A Child Sold in Bangkok Rakthai Sophia Loibl's earliest memory is of crying inside a locked supply room in Thailand. When she was 3, her mother was selling her for a few days at a time as a child labourer. When she was around 4, her mother took her to a home in Bangkok, where a man paid 2,000 baht. Her mother never came back. The man was the imam of the local Muslim community, and Rakthai grew up as his slave labourer. Twice she gave birth to his daughters, and twice the baby was taken from her at once. A Gentle Voice At 25, pregnant for the second time, she began to hear a gentle whisper: It's okay. Just stay alive. "I didn't know who or what this voice was, but it comforted me; it was powerful yet gentle." One night, not long after the second birth, the voice woke her at three in the morning and told her to escape through the window. She did. Later she followed a man to Chicago, where for six and a half years he abused her. She tested positive for HIV and developed tuberculosis. Sent back to Bangkok, she lay in hospital for three months, paralysed, unable to see or to remember her own name. In her heart she cried out to Jesus: If you are with me, come save me. The doctors told her relatives to prepare for a funeral. Afraid she was contagious, they put her in a small house far from their homes in the village to wait for her to die. For six weeks she had only water. Then the voice spoke again: Live. "In that little house, I understood that it had been Jesus' voice all along," she says. "My wounds healed and my spirits lifted." One day she stumbled out of the wooden house, and her family, the villagers and the doctors were shocked. A pastor who had visited her in hospital brought her to a ministry called The Well, and there she gave her life to Jesus. Bread for the Imam God called her back to the community she had escaped, to forgive them and to love them. About eight years later the imam, dying of cancer, phoned and asked to see her. "I sat next to him as he lay bedridden, and he asked me to forgive him." Then he asked for bread and coffee. She remembered Jesus' command to love her enemies, handed him the bread, and felt the chains in her heart break. Before he died, the imam asked if she wanted her daughters back. Both now live with her. Rakthai founded Walk with Love, a Bangkok ministry to people in desperate situations across Thailand. "I am living proof that God is working in the darkness."
featured.content_zh:
曼谷的Rakthai Sophia Loibl最早的记忆是, 3岁时,她的母亲一次以童工身份出卖她几天. 在她4岁左右的时候,她的母亲带她到曼谷的一家家庭,一个男人在那里支付了2000铢. 她妈妈再也没有回来

此人是当地穆斯林社区的伊玛目,拉克泰作为奴隶劳工长大. 她两次生下他的女儿,两次一次把孩子从她身边带走。 一个温柔的声音在25岁, 怀孕了第二次, 她开始听到一个温柔的低语: 没事的 只要活着。 "我不知道是谁或是什么声音,但它安慰了我;

它强大而温柔" 一天晚上,在第二次出生不久后,声音在凌晨三点叫醒她,叫她从窗户逃走. 没错 后来她跟随一个男人去了芝加哥,在那里他虐待了她六年半的时间. 她检测出艾滋病毒呈阳性,并患上了肺结核。

她被送回曼谷,在医院里躺了三个月,瘫痪,无法看到或想起自己的名字。 在她的心中,她向耶稣喊叫: 如果你和我一起,来救我。 医生让她的亲戚准备葬礼 他们把她关在离他们家很远的小房子里,等着她死。 六周来她只有水

然后声音又说:生活。 "在那个小房子里,我明白这一直是耶稣的声音,"她说. "我的伤口痊愈,我的精神被解除" 一天,她从木屋中滑出,她的家人,村民和医生都感到震惊. 一位牧师曾到医院探望她,把她带到一个名为The Well的部里,在那里她把生命献给了耶稣.

为伊玛目神的面包把她召回了她已经逃离的社区,以宽恕和爱他们. 大约8年后,伊玛目死于癌症,打电话要求见她。 "我坐在他旁边,他躺在床上, 他要求我原谅他。" 然后他问面包和咖啡。

她记得耶稣命令要爱她的敌人,将面包交给他,并感觉到她心中的锁链断裂. 临死前,伊玛目问她是否想要女儿们回来. 现在都和她住在一起 Rakthai为泰国各地的绝望人士成立了曼谷部, "我活在证明上帝在黑暗中工作"

featured.title: A widow heard the good news from a travelling salesman and could not unhear it
featured.summary: Laos· 2022
featured.title_zh: 一位寡妇从一位推销员那里听到了好消息，从此念念不忘。
featured.content: Pei was a fifty-two-year-old widow in Laos, raised the way her whole village was raised, worshipping ancestors and local spirits in a place where the government pushes atheism and neighbours warn that following the God of foreigners will offend the gods of home. Then a salesman came through and, somewhere between selling his goods, told her about Jesus. Salvation as a gift, not a payment. Pei believed it. She let go of the ancestor worship she had carried her whole life and quietly followed Jesus instead. The cost at her own front door She was discipled in secret for four months, growing strong enough to speak. The first people she told were her daughter and her son-in-law, who happens to be a policeman. They did not celebrate. He threatened her, saying that if she did not stop believing in Jesus, they would report her, jail her, or throw her out. In June they made good on it, tossing her clothes into the yard and telling her to go live with the people who gave her this Jesus. She went. She did not go back. A widow with nothing chose Jesus over a roof, because she had found something no one could evict from her heart. Following Jesus is not always safe, but it is always worth it. What Pei found is worth more than what it cost her, and it is offered to you too.
featured.content_zh:
裴 was在老挝是一位52岁的寡妇,养大了整个村庄的养殖方式,在政府推崇无神论的地方崇拜祖先和地方灵灵,邻居警告说,追随外国人神会冒犯家乡神灵. 然后一个推销员走过来,在出售他的商品之间,告诉她耶稣的事. 救世是礼物,不是报酬

裴 believed信之. 她放弃了她毕生怀念的祖先的崇拜,悄悄地跟随耶稣. 在她自己的前门付出的代价 她被秘密地关了四个月, 变得足够强大,可以说话。 她告诉的第一个人是她的女儿和女婿,她们碰巧是一名警察。 他们没有庆祝。

他威胁她,说如果她不停止相信耶稣,他们会告发她,监禁她,或者把她赶出去. 6月,他们在上面做得很好,把她的衣服扔到院子里,并告诉她去和给她这个耶稣的人一起生活. 她去了 她去了吗? 她没有回去。 一个什么都没有的寡妇选择了耶稣 而不是一个屋顶, 因为她已经发现了一些没人能从她的心脏里赶走的东西。

追随耶稣并不总是安全的,但总是值得的. 裴氏发现的比付出的代价更值钱,也是献给你的.

featured.title: He found a Bible in a secondhand shop and thought he was the only Christian in Yemen
featured.summary: 🇾🇪Yemen· 2000s
featured.summary_zh: 🇾🇪也门·21世纪初
featured.title_zh: 他在一家二手商店里找到了一本圣经，以为自己是也门唯一的基督徒。
featured.content: Mohammad grew up in Yemen, in a conservative Muslim home, in a country with almost no visible church at all. About seventeen years ago he found a Bible in a secondhand shop. He took it home and read it in hiding, because being caught with it could cost him everything. What he read pulled him in, and he gave his life to Jesus. Then came a strange loneliness. "When I came to faith, I thought I was the only believer in Yemen," he said. "For a long time, I didn't know any other Yemeni Christians." He was never actually alone He was wrong about being alone, and God kept proving it. Mohammad and his wife Alima, who came to Jesus after reading the Gospels herself, had been unable to have children for seven years. They prayed, and the infertility ended. Once, in a car accident, Mohammad says he saw a white light in the shape of a cross. Slowly he found other Yemeni believers, received discipleship, and today helps lead a house church in one of the hardest places on earth to follow Jesus. The man who thought he was the only one is now helping build a family of them. If you feel like the only believer in your world, take heart. Jesus is already gathering people you have not met yet, and He has not left you on your own.
featured.content_zh:
默罕默德成长于也门,在一个保守的穆斯林家庭,在一个几乎完全没有可见教堂的国家. 大约十七年前,他在二手店里发现了一本圣经. 他带回家藏起来读,因为被抓到会损失一切. 他读到的东西把他拉进来 他把生命交给耶稣 然后出现了奇怪的孤独

"当我回到信仰中,我以为我是也门唯一的信徒,"他说. "很久以来,我不认识其他也门基督徒". 他从不孤单 他不该独自一人 上帝一直在证明 默罕默德和他的妻子阿利玛在亲自阅读福音书后来到耶稣身边,已经无法生育7年. 他们祈祷,不孕症结束。

有一次,在一次车祸中,默罕默德说看到十字架形状的白光. 他慢慢地找到了其他也门信徒,获得了门徒资格,今天帮助带领一所位于地球上最难的地方的房屋教堂追随耶稣. 认为自己是唯一一个的人 现在正在帮助他们建立一个家庭。 如果你觉得自己是世上唯一相信的人,请记住。

耶稣已经聚集了你们尚未认识的人,他没有离开你们。

featured.title: Karma said he had to earn heaven. At 17 he heard he could be forgiven
featured.summary: Rakiraki· 1990s
featured.summary_zh: 拉基拉基·1990年代
featured.title_zh: 因果报应说他必须修功德才能上天堂。17岁时，他听说自己可以得到宽恕。
featured.content: Simon Gounder was born into a strict Hindu family in Fiji. His great-grandfather had been shipped from India as a contract labourer after the British took the islands in 1874, and the family settled in a small village in the north of Viti Levu. Simon grew up inside a system with clear rules. "As a Hindu, we believed in karma," he said. "If you do good karma, you get to heaven. If you do bad karma, you will be punished." It was a ledger he could never quite balance. He knew his own wrongs too well. The night the ledger closed At seventeen, a friend invited him to a Christian youth meeting in another town. There he heard something that did not fit anything he had been taught. That Jesus Christ could simply forgive sins. Not offset them, not average them out over lifetimes. Forgive them. Simon felt the weight of his own failures and, for the first time, an offer to be free of them. "I gave my life to Jesus that night," he said. He hid it from his parents at first. When they found out, they were not happy. But the son who came home changed did not stop there. In time he led his whole family to Christ, and he went on to plant a ministry that carries the same forgiveness to others. Karma keeps a running tab you can never clear. Jesus tears the tab up. Whatever you are carrying tonight, He is still in the business of forgiving it all at once.
featured.content_zh:
西蒙·古德出生于斐济一个严格的印度教家庭. 他的曾祖父在1874年英国人攻占群岛后,作为合同工从印度被运走,全家定居在维提莱武北部的一个小村庄. 西蒙在一个有明确规则的系统中长大. "作为一个印度教徒,我们相信因果报应,"他说. "若作善因缘即得上天.

若作恶报果报果报果. " 这是他无法平衡的分类账 他对自己的错误太了解了 结账的那一晚 17岁时,一位朋友邀请他到另一个城镇的一次基督教青年会议. 在那里,他听到一些不符合他所教过的东西。 耶稣基督可以宽恕罪过

不抵消它们, 也不平均出一生。 原谅他们 西蒙感受到了自己失败的轻重,并首次提出摆脱这些失败. "当晚我把生命交给耶稣,"他说. 起初他瞒着父母 当他们发现, 他们不高兴。 但回家的儿子变了 并没有停下来。

时他带领全家来到基督身边,他继续栽培一个对别人同样怀有宽恕的部. 卡玛一直有追踪器 你永远无法清除 耶稣撕开标签。 无论你今晚携带什么 他现在仍然要马上原谅这一切

featured.title: A soldier who should have died in battle walked into a demon's shrine
featured.summary: 🇲🇲Myanmar· 2010s
featured.title_zh: 一名本应死于战斗的士兵走进了恶魔的神殿
featured.content: Pastor Dano was a soldier before he was a pastor. He came out of the battlefield alive when he had no reason to, and he never shook the sense of why. "I believe God preserved my life from death on the battlefield for a purpose," he said. The purpose showed up in a Buddhist village that wanted nothing to do with him. The vice chief's son was tormented, demon-possessed, and no one could help. Dano fasted and prayed for three days. Then, near midnight, he went to the shrine where the boy was and did the only thing he knew to do. "I called upon the name of the Lord," he said, "and the demon left the young man." The night the shrines fell silent Villagers said every evil spirit left the village at once. Dano went from shrine to shrine, praying against the darkness that had ruled the place for generations. The vice chief's family, who had braced for his anger, found grace instead. They gave their lives to Jesus, and four more families followed. The people who once opposed him now follow his lead. There is a church in that village today where there used to be shrines. The name of Jesus is still stronger than every dark thing that has ever frightened you. One believer, praying at midnight, was enough to set a whole village free.
featured.content_zh:
牧师达诺在担任牧师之前是一名军人. 他毫无理由地活着走出战场,从未动摇过为什么的感官. "我相信上帝为了某种目的在战场上拯救了我的生命". 宗旨现于一佛村中欲与他无相. 副宰相的儿子被折磨,妖魔吞噬,无人能助.

达诺斋戒祈祷三天. 然后,近午夜,他去了男孩所在的神殿,做了他唯一知道该做的事. "我呼唤天主之名,"他说:"妖魔离开了少年. 夜神社失声村民说 每一个邪恶的灵魂 立刻离开村庄

达诺从神社到神社,祈祷反抗历代统治这个地方的黑暗. 副局长的家族,他为愤怒而坚韧不拔,却找到了恩典。 他们把生命献给了耶稣,还有四个家庭随行. 曾经反对他的人现在遵循他的路线。 今天村里有一座教堂 曾经有神社

耶稣的名字仍然比每件令你害怕的黑暗事物更强大. 一个信徒在午夜祈祷 足以让整个村庄自由

featured.title: Juan Alberto: A Security Guard Set Free at His Post
featured.summary: 🇦🇷Buenos Aires· 7 to 8 November 2025 (came to faith); 7 June 2026 (baptised)
featured.summary_zh: 🇦🇷布宜诺斯艾利斯·2025年11月7日至8日（归信）；2026年6月7日（受洗）
featured.title_zh: 胡安·阿尔贝托：在岗位上获得自由的保安
featured.content: Twenty-Five Years of Spirit Worship Juan Alberto, 64, lives in Guernica on the outskirts of Buenos Aires, Argentina. For 25 years he practised Quimbanda, an Afro-Brazilian form of spirit worship built around spirit possession and ceremonies that promise success and protection. Tears at the Stadium In November 2025 he was working security at Vélez Sarsfield Stadium for the Esperanza Buenos Aires Festival with Franklin Graham. On the first day, the musicians rehearsing on stage were praising Jesus and singing of His love. Juan Alberto had never heard anything like it. As he listened, the Holy Spirit touched his heart, and he began to weep and could not stop. Soon he felt sick, asked his supervisor if he could go home, and told no one what had happened. The next day his niece Melany, a Christian serving as a prayer volunteer, came to say hello. She told him the Lord had prepared that night for him to feel His love. When Franklin Graham invited people to come forward and receive Jesus, Juan Alberto could not leave his post, so he prayed silently right where he stood. Later that night Melany asked if he had prayed. He said yes, with wet eyes, and told her everything. "He told me he knew and understood that God loved him and forgave him," she said. Idols Burned at His Baptism In the months after the festival he lost his job and his rental home. He kept going to church with Melany at Iglesia Conexión con Dios and joined a small group. On 7 June 2026 he was baptised, and he burned all the idols, garments and spirit-worship objects he had used in Quimbanda. Since then, God has restored his relationships. "I always used to say I was the lost sheep. I never imagined that God would take notice of me," he says. Jesus told of the shepherd who leaves the ninety-nine "and go after the one that is lost, until he finds it" (Luke 15:4). He found Juan Alberto at a security post, in the middle of his shift. "Something extraordinary happened to me. I had an encounter with God, and it was the most beautiful experience of my life."
featured.content_zh:
二十五年精神 宗教 Juan Alberto,64岁,住在阿根廷布宜诺斯艾利斯郊区的Guernica. 25年来,他一直信奉昆班达教,这是一种非洲裔巴西人的精神崇拜形式,它以拥有精神和仪式为基础,保证成功和保护。

2025年11月,他在Vélez Sarsfield体育场与富兰克林·格雷厄姆一起为Esperanza布宜诺斯艾利斯音乐节工作。 第一天,在舞台上排练的音乐人称赞耶稣并唱出他的爱. 胡安·阿尔贝托从未听过这样的话 他听了,圣灵感动了他的心,他开始哭泣,无法停止.

不久他觉得病了,问他的主管他能否回家,没有告诉任何人发生了什么事. 次日,他的侄女梅拉尼(英语:Melany)作为祈祷志愿者的基督教徒前来打招呼. 她告诉他当晚上帝已经准备让他感受到他的爱

当富兰克林·格雷厄姆邀请人们站出来接受耶稣时,胡安·阿尔贝托无法离开他的岗位,所以他默默地祈祷就站在原地. 当晚晚些时候,梅拉尼问他是否有祷告. 他同意了,用湿眼睛, 告诉她一切。 "他告诉我他知道并理解上帝爱他并原谅了他,"她说.

被洗礼烧伤的偶像 在节日结束后的几个月里,他失去了工作和租房. 他继续和梅拉尼一起在Iglesia Conexión con Dios教堂教堂,并加入了一个小团体. 2026年6月7日,他接受了洗礼,他烧掉了他在昆邦达使用的所有偶像,服装和精神败坏的物品. 此后,上帝恢复了关系.

"我常说我是迷路的羊. 我从未想到上帝会注意到我, 耶稣讲述了牧羊人离开九十九人"追寻失落者,直到他找到"(公爵15:4). 他发现胡安·阿尔贝托在一个保安哨所,在值班中间. "某事非同寻常发生在我身上.

我和上帝相遇过,这是我一生中最美丽的经历".

featured.title: Her church offering came to the exact amount of her power bill, to the penny
featured.summary: 🇺🇸United States· 2020s
featured.title_zh: 她的教会奉献金刚好等于她的电费，一分不差。
featured.content: Lina Johnson did not have enough to cover her power bill. She had told no one the amount. Not a friend, not her church, no one. It was her private worry, the kind you carry quietly and hope somehow resolves. That same week an offering came around at church for a family in need, and Lina gave what she could. Twenty-six cents. It was almost nothing, and she gave it anyway. Down to the penny The next day a friend told her the rest of the story. The offering the church had taken was for her. And when they counted it, it came to the exact amount of her power bill. To the penny. "The offering they took in church yesterday was for me," Lina said, "and it was the exact amount as my power bill. It was to the penny and I never told anyone how much my bill was." Here is the detail that undoes you. Had she given more than her twenty-six cents, the total would have overshot the bill, and the provision would have lost its edge. Even her small gift was part of God's arithmetic. God is not rounding up or guessing. He knew the number she never spoke aloud, and He met it precisely, through people who had no idea. The Father who counts the hairs on your head knows your bill too, down to the last penny.
featured.content_zh:
莉娜·约翰逊没有足够的钱来支付她的权力法案. 她没有告诉任何人这个数额。 不是朋友,也不是她的教堂,没有人 这是她的私人担忧, 你悄悄地携带的, 希望某种程度上解决。 在同一周,教堂里出现了一具供奉物,供奉一个有需要的家庭,莉娜尽了力. 26分钱. 几乎什么都没有,她还是给了它。

下到一分钱 第二天,一个朋友告诉她了其余的故事. 教堂的供奉是给她的 当他们数起来时, 她的权力法案的准确数额就到了。 至一分钱. "他们昨天在教堂里接受的献礼是给我的,"莉娜说,"这是确切的金额,就像我的权力法案.

我从来没有告诉任何人我的账单是多少". 这是让你难受的细节 如果她付出超过26美分,总额会超过法案,而规定会失去优势. 她的小礼物也是上帝算术的一部分 神不是围观或猜测。

他知道她从不大声说话的号码 他通过不知道的人 准确地认识了这个号码 算你头上头发的神父也知道你的帐单 一直到最后一分钱

featured.title: You can kill me, but you cannot take my faith in Jesus
featured.summary: 🇧🇩Bangladesh· 2021-2022
featured.title_zh: 你可以杀了我，但你不能夺走我对耶稣的信仰
featured.content: Nur Alam and Afzal Hosen left Islam to follow Jesus in 2021, and they were baptised soon after. They did not keep it quiet. They wanted the Muslim community they came from to know the Jesus they had found, so they handed out Bibles and booklets around their part of Bangladesh. That is when the trouble started. A group seized Nur and locked him in a room for thirty hours, no food, no water, no sleep, demanding he return to Islam and threatening to kill him and his family. He would not bend. "At some point during the interrogation," Nur said, "they became hopeless, seeing my strong faith in Jesus." A faith they could not confiscate Days after Nur was freed, they came for Afzal. They beat him and accused him of being paid to convert. His answer has the ring of the early church about it. "You can kill me," he told them, "but you cannot take my faith in the Lord Jesus away from me." Both men were released, bruised and exhausted and still standing. They had discovered the thing every threat runs into eventually. You can take a man's freedom, his comfort, even his life, but the faith Jesus plants in a heart is not yours to seize. If Jesus is worth that to two young men in Bangladesh, He is worth your whole life too.
featured.content_zh:
努尔·阿拉姆(Nur Alam)和阿夫扎尔·霍森(Afzal Hosen)于2021年离开伊斯兰教跟随耶稣,他们不久就接受了洗礼. 他们没有保持沉默。 他们希望来自他们的穆斯林社区了解他们找到的耶稣,于是他们散发了他们所在的孟加拉国地区的圣经和小册子. 这就是问题开始的时候。

一群人抓住努尔,把他锁在一个房间里30小时,没有食物,没有水,没有睡眠,要求他返回伊斯兰教,并威胁要杀死他和他的家人. 他不会弯腰的 "在审讯期间的某个时候,"努尔说:"他们变得无望,看到我对耶稣的强烈信仰". 努尔解放后,他们无法没收信仰,他们来到阿夫扎尔。

他们殴打他,并指控他被收钱皈依。 他的答案是早期教会的戒指 他对他们说:你们可以杀我,但你们不能夺走我对主耶稣的信仰。 两人被释放,伤痕累累,仍然站立. 他们发现了每个威胁最终都遇到的东西

你可以拿一个人的自由,他的舒适,甚至他的生命, 但是信仰耶稣植根于一个心脏 不是你的夺取。 如果耶稣对孟加拉国的两个年轻人来说是值得的,那么他也值得你一辈子。

featured.title: He was taught Christians do not pray. Then he watched his uncle pray before a meal
featured.title_zh: 他被教导说基督徒不祷告。然后，他看到叔叔在饭前祷告。
featured.content: Charles Yabaga Diarra grew up in a strict Muslim family in Lere, Mali, where Christians were mocked and misunderstood. His father, a headmaster and politician, ran the house like a school. As a boy, Charles fled about a hundred and fifty miles to stay with an uncle, and there he ran straight into something he had been told did not exist. His uncle, a Christian pastor, bowed his head and prayed before the meal. Charles was stunned. "Because we are Christians, we pray before meals," the uncle explained. Charles had been taught that Christians do not pray at all. That simple prayer, in his own language, lodged in him and would not leave. Just show me the way His father pulled him back and forced him into Quranic school, but the seed was planted. Years later, back with his uncle, tired and searching, Charles finally prayed his own prayer. "Lord, I'm really tired of seeking the truth. Just show me the way." A verse he had heard at a Vacation Bible School came back to him, and in November 1981 he gave his life to Jesus. The cost has been real. Charles is a preacher now, displaced by Mali's conflict and facing daily pressure. But he did not go alone. Of his fourteen siblings, most now follow Jesus, and around a hundred Christians gather at his extended family events. One uncle praying over dinner turned a whole family toward Jesus. Your quiet, ordinary faithfulness may be planting more than you know.
featured.content_zh:
查尔斯·亚巴加·迪亚拉(Charles Yabaga Diarra)在马里勒尔一个严格的穆斯林家庭长大,在那里基督徒受到嘲笑和误解. 他的父亲是一名校长和政治家,他像学校一样管理着房子. 童年时,查尔斯逃离了大约一百五十英里,与一个叔叔住在一起,在那里,他直接遇到了他被告知的东西并不存在.

他的叔叔,一位基督教牧师,低头祷告,在饭前祷告. 查尔斯被惊呆了 "因为我们是基督徒,我们吃饭前祈祷",叔叔解释道. 查尔斯被告知基督徒根本不祷告 用他自己的语言祈祷,他不会离开。

只要告诉我他父亲把他拉回来的方式 强迫他进入古兰经学校 但种子是种的 多年之后,与他的叔叔一起回来,疲惫和寻找,查尔斯终于自己祈祷. "主啊,我真的厌倦了寻找真相. "给我带路" 他在一所假期圣经学校听到的一首诗回到了他身边,1981年11月他把生命献给了耶稣.

代价是真实的。 查尔斯现在是一名传教士,因马里的冲突而流离失所,每天都面临压力。 但他没有一个人去。 他的十四个兄弟姐妹中,大多数现在都跟随耶稣,大约一百名基督徒聚集在他的大家庭活动中. 一个叔叔为晚餐祷告 整个家庭都向耶稣倾斜 你安静的,普通的忠诚 可能是种更多 比你知道。

featured.title: Kasih Tuhan Tiada Taranya
featured.summary_zh: p style="margin-bottom:1em; ">作者：Romauli br Marpaung Shalom，我叫 Romauli br Marpaung。
featured.title_zh: 上帝的爱是无与伦比的
featured.content: p style="margin-bottom:1em;">Oleh: Romauli br Marpaung Shalom, Nama saya Romauli br Marpaung. Saat ini, saya berusia 23 tahun. Saya berasal dari keluarga Kristen. Saya anak pertama dari lima bersaudara. Keluarga saya, dahulunya, bukan keluarga yang harmonis. Orang tua saya sering bertengkar. Namun, saat kelas IV SD, bapak saya bertobat sungguh-sungguh dan menyerahkan dirinya untuk diperlengkapi di Sekolah Alkitab Purbasari Pematang Siantar. Setelah selesai sekolah, beliau akhirnya diangkat menjadi seorang Pendeta, dan saya mulai pelayanan sejak kelas V SD di Gereja Kemuliaan Sion sebagai pemain musik tunggal. Pada 2013, saat saya lulus SMA, saya berharap bisa kuliah di Universitas Sumatera Utara (USU) Medan. Namun, saat mengikuti SBMPTN, saya gagal karena tidak lulus seleksi. Akhirnya, bapak saya mengusulkan supaya saya kuliah di Solo karena dia punya rekan pendeta yang anaknya kuliah di Solo juga. Saya mengikuti keinginan bapak saya karena beliau rindu saya bisa menjadi seorang hamba Tuhan. Akhirnya, saya kuliah di STT Berita Hidup, Solo, dan mengikuti semua kegiatan, aturan yang ada di kampus tersebut. Saya dibaptis saat duduk di bangku SMA kelas XI. Awalnya, saya kuliah di Berita Hidup karena orang tua dan pelarian, tetapi pada akhirnya saya bertobat dan percaya sungguh-sungguh kepada Tuhan Yesus saat kuliah semester 2. Pelayanan-pelayanan yang Tuhan percayakan kepada saya itu tidak mudah. Ada banyak masalah yang saya hadapi, baik itu dari asrama, tempat pelayanan, maupun kampus. Kalau bukan karena kekuatan Tuhan, mungkin saya tidak mampu. Namun, Tuhan Yesus baik, Dia memberi pertolongan saat saya benar-benar tidak mampu menjalaninya. Saya pelayanan di Gereja Bethel Tabernakel, Karanganyar. Saya mulai melayani di sana sejak Agustus 2014 sampai saat ini. Saya dipercaya untuk melayani di beberapa bagian, seperti melayani anak-anak sekolah minggu, pemuda/remaja, jemaat dewasa, maupun yang sudah lanjut usia. Selain itu, saya juga ambil bagian dalam musik, yaitu melatih anak-anak sekolah minggu belajar musik. Selain itu, saya juga diberi kesempatan oleh pendeta saya untuk membuka Bimbingan Belajar di Bibis Luhur Solo. Sewaktu kuliah, saya ditempatkan praktik tahunan di Gereja Kristus Rahmani Indonesia (GKRI), Jimbaran Bali. Tantangan yang saya hadapi adalah saya melayani orang-orang Kristen yang sudah berkeluarga, tetapi belum terikat dalam pernikahan. Saya juga membantu mengajar di PAUD Shinam, Jimbaran, milik gereja tersebut. Saya bersyukur untuk semua pelayanan yang telah dipercayakan gereja kepada saya. Saya bisa menjalani semua ini dengan pertolongan Tuhan. Yang saya rindukan dalam pelayanan adalah saya bisa memberikan yang terbaik untuk Tuhan dan gereja, menjadi berkat bagi banyak orang, dan tetap setia terhadap panggilan Tuhan. Saya juga rindu suatu saat saya bisa membuka pelayanan sendiri. Saya tahu itu tidak mudah, tetapi saya percaya kuasa pertolongan Tuhan nyata bagi saya. Kiranya kesaksian ini bisa menjadi berkat bagi semua orang, dan saya rindu kita tetap percaya bahwa segala sesuatu yang kita lakukan untuk Tuhan tidak akan kembali dengan sia-sia, melainkan Dia akan memberkati kita senantiasa (Kolose 3:23). Mulailah mengatakan bahwa pelayanan itu adalah sebuah kehormatan, bukan beban. Tuhan Yesus memberkati. "Dan, Maria berkata, "Sesungguhnya, aku ini hamba Tuhan. Terjadilah padaku seperti yang engkau katakan itu." Kemudian, malaikat itu pergi meninggalkannya."(Lukas 1:38, AYT)
featured.content_zh:
p style="margin-bottom:1em;">作者：Romauli br Marpaung Shalom，我叫 Romauli br Marpaung。我今年 23 岁。我来自一个基督徒家庭。我是五个兄弟姐妹中的老大。我的家庭以前并不和谐。我的父母经常吵架。

然而，当我上小学四年级时，我父亲真心悔改，并前往位于Pematang Siantar的Purbasari圣经学校接受装备。毕业后，他最终被任命为牧师，而我从小学五年级开始就在锡安荣耀教会担任独奏乐手。

2013 年，当我高中毕业时，我希望能在棉兰的北苏门答腊大学 (USU) 上大学。然而，在参加全国统一高考（SBMPTN）时，我因为没有通过选拔而落榜了。最后，我父亲建议我去梭罗上大学，因为他有一位牧师朋友，他的孩子也在梭罗上大学。我听从了父亲的意愿，因为他希望我能成为神的仆人。

最后，我在梭罗的生命福音神学院（STT Berita Hidup）上学，并参加了该校的所有活动，遵守了该校的所有规定。我在读高一的时候受洗。起初，我因为父母和逃避现实的原因而就读于生命信息神学院，但最终我在第二学期时悔改并真心信靠主耶稣。

神托付给我的服侍并不容易。我面临着很多问题，无论是来自宿舍、事工场所还是校园。如果不是因为上帝的力量，我可能无法做到。然而，主耶稣是良善的，当我已经实在无法承受时，祂会伸出援手。我在卡朗亚尔的伯特利会幕教会（Gereja Bethel Tabernakel）服侍。

我从 2014 年 8 月开始在那里服侍，至今仍在继续。我受托在几个部门服侍，例如服侍主日学儿童、青年/青少年、成年会众以及老年人。此外，我还参与音乐方面的工作，即指导主日学儿童学习音乐。

此外，我的牧师还给了我机会，在梭罗的Bibis Luhur开设学习辅导班。在大学期间，我被安排在巴厘岛金巴兰的印度尼西亚基督慈悲教会（GKRI）进行年度实习。我面临的挑战是我要服侍那些已经有家庭但尚未缔结婚姻的基督徒。

我还协助在属于该教会的金巴兰 Shinam 幼儿教育中心（PAUD Shinam）进行教学。我感谢教会将所有这些事工托付给我。在神的帮助下，我能够做到这一切。我在侍奉中渴望的是，我能够为上帝和教会尽我所能，成为许多人的祝福，并始终忠于上帝的呼召。

我也希望有一天我能自己开办一间教会。我知道这并不容易，但我相信上帝的帮助对我来说是真实的。愿这个见证能成为所有人的祝福，我希望我们能继续相信，我们为神所做的一切都不会徒劳无功，祂必会永远赐福于我们（歌罗西书 3:23）。

开始说服自己，服侍是一种荣誉，而不是一种负担。愿主耶稣赐福。 “马利亚说：‘我是主的使女。愿照你的话成就在我身上。” 天使就离开她去了。”（路加福音 1:38，AYT）
