featured.title_zh: 印度奥里萨邦教堂遭暴徒袭击后被拆除
featured.content: A church in India’s eastern state of Odisha was demolished under the supervision of government authorities the day after its owner reported that villagers had vandalized the building, raising fresh concerns about the treatment of Christian minorities in the region. The Beersheba Church, located in Patraguda village in Koraput district, was damaged on Nov. 21 by a group of men who entered the property with pickaxes and hammers, pulled down a cross, and damaged part of a wall. Durjan Harijan, the local Christian who built the church, filed a police complaint naming seven alleged attackers. The next day, Nov. 22, police and local revenue officials demolished the remaining structure in public view. Harijan told The Indian Express that the church was built beside his home for his family, which he described as the only Christian household in the predominantly tribal village of about 900 residents. He said the land belonged to his father. The church served as a place of Sunday worship for his family and other Christians from nearby communities. Harijan also said that some villagers had begun attending services in recent months, prompting accusations that he was attempting to convert people to Christianity. He denied the allegations and said villagers verbally abused him and his family before the church was vandalized. Seeking Justice Police registered a First Information Report (FIR), the formal document initiating a criminal investigation in India, against seven individuals based on Harijan’s complaint. The charges reportedly include offenses related to property damage and acts committed with common intention. As of Nov. 25, police said the investigation remained underway and did not confirm any arrests. Pastor Franklin Josobonto said he joined about 40 other pastors in approaching the police station on Nov. 21 to seek action against those responsible for the vandalism. He told UCA News that villagers subsequently asked police not to pursue the complaint. Local officials offered a different account of the church’s demolition. Kotpad Tehsildar Parsuram Bhatra told The Indian Express that authorities visited the village after the vandalism report and held a peace meeting. During the meeting, villagers alleged that the church was built on government land. Officials then issued Harijan a show-cause notice asking why the structure should not be demolished. Bhatra said Harijan removed the building after receiving the notice. Kotpad police also stated that Harijan carried out the demolition. However, Harijan disputed that account, saying he was pressured to arrange the machinery and is seeking legal advice about taking the matter to court. The dispute over the land has not been independently resolved. Bhatra said a revenue official had been asked to submit a report on the property and demolished structure, with further action to follow. Christian leaders criticized the circumstances surrounding the demolition, particularly its timing so soon after the reported attack. Bishop Pallab Lima of the United Believers Council Network of India described the action as an alarming failure by local authorities to protect the Christian community. Ismail Patro, general secretary of the National Christian Front, visited Patraguda and said seven Christian families lived in the village. Three families had already left because of fear, intimidation, and persecution, he told UCA News. Patro said Christian representatives planned to approach the district’s senior administrator to request an official investigation and restoration of the church. Growing Hostility The incident comes amid longstanding concerns about anti-Christian hostility in Odisha. Christians account for approximately 2.77% of the state’s population of 42 million, according to figures cited by UCA News. The state has experienced some of India’s most serious episodes of anti-Christian violence. In 2008, coordinated attacks by extremist Hindu mobs in Kandhamal district killed more than 100 Chris
featured.content_zh:
印度东部奥迪沙邦的一所教堂在政府当局的监督下被拆除,次日,该教堂的主人报告说,村民破坏该建筑,引起人们对该地区基督教少数民族待遇的新关切. 位于科拉普特区帕特拉古达村的比尔谢巴教堂于11月被损坏.

由一行人用取斧和锤子入地,取出十字架并损坏了一堵墙的一部分. 建造教堂的当地基督教徒Durjan Harijan向警方提出申诉,指控7名据称袭击者。 次日(11月22日),警方和地方税收官员在公众视野中拆除了所剩建筑.

哈里扬告诉"印度快报",这座教堂是在他的家旁边为他的家人而建的,他形容这家是以部落为主的约900名居民村中唯一的基督教家庭. 他说土地属于他父亲 教堂作为他的家人和附近社区的其他基督徒的礼拜场所.

哈里扬还说,近几个月来,一些村民开始参加礼拜会,引起他试图将人们皈依基督教的指控. 他否认这些指控,并说村民在教堂被破坏之前对他及其家人进行辱骂.

根据Harijan的控诉,寻求司法警察登记了第一份资料报告,这是在印度启动刑事调查的正式文件。 据报告,这些指控包括与财产损失有关的犯罪和出于共同意图实施的行为。 截至11月25日,警方称调查仍在进行,没有证实有任何逮捕。

Franklin Josobonto牧师说,他与其他大约40名牧师一起于11月21日接近警察局,寻求对破坏行为责任人采取行动. 他告诉UCA News,村民们后来要求警察不要追诉. 当地官员对教堂被拆除的情况提出了不同的说法.

Kotpad Tehsildar Parsuram Bhatra告诉"印度快报",当局在破坏报告后访问了该村并举行了一次和平会议. 会议期间,村民声称教堂是建在政府用地上. 官员随后向Harijan发了一张展会,因为通知询问为何该建筑不应被拆除. 巴特拉说,哈里扬收到通知后拆除了大楼.

克特帕德警方还称哈里扬进行了拆除. 然而,Harijan对该说法提出异议,说他受到压力,要安排机器,并正在寻求关于将此事提交法院的法律咨询。 土地纠纷尚未独立解决.

Bhatra说,已要求一名税务官员提交关于财产和被拆除建筑的报告,并随后采取进一步行动。 基督教领袖们批评了拆除的周围环境,特别是在报道的袭击发生后如此快的时间.

印度联合信徒理事会网络的Pallab Lima主教称,这一行动是地方当局在保护基督教社区方面的令人震惊的失败。 全国基督教阵线总书记伊斯梅尔·帕特罗(Ismail Patro)拜访了帕特拉古达并说有七个基督教家庭住在该村.

由于恐惧、恐吓和迫害,三个家庭已经离开。 Patro说,基督教代表计划与该区的高级行政人员接洽,要求正式调查和修复教堂。 日益严重的敌意 这一事件是在对奥迪沙反基督教敌意的长期关切中发生的。

基督教徒约占全州4200万人口的2.77%, 印度经历了一些最严重的反基督教暴力事件。 2008年,Kandhamal区的极端印度教暴徒协同袭击,杀害了100多名克里斯。

featured.summary_zh: 我想我们都听过这句话的各种版本：“建立声誉需要20年，但毁掉它只需要5分钟。” 经过多年荣誉、成功或出色领导而建立起来的好名声，在不道德行为曝光的那一刻就会毁于一旦。另见零散文章（2月13日）《罪人对自己的看法》《不信的真正本质》
featured.title_zh: 花20年时间建造的东西，5分钟就能摧毁
featured.content: I think we’ve all heard many variations of the adage, “It takes 20 years to build a reputation, but only five minutes to destroy it.” A good name that has been established through many years of honor, success, or skilled leadership can be ruined in a moment when an act of immorality comes to light. Until a couple of weeks ago, Jensen Huang seemed to be on top of the world. While Nvidia, the company he co-founded, had long been a Silicon Valley success story, the rise of AI had driven it to new heights of success and its CEO to new heights of prosperity. Nvidia became the most valuable company in the world, its market capitalization of nearly $6 trillion surpassing even Apple’s. Huang’s net worth soared to over $200 billion, making him one of the wealthiest men in the world and one of the richest men in history. His two children have advanced positions within the company and his wife of more than 40 years distributes vast sums of money through their charitable foundation. Huang carefully curated his reputation and, as is so often the case in Silicon Valley, his image, with his slick black leather jackets becoming his trademark. Today, of course, Huang is no longer CEO of Nvidia or anything else. He was forced to resign after it came to light that he had engaged in extramarital affairs with multiple women, one of whom is allegedly a Chinese spy and another of whom is reportedly a subordinate within Nvidia. His image was shattered in a moment, and his reputation is now in tatters. The company lost over half a trillion dollars of value in the aftermath—value that was subtracted from Huang’s wealth, of course, but also from that of everyday investors whose wealth is far more modest. Pictures of his wife and children were splashed all over the news, and stories about his exploits were printed in every major media outlet in the world. The harm to his reputation is beyond repair, yet must pale in comparison to the harm and shame he has brought to his family. I hope that as Huang ponders what has become of his life, he has the wisdom to ask this: was it worth it? I hope each one of us asks the same, for Huang is not the first person to be tempted to grave sin , nor the first to succumb to temptation. In different ways and to different degrees, that is a battle we all fight every day. I have no experience of committing adultery, but I understand that it is exhilarating, and that doing what is forbidden delivers a great rush. And I suppose it must be exhilarating, for why else would a person risk so much to pursue it? Why else would a person do something that so defies common sense? Why else would a person gamble everything for the sake of illicit, fleeting pleasures? News reports describe him, in his final days at the company, calling himself “a piece of [expletive].” And while I wouldn’t phrase it that way, he’s not wrong that this situation has exposed him as what he truly is, and it’s actually far worse than the way he describes it. I might choose the word “wretch” to describe him, and not just him, but all of us. We are all wretches, for we are all wretched, people who trade short-term pleasure for long-term pain and fleeting joys for enduring sorrows. Sin makes us act like madmen, for sin is madness. And it leaves us wretched—desperately unhappy and in the sorriest of states. There has never been a sin that was more wise than foolish. There has never been a sin that delivered more gratification than the satisfaction of obedience. There has never been a sin that was worth more than the honor of a good name and an upstanding reputation. Thankfully, there has never been a sin that is beyond Jesus’s capacity to forgive. Though time and again we, like Huang, succumb to temptation, time and again Jesus forgives those who humble themselves before him to confess their sin and ask his forgiveness. May we all have the wisdom to see ourselves in Huang and to see in him a vivid example of the reality that sin promises joy while delivering sorr

我认为我们都听过许多不同的说法, “要建立名声需要20年, 一个通过多年的荣誉,成功,或熟练的领导而建立的良好名声,在不道德行为被揭发的一瞬间,可能会被破坏. 直到几周前,黄詹森似乎已经登上世界之巅.

虽然他共同创办的公司Nvidia长期是硅谷的成功故事,但是AI的崛起却将它推向了新的成功高地,其CEO也推向了新的繁荣高地. Nvidia成为了世界上最有价值的公司,其近6万亿美元的市场资本化甚至超过了苹果公司。

黄克诚的入股净值飙升至2000多亿美元,使他成为了世界上最富有的人之一,也是历史上最富有的人之一. 他的两个孩子在公司中担任高级职务,40多来年的妻子通过他们的慈善基金会发放一大笔钱.

黄克诚仔细地整理了自己的名声,并像硅谷经常出现的情况一样,他的形象被他浮出水面的黑色皮夹克也变成了他的商标. 今天,当然,黄已经不是恩维迪亚的首席执行官了

在得知他与多位妇女有婚外情后,他被迫辞职,其中一人据称是中国间谍,另一人据报是恩维迪亚的下属。 他的形象在一瞬间被打碎了,他的名声现在已经破灭了.

当然,该公司在事后损失了超过5万亿美元的价值 -- -- 当然,这一价值已经从黄家的财富中减去,同时也从日常投资者的财富中减去。 他妻子和孩子的相片被溅遍新闻,关于他剥削的故事被印入了世界上每一个主要的媒体渠道.

对他名誉的伤害是无法修复的,然而与他给家人带来的伤害和耻辱相比,必须苍白. 我希望,当黄帝思考他人生的结局时,他有智慧去问:这值得吗? 我希望我们每个人都问同样的问题 因为黄先生不是第一个 被严重罪孽诱惑的人 也不是第一个屈服于诱惑的人

我可能选择“错误”一词来形容他,而不仅仅是他,而是我们大家。 我们都是弱者,因为我们都是可怜人,他们以短期快活换取长期痛苦,以短暂的快活换取持久的悲伤。 罪恶让我们像疯子一样 因为罪恶就是疯狂 它使我们悲惨地 -- -- 极不幸福地 -- -- 在最烦恼的州里。

从未有过比愚蠢更明智的罪恶. 从来没有过罪过能带来比服从满足更多的满足. 从来没有一个罪过比一个好名声的荣誉和崇高的名声更值钱. 值得庆幸的是,从未有过耶稣无法宽恕的罪恶.

虽然我们像黄帝一样,一次又一次地屈从于诱惑,但耶稣一次又一次地原谅那些在他面前谦卑自卑的人,以忏悔他们的罪过并请求他的宽恕. 愿我们都有智慧去见自己在黄道上,在黄道上看到一个生动活泼的事例,说明罪恶许诺欢快,同时施以哀伤

featured.content: The following is the substance of a pamphlet published by Archibald G. Brown, a student and then great ally of C. H. Spurgeon in the cause of the gospel in London. Brown here draws attention to a practice that was gaining ground in the churches of his day: that of holding ‘amusements’ of various kinds, which obscured, diverted from, and in some cases replaced the proper ministry of local churches. Brown was savagely attacked in the wake of the publication of the pamphlet, derided as ‘a kill-joy,’ ‘a morbid pietist,’ and ‘a sour bigot.’ His meaning, however, had been deliberately misrepresented. 1 Brown nowhere objects to all amusement per se , but amusement which masquerades as ministry, distracting the church and deceiving needy sinners. While the context in which Brown wrote may be different from ours, we need to hear his burden for a Church—and for Christians—to make a decisive break with the world and its practices. An Evil in the Camp of the Lord DIFFERENT days demand their own special testimony. The watchman who would be faithful to his Lord and the City of his God has need to carefully note the signs of the times and emphasize his witness accordingly. Con­cerning the testimony needed now, there can the little, if any, doubt. An evil is in the professed camp of the Lord—so gross, so brazen in its impudence—that the most short-sighted of spiritual men can hardly fail to notice it. During the past few years it has developed at an ab­normal rate, ever for evil. It has worked like leaven until now the whole lump ferments. Look which way you may, its presence makes itself manifest. There is little if any­thing, to choose between Church, Chapel, or Mission Hall. However they may differ in some respects, they bear a striking likeness in the posters that figure upon and dis­figure their notice boards. Amusement for the people i s the leading article advertised by each. If any of my readers doubt my statement, or think my utterance too sweeping, let them take a tour of inspection and study “the announce­ments for the week” at the doors of the sanctuaries of the neighbourhood; or let them read the religious advertise­ments in their local papers. I have done this again and again, until the hideous fact has been proved up to the hilt, that “amusement” is ousting the preaching of the gospel as the great attraction: “Concerts,” “Entertain­ments,” “Fancy Fairs,” “Smoking Conferences,” “Dramatic Performances,” are the words honoured with biggest type and most startling colours. The burden of the Lord is upon me in this matter The Concert is fast becoming as much a recognised part of church life as the Prayer Meeting, and is already, in most places, far better attended. “Providing recreation for the people” will soon be looked upon as a necessary part of Christian work and as binding upon the Church of God, as though it were a Divine command, unless some strong voices be raised which will make themselves heard. I do not presume to possess such a voice, but I do entertain the hope that I may awaken some louder echoes. Anyway, the burden of the Lord is upon me in this matter, and I leave it with Him to give my testimony ringing tone, or to let it die away in silence. I shall have delivered my soul in either case. Yet the conviction fills my mind that in all parts of the country there are faithful men and women who see the danger and deplore it and will endorse my witness and my warning. Gratifying the Flesh and Retaining a Comfortable Conscience It is only during the past few years that “amusement” has become a recognized weapon of our warfare and de­veloped into a mission. There has been a steady “down grade” in this respect. From “speaking out,” as the Puri­tans did, the Church has gradually toned down her testi­mony; then winked at and excused the frivolities of the day. 在过去几年里,它以异常的速度发展,永远是邪恶的。 直到现在,它一直工作着,就像离开一样。 看看你们可以走哪条路,它的存在就变得明显了。 教会、礼拜堂或传教堂之间几乎没有任何选择。

然而,它们在某些方面可能有所不同,它们在海报上带有惊人的相似性,这些海报上显示它们的通知板并毁容。 为人民提供娱乐 我是每篇广告的主要文章

如果我的读者怀疑我的发言,或者认为我的言论过于笼统,让他们巡视视察,在附近圣所门口研究“一周的公告”;或者让他们在当地报纸上阅读宗教广告。

在令人发指的事实被证实之前,我一再这样做,即“辱骂”正在驱使福音的传道成为伟大的取景:“关注”、“参与”、“盛会”、“吸烟会”、“戏剧表演”是用最出名和最令人惊叹的颜色表达的言论。

主的重担在我这里 音乐会正迅速成为教会生活中 公认的部分 与祈祷会一样 并且已经,在大多数地方,

“为人民提供娱乐”将很快被视为基督教工作的必要部分,对上帝的教会具有约束力,似乎这是神的命令,除非有人发出强烈的声音,让自己听到。 我并不认为拥有这种声音,但我确实希望能够唤起一些更响亮的回声。

无论如何,上帝的重任 由我负责这件事, 我留给他 让我的证词响亮的语气, 或者让它静静地死去。 无论哪种情况,我都会送出我的灵魂 然而,这一信念使我满怀信心,即全国各地都有忠实的男女看到这种危险并对此感到痛惜,并将赞同我的证人和我的警告。

修行并保持舒适的良知 直到过去几年,“暴行”才成为我们战争的公认武器并发展成一个特派团。 这方面的“级别”稳步下降。 正如普里坦人所做的那样,教会从“大声疾呼”开始,逐渐淡出她的遗言;然后轻视并原谅了今天的纷争。

然后,她在边境上容忍他们,现在她收养了他们,在“影响群众,让人民听到他们的声音”的恳求下,为他们提供了家园。

featured.title_zh: 加剧迫害第4部分（共4部分） ：当经济压力结束时，迫害开始了
featured.content: By ICC Fellow Lisa Navarrette For years, Fadi has told his children the same thing: We stay. He is a Christian father in Lebanon. His family has lived in the same town for generations, and his parents are buried nearby. Fadi’s children were baptized in the church where he married his wife, Nour. His small business survived political unrest, the economic collapse, the Beirut port explosion, and another round of regional conflict. Leaving always felt like surrender. But lately, the calculation has changed. Fuel costs have risen again. Groceries take a larger share of the family’s income. Electricity is unreliable, so the business depends partly on a generator. Transportation costs more. His oldest daughter has been accepted to a university abroad, while his younger son talks openly about finding work in Europe. One evening, Fadi places two folders on the kitchen table. One contains bills. The other contains immigration documents. “We don’t have to decide tonight,” she said. Fadi looks at the paperwork for a long time. Years earlier, violence made the family afraid to leave home. Now economics is making them wonder whether they should leave the country. That is the final link in the chain this series examines. Fighting to Stay High fuel prices do not create religious persecution. But when families have already endured violence, displacement, discrimination, destroyed livelihoods, or political instability, rising energy costs can make recovery harder and staying less sustainable. In 2026, the World Bank warned that the Middle East conflict had created a major energy shock, raising fuel prices, increasing inflation, disrupting transportation and logistics, and weakening economic growth. Its October 2026 regional economic update found that fragile and conflict-affected economies were experiencing especially severe pressure , with poverty still rising in parts of the region even as it declined elsewhere. Those regional trends eventually become household questions: Can the business stay open? Can the family still afford food? Will there be jobs for the children? Is rebuilding worth the cost? Lebanon illustrates how those pressures can accumulate. Christians there have not experienced the same mass expulsion seen in parts of Iraq or Syria, but International Christian Concern (ICC) has documented how economic collapse, political instability, regional conflict, and emigration continue to weaken one of the Middle East’s most important Christian communities. No single crisis explains why a family leaves. That is what makes the process easy to overlook. A Christian family may survive violence but lose its savings. It may survive political instability but lose its business. It may rebuild after displacement only to discover that electricity, fuel, food, and transportation have become increasingly expensive. Eventually, the question is no longer only whether the family is safe. It is whether the family can build a future. Affording Daily Life The same dynamic is evident in Syria, where many people have tried to return after years of war. In May 2026, ICC reported that about 1.67 million refugees and 1.9 million internally displaced Syrians had returned since December 2024. Yet the agency warned that damaged housing, limited livelihoods, weak infrastructure, poverty, and restricted access to basic services continued to threaten the sustainability of those returns. A separate 2026 assessment hosted by UNHCR reached a similar conclusion : whether people remain after returning depends heavily on housing, employment, services, and economic opportunity. For Christian communities, that distinction matters. Imagine a family returning to a Syrian town after years abroad. They repair part of their home. Their children reenter school. The father begins rebuilding a small business. Then expenses start adding up. Electricity remains unreliable. Fuel for the generator costs more. Transportation to work and school takes a larger share of income. Food prices

由ICC研究员莉萨·纳瓦雷特(Lisa Navarrette) 多年来,法迪对他的孩子说了同样的话:我们留下。 他是黎巴嫩的基督教父亲. 他的家族世代居住在同一个城镇,父母也葬在附近. Fadi的孩子在与妻子Nour结婚的教堂接受洗礼。

他的小企业在政治动荡,经济崩溃,贝鲁特港口爆炸以及另一轮区域冲突中幸存下来. 离开总是觉得投降。 但最近,计算方式发生了变化。 燃料成本再次上升。 食谱占家庭收入的较大份额。 电力不可靠,因此业务部分依赖于发电机. 运输成本更高。

他的大女儿被录取到国外的一所大学,而小儿子则公开谈论在欧洲找工作. 一天晚上,法迪把两个文件夹放在厨房桌子上. 一个有账单。 另一个文件载有移民证件。 “我们不必在今晚决定, 法迪很长一段时间都在看文件 几年前,暴力使家庭不敢离家。

现在经济学让他们怀疑他们是否应该出国。 这是本系列审查的链条的最后环节。 高油价斗争不会造成宗教迫害。

但是,当家庭已经忍受了暴力、流离失所、歧视、生计被摧毁或政治不稳定时,能源成本的上升会使恢复更加困难,并降低可持续性。

2026年,世界银行警告说,中东冲突造成了严重的能源冲击,燃料价格上涨,通货膨胀加剧,交通和后勤中断,经济增长减弱.

其2026年10月的区域经济最新情况发现,脆弱和受冲突影响的经济体正承受着特别严重的压力,该区域部分地区的贫困现象仍在加剧,尽管其他地区的贫困状况有所下降。 这些区域趋势最终成为家庭问题:企业能否继续开放? 家人还能买得起食物吗? 孩子们会有工作吗?

重建值得付出代价吗? 黎巴嫩说明了这些压力如何能够累积。 但国际基督教关注组织(ICC)记录了经济崩溃、政治不稳定、地区冲突和移民继续削弱中东最重要的基督教社区之一。

没有一个危机能解释一个家庭为什么离开。 这使得这一进程容易被忽视。 一个基督教家庭可能会在暴力中幸存下来,但却会失去积蓄。 它可能在政治不稳定的情况下生存下来,但失去了业务。 它可能在流离失所后重建,只为了发现电力、燃料、粮食和交通越来越昂贵。

最后,问题不再仅仅是家庭是否安全。 家庭是否能够建立未来。 每日生活 同样的动态在叙利亚也很明显,许多人在多年战争之后试图返回叙利亚。 2026年5月,国际刑事法院报告说,自2024年12月以来,约有167万难民和190万境内流离失所的叙利亚人返回。

然而,该机构警告说,住房受损、生计有限、基础设施薄弱、贫穷以及获得基本服务的机会有限,继续威胁着这些回返的可持续性。 难民署主办的2026年的单独评估得出了类似结论:人们返回后是否仍留在当地,在很大程度上取决于住房、就业、服务和经济机会。

对基督教社区来说,这种区别很重要。 想象一个家庭在海外多年后返回叙利亚城镇。 他们修补了一部分家 他们的孩子重新入学。 父亲开始重建小生意. 然后费用开始增加。 电力仍然不可靠。 发电机的燃料成本更高。 工作和上学的交通占收入的较大份额。

featured.title_zh: 印度西孟加拉邦的印度教民族主义者将矛头对准基督徒
featured.content: At least 48 to 65 incidents of targeted harassment, church vandalism, and physical violence against Christian communities in West Bengal, India, have been recorded between May and November. The Bangiya Christiya Pariseba, a Christian organization working for the welfare of the state’s Christian community, compiled this data. The right-wing Hindu nationalist Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) came to power in West Bengal following the April 2026 Legislative Assembly elections. Independent tracking by the research group India Hate Lab verified 60 hate crime incidents explicitly targeting Christian individuals, domestic fellowships, and institutional properties within West Bengal during the same period, confirming the widespread geographic footprint of the escalation of attacks on Christians. According to reports, the latest attack occurred on Nov. 9, when vandals desecrated a sacred shrine and Marian grotto of a church in an overnight attack in Khari Bamuner Chak, located within the Raidighi and Baruipur pastoral region of West Bengal’s South Parganas. A week earlier, a heavily organized contingent of about 40 men attacked a house prayer fellowship in Rayan village of the Bardhaman area. The assailants stormed the private residence during a morning service, violently assaulting the officiating pastor and worshippers. Surge of Attacks The surge in targeted violence, intimidation, and vandalism against Christian communities, churches, and home prayer fellowships in West Bengal is proving that Hindu nationalists have found West Bengal to be the new hunting ground with tacit support of the authorities. The state is currently experiencing a rapid breakdown in local law enforcement deterrence. This erosion directly threatens the constitutional guarantees enshrined in Article 25 of the Indian Constitution, which ensures freedom of conscience and the right to freely profess, practice, and propagate religion. The emergence of organized Hindutva networks operating with near-total impunity represents not merely localized social friction, but a systemic challenge to the rule of law and civil stability across the state. Faith Space Shrinking Across rural and semi-urban districts of West Bengal, Hindu nationalists increasingly employ physical blockades, structural desecration, and coordinated mob actions to shrink the space for religious minority assemblies. By weaponizing social intimidation and exploiting police inertia, these actors seek to criminalize ordinary acts of devotion, transforming private exercise of faith into contested public security triggers. Detailed documentation by human rights organizations and community defense networks attributes the vast majority of these incursions to organized Hindutva-affiliated groups. Investigations specifically point to operational coordination by local cadres associated with the Vishwa Hindu Parishad (VHP) and the Bajrang Dal, the RSS’s militant arm. Assailants consistently deploy dual narratives of illegal “unlawful religious conversions” and fabricated “honey traps.” To read more news stories, visit the ICC Newsroom . For interviews, please email us . To support ICC’s work around the world, please give to our Where Most Needed Fund . 5月至11月期间,印度西孟加拉邦至少有48至65起针对基督教社区的有针对性骚扰、破坏教堂和人身暴力事件。 Bangiya Christiya Pariseba是一个致力于国家基督教团体福利的基督教组织,

右翼印度民族主义者Bharatiya Janata党(BJP)于2026年4月立法议会选举后在西孟加拉邦上台.

研究小组印度仇恨实验室的独立跟踪核实了同期60起仇恨犯罪事件,明确针对西孟加拉邦的基督教个人、家庭奖学金和机构财产,证实了对基督教徒袭击升级造成的广泛地域影响。 据报道,最近一次袭击发生在11月.

9日,在位于西孟加拉邦南帕尔干纳斯的Raigighi和Baruipur牧区Khari Bamuner Chak的一起夜间袭击中,被破坏者亵渎了一座圣地和一座教堂的Marian地道。 一周前,一支由约40名男子组成的组织严密的特遣队袭击了Bardhaman地区Rayan村的一个家庭祈祷研究金。

袭击者在上午礼拜时冲入了私人住宅,暴力袭击了牧师和礼拜者。

袭击的激增 西孟加拉邦针对基督教社区、教堂和家庭祈祷研究金的有针对性暴力、恐吓和破坏行为激增,证明印度教民族主义者在当局的默许下发现西孟加拉邦是新的狩猎地。 目前,该国地方执法威慑迅速崩溃。

这种削弱直接威胁到《印度宪法》第25条所载的宪法保障,该条确保良心自由和自由信奉、实践和传播宗教的权利。

有组织的印度人网络的出现几乎完全不受惩罚,这不仅是局部性的社会摩擦,而且是对全国法治和国内稳定的系统性挑战。

印度民族主义者在西孟加拉邦的农村和半城市地区越来越多地采取实际封锁、结构性亵渎、协调暴徒行动来缩小宗教少数群体集会的空间。

通过将社会恐吓武器化和利用警察惯性,这些行为者试图将普通的献身行为定为刑事犯罪,将个人信仰的行使转变为有争议的公共安全触发因素。 人权组织和社区防卫网络的详细文件将绝大多数入侵归因于有组织的印度教附属团体。

调查特别指向与印度印度人理事会(VHP)和RSS好战武装Bajrang Dal有关的当地干部的业务协调。 仆从们一贯使用非法的“非法宗教皈依”和捏造的“甜蜜陷阱”的双重说法。 更多新闻报导, 采访,请通过电子邮件。

支持电算中心在世界各地的工作, 印度西孟加拉邦后印度民族主义者以基督徒为目标,

featured.content: How old were you when you first learned that Jesus loves you? Perhaps you’ve always known it and can’t remember a day when you didn’t know the song “Jesus Loves Me” or couldn’t recite John 3:16 by heart. Maybe you were a teenager and learned about Jesus’ love through a friend or church summer camp. Or were in college and went to a concert where the gospel was clearly articulated. Maybe you were in the trenches of the workforce, and a coworker boldly shared with you about the God who radically changed their life. Regardless of how old you were, each of us who has chosen to follow Jesus has an origin story — a moment in our lives when the knowledge that “Jesus loves me, this I know, for the Bible tells me so” moved from head knowledge to heart belief. And from then on, our lives were transformed forever. This is the truth of the gospel and the power of understanding that Jesus loves you. People around the world are discovering the personal truth of John 3:16 for themselves in a language and format they clearly understand. Explore why understanding that “God so loved the world” transforms entire communities → A Changing Reality Throughout Christian history, the gospel has spread from one community to the next. Stories were told and retold, Scripture was translated, churches were planted, and discipleship deepened as people learned more about Jesus. Bible translation is foundational to all ministries of the church. It fuels evangelism, church planting, discipleship and more. It equips people to move from a blurry picture of who God is to a clear understanding and personal encounter with Jesus as Lord. Through Scripture, people are able to read, hear or see the love of God on display. Just two decades ago, most of the world’s language communities still needed Bible translation work to begin , let alone be completed. But praise God, in the last few years, we’ve seen tremendous progress made, with Bible translation underway in more languages than ever before . While the change in numbers is exciting, what’s more important is what they signify: Every number represents a person who has a story that matters to God. For these communities, the stories of future generations are being completely rewritten as children will now grow up never remembering a day when they didn’t have access to God’s Word in a language and format they clearly understand. That statement bears repeating: There will now be people who never remember a day when they didn’t have access to God’s Word in a language and format they clearly understand. From the first word of Genesis to the last word of Revelation, the Bible tells one incredible story: God’s love for the world and His invitation for people from every nation and language to know Him. Get a glimpse of how God continues writing this story today as more and more people are experiencing the power of His Word. Watch the video → A New Generation Growing Up With God’s Word Let’s take a look at some of the recent communities that are experiencing not only life transformation but generational transformation as they encounter Jesus personally through Scripture. Jakalteko | Guatemala The Jakalteko Bible was dedicated in July 2026 in Guatemala! During the celebration, John 1:1-18 was read aloud — a passage that focuses on Christ, the eternal Word and our Redeemer. Early on, many women in the community memorized Job 19 . Like Job, they had faced various hardships in their lives and identified with his suffering. The book reminded them that God remains in control and that, in the midst of difficult circumstances, their Redeemer will deliver them and comfort them in their pain. Today, they have the full counsel of God’s Word and can now see this Redeemer fulfilled in Jesus in the New Testament. They are overjoyed that the Bible has arrived in the language they were born into! When the Bible was distributed, one mother who is raising her family alone said with joy and tears: “Thank God we have the Bible in our language. Now

你第一次得知耶稣爱你时多大了? 或许你一直都知道, 也不记得有一天你不知道“耶稣爱我”的歌曲, 或许你还是个少年, 或者在大学时,去参加一个音乐会,其中福音被明确表达出来.

也许你在劳动力的战壕里, 一个合作者大胆地与你分享上帝 谁彻底改变了他们的生活。 无论你多大,选择跟随耶稣的我们每个人都有一个起源故事——在我们生活中的这一刻,“耶稣爱我,我知道,因为圣经如此告诉我”的知识从头知识转移到心信。

从那时起,我们的生活就永远改变了 这是耶稣爱你的福音和理解的力量的真理. 世界各地的人们正在用他们明白的语言和格式,为自己发现约翰3:16的个人真理.

探讨为什么“上帝如此热爱世界”会改变整个社区? 基督教历史上不断变化的现实,福音从一个社区传播到另一个社区。 故事被讲述和重播,圣经被翻译,教堂被种植,随着人们更多地了解耶稣,门徒身份加深. 圣经翻译是教会所有各部的基础.

它为福音派,教会的种植,门徒活动等等提供了燃料. 它使人们能够从模糊的上帝是谁的画面走向一个明确的理解和与耶稣作为主的个人交锋. 通过圣经,人们能够阅读,听到或看到上帝的爱在展示.

就在20年前,世界上大多数语言社区仍然需要开始圣经翻译工作,更不用说完成了。 但赞美上帝, 在过去几年里, 我们看到了巨大的进步,

虽然数字的变化令人振奋, 每个数字都代表着一个对上帝很重要的故事的人. 对于这些社群来说, 后代的故事正在被完全改写, 因为孩子们现在长大了,

这一声明值得重申: 现在人们将永远不记得有一天,他们无法以他们明白的语言和格式获得上帝的启示。 从创世纪的第一个字到启示录的最后一个字,圣经讲述了一个不可思议的故事:上帝对世界的爱,以及他邀请来自每个民族和语言的人来了解他.

当越来越多的人正在经历着他的话语的力量时, 让我们看看最近的一些社区,

危地马拉 2026年7月危地马拉献上雅卡尔特科圣经! 在庆典期间,约翰1:1-18被高声朗诵——这一段以基督,永恒之言和我们的救世主为焦点. 早期,许多社区妇女怀念工作19。 与Job一样,他们的生活也面临各种困难,并认同他的痛苦。

这本书提醒他们,上帝仍然在控制之中,在困难的情况下,他们的救赎者会将他们送去,并在他们的痛苦中安慰他们. 今天,他们有充分的神话的劝告,现在可以看到这个救世主在新约中的耶稣实现了. 他们太高兴了 圣经已经用他们生下来的语言传下来了!

在分发《圣经》时,一位独自抚养家人的母亲欢呼和流泪地说:“感谢上帝,我们的语言有《圣经》。 现在

featured.title_zh: 当神的话变成个人的
featured.content: How old were you when you first learned that Jesus loves you? Perhaps you’ve always known it and can’t remember a day when you didn’t know the song “Jesus Loves Me” or couldn’t recite John 3:16 by heart. Maybe you were a teenager and learned about Jesus’ love through a friend or church summer camp. Or were in college and went to a concert where the gospel was clearly articulated. Maybe you were in the trenches of the workforce, and a coworker boldly shared with you about the God who radically changed their life. Regardless of how old you were, each of us who has chosen to follow Jesus has an origin story — a moment in our lives when the knowledge that “Jesus loves me, this I know, for the Bible tells me so” moved from head knowledge to heart belief. And from then on, our lives were transformed forever. This is the truth of the gospel and the power of understanding that Jesus loves you. People around the world are discovering the personal truth of John 3:16 for themselves in a language and format they clearly understand. Explore why understanding that “God so loved the world” transforms entire communities → A Changing Reality Throughout Christian history, the gospel has spread from one community to the next. Stories were told and retold, Scripture was translated, churches were planted, and discipleship deepened as people learned more about Jesus. Bible translation is foundational to all ministries of the church. It fuels evangelism, church planting, discipleship and more. It equips people to move from a blurry picture of who God is to a clear understanding and personal encounter with Jesus as Lord. Through Scripture, people are able to read, hear or see the love of God on display. Just two decades ago, most of the world’s language communities still needed Bible translation work to begin , let alone be completed. But praise God, in the last few years, we’ve seen tremendous progress made, with Bible translation underway in more languages than ever before . While the change in numbers is exciting, what’s more important is what they signify: Every number represents a person who has a story that matters to God. For these communities, the stories of future generations are being completely rewritten as children will now grow up never remembering a day when they didn’t have access to God’s Word in a language and format they clearly understand. That statement bears repeating: There will now be people who never remember a day when they didn’t have access to God’s Word in a language and format they clearly understand. From the first word of Genesis to the last word of Revelation, the Bible tells one incredible story: God’s love for the world and His invitation for people from every nation and language to know Him. Get a glimpse of how God continues writing this story today as more and more people are experiencing the power of His Word. Watch the video → A New Generation Growing Up With God’s Word Let’s take a look at some of the recent communities that are experiencing not only life transformation but generational transformation as they encounter Jesus personally through Scripture. Jakalteko | Guatemala The Jakalteko Bible was dedicated in July 2026 in Guatemala! During the celebration, John 1:1-18 was read aloud — a passage that focuses on Christ, the eternal Word and our Redeemer. Early on, many women in the community memorized Job 19 . Like Job, they had faced various hardships in their lives and identified with his suffering. The book reminded them that God remains in control and that, in the midst of difficult circumstances, their Redeemer will deliver them and comfort them in their pain. Today, they have the full counsel of God’s Word and can now see this Redeemer fulfilled in Jesus in the New Testament. They are overjoyed that the Bible has arrived in the language they were born into! When the Bible was distributed, one mother who is raising her family alone said with joy and tears: “Thank God we have the Bible in our language. Now

featured.title_zh: 俄亥俄州派遣庆祝活动确认33名IMB传教士为全球服务
featured.content: Participants at the IMB Sending Celebration on Nov. 9, 2026, celebrated God's faithfulness in sending 33 new missionaries to the nations. Held at the Sugarcreek campus of First Baptist Kettering near Dayton, Ohio, the event launched the State Convention of Baptists in Ohio annual gathering. For security reasons, some newly appointed missionaries are not publicly identified. IMB Photo God continues to call His people to carry the gospel to the ends of the earth. During a Sending Celebration Nov. 9 at the Sugarcreek Campus of First Baptist Church Kettering, near Dayton, Ohio, 33 International Mission Board missionaries stood before family, friends and supporters, affirming their obedience to that call. Trustees of the IMB appointed the fully supported missionaries who represent 10 states – including two candidates from Ohio – and many Southern Baptist churches committed to sending and sustaining those called by God to go to the mission field. Senior Pastor Chad Keck welcomed those in attendance, sharing his appreciation for the partnership with Southern Baptist churches to cooperatively send and support missionaries. The Sending Celebration is meeting in conjunction with the State Convention of Baptists in Ohio. Chad Keck, senior pastor of First Baptist Kettering near Dayton, Ohio, left, and Jeremy Westbrook, executive director-treasurer of the State Convention of Baptists in Ohio, right, welcome guests gathered for the IMB Sending Celebration, which kicked off the convention’s annual gathering. IMB Photo Among those who shared their stories include a couple who answered an unexpected call later in life, a couple who are returning to Albania and to people they could not forget; and a couple who moved from welcoming the nations in Canada to going to Fiji. All of them shared their stories before the Sending Celebration. Unexpected invitation to go On Dec. 5, 2025, what seemed like an ordinary FaceTime call became a turning point for Rob Boss. As he spoke with his daughter, Hannah, during her IMB training, Rob sensed God speaking clearly to his heart: “You can do this too.” The impression was unexpected. After decades of writing, Christian education, seminary teaching and active support of missions, overseas service had never been part of Rob and Stephanie Boss’ plans. “It wasn’t an audible voice, but it was so clear,” Rob said. “It was Him. It was so kind and so gentle and so encouraging.” The moment drove him to his knees in surrender. When Stephanie came home later that day, he told her he believed God was calling them to the nations. Her response was immediate. “Thrilled is the right answer,” she said. The next day, the couple contacted the IMB and began the application process. Though missions had long been part of their family’s story, Rob and Stephanie Boss sensed God leading them to overseas service while encouraging their daughter, Hannah, during her missionary training. Sent by Wedgwood Baptist Church in Fort Worth, Texas, they are now headed to Colombia, where they will serve through theological education. IMB Photo Looking back, the Bosses see the Lord’s hand preparing them long before they realized where He was leading. “God brought us together in the summer of 1990 at Glorieta, New Mexico, where we met and married,” Stephanie said during the Sending Celebration. What followed was years of ministry, teaching, parenting and navigating life’s unexpected turns, which taught them to hold plans loosely and trust God completely. “We did not have a clue about what life held in front of us,” Stephanie said. “We just knew we wanted to follow the Lord.” Their calling also continues a family legacy. Rob’s mother served with the IMB in Africa after retirement, helping inspire Hannah’s service in South Korea. Now, three generations of the same family have answered God’s call to the nations. Rob and Stephanie expressed deep gratitude for their sending church, Wedgwood Baptist Church in Fort Worth, whose strong commitment to missions
featured.content_zh:
2026年11月9日的IMB送信庆典的参与者,庆祝上帝向各国派遣33名新传教士的忠诚. 该活动在俄亥俄州代顿附近的第一浸信会Kettling的Sugarcreek校园举行,在俄亥俄州发起了浸信会州议会年会。 出于安全考虑,一些新任命的传教士没有公开身份.

IMB图片神继续呼叫 他的族人将福音传到地底 11月9日,在俄亥俄州代顿附近的第一浸信会Kettling教堂的Sugarcreek校区,33名国际传教委员会传教士站在家人、朋友和支持者面前,申明他们服从这一呼吁。

IMB的受托人任命了代表10个州的全力支持的传教士 — — 包括俄亥俄州的两名候选人 — — 以及许多南方浸信会教会承诺将那些被上帝召唤去传教的传教士送去并维持下去.

高级牧师Chad Keck欢迎与会者,与他一样感谢与美南浸信会教会合作派遣和支持传教士。 送教庆典会与俄亥俄州的浸信会州会议同时举行.

俄亥俄州代顿附近第一浸信会Ketting的资深牧师查德·凯克(Chad Keck)左翼,俄亥俄州浸信会执行董事兼创始人杰里米·韦斯特布鲁克(Jeremy Westbrook)右翼欢迎前来参加IMB送信庆典的来宾,这驱散了大会的年度集会。

在分享自己故事的人中,有一对夫妇在生活后期意外地接了电话,一对夫妇正在返回阿尔巴尼亚,一对夫妇无法忘记;一对夫妇从欢迎加拿大各国搬到斐济。 他们都分享了他们的故事 在送信庆典之前。 意外邀请 Dec 上。

5, 2025, 看起来像一个普通的FaceTime电话成为Rob Boss的转折点. 当他和他的女儿汉娜在IMB训练期间交谈时,罗布感应到上帝对他说的很清楚:“你也可以这样做。” 印象出乎意料。

经过几十年的写作、基督教教育、神学院教学和对使团的积极支持,海外服务从未成为罗布和斯蒂芬妮·博斯计划的一部分。 Rob说, “这不是一个声音, “这是他。 它是如此善良和温柔,如此鼓舞人心。” 那一刻,他被迫跪在地上投降。

当斯蒂芬妮当天晚些时候回家时,他告诉她,他相信上帝在召唤他们到各国. 她立即作出反应。 她说,“令人惊叹的是正确的答案。” 次日,夫妇联系IMB,开始了申请程序.

虽然传教团早就是他们家庭故事的一部分,但罗布和史蒂芬妮·博斯感知到,在传教团训练期间,他们带领他们到海外服务,同时鼓励他们的女儿汉娜。 由德克萨斯州沃思堡的韦奇伍德浸信会(Wedgwood Baptist Church)派遣,他们现在前往哥伦比亚,通过神学教育服务.

IMB照片回想起来,老板们看到主的手 在他们意识到在哪里之前很早就准备了 他是领导。 " 1990年夏天,上帝把我们带到了新墨西哥州格洛里埃塔,我们在那里相遇并结婚。 " Stephanie在送货庆典上说。

接下来是多年的教职、教职、养育和过着意想不到的转折,教他们松动计划,完全相信上帝。 Stephanie说:“我们不知道我们面前的生活是什么。” 我们只知道我们想跟随主。 他们的召唤也延续了家庭遗产。

罗布的母亲退休后在非洲为IMB效力,帮助激励汉娜在韩国服役. 现在,同一家庭的三代人响应了上帝向各国发出的呼吁。 Rob和Stephanie深表感谢他们派来的教会Worth堡的Wedgwood浸信会教堂,他们坚定致力于使命

Perhaps you’ve always known it and can’t remember a day when you didn’t know the song “Jesus Loves Me” or couldn’t recite John 3:16 by heart. Maybe you were in the trenches of the workforce, and a coworker boldly shared with you about the God who radically changed their life. Regardless of how old you were, each of us who has chosen to follow Jesus has an origin story — a moment in our lives when the knowledge that “Jesus loves me, this I know, for the Bible tells me so” moved from head knowledge to heart belief. And from then on, our lives were transformed forever. This is the truth of the gospel and the power of understanding that Jesus loves you. Bible translation is foundational to all ministries of the church. It fuels evangelism, church planting, discipleship and more. It equips people to move from a blurry picture of who God is to a clear understanding and personal encounter with Jesus as Lord. Through Scripture, people are able to read, hear or see the love of God on display. Just two decades ago, most of the world’s language communities still needed Bible translation work to begin , let alone be completed. But praise God, in the last few years, we’ve seen tremendous progress made, with Bible translation underway in more languages than ever before . While the change in numbers is exciting, what’s more important is what they signify: Every number represents a person who has a story that matters to God. For these communities, the stories of future generations are being completely rewritten as children will now grow up never remembering a day when they didn’t have access to God’s Word in a language and format they clearly understand. That statement bears repeating: There will now be people who never remember a day when they didn’t have access to God’s Word in a language and format they clearly understand. From the first word of Genesis to the last word of Revelation, the Bible tells one incredible story: God’s love for the world and His invitation for people from every nation and language to know Him. Get a glimpse of how God continues writing this story today as more and more people are experiencing the power of His Word. featured.title_zh: 印度一个有8口人的基督徒家庭被驱逐，无家可归
featured.content: A Christian family of eight in the Sukma district of Chhattisgarh, India, was left homeless after Hindu nationalists ransacked and demolished their home on the morning of Nov. 16. During the eviction, the family’s essential household items — including food, clothing, bedding, kitchen utensils, and vital personal documents — were thrown out of their home. The house, belonging to Manglu Sodi and his wife, Hirmibai, was reportedly ransacked and demolished because of their Christian faith. Amid the destruction, 4,000 rupees (roughly $43), about five grams of gold, and a bicycle were stolen before the house was destroyed. Relief in Safe House Fleeing for their safety, the family traveled roughly 40 miles to reach the district headquarters of Sukma, where they were placed in a Safe House. Representatives of the Progressive Christian Alliance (PCA), a rights advocacy group working for the welfare of Christian minorities, coordinated with local pastor Harendra Madiya in Sukma to provide relief for the persecuted family. PCA State Coordinator Patras Balti visited the family to encourage and pray with them, urging them to remain steadfast in their faith despite the severe hardship. Although formal complaints have been submitted to the local police station, the Superintendent of Police (SP), and the district collector of Sukma, no formal inquiry or legal action has been initiated to date. Without their identification documents or savings, the family faces steep hurdles in rehabilitation and rebuilding their lives. Historic Church Building Razed Down In another development, up north of Sukma district, about 300 miles away, a historic church estimated by locals to be roughly 130 years old was demolished in Rajnandgaon district of Chhattisgarh in the past week. The structure was part of the campus of the Missionary Bands of the World Leprosy Hospital (also known as the Rajnandgaon Leprosy Hospital and Clinics), which stood on about 23 acres of government-leased land originally allotted for treating and rehabilitating leprosy patients. The Clearance Operation The demolition followed a lease-cancellation order issued on Nov. 6 by the Rajnandgaon district collector. The demolition drive razed not only the church, but also the old hospital wards, administrative offices, and residential quarters of the leprosy hospital. The administration said the reclaimed land will be used for public amenities, including a sports ground. However, Christian watchdogs are skeptical about the district collector’s action. Christian community leaders urged a clear distinction between the government’s right to recover land over alleged lease violations and the decision to destroy a heritage religious structure. 印度恰蒂斯加尔邦Sukma县一户由8人组成的基督教家庭在11月16日上午印度民族主义者洗劫并拆毁了他们的家后被无家可归. 在驱逐期间,家庭的基本家用物品 -- -- 包括食物、衣服、被褥、厨房用具和重要个人证件 -- -- 被赶出家门。

这所房子属于Manglu Sodi和他的妻子Hirmibai,据报因其基督教信仰被洗劫并被拆毁。 在被摧毁时,4 000卢比(约43美元),约5克黄金被偷走,还有一辆自行车被摧毁。

安全屋的救济为他们的安全而逃出,全家出行了大约40英里去到Sukma区总部,在那里他们被安置在安全屋.

进步基督教联盟(PCA)的代表,这是一个致力于基督教少数派福利的权利倡导团体,与苏克马的Harendra Madiya当地牧师协调,为受迫害的家庭提供救济. 常设仲裁法院州协调员Patras Balti访问了该家庭,鼓励他们和他们一起祈祷,敦促他们尽管遭遇了严重困难,但仍要坚定信念。

虽然已经向地方警察局、警察局长和Sukma地区收藏家提出正式申诉,但迄今尚未启动任何正式调查或法律行动。 没有身份证件或储蓄,家庭在恢复和重建生活方面面临严重障碍。

历史教堂建筑被刮倒 在位于相距约300英里外的Sukma区以北的另一项发展中,当地人估计大约有130年历史的一座历史教堂在过去一周被查蒂斯加尔的Rajnandgaon区拆除.

该建筑是世界麻风病医院(又名Rajnandgaon麻风病医院和诊所)传教团校园的一部分,该院占地约23英亩,最初分配给麻风病人治疗和康复。 清除行动 拆除是在11月签发的租约取消令之后进行的。

6由拉杰南德加翁区收藏家出品. 拆除运动不仅夷平了教堂,还夷平了麻风医院的旧医院病房,行政办公室和住宅区. 行政当局说,被开垦的土地将用于公共设施,包括体育场。 但基督教监督员对地区收藏家的行为持怀疑态度。

基督教社区领袖敦促明确区分政府收回土地的权利与摧毁传统宗教结构的决定。 更多新闻报导, 采访,请通过电子邮件。 支持电算中心在世界各地的工作,

featured.title_zh: 马来西亚法院将一名皈依基督教者的宗教自由诉讼移交地区法庭
featured.content: A 34-year-old law graduate’s multi-year battle exposes the severe reality of religious control and the legal trap facing citizens who want to leave Islam. A high-stakes constitutional challenge highlighting the erosion of religious freedom in Malaysia has taken a procedural step backward. The Kuala Lumpur High Court has ordered that a lawsuit filed by a 34-year-old legal researcher seeking legal recognition as a Christian be transferred to the Shah Alam High Court. The case lays bare the rigid and intrusive control exercised by state apparatuses and Islamic religious authorities over personal faith, showcasing a system where basic human rights — such as choosing one’s own religion — are tightly policed by the government. A Life Labeled Without Consent The plaintiff, Shameer PV, identifies as a Christian and has lived as one since he was 18. However, under strict Malaysian administrative regulations, the word “Islam” was stamped on his compulsory national identity card (MyKad) when he was just 12, following a bureaucratic policy introduced under the National Registration Act. Despite decades of personal conviction and his marriage to a Christian wife, the state continues to legally treat him as a Muslim, directly violating his parental and marital status and refusing to recognize his family. Shameer’s legal challenge names the federal government, the Selangor state government, and the Selangor Islamic Religious Council (MAIS) as defendants. He argues that labeling citizens by religion on state identity cards violates Article 11(1) of the Federal Constitution, which ostensibly guarantees every person the right to profess and practice their religion. Trapped in Shariah Bureaucracy Shameer’s ordeal underscores the labyrinthine and punishing hurdles forced upon religious minorities and converts in Malaysia’s dual-justice system, which runs a parallel set of Islamic (Shariah) courts alongside the civil judiciary. In 2018, Shameer initiated proceedings in a Selangor Shariah court seeking official recognition of his Christian faith. After an exhausting 72 court sessions spanning over seven years, the Shariah court dismissed his application in January. Rather than allowing him to move on with his life, the religious court went a step further, ordering state departments and Islamic authorities to “guide and control” his practice of Islam — effectively treating his desire to leave the faith as a disciplinary or correctional matter. Having exhausted the religious tribunal system, Shameer turned to the civil high court in July, filing an originating summons to ask the highest judicial authorities whether state-mandated religious labeling on identity cards is unconstitutional, and whether Shariah courts have any lawful jurisdiction over individuals who do not practice Islam. A Wider Crisis for Freedom of Conscience International human rights observers and religious freedom advocates have long criticized Malaysia’s legal framework regarding apostasy and conversion. While the Malaysian Constitution theoretically protects freedom of religion, civil courts have repeatedly ruled that only Islamic Shariah courts have the authority to permit someone to leave Islam — creating an effective judicial catch-22, as Shariah courts rarely grant permission to renounce the religion. For international human rights advocates and supporters of religious liberty, Shameer’s case is a stark reminder of the state-enforced religious controls facing millions in Southeast Asia. As his case moves to the Shah Alam court, the legal battle continues to test whether Malaysia’s secular constitutional framework can protect an individual’s fundamental right of conscience against a totalizing state religious bureaucracy. 一个34岁的法学毕业生的多年战斗暴露了宗教控制的严重现实和想要离开伊斯兰教的公民所面临的法律陷阱. 马来西亚宗教自由受到侵蚀,

吉隆坡高等法院下令将34岁法律研究者提出的寻求法律承认为基督徒的诉讼移交沙阿拉姆高等法院.

这一案件暴露了国家机构和伊斯兰宗教当局对个人信仰的严格和侵扰性控制,表明政府严格控制基本人权(如选择自己的宗教)的制度。 未经同意的生活标签 原告Shameer PV确认为基督教徒,自18岁起就一直作为一个教徒生活在一起。

然而,根据严格的马来西亚行政条例,他12岁时的强制性国民身份证(MyKad)上印有“伊斯兰”一词,这是根据《国家登记法》实行的官僚政策。

尽管几十年的个人信念和他与基督教妻子的婚姻,但国家继续在法律上将他视为穆斯林,直接侵犯了他的父母和婚姻状况,并拒绝承认他的家人. 沙门的法律质疑将联邦政府,雪兰莪州政府,雪兰莪伊斯兰宗教委员会(MAIS)列为被告.

他辩称,以宗教方式将公民贴在州身份证上违反了《联邦宪法》第11(1)条,该条表面上保障每个人信奉和奉行其宗教的权利。

伊斯兰教法官僚沙姆耶的折磨凸显了Labyrinthine和惩罚强加给宗教少数派和皈依马来西亚双重司法制度的障碍,马来西亚的双重司法制度与民事司法平行设有一套伊斯兰(伊斯兰教法)法院。 2018年,沙姆耶在塞兰哥教法法院提起诉讼,寻求官方承认他的基督教信仰.

经过历时七年的72次开庭,教法法院于1月驳回了他的申请。

宗教法庭没有让他继续自己的生活,而是更进一步,命令国家部门和伊斯兰当局“指导和控制”他的伊斯兰教习俗——实际上将他放弃信仰的愿望视为纪律或惩戒事项。

在用尽了宗教法庭制度之后,Shameer于7月向民事高等法院提交了原传票,询问最高司法当局在身份证上贴上国家规定的宗教标签是否违宪,伊斯兰教法法院是否对不信奉伊斯兰教的个人拥有任何合法管辖权。

国际人权观察员和宗教自由倡导者长期批评马来西亚关于叛教和皈依的法律框架。

虽然马来西亚宪法理论上保护宗教自由,但民事法院一再裁定只有伊斯兰教法法院有权允许某人离开伊斯兰教——这创造了有效的司法抓捕-22,因为伊斯兰教法法院很少允许放弃该宗教.

对国际人权倡导者和宗教自由支持者来说,Shameer一案明确提醒人们注意东南亚数百万人所面临的国家强制宗教控制。

I added lots of new books to the list yesterday. There are many great deals to be had! Recommended Reading Remembering John Allen Chau. P. R. Swain remembers and honors John Allen Chau. “There has been plenty of discussion around John’s level of wisdom and preparedness. Many feel these were lacking. I will admit that landing on an island whose inhabitants are known to be violent toward outsiders is unwise. The wiser thing would’ve been for him to invest his savings in a mutual fund for forty years. How short-sighted of him. In the words of one of the five in Ecuador who preceded him in martyrdom, ‘He is no fool who gives what he cannot keep to gain what he cannot lose.’ John was no fool.” How to Experience Gospel Transformation. This is a tremendous article from Nicholas McDonald on practicing repentance. “Here is my encouragement to you, as you learn to practice the prayer of reconciliation. Take 5-10 minutes each night, and try to choose one thing (not a million things) that needs repentance from your day. It’s very important that you go beyond just naming your sin to God, here. It’s important to name your sin (even out loud!), but that’s not going to transform you. What will transform you is learning to practice reconciliation with God, through the gospel.” The Quiet Voice. Catherine Mackenzie was one of those people who enjoyed the quiet that came to her life when Outlook crashed. “Although almost everything I had planned that day depended on email, and almost none of it got done, I actually talked to my colleagues. We caught up properly, in a way our inboxes don’t usually leave room for. I sat beside the designer instead of messaging her on Teams, and we all shared jokes and discussed our favourite period dramas.” She goes on to draw some observations from the marriage of John and Polly Newton. What We Get Wrong About the Tears of Jesus. Perhaps you’ve always known it and can’t remember a day when you didn’t know the song “Jesus Loves Me” or couldn’t recite John 3:16 by heart. Maybe you were a teenager and learned about Jesus’ love through a friend or church summer camp. Or were in college and went to a concert where the gospel was clearly articulated. Maybe you were in the trenches of the workforce, and a coworker boldly shared with you about the God who radically changed their life. Regardless of how old you were, each of us who has chosen to follow Jesus has an origin story — a moment in our lives when the knowledge that “Jesus loves me, this I know, for the Bible tells me so” moved from head knowledge to heart belief. And from then on, our lives were transformed forever. This is the truth of the gospel and the power of understanding that Jesus loves you. People around the world are discovering the personal truth of John 3:16 for themselves in a language and format they clearly understand. Explore why understanding that “God so loved the world” transforms entire communities → A Changing Reality Throughout Christian history, the gospel has spread from one community to the next. Stories were told and retold, Scripture was translated, churches were planted, and discipleship deepened as people learned more about Jesus. Bible translation is foundational to all ministries of the church. It fuels evangelism, church planting, discipleship and more. It equips people to move from a blurry picture of who God is to a clear understanding and personal encounter with Jesus as Lord. Through Scripture, people are able to read, hear or see the love of God on display. Just two decades ago, most of the world’s language communities still needed Bible translation work to begin , let alone be completed. But praise God, in the last few years, we’ve seen tremendous progress made, with Bible translation underway in more languages than ever before . While the change in numbers is exciting, what’s more important is what they signify: Every number represents a person who has a story that matters to God. For these communities, the stories of future generations are being completely rewritten as children will now grow up never remembering a day when they didn’t have access to God’s Word in a language and format they clearly understand. That statement bears repeating: There will now be people who never remember a day when they didn’t have access to God’s Word in a language and format they clearly understand. From the first word of Genesis to the last word of Revelation, the Bible tells one incredible story: God’s love for the world and His invitation for people from every nation and language to know Him. Get a glimpse of how God continues writing this story today as more and more people are experiencing the power of His Word. They are overjoyed that the Bible has arrived in the language they were born into! featured.content: Vietnamese authorities demolished a historic building belonging to the Redemptorist Catholic community in the central city of Huế on Tuesday, escalating a decades-long dispute over church property and raising renewed concerns about religious freedom in the communist-governed country. The demolition of the L’Accueil building followed the deployment of police by local authorities to block roads surrounding the Redemptorist monastery and Our Lady of Perpetual Help Church. Electricity to the area was also cut, preventing some parishioners from reaching the church to attend Mass or express solidarity with the religious community. According to the Redemptorists, heavy machinery began demolishing the structure while priests, religious brothers, and parishioners gathered nearby in prayer. The demolition continued through Nov. 18, leaving the property leveled and fenced off. The Redemptorist Provincial Chapter of Vietnam condemned the operation, arguing that authorities proceeded despite unresolved legal questions and repeated requests to review the property’s ownership. “Justice cannot be established through force, and the truth cannot be erased along with the structures that have been demolished,” the congregation said in a Nov. 17 statement as the demolition was proceeding. Communist Land Takeover The dispute centers on land that the Redemptorists purchased in 1930. According to historical documentation cited by the religious order, Huế municipal authorities formally recognized the congregation’s ownership in 1971. The L’Accueil complex was subsequently developed on the property between 1938 and 1943. It served as a center for educational, cultural, and community activities, housing a library, auditorium, and reading room. A sawmill was also established on the grounds in the 1950s, providing local employment. Following the communist takeover of South Vietnam in 1975, the government’s relationship with religious institutions changed significantly. Church properties throughout the country came under increasing state control, with religious communities frequently losing access to land and buildings they had previously owned. The Redemptorists maintain that they never voluntarily surrendered their rights to the L’Accueil property. They acknowledge that the congregation transferred assets associated with a sawmill to the state in 1978, but argue that the transfer did not include the land itself. Authorities subsequently assigned the property to government-controlled institutions. The remaining parcel, measuring about 2,550 square meters, is currently managed by a local sports vocational school. Recent Efforts The congregation has sought the property’s return since 1994. Its most recent formal complaint, submitted to the Huế People’s Committee on Oct. 24, requested recognition of its land-use rights and clarification of the property’s legal status. Authorities reportedly rejected the complaint in a Nov. 8 response, stating that it had no basis for consideration. A notice posted at the property in October announced plans to develop a public park and parking lot on the site. Local authorities have defended the project as serving public interests, including improving traffic conditions and providing additional green space in a densely populated area. Vietnamese law establishes that land is collectively owned by the people and administered by the state. Government authorities have also invoked a 2003 National Assembly resolution that generally prevents reconsideration of certain land and housing arrangements established before July 1, 1991. The Redemptorists, however, dispute the government’s interpretation of the property’s history and say authorities have not adequately explained the legal grounds for demolishing the building. They have asked officials to publicly disclose the documentation supporting their decision and review the historical records presented by the congregation. 在L ' Accueil大楼被拆除之前,地方当局部署了警察,封锁救赎会修道院和永生圣母助教周围的道路。 该地区的电力也被切断,使一些教区人士无法前往教堂参加弥撒或表示对宗教界的声援.

据救赎派说,重型机械开始拆除该建筑,而祭司,宗教兄弟,以及教区教徒聚集在附近祈祷. 拆除工作一直持续到11月18日,财产被夷为平地和围起来。

越南救赎主义省分会谴责了这次行动,认为当局不顾尚未解决的法律问题和一再要求审查该财产的所有权而继续行动. “正义不能通过武力建立,真理不能与被拆除的建筑物一起抹去。”

17份在拆除过程中的声明。 共产党夺地 争端集中在救赎者在1930年购买的土地上。 根据宗教秩序所引用的历史文献,胡瓦克市当局于1971年正式承认该教会的所有权. L ' Accueil建筑群后来于1938年至1943年间在地产上发展.

它作为教育、文化和社区活动中心、图书馆、礼堂和阅览室。 1950年代还在当地建立了锯木厂,提供当地就业。 1975年共产党接管南越后,政府与宗教机构的关系发生了重大变化.

全国各地的教会财产受到越来越多的国家控制,宗教社区往往失去获得其以前拥有的土地和建筑物的机会。 救赎者坚持认为,他们从未自愿放弃对L ' Accueil财产的权利。

他们承认教会在1978年将与锯木厂有关的资产转移到了国家,但辩称转让不包括土地本身. 当局随后将财产分配给政府控制的机构。 其余部分占地约2,550平方米,目前由当地体育职业学校管理.

最近的努力 自1994年以来,教会一直要求归还财产。 它最近于10月24日向胡瓦克人民委员会提出正式申诉,要求承认其土地使用权并澄清财产的法律地位。 据报告,当局在11月8日的答复中驳回了申诉,称申诉没有审议依据。

10月在该地产张贴了一份通知,宣布计划在该地开发一个公共公园和停车场. 地方当局捍卫该项目是为了公共利益,包括在人口稠密地区改善交通条件和提供更多的绿色空间。 越南法律规定,土地属于人民集体所有,由国家管理。

featured.content: This may come as a surprise, but Christmas is a national holiday in Iraq — ever since the government formally declared it so in December 2018. “It feels like a token move to appear non-discriminatory,” said “Petros,” an Assyrian Christian living in the U.S. with an Iraqi expat family. He added that this “token” celebration of Christmas “ignores the native traditions” of the region’s Christians and “instead opts for a European-style Christmas” with Santa Claus and various types of Christmas trees that don’t naturally grow in the area. Iraq, which was already celebrating the birth of Christ when most of Europe was still pagan, has among the world’s oldest Christian communities, with the faith arriving in the first century A.D. Petros feels that the Iraqi government’s acknowledgment of Christmas is more of a public relations strategy to deflect from the recent horrors faced by Iraq’s Christians. “Yonita,” an Assyrian woman who is Chaldean Catholic and lives in the U.S., believes the recent recognition of Christmas is financially motivated. “Iraq is trying to rebuild itself,” she said, adding that it might be “taking notes” from more successful countries in the region that have comparatively more religious freedom. Yonita suspects that celebrating Christmas could be an attempt at showing camaraderie with the West. It could also be a way to make the homeland seem more congenial to the many Iraqi Christians abroad. As she pointed out, the Christian Iraqi diaspora tends to be quite well-off financially. “There was a formal call inviting us back to Iraq [to] invest in the rebuilding of the cradle of civilization,” Yonita said. A Sad Reality Whatever the Iraqi government’s true motivation, one painful aspect is hard to deny: By the time Christmas became a national holiday, most Iraqi Christians had already been driven out of their homeland. Conditions were so difficult during the previous 15 years that the country had lost up to 90% of its Christian community. Iraq’s remaining Christians, most of whom belong either to the Chaldean Catholic Church or the Assyrian Church of the East, now comprise less than half of 1% of the country’s overall population. The Christian population had already seen considerable decline during the 24-year reign of former Iraqi president Saddam Hussein, a man of immense sadism. But, for all his homicidal flaws, Hussein — though Muslim by background — was no Islamic extremist. In fact, his longtime right-hand man, Deputy Prime Minister Tariq Aziz, was a Christian, at least technically. It would likely be an exaggeration to say that Hussein cared about the welfare of Iraqi Christians, but the bone-crushing force of his reputation rendered most Iraqis, regardless of their faith, too intimidated to indulge in sectarian hostilities. Petros said that his fellow Assyrian Christians “either liked Hussein for providing stability and jobs, or hated him for killing their family members.” Many of Iraq’s Christians wanted him to stay in power only because they had an acute sense of the mayhem that would erupt after their secular tyrant was deposed. “It’s like the saying goes,” Petros said. “Better to deal with the devil you know than the devil you don’t.” At this point, though, both “devils” have fully acquainted themselves with Iraq. The Rise of Extremism The ousting of Hussein from power in 2003 brought in an era of rising Islamic extremism, most notably with the Islamic State group (ISIS), formerly known as “al-Qaida in Iraq.” Some Iraqi Christians were even accused of collaborating with the U.S. military. As the atmosphere grew increasingly precarious in post-Hussein Iraq, most Christians fled the country, having decided the other options — violent death, forced conversion, or paying a religious tax — were unpalatable. Those who remained were often hunted. In June 2007, in the northern Iraqi city of Mosul, a priest and his assistants were killed right in front of his church. 这也许是个惊喜, 但圣诞节是伊拉克的国庆节, “Petros”是一位居住在美国的亚述基督教徒,

他补充说,这种对该地区基督教徒的圣诞节 " 玷污当地传统 " 的 " 庆祝 " , " 而不是选择一个欧洲式的圣诞节 " ,圣诞老人和该地区自然不会生长的各类圣诞树。

伊拉克在庆祝基督诞生时,欧洲大部分地区仍然是异教徒,伊拉克是世界上最古老的基督教社区之一,公元一世纪时,信仰就已经降临。 彼得罗斯认为伊拉克政府承认圣诞节更是一种公共关系策略,旨在转移伊拉克基督徒最近面临的恐怖。

“Yonita”是一位信奉迦勒底天主教、居住在美国的亚述妇女, 她说,“伊拉克正在努力重建自己”,她补充说,它可能“注意到”该区域比较成功的宗教自由的国家。

Yonita怀疑庆祝圣诞节可能是试图与西方展示友情. 这也可以成为使祖国看起来对海外许多伊拉克基督徒更加融洽的方法. 正如她指出的那样,伊拉克的基督教散居国外者往往在财政上相当富裕。

Yonita说,“有人正式邀请我们回到伊拉克,投资重建文明的摇篮。” 一个悲哀的现实 无论伊拉克政府的真正动机如何,一个痛苦的方面很难否认: 到圣诞节成为国家节日时,大多数伊拉克基督徒已经被驱逐出家园.

在过去15年里,情况十分困难,以至于该国丧失了90%的基督教徒。 伊拉克其余的基督教徒,大多属于迦勒底天主教会或东方亚述教会,现在占该国总人口的不到1%。

伊拉克前总统萨达姆·侯赛因24年的统治期间,基督教徒人数已经大幅度减少,他是一位极度虐待的人。 但是,侯赛因尽管有穆斯林背景,但他的杀人缺陷并非伊斯兰极端主义分子。 事实上,他长期担任右手的副总理塔里克·阿齐兹是基督徒,至少在技术上是这样.

如果说侯赛因关心伊拉克基督徒的福利,那很可能是一种夸张的说法,但他的名声的骨折力量使大多数伊拉克人,无论其信仰如何,都过于恐吓,不敢陷入教派敌对行动。

Petros说,他的亚述基督徒同胞“要么喜欢侯赛因提供稳定和工作,要么恨他杀害家人”。 许多伊拉克基督徒希望他继续掌权,只是因为他们对世俗暴君被废黜后爆发的混乱有强烈的感受。 Petros说,

“最好对付你认识的恶魔, 然而,此时,这两个“恶魔”已完全熟悉伊拉克。

极端主义的兴起 2003年侯赛因被赶下台,带来了伊斯兰极端主义抬头的时代,其中最突出的是伊斯兰国集团(ISIS),它以前被称为“伊拉克基地组织”。 一些伊拉克基督徒甚至被指控与美国军方勾结.

由于后侯赛因的伊拉克气氛越来越不稳定,大多数基督徒逃离该国,决定了其他选择——暴力死亡、强迫皈依或缴纳宗教税——是令人不快的。 留下来的人经常遭到追捕。 2007年6月,在伊拉克北部城市摩苏尔,一名牧师及其助手在他教堂前被杀死。

featured.title_zh: 南苏丹戈罗姆难民营的礼拜者遭遇暴力袭击
featured.content: Around 8:30 a.m. on Sunday, Nov. 15, the courtyard of the Darfur Christian Council church in Gorom Refugee Camp near Juba, South Sudan, became a scene of sudden violence. As worshippers gathered for prayer, a group led by Baqir Muhammad Saleh launched a brutal attack. Stones were thrown, sticks were used to beat people, and some victims were bitten and strangled. “Pastor Daniel Hassan suffered severe injuries: a large part of his left ear was lost to a bite, and the tendon in his middle finger was damaged,” a local bishop who wished to remain anonymous said. “Pastor Samuel Omer received serious blows to the head that caused internal injuries. His wife was beaten in the abdominal area and sustained internal trauma. Brother Michael Yusuf was struck in the nose, while Brother Elias Ibrahim Mohammed was strangled and beaten on the stomach, resulting in minor injuries. Others, including Ahmed Khalid and Fatima Ahmed Khalid, were also exposed to the violence.” This was not the first time the church courtyard had been attacked. On April 17, 2025, Pastor Hassan was shot, sustaining injuries to his thigh and hand. The repeated nature of these assaults has left the congregation shaken and deeply concerned for their safety. “We continue to pray for peace and forgiveness, asking believers to restrain themselves and offer words of love, because the church is a place of holiness and prayer. As the Psalmist writes, ‘Turn from evil and do good; seek peace and pursue it’ (Psalm 34:14). Christ teaches us to forgive and to be a blessing even in the face of hatred.” Hassan stated. The Darfur Christian Council serves believers who have already fled conflict and persecution in Sudan. For many, the refugee camp was meant to be a place of relative safety. Instead, the church has become a target. The latest attack has deepened fear among worshippers, many of whom now wonder whether they can gather freely to pray without risking further violence. “We demand that the authorities in the camp provide as much protection as possible to the worshippers,” another victim said. “We also demand that a proper investigation be carried out and that justice be done according to the law. The Lord is a God of justice; ‘He will judge the world in righteousness and the peoples with equity’ (Psalm 98:9). We cry out for that justice to be seen here.” Despite the pain and injury, the leaders of the Darfur Christian Council have chosen the path of restraint and faith. They continue to call their people to respond with the love of Christ rather than retaliation, holding fast to the truth that the church must remain a place of peace and holiness even when surrounded by hostility. “Though the attack has wounded our bodies and our hearts, we refuse to abandon the way of the cross,” Pastor Hassan said. “‘The Lord is close to the broken-hearted and saves those who are crushed in spirit’ (Psalm 34:18). We trust him to heal our wounds, protect his people, and turn this suffering into a testimony of his grace.” To read more news stories, visit the ICC Newsroom . For interviews, please email us . 当地一位希望匿名的主教说,“Daniel Hassan牧师受重伤:左耳大部被咬伤,中指的阴茎受损”。 “Samuel Omer神父头部受到严重打击,造成内伤。 他的妻子在腹部遭到殴打,并受到内伤。

Michael Yusuf兄弟被击中鼻子,而Elias Ibrahim Mohammed兄弟被勒死并殴打腹部,造成轻伤。 其他人,包括艾哈迈德·哈立德和法蒂玛·艾哈迈德·哈立德也遭到暴力。 这不是教堂庭院第一次遭到袭击。 2025年4月17日,哈桑牧师中弹,大腿和手受伤.

这些袭击一再发生,使教会感到动摇,并深为关切其安全。 “我们继续祈求和平和宽恕,要求信徒克制,献出爱语,因为教堂是神圣和祈祷的地方。 如"诗经"所记载:"从恶反善;求和而追之(诗经34:14).

基督教导我们,即使面对仇恨,也要宽恕和成为祝福。” 哈桑说。 达尔富尔基督教理事会为已经逃离苏丹冲突和迫害的信徒服务。 对许多人来说,难民营是相对安全的地方。 相反,教堂已经成为目标.

最近的一次袭击加深了礼拜者的恐惧,其中许多人现在怀疑他们是否可以自由聚集在一起祈祷,而不会面临进一步暴力的风险。 另一位受害者说,“我们要求难民营当局向礼拜者提供尽可能多的保护。” “我们还要求进行适当调查,并依法伸张正义。

主是正义的神; " 他将以正义和公平来评判世界和人民 " (第98:9段)。 我们要求在这里看到这种正义。” 尽管遭受了痛苦和伤害,但达尔富尔基督教理事会的领导人选择了克制和信仰的道路。

他们继续号召自己的人民以基督的爱而不是报复来回应,坚守真理,即即使周围充满敌意,教会也必须保持和平和神圣。 “尽管袭击伤害了我们的身体和心灵,但我们拒绝放弃十字架的道路,”哈桑牧师说。

" `主近于伤心者,救精神所压者'(34:18). 我们信任他医治我们的创伤,保护他的人民,并把这种痛苦变成他恩惠的见证。” 阅读更多新闻, 请给我们发电子邮件 支持电算中心在世界各地的工作,

featured.title_zh: 2名基督徒女孩在特伦甘纳邦遭到袭击
featured.content: A group of men who assaulted two Christian girls for attempting to convert Hindus to Christianity in Telangana, India, has sparked outrage throughout India. A video of the incident, which became public in early November, has raised concerns over Hindu nationalists taking the law into their hands and attacking Christians over allegations of conversion. The incident took place around two months ago in Almasguda, Maheshwaram mandal, under the Meerpet police station limits in Rangareddy district of Telangana state near Hyderabad, the capital city. Two of the attackers have been identified and arrested by the police after protests by the Christian community in front of the police station. Accusations and Assault In the video, a group of men is seen confronting the two young women — who appeared to be minors — accusing them of attempting to convert school children to Christianity by offering them chocolates. The two girls are heard denying the allegations, saying they were merely visiting relatives in the area. However, one of the men slaps them brutally and verbally abuses them in public. One woman is seen sitting nearby, but she does not make any attempt to stop the men from attacking the girls. While the girls’ agonized apologies are heard, the man is relentlessly hitting the two girls alternately without mercy, even as another man is making half-hearted attempts to restrain the attacker. One of the girls has her glasses shattered by a forceful blow to her face from the man, who is not done hitting before he assaults the other pleading girl. The attackers accused the young women of attempting forced religious conversions by allegedly distributing chocolates to schoolchildren — a frequent, unsubstantiated trope used by Hindu nationalists in India to justify street-level violence. Protests and Public Response Meanwhile, the video of the assault went viral, triggering immediate street protests by members of the Dalit Christian organizations on Nov. 4 to demand the arrest of the perpetrators. Dalit Christians (or Christian Dalits) are people in the Indian subcontinent who converted to Christianity from historically marginalized, low-caste or “untouchable” (Dalit) backgrounds. The protests by the Dalit Christians were met with aggressive counter-sloganeering by local Hindu outfits, forcing the Telangana state police to deploy additional forces and use force to prevent a full-scale riot. While the police swiftly arrested the primary perpetrators, the incident underscored a deeper systemic shift: the normalization of extrajudicial moral policing. Christian leaders, political figures and human rights advocates condemned the assault and called for an impartial investigation and protection. Sabitha Indra Reddy, former Telangana minister, condemned the brutality on X. Reddy stated that objections regarding religious freedom should be pursued legally rather than through violence against women. To read more news stories, visit the ICC Newsroom . For interviews, please email us . To support ICC’s work around the world, please give to our Where Most Needed Fund . 一群人因试图在印度特拉干纳将印度教皈依基督教而袭击了两名基督教女孩,这引起了整个印度的愤怒。 11月初公开的一则事件视频引起了印度民族主义者对印度教徒掌握法律并攻击基督教徒指控皈依的关注.

事件发生在两个月前,在首都海得拉巴附近的Telangana州Rangareddy区的Meheshwaram mandal的Almasguda, 两名袭击者在警察局门口基督教社区抗议后被警方指认并逮捕.

指控和攻击 在影片中,一群男子面对两名年轻女子——她们似乎是未成年人——指责他们试图通过提供巧克力来使在校儿童皈依基督教. 听到两名女孩否认这些指控,说她们只是去探访该地区的亲属。

然而,其中一人在公开场合粗暴地殴打他们并辱骂他们。 一名妇女被看见坐在附近,但没有试图阻止男子攻击女孩。 这名男子毫不留情地不择手段地殴打两名女孩,

其中一个女孩的眼镜被那个男人猛烈地打到她脸上打得粉碎了,而那个男人在攻击另一个恳求的女孩之前没有打完。 袭击者指责青年妇女试图强迫改变宗教信仰,据称他们向学童分发巧克力——印度印度民族主义者经常用来为街头暴力辩护,但没有根据。

同时,袭击的视频也传入了病毒,引发了达利特基督教组织成员于11月4日立即上街抗议,要求逮捕肇事者。 贱民基督徒(或称基督教贱民)是印度次大陆上从历史上被边缘化、低种姓或“不可接触”(达利特)背景皈依基督教的人。

达利特基督徒的抗议活动遭遇了当地印度教服饰的猛烈反攻,迫使泰兰加纳州警方增派了部队并使用武力来防止全面骚乱. 虽然警方迅速逮捕了主要肇事者,但这一事件突出表明了更深刻的系统转变:法外道德警察的正常化。

基督教领袖、政治人物和人权倡导者谴责这次袭击,并呼吁进行公正的调查和保护。 前特兰加纳部长萨比莎·因德拉·雷迪(Sabitha Indra Reddy)谴责了对X的残暴行为. 雷迪表示,对宗教自由的反对应该通过法律手段而不是通过对妇女的暴力行为来进行. 更多新闻报导,

featured.title_zh: 单点菜肴（11月26日）
featured.content: Happy Thanksgiving to my American friends and family. I pray you have a restful and thankful day. As you feast, I’ll be prepping a roundup of Black Friday deals that are of interest to Christians, so be sure to check in tomorrow for that. Sales & Deals Today’s Kindle deals include the repackaged edition of J.I. Packer’s classic A Quest for Godliness , Tim Chester’s Isaiah for You , Brant Hansen’s Blessed Are the Misfits , and more. Recommended Reading Evangelicalism and ‘High’ Culture. Michael Jensen writes about the lack of Evangelical influence in high culture. “There’s good reasons for this absence. The instinct of true Christianity is thoroughly egalitarian, in recognition of the significance of every human individual and the universal appeal of the gospel. Elitism is abhorrent to true Christianity and especially to missionary Christianity. As Davison Hunter says, ‘elitism for believers is despicable and utterly anathema to the gospel they cherish’.” Reflection on a Public Memorial Service. Kraig Keck tells movingly about his experience at a public memorial service for two police officers who were killed in the line of duty. “Each element of the memorial service evoked powerful emotions in me. As I sat there I was struck by the dignity and honor of it all, and I wondered how a committed atheist evolutionist would understand this. I’m sure he would try to find some evolutionary purpose for it all, but it seemed to me that it would be ultimately unexplainable by his worldview. Why the ceremony, the quiet, the traditions, the dignity, and the honor of it all?” The Pilgrims Did Not Invent Thanksgiving. Allen C. Guelzo reminds American readers that the Pilgrims were not the ones who invented Thanksgiving. “To be sure, the Massachusetts Pilgrims probably did host a harvest dinner in 1621 to mark their survival through their first year in America. But the Thanksgiving we celebrate annually in November had its real origins much closer to the present, and its real designer not in William Bradford or William Brewster, but in the sixteenth president of the United States, Abraham Lincoln.” Quarters and Contentment. Marie Garreau explains how she has sometimes found it easier to be content during times of extreme distress than during “normal” difficulties. “The Lord gave me contentment in that season of extreme need, while in times of lesser need I have found it easier to slip from the confidence of his provision. Perhaps I lose sight of the fact that it is not just in extreme times of need that the circumstances of our lives are completely out of our own hands.” Are We Asking Too Much of Our Kids? Beth Barthelemy asks a question a lot of Christian parents wonder about, and perhaps especially those in missions or other forms of ministry: Are we asking too much of our kids? “As full-time ministry workers, my husband and I have anticipated and accepted all kinds of sacrifices on behalf of working for the kingdom. For our years overseas, those sacrifices looked like family, a sense of security, and cultural familiarity, among others. In pastoral ministry now, these sacrifices are financial, relational, and of our time. We are still discovering others.” Do We Have a Spirit of Entitlement or a Spirit of Gratitude? Randy Alcorn: “Ingratitude is not just wrong thinking—it’s the source of endless wrong thinking. An ungrateful person not only offends God, but is also the source of his own misery, and a cancer to others, spreading his misery. Ungrateful people are not only ungrateful to God but to their families and friends and co-workers and neighbors. They’re ungrateful to their church leaders, and quick to judge and condemn everyone for falling short of their standards.” Flashback Proven Faith Is More Precious than Gold. It can be difficult to make sense of our trials as we endure them. But the Bible always assures us that our difficulties are never purposeless but always in some way purposeful. God is always using them to accomplish somethin

感恩节快乐 我的美国朋友和家人。 祝你有愉快的一天 我将准备一个黑人星期五交易, 今天的销售和交易包括重新包装的J.I.

Kraig Keck 感动地讲述了他在公开追悼仪式上为两名在执勤中丧生的警官的经历. “追悼会的每一个内容都激起了我强烈的情绪。 当我坐在那里时,我对这一切的尊严和荣誉深感震惊,我想知道一个执着的无神论进化主义者会如何理解这一点.

“当然,马萨诸塞朝圣者们很可能在1621年举办了丰收晚宴,以纪念他们在美国度过第一年的生存。

但我们每年11月庆祝的感恩节,其真正的起源远近于现在,其真正的设计者并非威廉·布拉德福德或威廉·布鲁斯特,而是美国第十六任总统亚伯拉罕·林肯". 四方与内容.

Marie Garreau解释了她如何有时发现在极端困难时期比“正常”困难时期更容易满足。 “在那个极为需要的季节,上帝给予我满足,而在不太需要的时候,我发现更容易从他所提供的信任中溜走。

或许我忽视了这样一个事实,即我们的生活环境不仅在极端需要的时候,而且完全不能靠自己。” 我们问太多我们的孩子了吗? Beth Barthelemy向许多基督教家长提出一个问题, 我们要求太多孩子了吗?

“作为专职的部委工作人员,我和我丈夫期望并接受为王国工作的各种牺牲。 在我们海外的岁月中,这些牺牲看起来像家庭、安全感和文化熟悉等。 在现在的牧业部,这些牺牲是财政、关系和我们时代的牺牲。

我们还在发现其他人。” 难道我们有应享的精神和恩惠的精神吗? Randy Alcorn:“忘恩负义不仅仅是错误的想法, 一个忘恩负义的人不仅冒犯了上帝,而且也是他自己痛苦的根源,也是对他人的癌症,分散了他的痛苦.

忘恩负义的人不仅对上帝不感恩,而且对家人和朋友以及同事和邻居也不感恩。 他们对教会领袖忘恩负义, 闪回证明信仰比黄金更珍贵 在我们忍受这些考验时,可能很难理解我们的审判。

但是,圣经总是向我们保证,我们的困难永远不是无目的的,而是以某种方式有目的的。 上帝总是利用他们来完成一些事情
