featured.content: At least 14 Christians have been killed in fresh attacks across four local government areas of Plateau state, Nigeria, days after President Bola Ahmed Tinubu appealed for forgiveness over his failure to visit violence-affected communities during an earlier trip to the state and promised to rebuild destroyed communities and return internally displaced persons (IDPs) to their ancestral homes. The killings occurred between Sunday, Nov. 15, and Monday, Nov. 16, in Mangu, Riyom, Barkin Ladi and Bokkos local government areas, according to community sources and local security groups. Armed attackers reportedly targeted rural settlements and ambushed residents traveling between communities. The latest violence followed Tinubu’s visit to Jos on Saturday, Nov. 14, for an All Progressives Congress (APC) political rally at Zaria Road Stadium, where he acknowledged the suffering of communities affected by recurring attacks and displacement. Addressing residents and party supporters, Tinubu asked Plateau residents to forgive him for not visiting affected communities during his previous trip to the state in April. “When I last visited the other time, I was limited to the airport,” he said. “Forgive me if you didn’t see me in the hinterland, but I saw the devastation. I got the report from the governor. I saw horror in the faces of our people.” The president promised to rebuild communities destroyed by violence and facilitate the return of displaced residents. “We will rebuild your communities, and we will bring you back to your communities,” Tinbu added. “I have directed all the security agencies to take decisive action and sustain peace and stability on the Plateau.” He also commended the Minister of Humanitarian Affairs and Poverty Reduction, Dr. Bernard Doro, for identifying vulnerable populations and coordinating humanitarian assistance. Tinubu announced that 1,000 forest guards were undergoing training and that surveillance cameras promised to Plateau state had been procured to strengthen security monitoring and early warning operations. However, fresh attacks were reported within hours of the president’s departure from the state. In Mangu Local Government Area, armed attackers invaded Zwagal community in Jipal District at about 9 p.m. on Sunday, killing nine people. Other residents were reportedly missing following the attack. Silas Nanfwang, a resident who confirmed the incident to journalists, called on security agencies to intensify efforts to locate the attackers and bring those responsible to justice. In Barkin Ladi, 79-year-old Da Ishaku Pam Vwos was killed when armed men invaded Sho village at about 5:20 p.m. on Sunday, according to the Berom Youth Moulders Association (BYM). The association’s National Publicity Secretary, Rwang Tengwong, also reported the killing of 42-year-old Dauda John Davou during an attack on the Sambak community in Hoss District, Riyom LGA, at about 2 a.m. on Sunday. Another attack was reported in the Jol community around 12:10 a.m. on Sunday. According to BYM, local vigilantes responded to the attackers, preventing further casualties. The association said the incidents followed the shooting of Joshua Doro Dafwel in Jol on Wednesday. He is currently receiving medical attention. BYM also reported that Ina Arin was killed when armed men ambushed him and his friend, Abok Gyang, as they returned to Dorong village in Foron District. Gyang survived the attack. In Bokkos Local Government Area, two people, including a unit commander of the Plateau state-owned security outfit, Operation Rainbow, were killed in an ambush on Monday afternoon. The victims, identified as Gambo and his companion, were traveling on a motorcycle from Hurti village to Tadai in Manguna District when armed men attacked them at about 1:30 p.m. They had reportedly visited Hurti for a condolence visit and died at the scene. featured.content:
세계 곳곳의 교회와 대성당, 공공건물이 붉은빛으로 물들었다. 신앙을 지키다 박해와 폭력에 노출된 기독교인들을 기억하고, 이들을 위한 국제사회의 연대를 촉구하는 ‘레드 위크’(Red Week) 캠페인이 11월 세계 각국에서 진행되고 있다.

국제 가톨릭 구호단체 ‘에이드 투 더 처치 인 니드’(Aid to the Church in Need, 이하 ACN)이 주관하는 이번 캠페인은 11월 15일(이하 현지시각)부터 22일까지 이어지며, 18일을 중심으로 세계 각국에서 다양한 기념행사가 열렸다. 2015년 시작된 레드 위크는 순교자들의 피를 상징하는 붉은색 조명을 통해 박해받는 기독교인들의 현실을 알리는 국제적인 종교자유 캠페인이다.

ACN에 따르면 올해 행사에는 전 세계 12만5,000명 이상이 참여하며, 130개 대성당과 약 1,000개의 교회 및 건축물이 붉은빛으로 밝혀질 예정이다. 교회 조명 행사뿐 아니라 기도회와 박해 생존자 증언, 공개 행사, 학교 프로그램 등도 마련돼 신앙 때문에 고통받는 기독교인들과 연대하는 시간을 갖는다.

프랑스에서는 파리 노트르담 대성당과 사크레쾨르 대성당, 샤르트르 대성당 등 주요 종교·역사 건축물이 붉은빛으로 밝혀졌다. 프랑스 전역에서는 약 80개 교회와 장소가 참여하고 4,000여 명의 자원봉사자가 농촌 지역까지 캠페인을 알리고 있다. 스페인에서도 250개가 넘는 교회와 대성당, 기념물 및 공공건물이 참여했으며, 영국에서는 런던 사우스워크의 성 조지 대성당에서 특별 미사가 열렸다. 아일랜드의 녹 대성당과 오스트리아 대통령궁 등도 캠페인에 동참했다.

이번 행사는 세계 기독교 박해 상황이 악화하고 있다는 우려 속에서 진행됐다. ACN의 최근 종교자유 보고서에 따르면 전 세계 약 4억1,300만 명의 기독교인이 종교자유에 대한 심각한 침해가 발생하는 국가에 살고 있으며, 약 2억2,000만 명은 직접적인 박해에 노출돼 있다. 특히 ACN이 집중적으로 관찰한 18개국에서는 지난 2년간 기독교인의 종교자유 상황이 개선되지 않았으며, 절반이 넘는 국가에서 상황이 악화한 것으로 나타났다.

보고서는 극단주의 폭력과 권위주의 정부, 종교적 민족주의가 기독교 공동체에 대한 압박을 가중하고 있다고 지적했다. 아프리카와 아시아 일부 지역에서는 무력 분쟁과 종교적 폭력으로 기독교인들이 거주지를 떠나는 상황도 이어지고 있다. 중동에서는 정치적 혼란과 전쟁이 지속되면서 기독교 신앙의 역사적 중심지에서 공동체의 존속 자체가 위협받고 있다는 우려도 제기됐다.

ACN 국제본부 레지나 린치 대표는 영상 메시지를 통해 “우리는 순교자들의 피를 상징하는 붉은색으로 교회와 건물들을 밝히고 있다”며 “그들은 종종 외로움과 고립감을 느끼며 희망이 필요하다. 우리가 드리는 기도를 통해 그들에게 희망을 전할 수 있다”고 말했다.

캠페인은 11월 23일 프랑스 스트라스부르 유럽의회 건물 점등 행사로도 이어질 예정이다. 필리핀에서는 주교회의가 11월 25일을 레드 웬즈데이로 지정했으며, 전국 87개 교구가 참여해 박해받는 기독교인을 위한 기도와 특별 헌금을 진행할 계획이다.

世界各地的教堂、大教堂和公共建筑都被染成红色。 11月，世界各地将举办“红色周”活动，纪念那些在保护信仰的同时遭受迫害和暴力的基督徒，并呼吁国际社会声援他们。这项活动由国际天主教救援组织援助有需要的教会（ACN）主办，从当地时间11月15日持续到22日，18日左右世界各地举行了各种纪念活动。红色周始于2015年，是一项国际宗教自由运动，通过象征烈士鲜血的红色灯光来宣传基督徒受迫害的现实。

据ACN报道，来自世界各地的超过125,000人将参加今年的活动，130座大教堂和约1,000座教堂和建筑将被点亮红色。除了教堂点灯活动外，还举办祈祷会、迫害幸存者见证、公共活动和学校活动，为因信仰而遭受苦难的基督徒提供时间与团结。在法国，巴黎圣母院、圣心大教堂、沙特尔大教堂等主要宗教和历史建筑都被红色照亮。法国各地大约 80 个教堂和场所参与其中，超过 4,000 名志愿者甚至向农村地区传播这项活动。在西班牙，超过250座教堂、大教堂、纪念碑和公共建筑参加了活动；在英国，在伦敦萨瑟克区的圣乔治大教堂举行了一场特别弥撒。

爱尔兰诺克大教堂和奥地利总统府也参与了此次活动。这次活动是在人们担心世界各地基督徒受迫害的情况日益恶化的背景下举行的。根据ACN最新的宗教自由报告，全球约4.13亿基督徒生活在宗教自由受到严重侵犯的国家，约2.2亿基督徒面临直接迫害。尤其是在ACN重点观察的18个国家中，基督徒的宗教自由状况近两年来并没有改善，超过一半的国家情况还进一步恶化。报告指出，极端主义暴力、独裁政府和宗教民族主义正在给基督教社区带来越来越大的压力。

在非洲和亚洲部分地区，基督徒因武装冲突和宗教暴力而背井离乡。随着中东政治混乱和战争的持续，人们担心基督教信仰历史中心社区的存在正在受到威胁。 ACN 国际总部代表雷吉娜·林奇 (Regina Lynch) 在视频信息中表示：“我们用红色点亮我们的教堂和建筑物，象征着烈士的鲜血。” “他们常常感到孤独和孤立，需要希望。通过我们的祈祷，我们可以给他们希望。”该活动还将继续于 11 月 23 日在法国斯特拉斯堡的欧洲议会大厦举行灯光活动。

在菲律宾，主教团将11月25日定为红色星期三，全国87个教区计划参加为受迫害基督徒的祈祷和特别捐款。

featured.title_zh: 隆重介绍圣若瑟天主教堂助理神父马丁·基隆佐（Martin Kilonzo）
featured.content: My name is Fr. Martin Kilonzo, ALCP/OSS. I am a Roman Catholic priest and a member of the Apostolic Life Community of Priests in Opus Spiritus Sancti (ALCP/OSS). Originally from Kenya, East Africa, I currently serve as parochial vicar at St. Joseph’s Church in Devils Lake, N.D. My journey has been a remarkable experience of faith, formation, missionary service, and trust in God’s providence. I was born in 1978 in Kilenge, a small village in Makueni County, southeastern Kenya, where I attended elementary school. I later joined Pope Paul VI Minor Seminary in the Diocese of Machakos, my home diocese, where I received a high school education and spiritual formation that helped prepare me for the priesthood. After four years at the minor seminary, I pursued three years of philosophical studies at the Spiritan Missionary Seminary in Arusha, Tanzania, followed by four years of theological studies at Jordan University College in Morogoro, Tanzania. I was ordained a priest in July 2012 in the Diocese of Moshi, in Tanzania’s Kilimanjaro Region. Since my ordination, I have served in various pastoral assignments in Tanzania and Italy, enriching my missionary experience and understanding of different cultures. In 2026, following consultations between my religious superiors and the Bishop of Fargo, I was assigned to the Diocese of Fargo, N.D., beginning a new chapter in my priestly ministry. October 15 holds special significance for me as the anniversary of the day I first set foot on American soil. I arrived in Chicago before taking a connecting flight to Minot, N.D. After spending approximately one week serving at St. Mary’s Cathedral in Fargo, I was assigned to St. Joseph’s Church in Devils Lake, where I officially began my ministry as parochial vicar in February 2026. I consider my assignment in North Dakota a privilege and a renewed call to missionary service. Through God’s grace, I am grateful for the opportunity to celebrate the sacraments, provide spiritual guidance, and serve the parishioners of St. Joseph’s Church and the wider Devils Lake community, regardless of religious affiliation or background. For me, the journey from Kilenge, Kenya, to Devils Lake, N.D., is more than a change of place; it is a continuing response to God’s call to faith, service, and missionary discipleship with humility.
featured.content_zh:
我叫马丁・基隆佐,ALCP/OSS。 我是一名罗马天主教神父,也是奥普斯·斯皮里图斯·桑茨蒂(ALCP/OSS)牧师的使徒生活社区的成员。 我最初来自肯尼亚、东非, 我的旅程在信仰、组织、传教仪式和对上帝之赐的信任方面,是非凡的经历。

1978年出生于肯尼亚东南部马库埃尼县的一个小村庄Kilenge,在那里就读小学. 我后来加入教宗保罗六世小神学院(Pope Paul VI Minor Seminary),参加我的家乡教区马查科斯教区,在那里我接受了高中教育和精神培养,帮助我为神职做好准备.

在小神学院学习了四年之后,我在坦桑尼亚阿鲁沙的Spiritan传教士神学院学习了三年哲学,之后在坦桑尼亚莫罗戈罗的约旦大学学院学习了四年神学。 我于2012年7月在坦桑尼亚乞力马扎罗大区莫希教区被任命为牧师。

自从我担任教职以来,我在坦桑尼亚和意大利从事各种牧业任务,丰富了我的传教经验和对不同文化的理解。 2026年,经我的宗教上司与法尔戈主教磋商,我被分配到北大法尔戈主教座堂,开始了我牧师部的新篇章.

10月15日是我第一次踏上美国土地的纪念日,对我来说具有特殊的意义. 我在搭乘连接航班去纽约州米诺特之前到达芝加哥 在法戈的圣玛丽大教堂服役约一周后,我被分配到魔鬼湖的圣约瑟教堂,2026年2月正式开始我的牧师部。

我将我在北达科他州的任务视为一种特权,也是对传教士服务的再次呼吁。 通过上帝的恩典,我感谢有机会庆祝圣训,提供精神指导,并为圣约瑟教堂的教友和更广泛的恶魔湖社区服务,而不论其宗教信仰或背景如何.

对我而言,从肯尼亚基伦格到N.D.D.的恶魔湖的旅程不仅仅是改变地方;它是对上帝发出的信仰、服务和谦逊的传教士的不断响应。

featured.title: 我在這裡，請差遣我｜2026 台中場萬軍宣教年會回顧
featured.source: 中華宣教聯盟 · 宣教故事1001（中）
featured.summary: 2026 年 9 月 20 日，萬軍宣教年會在台中思恩堂美福教會舉行。這不只是一場禾場近況的分享，更是一個邀請：讓門徒訓練不只改變生命，也使人活出使命；從聽見遠方，到願意把自己放進神正在工作的地方。
featured.content: 2026 WANJUN MISSION・TAICHUNG 我在這裡， 請差遣我 這不只是一場禾場報告，而是一個回應的邀請：從聽見遠方，到願意把生命放進神正在工作的地方。 2026 台中場萬軍宣教年會回顧 讓門徒訓練，不只改變生命，也使人活出使命 2026 年 9 月 20 日，我們在台中思恩堂美福教會相聚。從非洲、中東、黑海到南島，講台上的每一段分享，都不是遙遠的故事，而是正在發生的生命現場。 有人在艱難的環境裡長久陪伴，有人用教育與生活技能扶持一個家庭重新站起；也有人在受裝備之後，預備回到自己的家鄉建立教會。宣教因此不只是一趟旅程，而是一種被福音更新後的生活。 「我在這裡，請差遣我。」 宣教不是只把消息帶回來，而是讓台灣的教會看見：生命如何在長久陪伴中被建立。 從難民青年到返鄉的門徒 在生活裡接受裝備，也在生活裡預備被差遣 年會影片分享了難民青年接受一年裝備的過程：聖經、音樂、電腦、體育與生活技能一起進入每天的學習。訓練不是把信仰留在課堂，而是讓人學習承擔、服事，並在帳篷教會中實習。 當第一批學生預備回到家鄉，他們帶回去的不只是一份知識，更是一個建立教會、陪伴社區的使命。福音在這裡成為能夠走進家庭，也能夠走回故鄉的力量。 一張地圖讓遠方不再只是地名，也讓每一個禱告有了方向。 移動中的世代，也能成為被差遣的世代 把離開家鄉的路，轉化為帶著使命前行的路 在尼泊爾的分享中，青年大量前往海外工作，是家庭的盼望，也是當地教會長期面對的挑戰。好不容易建立的年輕門徒，可能很快就離開熟悉的土地。 但年會提出另一個眼光：如果門徒被健康地建立，他們不只是外出工作的人，也能在所到之處成為宣教士。流動不再只是失去，也可能成為福音跨越文化、進入新群體的道路。 ONE BODY・MANY FIELDS 四個區域，一個彼此承接的宣教身體 年會把非洲、中東、黑海與南島的工作放在同一個視野中。不同禾場有不同的語言、需要與節奏，但都指向同一件事：教會要在真實生活裡陪伴人，也要預備下一代接續前行。 非洲 難民青年裝備、社區陪伴與返鄉開拓 中東 在艱難之地以生活、產業與福音長久同行 黑海 面對變動與流離，建立能承擔使命的門徒 南島 跨越島嶼與文化，承接福音最後一棒 從聽見，到一起回應 敬拜、禱告，也讓每一個人說出自己的下一步 聚會的最後，不是停在「知道更多」。會眾一起敬拜、禱告，並在小組中分享與聆聽。有人重新看見自己的位置，有人開始為禾場守望，也有人思考：我能如何參與神已經開始的工作？ THE NEXT STEP 宣教從一個願意的回應開始 不是每一個人都立刻走到遠方，但每一個人都能開始聆聽、禱告、關心，並在神所託付的位置上踏出下一步。 認識萬軍宣教禾場 加入禱告與守望

À 26 ans, une rencontre inattendue sur une route de Terre sainte bouleverse le destin de cet Américain qui, quelques années plus tôt, exerçait encore des métiers manuels. Rien ne le prédestinait à devenir chirurgien, encore moins à consacrer une grande partie de son existence aux populations les plus pauvres d’Afrique. Pourtant, depuis près de trois décennies, c’est au Kenya, dans un hôpital isolé, qu’il met ses compétences médicales au service des plus démunis, guidé par sa foi profonde en Jésus-Christ. Tout commence dans les années 1970. featured.content_zh:
上帝有时会走意想不到的道路，引导每个人找到自己的使命。现年 72 岁的比尔·罗兹（Bill Rhodes）的人生就是一个很好的例子。26岁时，这位美国人在圣地的公路上意外邂逅，从此改变了他的命运。就在几年前，他还从事着体力劳动。

没有任何迹象表明他注定会成为一名外科医生，更不用说将自己一生的大部分时间奉献给非洲最贫困的群体。然而，近三十年来，他一直身处肯尼亚的一家偏远医院，在对耶稣基督的深厚信仰的指引下，将自己的医学技能用于为最贫困的人群服务。这一切始于 20 世纪 70 年代。

featured.title_zh: Félix Lungu ： É muito difícil ser cristão em países fundamentais
featured.content: É a maior comunidade religiosa, mas também a mais perseguida do mundo. Os cristãos são notícia quase diariamente por serem alvo de ataques ou assassínios; ou por as suas instalações e símbolos terem sido danificados. Só em setembro, o Observatory on Intolerance and Discrimination against Christians dá conta de 30 casos na Europa, entre atos de vandalismo a igrejas, cemitérios, ataques a sacerdotes - um foi assassinado - ou mesmo a discriminação profissional por se ser cristão. Se a Nigéria é considerada o país mais perigoso para os católicos, o México é o inferno para padres, pois é aí que mais são assassinados. O Nascer do SOL entrevista Félix Lungu, um romeno a viver em Portugal há 31 anos, porta-voz, em Portugal, da fundação Ajuda à Igreja que Sofre (AIS). Esta organização faz relatórios sobre a liberdade religiosa no mundo, e tenta explicar onde as religiões são mais perseguidas e quais os desafios que enfrentam, com especial ênfase na Igreja Católica. Félix Langu, à semelhança dos seus chefes - a organização tem sede na Alemanha -, procura não alimentar divisões, mas é impossível fugir a factos: no Paquistão, só muito recentemente é que os empresários do lixo deixaram de recrutar obrigatoriamente cristãos; não faltam países fundamentalistas onde meninas de 10 anos são violadas e obrigadas a casar, ‘adquirindo’ automaticamente a religião islâmica; e são ainda muitas as nações onde os católicos não podem desempenhar cargos na função pública. O Vaticano calcula que, anualmente, são mortos cerca de cinco mil cristãos, mas a liberdade religiosa afeta também os muçulmanos moderados, que são alvo da ira dos fundamentalistas, acabando muitos deles assassinados. Qual o papel da Fundação Ajuda à Igreja que Sofre? A Ajuda à Igreja que Sofre, fundação Pontifícia, é uma organização que tem quase 80 anos e foi criada na Alemanha. Nasceu no final da Segunda Guerra Mundial para ajudar os refugiados alemães que se deslocavam pela Europa. Depois, pouco a pouco, ajudou cristãos dos países do Leste, por causa do comunismo, do ateísmo, de toda essa situação. Ou seja, não somos como a Cáritas, ou outras ONGs, no sentido de dar ajuda social, ou educação, ou saúde. Também chegamos a estas áreas, o foco, contudo, é a ajuda pastoral, ajudar a Igreja, ajudar sacerdotes, construir igrejas, formação de seminaristas, ajudar nas missões os missionários, com carros, com rádios, televisões, bíblias, o que é necessário para fazer a evangelização. Basicamente é isso e estamos em 24 países. A sede é na Alemanha, onde se faz a gestão de tudo isso. E nos outros 24 secretariados fazemos a angariação de fundos. Para fazer a angariação de fundos é preciso saber por que se pede dinheiro, por que se pede esta ajuda. Temos três pilares, digamos assim, da nossa missão: informar, rezar e ajudar. Informar é tentar dizer qual é a situação no mundo, sobretudo onde há carências, que tipo de carências, sempre com foco nesta dimensão pastoral ou de evangelização. Nos últimos anos, a Ajuda à Igreja que Sofre dedica-se ao estudo ou análise da situação da liberdade religiosa no mundo. Porque se nós somos uma organização da Igreja, e se temos parceiros em todo o mundo, em 186 países, é importante saber onde há carências, que tipo de carências são. E temos percebido que, por exemplo, no Médio Oriente, junto com as carências materiais, falta de escola, de saúde, da alimentação, há também esta dimensão da perseguição. Falta algo que valorizamos muito, que é a questão da liberdade religiosa, dos direitos, que estão valorizados no ocidente. O que fazem nesses países onde os cristão são perseguidos? Na Arábia Saudita, por exemplo, não há hipótese de haver uma igreja? Não, na Arábia Saudita não temos uma presença. A única presença nesses países é através da representação consular. É na capela de uma embaixada, por exemplo, de França ou de Itália, que se pode celebrar a missa, porque não há possibilidade de ter uma igreja na Arábia Saudita. featured.content:
제47회 신촌포럼이 ‘듣고, 읽고, 행하자’는 주제로 서울 마포구 신촌성결교회(담임 박노훈 목사)에서 개최됐다.

이번 포럼에서는 ‘함께 읽고, 함께 듣고, 다시 오래 머무는 신앙의 여정’을 부제로 공동체 성경읽기 운동을 벌이고 있는 G&M ASIA and Japan 김승환 이사장의 주제강연과 교수들의 패널토의가 마련됐다.

박노훈 목사는 “신촌포럼은 1997년 시작돼 30년을 맞이했다. 매년 두 차례 이상 포럼을 통해 교회와 사회, 신학과 목회 사이 다리를 놓고 새로운 대안을 제시하는 일에 집중해 왔다”며 “이번 포럼은 신앙의 생활화를 제안하고 학교와 교회의 실제 적용 모델을 모색하고자 한다. 참여하는 우리 모두에게 하늘의 귀한 복이 임할 줄 믿는다”고 인사했다.

읽는 것과 듣는 것이 다른가? PRS, 아시아 41개 도시 진행

오희천 박사 사회로 신촌포럼 이상직 위원장의 포럼 소개 후, 김승환 이사장은 ‘Listening the Scripture, Doing the Scripture(성경을 듣고, 행하는 삶)’라는 제목으로 주제강연을 전했다.

김승환 이사장은 “성경을 읽고 들을 때 어떠한 자세와 마음으로 들어야 할지 수많은 사람들이 이야기하고 있다. 유진 피터슨 목사는 내게 필요한 말씀을 선택하고 소비하는 성향을 지적하기도 했다. 이런 ‘성경 소비자들’을 향해, 느헤미야 선지자는 백성들이 말씀에 귀를 기울였다고 전한다”며 “공동체 성경읽기는 디모데전서 4장 13절 말씀 ‘the Public Reading of Scripture’에서 왔다”고 소개했다.

김 이사장은 “말씀이 우리를 깨우치게 하신다. 요한계시록 1장 3절 말씀에서 ‘읽는 자’는 단수형, ‘듣는 자’는 복수형으로 기록돼 있다. 훈련된 사람이 읽고, 청중들이 함께 듣는 것”이라며 “읽고 듣는 데서 끝내지 않고, 행함이 따라와야 한다. 저희 재단은 하나님께서 자라나게 하심을 믿고, 6년 전부터 교회와 신학교를 섬기기로 했다. 지금은 서울과 도쿄를 중심으로, 아시아 41개 도시에서 PRS가 진행되고 있다”고 말했다.

그는 “현재 PRS는 한국에서 서울신대가 가장 밀접하게 함께하고 있다. 고신대와 한동대, 명지학원 등 많은 단체들과 교회들이 함께하고 있다”며 “세계로도 확산되고 있다. 뉴욕을 중심으로 북미와 남미, 유럽과 중동, 아프리카 대학에서도 함께 성경을 읽고 있다. 그리고 하버드 로스쿨에서 몇 년째 모임이 이뤄지고 있다”고 소개했다.

김 이사장은 “읽는 것과 듣는 것이 뭐가 다르냐고 하신다. 그러나 성경을 연구하듯 읽기보다(Reading), 말씀의 현재성에 주목하고자 한다”며 “지나간 글이 아니라 살아있는 말씀을 관계적으로 듣는 행위로서(Listening) 풍성함으로 초대하는 것이다. 이를 위해서는 경청의 자세와 청종이 필요하다”고 덧붙였다.

하나님 말씀과 인간의 들음 들음의 능력, 말씀으로 회복

2부 패널토의에서 ‘믿음은 들음에서 나고’라는 제목으로 오희천 교수(호서대)는 “들음은 행함을 내포한다. 한국어에서 ‘들으라’는 말에는 행하라는 의미도 함축돼 있다. 성경을 왜 들어야 하는가? 들어야 믿음이 생기기 때문”이라며 “하나님 말씀은 살아있고 생명력이 있기 때문에(히 4:12), 그리스도의 말씀(비유)은 지금 여기 생생한 삶의 현장에서 해석돼야 한다”고 말했다.

오희천 교수는 “본래 하나님 말씀과 인간의 들음은 불가분적으로 종속적이었다. 그러나 인간은 보암직도 먹음직도 한 것에 유혹돼, 들음의 능력을 상실했다. 들음의 능력을 상실한 시대는 궁핍한 시대”라며 “설교자는 시인이자 사상가로서 이런 궁핍한 시대의 전도자여야 한다. 상실된 들음의 능력은 그리스도의 말씀(레마)을 통해, 그리스도의 말씀으로 말미암아 회복된다”고 설명했다.

오 교수는 “인간이 하나님을 직접 볼 수 없듯, 하나님 말씀도 직접 들을 수 없다. 기록된 말씀을 읽어야 하나님을 볼(알) 수 있고, 기록된 말씀을 들어야 하나님 말씀(음성)을 들을 수 있다”며 “색과 소리가 너무 강하면, 영적 상상력이 약해진다. ‘무엇을 먹을까 무엇을 마실까’에 대한 관심의 색과 소리가 너무 과하면 하나님 나라와 의를 보기 어렵다. AI의 색과 소리에 너무 집착하면, 소리를 듣지 못하고 자발적으로 문명과 인공지능의 노예가 되기 쉽다”고 우려했다.

예배학적 관점 공동체 성경읽기 신·구약, 공동체 성경 읽기 증언

‘공동체 성경읽기에 대한 예배학적 관점’이라는 주제로 조기연 교수(서울신대)는 “구약 느헤미야 8장 1-10절은 이스라엘 공동체가 ‘공동체 성경읽기’를 통해 모든 백성들이 하나님 말씀을 듣고 깨달으며 하나님을 예배했다고 증언한다”며 “신약 누가복음 4장 16절 이하는 예수께서 공생애 기간 정기적으로 회당에 가셔서 예배에 참여하셨음을 증언한다. 예수께서 ‘이 글이 오늘날 너희 귀에 응했다’고 해석하신 것은 랍비의 자격을 갖추셨음을 의미한다”고 풀이했다.

조기연 교수는 “사도 시대 예배는 크게 성경봉독과 설교, 성찬으로 이뤄져 있었다. 4세기 말까지는 ‘예배의 부름’ 직후 성경봉독으로 예배가 시작됐는데, 이는 동방·서방 교회의 공통적 방식이었다”며 “4세기 안디옥 예배 전통에서는 율법서와 예언서를 읽은 후 신약의 서신서와 사도행전을 읽고, 마지막으로 복음서를 읽었다. 7세기부터는 구약과 신약 한 곳씩 읽었고, 9세기 이후 비잔틴 예전에서는 주일에 신약만 두 곳을 읽었다”고 소개했다.

조 교수는 “초대교회의 성경읽기 방식은 주로 ‘연속 읽기(lectio continua)’였으나, 점차 특정 절기에 읽어야 할 특정 본문들을 결정해서 읽는 ‘선택 읽기(lectio selecta)’로 바뀌었고, 동방·서방 교회 모두 부활절에는 사도행전을 봉독했다”며 “성 주간(Holy Week)에는 예수 그리스도의 수난을 공동체 성경읽기 형식으로 재현하고 묵상했다. 이러한 방식은 예수의 수난을 오늘 예배 공동체가 참여하고 묵상한다는 의미”라고 설명했다.

성서적 토대와 학원 사례 PRS 후 식사, 환대의 표현

‘읽어주는 사람과 듣고 지키는 사람들은 복되도다: PRS/JSU의 성서적 토대와 학원 사례를 중심으로’라는 제목으로 이승문 교수(명지전문대 교목실장)는 “공동체 성경읽기(PRS)는 초대교회 공적 낭독 구조를 현대적으로 회복하려는 실천”이라며 “PRS에서 성경을 함께 들은 직후 즉각적 해석이나 감상 나눔을 유보하는 것은 생각을 금지하기 위해서가 아니라, 본문 자체가 공동체 안에서 충분히 들리도록 시간을 확보하기 위해서”라고 전했다.

이승문 교수는 “‘Just Show Up(JSU)’은 성경이 아닌 일반 도서를 함께 읽는 실천이라는 점에서 PRS와 구별된다. PRS가 말씀의 공적 청취에 초점을 둔다면, JSU는 독서 뒤 자기표현과 상호 경청을 훈련한다”며 “PRS와 식사 제공 후 JSU를 진행하는 것은 처음 온 사람에게도 자리를 내어주고 참여 자격을 묻지 않는 환대의 표현”이라고 밝혔다.

이 교수는 “명지중학교는 청소년 PRS/JSU 그룹 모델을 이루고, 명지전문대학은 대규모 채플(PRS)과 소규모 채플(JSU), 오픈 PRS/JSU, 학과 비전모임 등 기존 교육·신앙 활동에 PRS와 JSU를 정기적으로 진행하고 있다”며 “공동체 성경읽기의 성패는 얼마나 많이 읽고 들었는가보다, 그 말씀이 삶으로 발현되는 것이 얼마나 중요한가를 알게 한다. 한 사람이 읽어주고, 공동체가 함께 듣고, 말씀을 삶에서 지킨다는 원리를 각 기관 상황에 맞게 구현해야 할 것”이라고 제언했다.

기독교 상담의 관점에서 성경 속 ‘나의 이야기’ 듣기

‘들음과 멈춤과 나눔의 미학: 기독교 상담의 관점에서 바라본 공동체 성경읽기(PRS)와 독서모임(JSU)’을 제목으로 홍정택 목사(솔트기독상담센터 대표)는 “PRS와 JSU에서 가장 주목한 것은 공동체 안에서 함께 성경을 읽고 공동체 앞에서 느낀 바를 자유롭게 이야기할 수 있도록 분위기를 제공하는 나눔의 기능”이라고 전했다.

홍정택 목사는 “JSU 독서모임이 ‘읽기→ 멈춤→ 자기언어→ 경청’의 핵심 리듬을 지향하는 점은 기존 주입식 성경공부와 다른 장점을 제공할 수 있다”며 “권위자에게 받는 일방향 교육에서 확장해 성경 이야기에 머물러 있으므로, 성경 이야기 속에서 ‘나의 이야기’를
featured.content_zh:
第47届新村论坛在首尔麻浦区新村圣洁教会（主任牧师朴鲁勋）举行，主题为“聆听、阅读、践行”。本次论坛以“一起阅读、一起聆听、在信仰的旅程中再次长久停留”为副标题，安排了正在开展团体圣经阅读运动的G&M ASIA and Japan理事长金胜焕的主题演讲以及教授们的专题讨论。朴鲁勋牧师表示：“新村论坛始于1997年，如今已走过了30个年头。每年通过至少两次论坛，我们一直致力于在教会与社会、神学与牧会之间搭建桥梁，并提出新的替代方案。”他还表示：“本次论坛旨在倡导将信仰融入生活，并探索学校与教会的实际应用模式。我相信，天上宝贵的祝福将临到我们所有参与者。” 阅读和聆听有什么不同吗？

PRS在亚洲41个城市举办

在由吴熙千博士主持、新村论坛理事长李相直介绍论坛之后，金承焕理事长发表了题为“Listening the Scripture, Doing the Scripture（聆听圣经，践行圣经）”的主旨演讲。金胜焕理事长表示：“有很多人在谈论阅读和聆听圣经时应该以怎样的态度和心态来聆听。尤金·彼得森牧师也指出了人们倾向于选择和消费自己需要的话语。针对这些‘圣经消费者’，先知尼希米说，百姓们聆听了神的话语。”他还介绍说，“集体读经源于提摩太前书4章13节的‘the Public Reading of Scripture’（圣经的公开宣读）。”

金理事长表示：“神的话语使我们得到启迪。在启示录第1章第3节中，“念”是单数，“听”是复数。受过训练的人来朗读，听众们一起聆听。”他还表示：“不能止步于阅读和聆听，而是要付诸行动。我们基金会相信上帝会使我们成长，因此从6年前开始就决定要服侍教会和神学院。目前，PRS正在以首尔和东京为中心，在亚洲的41个城市开展。” 他说：“目前在韩国，首尔神学大学与PRS的合作最为紧密。高神大学、汉东大学、明知学园等许多团体和教会都在参与其中。”他还表示：“PRS也在向全世界传播。以纽约为中心，北美、南美、欧洲、中东和非洲的大学也在共同阅读圣经。

此外，在哈佛法学院，这样的聚会已经持续了好几年。” 金理事长表示：“有人会问，阅读和聆听有什么区别。然而，我们希望关注的是话语的当下性，而不是像研读圣经那样去阅读（Reading）。”他还补充道：“这是一种以关系性的方式聆听（Listening）活生生的话语，而不是过去的文章，从而被邀请进入丰盛的境界。为此，我们需要有倾听的态度和顺服的行动。” 神的话语与人的聆听 聆听的能力，藉着话语得着恢复

在第二部分的专题讨论中，以“信心是因听道而生”为题，湖西大学的吴熙千教授表示：“听道包含了行道。在韩语中，“听”这个词也隐含着“行”的意思。为什么我们要聆听圣经？

因为只有听了才能产生信心。”他还说：“由于神的话语是活泼有力的（来4:12），基督的话语（比喻）必须在当下、在鲜活的生活场景中得到诠释。” 吴熙千教授表示：“本来，神的话语和人的聆听是不可分割地相互依存的。然而，人类被好看又好吃的东西所诱惑，失去了聆听的能力。丧失聆听能力的时代是一个贫乏的时代。”他还表示：“传道人作为诗人兼思想家，应当成为这样一个贫乏时代的传道者。失去的聆听能力将通过基督的话语（rhema），藉着基督的话语得到恢复。” 吴教授表示：“正如人无法直接看见神一样，人也无法直接听见神的话。

只有阅读记录下来的话语，才能看见（认识）神；只有聆听记录下来的话语，才能听到神的话语（声音）。”他还表示：“如果色彩和声音过于强烈，灵性的想象力就会变弱。如果对“吃什么、喝什么”的关注所产生的色彩和声音过于强烈，就很难看到神的国和神的义。如果过于沉迷于人工智能的色彩和声音，就容易听不到声音，从而自愿成为文明和人工智能的奴隶。”

从礼拜学的角度看共同体读经 新约与旧约、共同体读经的见证

以“从礼拜学角度看待团体读经”为主题，赵基妍教授（首尔神学大学）表示：“旧约《尼希米记》第8章1-10节见证了以色列团体通过‘团体读经’让所有百姓聆听并领悟神的话语，并敬拜神。”他还表示：“新约《路加福音》第4章16节以下见证了耶稣在传道期间定期前往会堂并参与礼拜。耶稣解释说‘这段经文今天在你们耳中应验了’，这意味着他具备了拉比的资格。” 赵基妍教授表示：“使徒时代的礼拜主要由圣经朗读、讲道和圣餐组成。

直到4世纪末，“礼拜的呼召”之后，礼拜都以圣经朗读开始，这是东方和西方教会的共同做法。”他还介绍说：“在4世纪安提阿的礼拜传统中，先读律法书和先知书，然后读新约的书信和使徒行传，最后读福音书。从7世纪开始，人们分别读一段旧约和一段新约；9世纪以后，拜占庭礼仪在主日只读两段新约。”

赵教授表示：“早期教会的圣经阅读方式主要是‘连续阅读（lectio continua）’，但后来逐渐转变为‘选择阅读（lectio selecta）’，即确定在特定节期应阅读的特定经文并进行阅读。东方和西方教会都在复活节诵读《使徒行传》。这种方式意味着今天的礼拜群体参与并默想耶稣的受难。”

圣经基础和学校案例 PRS PRS 用餐后、热情好客的表达

李承文教授（明知学院牧师主任）在题为“阅读者、倾听者和坚持者有福：聚焦 PRS/JSU 的圣经基础和学院案例”的标题下说，“社区圣经阅读（PRS）是一种寻求以现代方式恢复早期教会公共阅读结构的实践。”他补充说，“在 PRS 中一起听完圣经后，不立即解释或分享欣赏的原因并不是为了禁止思考，而是因为文本本身是在社区中使用的。“这是为了确保有足够的时间让人们听到。李升文教授表示：“‘Just Show Up (JSU)’与PRS不同，它是阅读一般书籍而不是圣经的做法。

“如果说 PRS 专注于公众聆听神的话语，那么 JSU 则训练阅读后的自我表达和相互聆听，”他说。 “在 PRS 和用餐后举办 JSU 是一种热情好客的表现，为首次来访者提供空间，并且不询问参与资格。”李教授表示：“明知中学形成了青年PRS/JSU团体模式，明知学院设有大礼拜堂（PRS）和小礼拜堂（JSU），开放PRS/JSU，并举办部门愿景会议。” “除了现有的教育和宗教活动之外，PRS 和 JSU 也是定期开展的，”他说。 “社区读经的成功或失败，比读或听多少圣经更重要，而更重要的是在一个人的生活中表达出来的话语有多重要。”

他建议，要根据各机构的情况，落实一个人读、社区共同听、生活中守信用的原则。从基督徒辅导的角度聆听圣经中的“我的故事”

洪正泽牧师（Salt基督教咨询中心代表）在题为“倾听、暂停、分享的美学：从基督徒咨询的角度看社区读经（PRS）和阅读俱乐部（JSU）”的主题中说：“在PRS和JSU，我最关注的是分享功能，它提供了一种氛围，让人们可以在社区中一起阅读圣经，并在社区面前自由地谈论自己的感受。”

featured.summary_zh: 2026年11月7日，教宗利奥十四世抵达蒙得维的亚百年体育场参加祈祷守夜活动，他在教宗座驾上向信众挥手致意。（法新社照片）教宗利奥十四世于11月7日告诫学生们
featured.title_zh: 教皇警告人工智能会导致非人性化
featured.content: Pope Leo XIV waves to faithful from the popemobile upon his arrival for a prayer vigil at the Centenario Stadium in Montevideo on November 7, 2026. (AFP Photo) Pope Leo XIV warned students on Nov. 7 of “dehumanization” through the use of AI in education, and urged schools and university to place the “person before the algorithm.” “The process of dehumanization we are experiencing poses a challenge,” the pope, who has warned repeatedly about the need to ensure AI is used ethically, said in a speech at the Catholic University of Uruguay. Just three weeks after undergoing surgery for lung cancer, the 71-year-old pontiff is on a 12-day tour of South Africa where he served nearly two decades as a missionary. On Nov. 7, he visited the crime-blighted Montevideo neighborhood of Casavalle. The murder rate in the impoverished district is four times the national average and residents spoke movingly of the dangers they faced, like commonplace gun violence. Katherine Silva’s voice cracked with emotion as she told the pope about the violence and abuse she had suffered as a child. After ending up homeless at 15, the young mother said she “went through very dark times” and “nearly died.” “There are children in Uruguay who do not go to school for fear of never returning home,” Leo said. “In a country as rich in resources as this, children should never have to go to bed hungry... Much less should they have to suffer violence to the point of losing their lives,” he added. As police helicopters flew overhead, locals waved and cheered to welcome the head of the world’s 1.4 billion Catholics, who blessed 12 new low-income houses financed by the Church.

教皇利奥十四世于2026年11月7日抵达蒙得维的亚百人马体育场举行祈祷仪式时,从教皇座堂向忠实者挥手. (AFP Photo)教宗利奥十四在11月警告学生.

featured.content: About 130 cathedrals, thousands of churches, and over 125,000 people around the world are expected to take part in Red Week this month, with the European Parliament in Strasbourg, France, honoring the occasion by lighting up in red on Nov. 23. Red Week 2026 will take place from Nov. 15–22, with Red Wednesday falling on Nov. 18 in most regions, although it will be observed on Nov. 25 in the Philippines. The observance began in 2016 by Aid to the Church in Need (ACN), an international Catholic aid organization and Pontifical Foundation of the Church that supports Christians who are persecuted, oppressed, or in material need. The week includes illuminating monuments in red, prayer vigils, testimonies, and seminars on Christian persecution around the world. Designed to raise awareness of the ongoing Christian persecution in countries particularly in Africa and Asia, Red Week brings together those who are persecuted and those who are working to end violence and hatred against people of faith. At various events, testimonials from survivors of religious persecution will provide powerful moments of reflection about the suffering and human rights violations happening around us that go unnoticed. According to the latest figures provided by ACN, 413 million Christians live in countries where serious violations of religious freedom occur, and around 220 million Christians worldwide are directly exposed to persecution. "Faced with this reality, the pontifical foundation is once again promoting the Red Week this November, an international mobilization of prayer, witness, and awareness-raising to draw attention to the deterioration of religious freedom and remember the millions of Christians who suffer discrimination and persecution because of their faith," said Regina Lynch, executive president of ACN International. Red is more than a color According to ACN's "Religious Freedom in the World Report 2025," more than 5.4 billion people — almost two-thirds of humanity — live in countries where religious freedom is not fully guaranteed. The color red is used to symbolize the blood of martyrs and all those who suffer for their faith. In 33 countries Christians have been forced to leave their homes because of their faith while in 57 countries Christians suffer physical violence or even detention because of their faith. Each church and monument taking part in Red Week serves as a reminder of Christians who cannot freely practice their religion. In line with article 18 of the Universal Declaration of Human Rights, every individual has the freedom of thought, religion, and conscience with the right to practice their beliefs, free from persecution and violence. Through this weeklong initiative, ACN aims to promote one shared goal of making visible the shared suffering of the Christian people and defend everyone's fundamental rights to religious freedom.

featured.title_zh: 数字化之门为东南亚岛民打开福音之门
featured.content: Just as young people today have become more comfortable with talking online than in person, the same is true for people in Southeast Asia. IMB missionaries are creating and publishing Jesus-focused ads, videos and other digital content to connect with the lost through the internet. IMB Photo Recently, an International Mission Board team in Southeast Asia asked a young woman if she had heard the story of Jesus. She replied that, yes, she had heard about Him through a video online! “Back in the day,” shared Amanda Clarkston, an IMB missionary who has served in Southeast Asia for 33 years, “when I first came on the field, you’d go somewhere and gather all the people together in the village to watch the JESUS film.” Now, face-to-face conversations about Christ on the Southeast Asian islands are harder to accomplish. While teams travel to these remote islands often, living in a sparsely populated, animistic background culture as a foreigner creates suspicion and make long-term ministry difficult. Furthermore, young people today have become more comfortable with talking online than they are in person, Clarkston said, which is true of the islanders as well. Attempting to have a spiritual conversation face-to-face has become “too much” for locals, Clarkston shared. So, how do you share the gospel with multiple people groups who are constantly online and less comfortable with in-person interactions? For these Southeast Asia teams, digital engagement — the use of social media platforms to share a message — has become a plausible and effective entry point. The social media agency We Are Social confirmed this, revealing that 82.4% of Southeast Asia’s population uses the internet. “No matter where they go, how far they go, how remote it is, people have phones,” Clarkston and her team realized, “And though sometimes they do have to climb up the highest peak to get reception, people do it.” Clarkston’s team has begun creating and publishing Jesus-focused ads, videos and other digital content in hopes of building bridges to the islanders through the internet. Viewers can click on the ad to message back and forth with a responder, a local believer or missionary who is available to pray, build relationships and answer spiritual questions. “It seems like locals are more open to watching those things in the privacy of their own cell phones,” Clarkston said. Clarkston intends to use digital engagement as a means for initial contact with people with animistic backgrounds, evangelism and, eventually, discipleship. She said that this new ministry has the potential to open doors with individuals across these islands who would normally never reach out on their own or respond to the gospel in person. “Maybe they’ll respond this way,” Clarkston said, “I know without a shadow of a doubt that God is calling people to Himself.” Now, more than ever, technology has a grip on society. Many spend hours each day mindlessly scrolling, searching for meaning, for happiness. And now, more than ever, there is an incredible opportunity to plant seeds across Southeast Asian islands through digital engagement. The IMB Southeast Asia team gives praise to the Lord that He has provided a creative way to reach the lost and plant seeds. Pray the people among the Southeast Asian islands would see these ads and engage with responders boldly, even though they may face persecution or harm because of it. Names were changed for security. featured.content_zh: 正如今天的年轻人对在线交谈比亲自交谈更加自在,东南亚人民也是如此。 IMB传教士正在创作并出版以耶稣为主的广告,视频等数字内容,以通过互联网与失落者相接. 最近,东南亚国际使团委员会的一个小组问一名年轻妇女是否听说过耶稣的故事。 她回答说,是的,她通过网络视频听到了他的消息! “回到今天 ” , 分享了IMB在东南亚服役了33年的传教士阿曼达·克拉克斯顿(Amanda Clarkston ) , “ 当我第一次来到现场时,你会去一个地方,把村里的所有人聚集在一起观看JESUS电影。 ” 现在,关于东南亚岛屿上的基督的面对面对话更难完成。 虽然各小组经常前往这些偏远岛屿,但作为外国人生活在人口稀少的厌世主义背景文化中,这造成了怀疑,使长期部委变得困难。 此外,克拉克斯顿说,今天的年轻人对在线交谈比他们本人感到更加自在,岛上居民也是如此。 Clarkston分享, 试图面对面进行精神对话, 所以,你如何与多个人群体分享福音呢? 他们经常在线,对亲身互动不太满意。 对于这些东南亚小组来说,数字参与——利用社交媒体平台分享信息——已成为一个可信而有效的切入点。 东南亚82.4%的人口使用互联网。 克拉克斯顿和她的团队意识到,“尽管有时他们必须爬上最高的山峰才能得到接待,但人们还是这么做了。” Clarkston的团队开始创作和发布以耶稣为焦点的广告,视频等数字内容,希望通过互联网为岛民搭起桥梁. 取景者可以点击广告,与回复者,当地信众或传教士相接来回留言,他们可以进行祈祷,建立关系并回答精神问题. Clarkston说, “当地人似乎更愿意在手机的隐私中观看这些东西。 克拉克斯顿打算用数字化的接战作为与有动画背景,福音派,并最终有门徒身份的人进行初步接触的手段. 她说,这个新的部有可能对这些岛屿上的个人敞开大门,他们通常不会独自伸出援手或亲自回应福音。 “也许他们会以这种方式回应,”克拉克斯顿说,“我毫不怀疑地知道,上帝正在号召人们投靠自己。 ” 现在,技术比以往更加控制社会。 许多人每天花上数小时无所顾忌地滚动,寻找意义,追求幸福. 现在,比以往任何时候,通过数字化参与,在东南亚各岛屿播种种子的机会比以往任何时候都多。 IMB东南亚队称赞了"主",他为到达失落地并播下种子提供了创造性的方法. 请东南亚各岛屿人民看到这些广告,并大胆地与回应者接触,尽管他们可能因此而面临迫害或伤害。 更改了安全名称。 米卡·杨在IMB海外服役. featured.title: How We Saw God’s Goodness Through Our Child’s Cancer
featured.summary: It was not in the good moments where God’s care was most evident. It was in the dark moments, often at night, when we were unsure if our son would survive.
featured.summary_zh: 这不是在神的关怀最明显的美好时刻。在黑暗的时刻，通常是在晚上，我们不确定我们的儿子是否能活下来。
featured.title_zh: 我们如何从孩子的癌症中看到神的良善
featured.content: To encounter profound suffering is to wrestle with isolation. From Job’s seat in the ashes to your neighbor’s loss, news of suffering often includes a struggle to connect. Our family’s cancer journey was like that. We felt alone. And we sensed disconnection—even helplessness—from people who heard the news. Childhood cancer is a blessedly uncommon experience, but navigating pain is inherent to life in a fallen world. When we encounter others’ pain, we have a “Good Samaritan choice”—to step forward and show compassion or to walk away. Nightmare Our 3-year-old son, Ben, had an unexplained illness. After a week in the hospital, we were ushered into an ICU conference room full of doctors and nurses. They delivered the news: “Your son has cancer.” One of the nurses was crying before they even said a word. Our family is from Washington, DC, but we were about 10,000 miles from home. We’d been serving as missionaries in Costa Rica, yet we weren’t there either. On that January day, we were in a hospital in Sydney, Australia, on our dream trip—a family Christmas in summertime. It was quickly becoming a nightmare. The days after the diagnosis were filled with rapid changes. We couldn’t go back to Costa Rica. Returning to DC was almost impossible. The Ronald McDonald House was our new home. My daughter started kindergarten at a new school, in a new country. She drew a picture of her family. There was no home, garden, or pets—just a hospital bed. Ben on his last day of chemotherapy / Courtesy of Peter Morris Over the next six months, Ben endured 96 nights in the hospital, 25 general anesthetics, and chemotherapy so strong it could blind or even kill an adult. He was traveling through the metaphorical valley of the shadow of death, and it was decorated with bright colors and superhero stickers. May 22 is a day we still celebrate in our family as “no more chemo day.” Ben took his final dose of chemotherapy, and we rejoiced with a trip to McDonald’s and a chocolate cake. Despite the celebration, the years ahead held mortal peril. His doctor told us relapse was a risk without a treatment plan. All we could do was watch and wait. Ben was immunocompromised for the years that followed, extending into the 2020s when the disruption of a health crisis—previously rare—became globally mundane. Today, Ben’s body still carries the scars of his cancer and the side effects of the lifesaving treatment he received. But he’s a survivor. To any passerby, he looks like an ordinary 12-year-old boy. My wife and I have scars too. But we also carry the lessons the Lord taught us along the way. Those lessons are available to all believers as we encounter the pain of others. Here are three that stand out. 1. You can’t depend on people. Suffering has an odd way of resetting relationships. We saw it repeatedly, in our experience and with other cancer families we met. The apparent uniqueness of the suffering—and the emotional reactions it stirred—drove some people away. They wouldn’t, or couldn’t, step close and walk with us. However, those people stepping away opened the door to gospel opportunities for us. Australian hospitals rarely have private rooms, so we spent most of our 96 nights sharing rooms with people from diverse cultures and faiths. As other people pulled back from them, we were able to step forward and hold out the hope of the gospel in a dark and hopeless place. 2. You can depend on people. While some in our life pulled away, others chose to pull close. We were thousands of miles from our church family, but people still found ways to care for us. When we shared the news about Ben’s illness, our Facebook post reached more than 15,000 people around the world. It wasn’t the eyeballs that made a difference but the thoughtful actions. Local believers jumped into action with a meal roster. Costa Rican friends translated our English updates to equip our Spanish-speaking friends to pray. American friends prepared care packages, sent encouraging texts, and came
featured.content_zh:
面对深刻的痛苦就是与孤立相搏。 从乔布在灰烬中的座位到邻居的损失, 我们家族的癌症旅程就是这样。 我们感到孤独。 我们感到与那些听到消息的人断绝关系,甚至是无助的。

童年时期的癌症是一种吉祥的罕见经历,但航海痛苦是堕落世界中生命所固有的. 当我们遇到其他人的痛苦时,我们有一个“好撒玛利亚人的选择”——站出来表示同情或离开。 噩梦我们3岁的儿子,本,有一个无法解释的疾病。 在医院里呆了一个星期后,我们被带入了一个由医生和护士组成的ICU会议室.

他们播下了一个消息:“你的儿子得了癌症。 其中一个护士甚至还没说一句话就哭了. 我们的家庭来自华盛顿特区 但我们离家约一万英里 我们一直担任哥斯达黎加的传教士, 1月当天,我们在澳大利亚悉尼的一家医院进行梦想之旅——夏天是家庭圣诞节。

它很快变成了一场噩梦。 诊断后的几天充满了快速的变化. 我们无法回到哥斯达黎加。 返回华盛顿几乎是不可能的。 罗纳德麦当劳之家是我们的新家 我女儿在新学校开始上幼儿园, 在新国家。 她画了一张她家人的照片。 没有家,没有花园,也没有宠物,只有一张医院床。

本最后一天的化疗 / 彼得・莫里斯的礼仪 在接下来的六个月里,本在医院忍受了96个晚上,25个一般麻醉药,化疗如此强大,可以盲目甚至杀死成人. 他穿梭在死亡阴影的隐喻山谷中,装饰着明亮的颜色和超级英雄贴纸.

5月22日仍是我们家庭庆祝的一天, Ben接受了最后的化疗, 尽管有庆典, 未来的岁月仍然有致命的危险。 他的医生告诉我们 复发是一种风险 没有治疗计划。 我们能做的就是观察和等待。

其后的几年里,本被免疫妥协,一直延续到2020年代,以前罕见的一次健康危机的破坏成为全球风云。 今天,Ben的身体仍带有癌症的伤疤和他接受救生治疗的副作用。 但他是个幸存者。 对于任何路人来说,他看起来像一个普通的12岁男孩. 我妻子和我也有伤疤

但我们也带着上帝教给我们的教训 当我们遇到其他人的痛苦时,所有信徒都可以接受这些教训。 这是三个突出的。 1. 你不能依赖人。 受苦有怪异的重构关系方式. 我们从我们的经验和我们遇到的其他癌症家庭中反复看到。

痛苦的明显独特性——以及它激起的情绪反应——驱赶一些人。 他们不会或无法靠近我们, 然而,那些走开的人为我们带来了机会。 澳大利亚的医院很少有私人房间,因此我们在96个晚上的大部分时间都与来自不同文化和信仰的人共用房间.

当其他人从他们那里撤退时,我们得以挺身而出,在一个黑暗和无望的地方抓住福音的希望。 2. 你可以依赖人。 在我们生命中有些人被拉走时,另一些人选择拉近。 我们离教会家数千英里 但人们仍然想方设法照顾我们

当我们分享本病的消息时, 并不是眼球的作用, 当地信徒以餐具名册跳跃行动. 哥斯达黎加朋友翻译了英语最新消息,

featured.title_zh: IMB传教士通过新信徒和当地教会看到神在工作
featured.content: In South Asia, Maryam and a local pastor baptize Tara, a new believer. IMB missionaries work alongside local believers and churches to fulfill the Great Commission. IMB Photo Twenty minutes had passed already. The sun was going down, and they were looking everywhere, but they only saw men in the park. Sophia, an International Mission Board missionary, joined another IMB missionary and Maryam, a South Asian Christian. They went to the park to share the gospel, but approaching a man in their Muslim-majority city was out of the question. They kept walking and watching. Even if they went home without a single conversation, Sophia knew Maryam would want to try again. This woman who had grown up with a distrust of Muslims, now searched a park for a Muslim woman to tell about Jesus. When Sophia first invited her along, Maryam never imagined a Muslim could come to know Jesus. But the more they went out sharing the gospel together, the more God softened her heart. “One day, I found she was sharing in the park by herself, without me,” Sophia said with a laugh. These days, she shares regularly — with classmates, with rickshaw drivers, with women in the park, when she can find them. God transformed Maryam’s heart. He could transform this walk through the park, too. “So we stopped,” Sophia said, “and prayed, ‘God, give us just one woman to talk to.’” Then they spotted her — a girl sitting alone on a bench. Meeting the girl on the bench She looked like other conservative Muslim women in the area, covered in black except for her face. They approached casually, not wanting to frighten her. It was Eid al-Adha – “one of the biggest Muslim holidays here,” Sophia said. They greeted her and asked about her holiday plans. Her name was Tara, and she wasn’t intimidated at all. “You may think I’m a Muslim from the way I dress,” she said, “but actually in my heart, I have left Islam.” “I was a little shocked,” Sophia said, hearing such a bold statement from a stranger. Tara told them she was a university student at a conservative Islamic school, but she had grown disillusioned and discontent with the religion. “ I don’t believe in Islam anymore,” Tara said. Without knowledge of God, she had no one to pray to, and it left her lonely. She’d been searching — Buddhism and Hinduism from friends, even a meeting with atheists, who struck her as unhappy, following only themselves. “Do you know any Christians?” Sophia asked. “Would you like to hear what we believe?” “Sure, please share.” They read about Jesus’ birth, and Tara was hungry for more. When she asked about church, Sophia described their congregation of about 40 believers, many from a Muslim background. Though she wasn’t ready to visit the church, Tara continued her interest in learning. Sophia and Maryam met with her every week in coffee shops, tea shops, Sophia’s home, wherever they could talkthat wasn’t too loud or have “too many ears and eyes” observing them. Finding her closest friend They read through the Gospel of John. One November day in a coffee shop, they reached the passage on the Samaritan woman at the well, and Sophia noticed Tara was crying. “Tara, I see you have tears,” Sophia said. “Let’s stop. Let’s talk about it .” That day, Tara prayed to receive Christ. Soon after, she wanted to visit the church, though nervous how believers would receive her in a hijab. “They will love you,” Sophia told her. “Don’t worry.” Tara went and was welcomed. That Christmas, 80 people packed Sophia’s apartment, singing and dancing in circles. Across the room, Sophia saw Tara, wearing red Christmas garland like a scarf and a smile stretched across her face. “Tara grew up very conservative – music was not even allowed in her home. But now she’s dancing, worshiping the Lord with us with music and songs.” In South Asia, Maryam and a local pastor baptize Tara, a new believer. IMB missionaries work alongside local believers and churches to fulfill the Great Commission. IMB Photo That spring, Tara was baptized.

featured.title_zh: 对南亚的IMB事工合作伙伴来说，这“只是一个开始”
featured.content: IMB missionary Derrick Waters spent many days in areas like this market, learning his mission field. He made a breakthrough when he met Siraj, who now confidently shares the gospel. IMB Photo The conversation began on a dusty road in rural South Asia. Siraj, a Christian, told Derrick Waters about his desire to share the gospel with Muslims. How could he begin discussions about Christ with his neighbors? After months of training and encouragement, Siraj said, “I will soon share the gospel with 100 Muslims. I know that at least a few will believe.” Waters and his wife, Rosemary, are International Mission Board missionaries who serve in South Asia. His connection with Siraj is a breakthrough in sharing the gospel in this strongly Muslim region. When he first arrived on the mission field, Waters spent his early days getting acclimated to his new community by riding on the back of a motorcycle with a national partner, traveling around and making contacts. “My partner was trying to convince me not to buy a helmet because he said he was a safe driver,” Waters said, though he chose to wear the headgear. “It’s a good thing I wore the helmet because he drove into the back of a truck with a metal bar hanging out that smacked my head.” Surviving the motorcycle ride led to the relational network that eventually allowed Waters to meet Siraj. After they connected, Siraj introduced Waters to Muslim friends and watched him share the gospel. “At first, that’s how it was with Siraj,” Waters said. “But what I really wanted was for him to get involved in the work himself.” A few months later, Waters and local ministry partners traveled to Siraj’s village to lead evangelism training. They discussed God’s love for all people, learned key vocabulary and practiced a straightforward way to share personal testimonies and the story of Jesus. Then came the hard part. Waters began asking Siraj to lead conversations. Siraj stumbled through explanations and searched for the right words. He sprinkled in newly learned terms and nervously worked through the gospel message. Slowly, confidence replaced fear. After another season of ministry together, Siraj told Waters something he would never forget. “Before you came, I didn’t know how to share the gospel with Muslims,” Siraj said. “I wanted to, but I didn’t know how. Now I feel like I can do it.” The transformation became visible during a gathering arranged by a local teacher. Dozens of parents assembled to listen. Siraj stood before them, visibly nervous. His first few sentences faltered. He started, stopped and restarted. Then, something changed. Finding his rhythm, he shared what he had learned, speaking clearly and naturally. He used the vocabulary he had practiced and explained the message of Jesus with growing confidence. By the end of the meeting, the listeners invited the believers to pray for sick family members. They served snacks and chai, thanked them for coming and invited them back. For Waters, it was a glimpse of what God could do through one willing believer. featured.title: A construction engineer in Madagascar became convinced the Bible was true
featured.summary: 🇲🇬Madagascar· 2013
featured.summary_zh: 🇲🇬马达加斯加·2013年
featured.title_zh: 一位在马达加斯加的建筑工程师确信圣经是真的
featured.content: Melias was building things for a living in Madagascar, a construction engineer with a steady trade and, by his own account, no particular expectation that God would interrupt him. In 2013, at twenty-one, God did. It was not dramatic thunder. It was quieter and harder to argue with. "The Holy Spirit convinced my heart that the Bible is true," Melias said. "I found new joy and excitement learning about Jesus through the Scriptures." The book he might have dismissed became the most alive thing in his life. From building houses to building the church He could have kept his new faith as a private comfort and gone on with engineering. Instead he gave it everything. In 2015 he trained for six months as a missionary, and since then he has planted churches and discipled new believers among the Tanala people in Ikongo and the Sakalava in Nosy Be, some of the least reached corners of the island. Now he is training three more Malagasy missionaries to do the same. Madagascar is not a footnote in what God is doing. He is raising up local people like Melias, engineers and tradesmen and ordinary workers, and sending them to their own unreached neighbours. When the Holy Spirit convinces your heart that this is all true, it does not stay a hobby. It becomes the thing you build your life around. He is ready to convince yours.
featured.content_zh:
梅利亚斯在马达加斯加为生计而建东西,他是一位稳定的建筑工程师,据他自己说,他并不特别期望上帝会打断他。 2013年,21时,上帝做到了. 这不是戏剧性的雷声。 更安静,更难争论 "圣灵使我的心相信圣经是真的,"梅利亚斯说.

"我发现新的快乐和兴奋 通过圣经学习耶稣。" 他可能放弃的书 成为他一生中最活的 从建房到建教堂 他本可以保持他作为私人慰藉的新信仰,继续从事工程工作. 相反,他给了它一切。

2015年,他作为传教士接受了半年的训练,此后他在伊孔戈的塔纳拉人和诺西贝的萨卡拉瓦人中种植了教堂和门徒新信徒,其中部分到达的岛角最少. 现在他正在训练另外三名马达加斯加传教士, 马达加斯加不是上帝所作所为的一个脚注。

featured.title: A New Testament sat in his welding workshop until a teenager finally read it
featured.summary: 🇳🇪Agadez· 2000s
featured.summary_zh: 🇳🇪阿加德兹·21世纪初
featured.title_zh: 一本新约圣经一直放在他的焊接车间里，直到一位少年终于读了它。
featured.content: Someone left a New Testament in Pierre's welding workshop in Niger, and for a while it just sat there. He was a teenager, and eventually he picked it up. What he read did not match what he had been told about Christians. It was full of tenderness, of nearness to the poorest, exactly the kind of world his young heart had been quietly hoping was real. Years later he moved to Agadez, out toward the desert, and there he found the thing the book had described. A church family drawn from Benin, Togo, Burkina Faso, France, and Niger, living out what he had only read about. No regret, not for a single day Pierre became a lay missionary, and he does not hedge when he talks about it. "I have never regretted converting to the Christian faith," he says, "not even for a single day." That is a bold thing to say in Niger, where jihadist groups make following Jesus dangerous and his own children have stayed Muslim, something he carries with love and without pressure. Still, no regret. Not one day. He read about a God who is tender toward the poor, and he found that God to be exactly as advertised. Whatever you have heard about Jesus secondhand, He holds up when you finally meet Him yourself. Pierre would tell you to open the book and see.
featured.content_zh:
有人在尼日尔的皮埃尔焊接车间留下了一份新约, 他少年时期,最终他捡到了. 他所读的内容与他被告知的基督徒的情况不符。 它充满了温柔,与最贫穷的人的亲近, 正是他年轻时所希望的世界是真实的。

多年后,他搬到阿加德兹, 向着沙漠, 在那里他发现了书上描述的东西。 一个来自贝宁、多哥、布基纳法索、法国和尼日尔的教会家庭,靠他只读过的东西生活。 没有遗憾,没有一天,皮埃尔成为了一名非专业的传教士,他谈论这件事时不设套.

"我从未后悔过皈依基督教信仰",他说:"即使是一天也没有". 在尼日尔,这是一件大胆的事,在那里,圣战团体追随耶稣,而他自己的孩子则留在穆斯林手中,他带着爱,没有压力。 不过,没有遗憾。 一日不见.

他曾诵读了真主--对于贫民是温和的--他发现真主确是彻知的。 无论你听到什么关于耶稣的二手消息 当你们终于亲眼见到他时 他都挺过来了 Pierre会告诉你打开书看看

featured.content: Staff members at First Baptist Church in Wagoner, Oklahoma, evaluate their church’s involvement with missions and missionary support. IMB Photo The chapel at Council Road Baptist Church in Oklahoma City turned into a science lab on Oct. 5-6. Microscopes, beakers and test tubes weren’t in the room, but this Sending Church Lab drew nearly 40 people representing 12 Oklahoma Baptist churches committed to send and care for international missionaries well. The Sending Church Lab, facilitated by the International Mission Board, brought pastors, church leaders and missionaries together for two days of discussion, self-assessment and planning centered on one question: What does it mean for a church to truly be a sending church? For Mike Wall, a global missions ministry partner of Oklahoma Baptists, the answer begins with churches reclaiming responsibility for the Great Commission. Wall first attended a Sending Church Lab last year in Tulsa with few expectations. He left convinced more churches needed the training. “When I went there, I thought, ‘You’ve got to do this in Oklahoma City,’” Wall said, “because of the content and how much our churches need something just like this.” After observing churches work through the exercises in the lab, Wall said he was encouraged by an emphasis on local church ownership in missions. “We can’t just send our people and say, ‘OK, now this is your job, IMB,’” he said. “We have to do our job in sending, preparing and training the best ‘sent ones’ so that when they get to the field, they can already hit the ground running.” Bryan Wooten, IMB senior church engagement specialist, leads a Sending Church Lab at Council Road Baptist Church in Oklahoma City. He is emphasizing the importance of sending churches assessing and equipping future IMB missionaries. IMB Photo Leading the lab was Bryan Wooten, IMB senior church engagement strategist, who developed the concept after seeing the need for stronger relationships between missionaries and local churches. “A Sending Church Lab is our attempt to raise up a host of IMB sending churches,” Wooten said, crediting the North American Mission Board for doing similar events and having successful results. The lab helps churches understand what Wooten calls the church engagement pathway: praying, cooperating, partnering and sending. While many churches faithfully pray, give and go, he said sending requires something more intentional. “Sending includes taking responsibility for an IMB missionary by providing ongoing encouragement, accountability and soul care throughout their term of service,” he explained. During the two-day event, participants gathered around whiteboards to evaluate their church’s missions practices, identify strengths and weaknesses and develop plans for improvement. “We don’t just need to deliver content,” Wooten said. “We need to invite churches to do some work on their own.” Rather than simply listening to presentations, attendees worked through practical questions about prayer, giving, short-term missions, missionary assessment and long-term care. Wooten said churches consistently tell him the greatest benefit is clarity. “They are thankful for clarity on what an IMB sending church is and what our roles and responsibilities are,” he said. For IMB missionaries Peter and Katie Weeks, that clarity is especially valuable. They participated in the lab alongside church leaders. Their real names have been changed to protect their work in Southeast Asia. “There’s no other place I’d rather be during these few days than here,” Peter said. Katie appreciated the interactive nature of the training. “I really appreciate the way they’re actually requiring information from the different churches and encouraging dialogue about how they can go through the steps,” she said. featured.title: Finding Wonder in the Midst of Christmas Weariness
featured.source: Wycliffe Bible Translators · 译经故事
featured.summary: Rediscover the wonder of Christmas by focusing on God’s faithfulness and the hope found in Jesus.   The post  Finding Wonder in the Midst of Christmas Weariness  appeared first on  Wycliffe .
featured.summary_zh: 通过关注神的信实和耶稣的盼望，重新发现圣诞节的奇迹。“在圣诞节疲惫中寻找奇迹”一文首次出现在威克里夫。
featured.title_zh: 在圣诞节疲惫中寻找奇迹
featured.content: Christmas is supposed to be a season of wonder. Twinkling lights, familiar songs, meaningful traditions and time with people you love can all point toward the joy of celebrating Jesus’ birth. But when your December calendar fills with responsibilities and expectations, weariness can settle in before you realize it. Maybe you remember a time when Christmas felt different. As a child, you may have counted down the days and experienced joy in even the smallest traditions. As an adult, you might find yourself simply trying to catch your breath as you move from one responsibility to the next. In the middle of trying to make Christmas special for everyone else, it can be easy to miss the wonder yourself. But the Christmas story gives you an opportunity to slow down and remember what this season is really about. In Luke 1, before the story of Jesus’ birth begins, you meet people who knew what it meant to wait, wonder and trust that God was at work even when they couldn’t yet see what He was doing. Weary of Waiting Luke’s account of the life of Jesus doesn’t begin with Jesus’ birth; it begins instead with the story of Zechariah, an elderly priest who was tired of waiting. Zechariah had heard promises of Israel’s rescue from oppression and sin his entire life. That future must have seemed out of reach under Rome’s harsh control. But Zechariah and his wife, Elizabeth, also had an unfulfilled personal longing: “They had no children because Elizabeth was unable to conceive, and they were both very old” ( Luke 1:7, NLT ). One day, as Zechariah performed his duties in the temple, he was chosen to burn incense in the sanctuary — a rare honor with an unexpected result: While Zechariah was in the sanctuary, an angel of the Lord appeared to him, standing to the right of the incense altar. Zechariah was shaken and overwhelmed with fear when he saw him. But the angel said, “Don’t be afraid, Zechariah! God has heard your prayer. Your wife, Elizabeth, will give you a son, and you are to name him John. You will have great joy and gladness, and many will rejoice at his birth, for he will be great in the eyes of the Lord. He must never touch wine or other alcoholic drinks. He will be filled with the Holy Spirit, even before his birth. And he will turn many Israelites to the Lord their God. He will be a man with the spirit and power of Elijah. He will prepare the people for the coming of the Lord. He will turn the hearts of the fathers to their children, and he will cause those who are rebellious to accept the wisdom of the godly” ( Luke 1:11-17, NLT ). Trusting God in the Waiting An angel of the Lord appeared to Zechariah and announced that God had heard his prayer. Elizabeth would have a son named John who would “… prepare the people for the coming of the Lord” ( Luke 1:17b, NLT ). After years of waiting, God answered Zechariah and Elizabeth’s prayer as part of an even bigger story: They would finally have the child they had prayed for, and their son would prepare the way for Jesus. But Zechariah struggled to understand how it could possibly happen: “… ‘How can I be sure this will happen? I’m an old man now, and my wife is also well along in years’” ( Luke 1:18, NLT ). Zechariah could only see what seemed possible based on his circumstances. But God was asking him to trust what He had promised. The angel Gabriel responded by telling Zechariah that he would be unable to speak until the child was born, adding, “For my words will certainly be fulfilled at the proper time” ( Luke 1:20b, NLT ). Maybe you know what it’s like to pray about something for months or even years. It can be hard to keep trusting that God is working when it seems like nothing is changing. Zechariah’s story reminds us that even when we can’t see what God is doing, He is still faithful to His promises. Waiting is woven throughout the Christmas story. Maybe it’s part of your story too. Our free four-week Advent devotional, “Hope in the Waiting,” can help you spend time in Scripture a

圣诞节应该是奇迹的季节 闪烁的灯光、熟悉的歌曲、有意义的传统和时间, 但当您12月的日历充满了责任和期望时,疲惫可以在您意识到之前安顿下来. 也许你记得圣诞节感觉不一样的时候

但圣诞故事给了你一个机会,让你慢下来,并记住本季的真正内容. 在卢卡斯一世,耶稣诞生的故事开始前,你遇见了那些知道等待、好奇和相信上帝在工作的意义的人,即使他们还看不到他在做什么。 等待卢克对耶稣生活的描述,

以撒迦利亚的故事开始 撒迦利亚是一位老牧师 他厌倦了等待 撒迦利亚曾听到过以色列从压迫中解救出来的承诺,他一生都有罪。 罗马的严酷控制下,这一未来似乎已遥不可及。

但是,Zachariah和他的妻子Elizabeth也有未实现的个人愿望:“他们没有孩子,因为Elizabeth无法怀孕,而且他们都非常老”(Luke 1:7, NLT)。

一天,当撒迦利亚在圣殿中履行职责时,他被选中在圣殿烧香——这是罕见的荣誉,结果出乎意料:撒迦利亚在圣殿时,上帝的天使出现在他面前,站在香坛的右边. 撒迦利亚见到他时,被震撼和恐惧所压倒. 但天使说:"撒迦利亚,不要害怕!

他将是一个拥有以利亚精神和力量的人。 他会为主的到来为人民做准备. 他将把父亲们的心转向他们的孩子,他将使那些叛逆的人接受神的智慧”(Luke 1:11-17,NLT). 相信上帝在等待上帝的天使出现在撒迦利亚面前,并宣布上帝听到了他的祈祷.

Elizabeth将有一个名叫John的儿子,他将“为主的到来为人民做好准备”(Luke 1:17b, NLT)。 经过多年的等待,上帝回答了撒迦利亚和伊丽莎白的祈祷,作为更大的故事的一部分: 他们最终会有他们祈祷的孩子,他们的儿子会为耶稣准备道路.

但撒迦利亚却挣扎着去理解这怎么可能发生:“......我怎么能肯定这会发生呢? 我已是老人, Zachariah只能从他的情况看出什么是可能的。 但上帝要求他相信他所承诺的

天使Gabriel在回答时告诉Zachariah, 在孩子出生之前, 他无法说话, 并补充说, “我的话一定会在适当的时候实现”(Luke 1:20b, NLT)。 也许你知道祈祷几个月甚至几年是什么感觉。 很难继续相信上帝在工作 似乎没什么变化

撒迦利亚的故事提醒我们,即使我们看不到上帝在做什么,他仍然忠实于他的诺言。 等待被编织 整个圣诞节的故事。 也许这也是你的故事的一部分。 我们的四周免费的礼拜,“期待在等待中”,可以帮助你在《圣经》中度过时间。

featured.content: IMB Graphic NASHVILLE – As the books closed on the latest fiscal year, receipts for the two Southern Baptist national annual missions offerings underscored the value Southern Baptist churches place on reaching the world with the gospel. The Lottie Moon Christmas Offering® (LMCO) totaled $212.5 million to support International Mission Board (IMB) missionaries, and the Annie Armstrong Easter Offering® (AAEO) reached $73.6 million to support the North American Mission Board’s (NAMB) church planting, compassion ministry and other evangelistic efforts to reach North America. IMB President Paul Chitwood said he celebrates what God did in the 2025-26 season and what He is doing now to lead Southern Baptists toward historic generosity. “I thank God for Southern Baptists! With giving through the Lottie Moon offering at an all-time high, churches and individual givers continue to display a heart for the gospel to be proclaimed to every nation, all tribes, peoples and languages,” Chitwood said. The Annie total marked the second highest in NAMB’s history. The record Lottie Moon offering total surpassed last year’s total by more than $5 million and is the best offering in IMB history. “God is giving our generation unprecedented opportunity to send missionaries to the most unreached peoples and places,” Chitwood continued. “Though the challenges faced by our missionaries are enormous, the generosity of Southern Baptists ensures they have what they need to face those challenges and continue in the work while we hold the ropes with our support.” IMB missionary Landon Williams (center) walks with a Chilean pastor and a U.S. pastor on a remote island in Chile. Cooperation and generosity among Southern Baptists fuels the work to reach the uttermost parts of the world with the gospel. IMB Photo National goals for both offerings are set in partnership with Woman’s Missionary Union (WMU) each year. In response to the offering totals, Sandy Wisdom-Martin, executive director-treasurer of WMU, said: “As Southern Baptists, we are all in for His mission. When we give sacrificially, we prioritize the mission of God. Together our fervent prayers, our faithful generosity and our wholehearted obedience become channels for the gospel to reach our neighbors as well as the nations.” For the last 10 years, Southern Baptists have increasingly supported the Annie offering, setting records in seven of the last 10 years. Totals in each of the last four years have surpassed $70 million. “I am so grateful to the pastors and churches for the faithfulness and generosity they have demonstrated through this offering,” said NAMB president Kevin Ezell. “As I travel and speak in churches of all sizes, I love seeing the posters in the hallways showing their offering goals. For some it is a few hundred dollars, for others several thousand.” The Annie Armstrong offering supports more than 3,000 missionaries in North America, including the ongoing work of church planting in the U.S. and Canada. In 2025, Southern Baptists planted the largest number of churches, 699, since 2016. Including church plants and replants, Southern Baptists have surpassed 700 new churches in four of the last five years. More than 12,000 churches have been planted since 2010. To go along with the increased giving totals to the SBC’s missions offerings, Southern Baptists have also increased their local outreach efforts, indicating that the focus is not just on giving but on sending. featured.title_zh: 创作者的心
featured.content: Holly Neal loves people, and she loves making things. And when something catches her interest, she dives in. “I’m a maker,” she said simply. But making has become more than just a hobby for Holly. Through some of her family’s hardest seasons, it has offered them comfort and connection. And eventually it became an unexpected way to give back to what God is doing around the world. When Holly’s adult daughter Julia was being treated for leukemia, a friend invited them to learn how to quilt. The creative process gave Holly something to focus on as their family walked through a difficult season. It became a way to work through hard things alongside her daughter. Years later, when Holly’s grandson Graham was born during the COVID-19 pandemic, she reached for another familiar project: cross-stitching. Graham spent his first four months in the hospital. And because of visitation restrictions at the time, Holly spent long hours waiting in the cafeteria. So she brought her cross-stitch. Being busy helped calm Holly’s mind. Cross-stitching was a small, practical way to make the waiting a little easier. Holly and her husband, Steve, have continued to navigate some unique family circumstances as they’ve cared for their daughter and grandson. So when Chris and Lindsay Beals, Holly and Steven’s daughter and son-in-law, invited the couple to a Wycliffe event, they were especially excited. After a season of isolation, they looked forward to reconnecting with other Christians and hearing stories about what God was doing through Bible translation. One part of the work specifically stayed with Holly: sign language Bible translation. Curious about what sign language Bible translation actually looks like? See for yourself when you visit our interactive Bible Translation Experience! You’ll go on a global journey where you’ll meet some of the hardworking Deaf translators bringing the Bible to their people in a language and format that capture their hearts. Start your journey! → As a grandmother of a child with unique needs, Holly has a special place in her heart for communities and families who navigate specific challenges and contexts. Learning about the work of making God’s Word accessible to Deaf communities worldwide gave Holly a personal connection to a ministry she’d never fully understood before. Holly and Steve had already talked and prayed about a financial gift they wanted to make to Wycliffe. But as she continued thinking about the ministry and Bible translation projects for sign languages, another question kept coming to mind: “Steve and I had already come up with a number that we felt like to donate, but the Lord kept speaking to me. And I kept thinking, ‘But what can I do? … That’s our money, but how can I make an impact?’” So Holly began thinking about how much she had invested — in supplies, patterns, fabric and tools — over the years in her love of crafting. She wondered if some of those things could become part of her gift to Bible translation. And what if Holly passed some of those supplies along to other makers and used the proceeds to support Bible translation for sign languages? See how one couple in Alabama also creatively used their gifts and skills to give back to Bible translation → Giving in Community Holly decided to hold what the stitching community calls a “destash” — an opportunity for her to sell supplies she already owned to other stitchers who could put them to good use. She shared the idea through her YouTube channel and social media, where she had already connected with a community of people who love cross-stitch. So when Holly told her stitching community about Wycliffe and her desire to support sign language Bible translation, she invited them into partnering with something that mattered to her. And people responded with generosity! Some people paid more for supplies and projects than the asking price, wanting to give a little extra toward the cause. featured.title: Living Out a Legacy of Stewardship and Faith
featured.source: Wycliffe Bible Translators · 译经故事
featured.summary: Ken and Sally discovered a way to give God’s Word — a gift they’d had access to their whole lives — to others.    The post  Living Out a Legacy of Stewardship and Faith  appeared first on  Wycliffe .
featured.summary_zh: Ken和Sally发现了一种方法，可以将上帝的话语--这是他们一生都能接触到的礼物--传递给他人。“活出管理和信仰的遗产”一文首次出现在威克里夫。
featured.title_zh: 活出管理和信仰的遗产
featured.content: What did your journey to faith look like? Perhaps it was a story of how God showed up in the midst of uncertainty, doubt or fears. Maybe it involved Him seeking you out and rescuing you. Or maybe you grew up in a Christian household and your story is a bit different — perhaps your family regularly read the Bible together and have always known about Jesus’ love. Ken Trager was raised that way. He reflected, “I think when you’re raised in a Christian home … and you have the routines of a life that is built around church and prayer, you just take it for granted.” He added, “It was just the air I breathed.” For Ken and his wife, Sally, faith was always part of their stories. They were each raised in Christian homes, followed Christ, got baptized and had parents who faithfully modeled church attendance, prayer and generosity.  Ken and Sally’s paths eventually crossed at Greenville University in southern Illinois, where they met and fell in love. They went on to build a life centered around family, faith and service. Ken spent his career as a teacher and coach while Sally worked as an accountant, and together they raised two children. Now retired, they’ve moved to be closer to their children and grandchildren, giving them a new opportunity to pour into the next generation. Through all those years and seasons, the faith Ken and Sally had seen modeled by their families continued to shape their home. Early in their marriage, Ken and Sally met a mentor who encouraged the couple to go deeper with their faith — to study Scripture, ask questions and wrestle honestly with what they believed. It was an important season of discovering that the faith that had been passed down from their families could also become something they personally owned and lived out together. What Do You Take for Granted? Years later, the couple experienced an aha moment when they were introduced to Wycliffe at an event. There, Ken and Sally heard story after story from people who had received Scripture in their own languages. Something clicked for Sally: “We’ve never known a day where we couldn’t access the Bible. And these people have just longed for it, and they’re finally getting it.” For the first time, something that had always surrounded the couple became visible — and it was a gift they could no longer take for granted . Ken and Sally had spent years thinking about the importance of God’s Word. Seeing people receive Scripture in their own languages helped them understand just how extraordinary that access is. “The power of salvation comes through that,” Ken said. “I can’t think of … [a more] important work than providing God’s Word to everybody in the world.” Sally agreed. “To have His Word is as if we’re hearing the voice of God,” she said. “God works through His Word.” This conviction — for people around the world to be able to access Scripture for themselves — became one of the reasons Ken and Sally prioritized a place in their giving for Wycliffe. But it also became part of a larger question about generosity they had been asking themselves for years: “If everything we have is a gift from God, what does it look like to live generously with it?” A Generous Heart Generosity, like faith, was something Ken and Sally had grown up around. Ken remembers his dad giving him money to put in the offering plate, and Sally remembers watching her parents give not just to their church but to people and organizations in need. Sally’s father especially enjoyed giving anonymously. As Ken and Sally have grown older, they’ve learned that generosity isn’t simply about giving a certain percentage or checking a box; it’s about continually asking what it means to have a generous heart . For Ken, the question of what it means to be generous has become what he calls “Kingdom Advancement Giving.” When contemplating giving, he asks, “Is this going to advance the Kingdom for God’s glory?” That question has shaped the way the couple thinks about which individuals and organizations they
featured.content_zh:
你的信仰之旅是什么样子的? 也许这是上帝如何在不确定、怀疑或恐惧中出现的故事。 也许这涉及到他寻找你 并救你。 或者你在一个基督教家庭长大,你的故事有点不同——也许你的家人经常一起阅读圣经,并且一直知道耶稣的爱。 肯崔格是那样长大的

他回想道 , “ 我想当你在基督教家庭长大... 你有一个在教堂和祷告周围建造的日常生活, 你只是把它视为理所当然。 ” 他又说:“只是我呼吸的空气。” 对于肯和他的妻子莎莉来说,信仰总是他们的故事的一部分.

他们各自在基督教家中长大,跟随基督,接受洗礼,并有忠实的模范教会出席,祈祷和慷慨的父母. 肯和莎莉的道路最终在伊利诺伊州南部的格林维尔大学交叉,在那里他们相遇并坠入爱河. 他们继续建立一个以家庭、信仰和服务为中心的生活。

肯在萨利担任会计期间度过了教师和教练的生涯,两人一起抚养两个孩子. 他们已经退休了, 他们已经搬到更亲近他们的儿孙, 给他们一个新的机会, 注入下一代。 在那些年和季节中,肯和莎莉所见到的由家人塑造的信仰继续塑造自己的家园.

早年的婚姻中,肯和莎莉结识了一位导师,他鼓励这对夫妇更深入地信仰——学习圣经,提出问题,并诚实地与所相信的东西搏斗. 这是一个重要的季节,发现从家人传下来的信仰也可能成为他们个人拥有和共同生活的东西. 你拿什么给格兰特?

多年后,夫妇俩在一次活动上被介绍到怀克利夫(Wycliffe)时,经历了一段愉快的时刻. 在那里,肯和莎莉从以自己语言接受圣经的人那里听到一个接一个的故事. “我们从未知道有一天我们无法阅读圣经。

而这些人也只是渴望, 第一次,一直包围着这对夫妇的东西变得明显——这是他们不能再视为理所当然的礼物了. 肯和莎莉花了多年时间思考上帝之言的重要性.

看到人们用自己的语言接受圣经 有助于他们理解这种访问是多么非凡 肯说,“救赎的力量来自此”。 " 我无法想象......比向全世界每个人提供上帝的话更重要的工作。 " 萨莉同意了 ”她说,

“真主通过他的话而工作。” 这种信念——让世界各地的人们能够为自己获得圣经——成为肯和莎莉在为威克利夫奉献一个位置时优先考虑的原因之一.

但是,它也成为了一个更大的问题的一部分,即他们多年来一直问自己:“如果我们所拥有的一切是上帝的礼物,那么与它慷慨相处是什么样子?” 和信仰一样 善良的心是肯和莎莉成长的

肯记得父亲给了他钱放进祭品盘中,莎莉记得看着她的父母不仅把钱送给他们的教堂,还送给需要帮助的人和组织. Sally的父亲特别喜欢匿名赠送。 肯和莎莉已经长大了, 他们已经了解到慷慨不只是给予一定的百分比或检查一个盒子。

需要不断问, 对肯来说,慷慨意味着什么的问题已经变成了他所谓的“提高国王地位”的问题。 当他考虑施舍的时候,他问道:"这难道是为了真主的荣耀而推动王国吗? 这个问题决定了夫妻双方对哪些个人和组织的看法

featured.content: IMB missionary Dr. Heidi Haun, left, checks on patients at Baptist Medical Centre in Nalerigu, Ghana. There are needed roles for IMB missionaries in healthcare, ministering to the needs of local populations and utilizing this time to minister to spiritual needs. IMB Photo When most Southern Baptists think of missionaries, they often picture church planters and evangelists. But leaders with the International Mission Board say some of the greatest needs today are for professionals whose work happens behind the scenes. IMB leaders report that critical roles such as teachers, healthcare workers, counselors, accountants, logistics specialists and member care personnel are helping advance the Great Commission in ways many churches never see. Doreen Baker, IMB director of TCK (third culture kid or missionary kid) education, sees a constant need for education professionals. Teachers are needed in international schools, which cover a variety of global educational entities, and in other settings to provide for missionary kids and their educational needs. “Teachers are significant in that not only are they providing instruction for students, but they are an integral part of the core missionary task ,” Baker said. “We also have great needs for consultants to support our families on the field with their children’s education in many ways.” Baker previously served 25 years teaching in Asia and experienced how education creates access to missions where traditional pathways may be limited. IMB missionary Ellie Bohrer teaches a 12th grade World Views class at Black Forest Academy in Germany. The IMB is seeking other educators, like Bohrer, who are willing to use their skills on the mission field. IMB Photo Scott Ray, IMB senior director of global deployment, noted that many missionary positions go unfilled simply because they fall outside traditional perceptions of missionary service. He said professional skills can provide both practical ministry support and access to countries where traditional missionary visas are difficult to obtain. Opportunities exist for finance professionals, veterinarians, medical workers, Send Relief personnel and others. Healthcare remains one of the most strategic areas in demand. Tom Hicks, IMB director of global health strategies, said many medical professionals have the wrong perception about mission work. “We do have an issue where people will select out because they don’t think that what they do is useful on the mission field,” he said. In reality, Hicks said many areas across the globe are increasingly seeking family medicine physicians, internists, pediatricians, pediatric nurse practitioners, OB providers, physical therapists, occupational therapists, speech pathologists and lactation consultants. The need is especially significant in sub-Saharan Africa, where young populations create a growing demand for pediatric care. Healthcare professionals also provide a unique advantage in countries that restrict missionary activity. “Missionaries with a vocational value, like healthcare missionaries, have opportunities to go places that others can’t go,” Hicks said. Another often-overlooked ministry is member care, which focuses on the spiritual, emotional, mental and relational health of IMB missionaries. Chris Martin is the IMB director of global member care. “Member care missionaries stand alongside those missionaries that are thought of traditionally as church planters or evangelists and support them,” Martin said. Many who serve in these roles come from counseling backgrounds and help missionaries navigate stress, conflict, grief and other challenges that can affect long-term ministry effectiveness. Martin compares their role to Aaron and Hur in Exodus 19, holding up Moses’ arms during battle, strengthening those serving on the front lines. IMB missionary Glen Garner uses his business skills and experience as the logistics director for missionaries serving globally. He lives in Lima, Peru, with his wife, Shannon

featured.content: Rebeca Couto, a global missionary partner from the Azores islands, practices writing characters with her tutor in Japan. IMB Photo Rebeca Couto poses with her violin. Couto is a professional violinist who is serving as a global missionary partner with the IMB in Japan. Doors have opened for her to use her skills with evangel ical Japanese musicians who perform. IMB Photo Rebeca Couto moved from one volcanic archipelago to another, leaving Portugal’s Azores islands to anchor her life in Japan. The percentage of evangelical Christians in the Azores and Japan is similar, with both populations under 1%. Couto is a fourth-generation Christian, a rarity on the small islands. She is one of few, if any, believers in the Azores with such a long spiritual lineage. This rich legacy shaped her and prepared her for ministry. “I’ve always understood the Great Commission as a call for all believers and all disciples of Christ to be missionaries, wherever they are, whatever they’re doing, and whatever God has equipped them with,” Couto said. Couto’s great-grandfather became a Christian through the witness of missionaries from the United Kingdom. Later, missionaries from the Foreign Mission Board, now the International Mission Board, started the first Baptist work in the Azores by planting an English-speaking church near an American military base. A Baptist Brazilian couple planted a Portuguese-speaking church, which became the congregation where Couto grew up and was commissioned as a missionary. Ministry has been passed down through the generations of her family. Couto’s father has pastored for 20 years, and both of her parents have been involved in ministry for most of their lives. Couto now serves in Japan as a global missionary partner, a missionary who is financially supported by a sending church or organization in their home country and serves with IMB teams. Close to 400 GMPs currently serve on IMB teams around the world. Language learning Couto is immersed in language study in Yokohama, Japan. She had a head start before she even arrived. After graduating from high school, Couto moved from the Azores to Lisbon to pursue a degree in music. She spent hours on public transportation and wanted a challenge to pass the time. She decided to study Japanese because she thought it sounded beautiful. At the time, she had no intention of becoming a missionary in the traditional sense. However, the more she learned about the language and the culture, her burden for the lost grew. She began researching Christianity in Japan. “I understood how bleak the scenario was, and how much the country needed Jesus. I struggled with that calling because the doors were closed, and it didn’t seem possible to come to Japan for a myriad of reasons,” Couto said. After finishing master’s degrees in music and violin performance, along with a seminary degree, Couto was considering pursuing a Ph.D. or returning to seminary when her seminary professors, IMB missionaries Jonathan and Bethany Sharp, contacted her about serving as a missionary in Japan. They introduced her to the GMP program and invited her to attend a missions immersion school they piloted . Music to their ears As a professional violinist, Couto brought her violin to Japan, unsure of what opportunities existed, but she knew her call to the mission field somehow involved her gifting. “I see myself as having been called to serve through music. I never even conceived doing missions while excluding the violin entirely,” Couto said. She continued, “Music is such a universal way to connect with people, and it’s so intuitive to pair that with the gospel and with God’s message to people’s hearts.” While she knew the Lord would somehow open a door for her to use the violin for kingdom work, she was at peace with the possibility that, for a season, she may not be as active in music.
