featured.title: Why Christianity Explains Our Deepest Longings
featured.summary: ‘Why Christianity Makes Sense’ offers a compelling argument that Christianity explains the condition of both the world and the human heart.
featured.summary_zh: 《基督教为何有道理》提出一个令人信服的论点，即基督教解释了世界和人心两种状态。
featured.title_zh: 为什么基督教能够解释我们最深切的渴望
featured.content: Throughout church history, God has raised up faithful voices to speak the gospel to each generation. The apostle Paul traveled through much of the known world, preaching in synagogues and public settings. In Athens, he used the questions the culture was asking as a platform from which to proclaim the gospel. Similarly, Augustine, Anselm, Blaise Pascal, C. S. Lewis, Tim Keller, and many others helped readers see Christianity’s coherence amid the questions and assumptions of their times. Through his online ministry, Truth Unites , Gavin Ortlund fills that sort of role in our cultural moment. In Why Christianity Makes Sense: A Book About Jesus, the Mysteries of the World, and the Longings in Your Heart , Ortlund offers an accessible defense of the faith for readers unsure whether Christianity can withstand serious examination. It’s also a useful tool for discipling believers bombarded with hard questions about Christianity on the internet. Ortlund’s goal is to show “why it makes sense to be a Christian” (xiii). Ortlund’s particular strength is that he recognizes our questions aren’t merely intellectual. They arise from deeper longings for meaning, purpose, and transcendence. Unknown God In Athens, Paul thoughtfully noticed an altar established “to the unknown god” (Acts 17:23). He didn’t mock them for it. Every generation builds an altar of its own. Augustine called it the restless heart; Lewis called it Sehnsucht , the longing that joy itself cannot satisfy. Keller called the traces it leaves behind clues . Ortlund has a name for it: “the ache.” Ortlund doesn’t begin with a technical exposition of the ache but by showing it’s the desire behind every altar to every unknown god. He asks, “Are you genuinely curious about what life means—why you’re here, and what it’s all for?” (xi). The ache is the restless longing for the transcendent that we can’t put into words. Just as hunger implies we live in a world where food is meant to fuel our bodies, so the desire for meaning points to the existence of something that will satisfy that desire. So many counterfeits promise to satisfy our desire for God. Many people have learned to deny any sense of longing for the divine or simply scroll past the question before it finishes loading in their minds. Just as hunger implies we live in a world where food is meant to fuel our bodies, so the desire for meaning points to the existence of something that will satisfy that desire. In a culture where the most shocking content on social media becomes boring, it’s worth drawing attention to Jesus’s radical claims. “He claimed to be the way, the truth, and the life,” notes Ortlund. “Muhammad taught the five pillars, Buddha spoke of enlightenment, Confucius pointed to the Way, but Jesus pointed to himself as the answer. In fact, Jesus claimed to be God” (104). The claim is preposterous, unless it’s true. So Ortlund asks his readers to put on their thinking caps: “What if God is real, and Jesus is this God, showing up in history to reveal himself to us? Why not? Is it really all that much crazier than the alternatives?” (104). It’s not. And more importantly, the solution Jesus offers is the most complete answer to the ache. This message deserves to be proclaimed in public. In the Marketplace When Paul was in Athens, he “reasoned . . . in the marketplace” (Acts 17:17), the agora, which is where ideas were exchanged. Our modern agora is increasingly virtual, less of a town square and more like the comment section of a microvlog. Ortlund has excelled in this space, making hard things plain in his videos without making them small. His talent for public communication comes through in this book. For example, Ortlund tackles divine hiddenness: Have you ever wondered why, if God is indeed real, his existence isn’t completely obvious? Why are religious matters so ambiguous ? Wouldn’t a loving God want to make things clear to us? (176) It’s an intuitive argument that undermines the sense that the ache is a longing

featured.content: Several times now, I have been out in creation with unbelievers, speaking to them of eternal matters, and, passing by a dying branch at the base of a tree, I have picked it up and said, “This is your life apart from Christ.” Speaking about their souls, Jesus’s illustration is irresistible. The conversation goes something like this: Jesus gives us this illustration. He looks you in the eye and says that he is the tree (to augment the illustration slightly), and you are the branch. Look up and see the branches above us, beautiful leaves waving, healthy in their vibrant greens, bearing evidence of life. And then there is this branch. Dry. Leafless. Withered. Why? Because it is detached from the source of its life. Cut off from the one it was made to have communion with. And so, it lies here, detached from its purpose and severed from the only thing that can make it flourish. Jesus claims to be man’s source. He claims to be the Tree to whom you belong. In relationship with him, you have life. Apart from him, he teaches, you spend life withering. I usually pause to let the claim have its proper space. I ask what they think of such an assertion. I give them an opportunity to respond. I have often expected indifference or offense, but I have consistently been met with quiet consideration or outright acknowledgment that such an illustration made sense to them. Or at least they would like to hear more. So I go on to wonder aloud with them. What is it like to be a branch fallen from the tree that is, as Jesus says, withering ? Don’t you know? Need we ask? The restlessness, the fatal dryness, the looming death. The reaching out to anything and everything for life — except for the tree standing beside and over us. Him we do not want. Him we can do without. We can make it our own way. The adverb is different, but the end is the same — restless withering, drunken withering, religious, secular, or thoughtless withering . Some overdose on pleasure. Others get high on their own morality. Still others distract themselves from death’s shadow creeping over them with fantasy football and rounds of golf. But for all that, withering. But Jesus himself asserts that he is the Tree. He is the one we were made for; in him alone can we find the life that haunts us in still and sober moments. Be grafted to him through repentance and faith, be attached to him by the Spirit of the living God, have his words live in you, direct you, amaze you, and dead things will come to life. And what will it be on that day, I am compelled to continue, for those dry and fruitless branches who refused life in him? They will be gathered and thrown into the fire and burned as useless things. But Jesus came that you might have otherwise. He told us his mission was to bring life — life abundantly . Imagine the branch grafted to the tree, suddenly infused with life and purpose and the vital sap of God’s own Spirit. We are as branches; the Father, Son, and Spirit are the source of everlasting life. With him, we flourish though all may seem to go poorly. Without him, only sapped wood remains. Would you like to know more about this Jesus? Now, I tell you this to highlight one of many places where the Bible addresses the interiority of man and its solution: God. I want you to see how dangerous the alternative answers found in modern therapeutic culture are to our souls and our churches. It is a scourge, especially to this inward age, not because a therapeutic culture takes distresses of the heart seriously, but because it too often sends branches reaching out for anything but the Tree. Ingrown Toenails The problem comes not from a focus on the inner man. Anyone who says the Bible has little to say about internal battles, demons, depressions, anxieties, doubts, and the despairs of human life should not air his ignorance. The Scriptures abound with stories of the faithful brought into all the perplexities and pains of life in a fallen world. The Psalms, as one profound example, give u

featured.title: Who or What? A Continuum for Using AI Wisely
featured.summary: From AI as god to AI as assistant. Here is a continuum of nine roles that can help Christians tell legitimate uses of AI from illegitimate ones, and wise from unwise. See Also A Christian’s Guide to AI Technology is Fast, Sanctification Is Slow, and Claude Can’t Do It For You A La Carte (October 16)
featured.summary_zh: 从AI为神到AI为助手。这里有九个角色的连续体，可以帮助基督徒区分人工智能的合法使用和非法使用，以及明智和不明智的使用。另请参阅基督徒的人工智能指南：人工智能技术快，成圣慢，克劳德无法为你点菜（10 月 16 日）
featured.title_zh: 谁或什么？明智使用人工智能的连续体
featured.content: It is sometimes hard to believe that it has been only four years since AI became widely available. Few technologies have made so massive and rapid a leap into our daily lives, to the extent that AI now exists in the background of all of our lives and, for many of us, in the foreground as well. Few technologies have evolved as quickly, so that the latest ChatGPT model bears about as much resemblance to its debut as the latest MacBook does to a Commodore 64. If all this has happened in just four years, imagine what the next four—or the next fourteen—might hold. As AI’s capabilities have increased, so too have the ways we can use it in our homes, churches, and workplaces. It seems like every month or two we read of a feature that can make a difference to our lives by adding a new ability or taking on work that used to be done by a person. The latest trend is the rise of agents—AI tools like Meta’s Muse or xAI’s Grok Bot that can carry out tasks, routines, and duties on an ongoing basis. With all of the tools available to us and all of their capabilities, it can be difficult to know which uses are legitimate and which are not. We all know that just because AI can do a task doesn’t mean that it should . So how can we determine the legitimate roles AI can play in our lives? I think sketching out a continuum of some of AI’s potential roles can help us. At the beginning are roles that most of us would agree are illegitimate, and at the end roles that most of us would agree are legitimate. Between them are roles that may be illegitimate in some cases and perfectly fine in others. These demand that we approach them thoughtfully to determine whether integrating them into our lives would be an act of wisdom or folly. As you will see, illegitimate roles tend to be those that require a who whereas legitimate roles tend to be those that require a mere what . The Continuum AI as God . There are some people, most of them deeply engaged in the tech industry, who ascribe to AI god-like qualities and who relate to it accordingly. They may believe it is an evil god that is likely to destroy humanity or a benevolent god that is likely to redeem humanity, but in either case, they treat AI as something far more than software. These people go too far and commit idolatry as they attribute to tech what rightly belongs to God. AI as Friend . There are some people who relate to AI as a friend, and even a few troubled people who relate to it as a lover. While AI is capable of mimicking the kind of relationship one might enjoy with a fellow human being, it can only ever mimic it. To relate to AI as a friend is to anthropomorphize a mere technology and worse, to deprive oneself of actual friendship. Though AI can imitate friendship, it cannot be a friend in any legitimate sense of the word, for friendship depends upon personhood. Not only that, but friendship depends upon mutuality and both the blessings and risks that come with relationship. You cannot be friends with AI any more than you can be friends with a tree, a PlayStation, or any other non-being. AI as Counselor . Many people today relate to AI as a counselor—a confidant who will listen patiently and counsel them with a trusted voice. Yet because AI is a what , not a who , it cannot offer answers based on a true understanding of their circumstances, true wisdom that comes from learning and experience, or true compassion that comes from sharing their humanity. It cannot empathize with them, pray for them, or plead with the Holy Spirit for wisdom in helping them. AI is capable of advising in many ways, but not of counseling, for counseling is inherently personal. AI as Pastor . Increasingly, people bring to AI the matters of spiritual health, growth, and well-being that in the past would have been addressed to a pastor. Every Christian needs to be under the loving oversight of a pastor who will care for their soul, and such crucial matters must be entrusted not to AI, but to a pastor who is called and
featured.content_zh:
有时很难相信,自AI广泛提供至今才四年。 很少有技术使我们的日常生活如此巨大和迅速地跃入,以至于AI现在存在于我们所有生活的背景中,对我们许多人来说,也存在于前景中。

很少有技术发展得这么快,因此最新的ChatGPT模型与其首发版的相近程度与最新的MacBook对准将64的相近程度相同. 如果这一切在短短的四年内就发生了,想象下四年,或下十四年可能发生的情况。 随着AI能力的增强,我们在家里、教堂和工作场所使用它的方式也一样。

我们似乎每个月或两个月都读到一个特点,通过增加新的能力或从事过去由一个人完成的工作,可以改变我们的生活。 最近的趋势是,诸如Meta的Muse或xAI的Grok Bot等能够持续执行任务、例行公事和职责的代理-AI工具的兴起。

有了我们可以利用的所有工具及其所有能力,就很难知道哪些用途是合法的,哪些用途不是。 我们都知道, 我们如何确定AI在生活中可以扮演的合法角色? 我认为勾画出AI的一些潜在角色可以帮助我们。

开始时,我们大多数人都认为这种角色是非法的,最后,我们大多数人都认为这种角色是合法的。 两者之间是在某些情况下可能是非法的,而在另一些情况下则完全正确。 这些要求我们深思熟虑地对待他们,以确定将他们融入我们的生活是明智还是愚蠢。

你会看到,非法角色往往是那些需要谁的角色,而合法角色往往是那些只需要什么的角色。 连续AI作为上帝。 有一些人,其中大多数人深入从事技术产业,他们把AI的神性描述为"类似"的特质,并与之相应相通.

他们可能相信是邪恶的神有可能毁灭人性或者仁慈的神有可能赎回人性,但无论在哪种情况下,他们都把AI视为远远超出软件的东西. 这些人太过分了 以偶像为神 因为他们把属于上帝的东西归为技术 作为朋友的AI.

有些人以朋友身份与AI有关,甚至有少数人以恋人身份与之有关系. 虽然AI能够模仿人们可能享受的那种与人类同胞的关系,但它只能模仿它. 作为朋友与AI的关系就是人类化,将一种简单的技术变成更糟糕的技术,剥夺了自己的实际友谊。

虽然大赦国际可以模仿友谊,但它不能是任何合法意义上的朋友,因为友谊取决于人性。 不仅如此,友谊还取决于相互以及关系带来的幸福和风险。 你不可能成为AI的朋友 也不可能成为树上的朋友,PlayStation,或者其他的不幸福. 作为律师的AI.

今天,许多人都把大赦国际当作一个顾问——一个会耐心地倾听他们的意见并以一个值得信赖的声音给他们提供建议的告密者。 然而,由于大赦国际是一个什么人,而不是谁,它不能根据对他们情况的真正理解、来自学习和经验的真正智慧或来自分享其人性的真正同情来提供答案。

它不能同情他们,不能为他们祈祷,也不能恳求圣灵的智慧帮助他们。 大赦国际能够在许多方面提供咨询,但不能提供咨询,因为咨询本质上是针对个人的。 作为牧师的AI. 人们越来越多地将精神健康、成长和福祉等问题带到大赦国际,这些问题过去本来是交给牧师的。

每个基督徒都需要接受一位会关心自己灵魂的牧师的慈爱监督,这种关键事项必须不委托给大赦国际,而委托给一位被叫作"和"和"的牧师".

featured.title_zh: 讲道中的陷阱：一封关于申请的信
featured.content: The following letter was published in the December 2025 issue of the Banner Magazine. It is published here at the request of a reader who found it helpful, in the hope that its counsel might be blessed to others also. You can also listen to a reading of this letter on the Banner Podcast. Dear J______, Following our conversation about application in preaching, I thought I would send along some thoughts I have had over the years on the subject. I want to point out some pitfalls you may want to keep in mind as you train R______. The only reason I know about them is from spending too much time in them myself! There has been a lot of self–examination and repenting over the years for me in this matter. The first thought is that too often (even in some of the best books on preaching) we hear that the text drives the sermon. This is a half-truth. A potentially dangerous half-truth. I have seen a man so intent on expositing his text well (and he did it very well) that he did not seem to notice or care that a third of the people in the room walked out before he finished preaching because he went on so long and the last meal of the conference was being served to meet the constraint of local train times. A wrong type of focus on the text and its explanation can make us oblivious to the very people the text is for. A preacher who stands up to preach having spent ninety per cent of his sermon preparation time in the week concentrating on the biblical text has not sufficiently realized what preaching actually is. In their book Letters Along the Way D. A. Carson and John Woodbridge put it this way: A chief reason why so much of what passes for evangelical expository preaching is so boring and irrelevant is that the preacher has spent a vastly disproportionate amount of preparation time in exegesis and outlines, and so little in thinking through how the Word of God is to wound and heal (to use the language of Hosea). 1 So preaching is about people. Preaching is about what God has to say to people about their lives . The text for a sermon is what God has to say to people . So the text of a sermon is like the recipe for a dish. A good cook would never be so focused on a recipe that she did not stop to realize that this was not at all the type of food her guests would need or appreciate. She would have her guests in mind from the start. After all, the goal of a good cook is not simply a matter of a recipe or a certain dish. It is feeding and feasting people . People drive the sermon. People are the reason God has given us the message in the biblical text. The biblical text leads the preacher to what the people need to hear from God. But the biblical text is only a means . The goal is people—to bring them somewhere that God wants them to go. To enlighten them, change them, help them, console them, correct them, train them to worship and serve God. People-oriented preaching comes from a God-centred, loving interest in them . Text-oriented preaching may simply come from the preacher’s love for preaching, for exegesis or for theology. A physician may be fascinated by medical treatments. But the good physician’s real interest is not treatments but people whose suffering has called for those treatments. Just so, true preaching is about people. That brings me to a second, related thought. We are often told that in preparing a sermon the key is finding the main idea of the text. To consider this as the key is not a people-oriented point of view and does not produce good preaching. It produces preaching with lots of emphasis on ideas and little emphasis on application. The key to preparing a sermon is not to find the main idea of the text. It is to find the main goal of the text. Not ‘What does the biblical text mainly say?’ But rather ‘What does this text intend to mainly do for people?’ What does the text intend mainly to effect in the lives of people? What does this text aim to move the people to believe, to do, to become? Application! A. T. Pierson, i
featured.content_zh: 以下信件发表于"班纳杂志"2025年12月号. 它应一位读者的要求在这里出版,他觉得它很有帮助,希望它的律师也能得到他人的祝福。 也可以在"班纳·波德克特"上收听对这封信的读取. 亲爱的J-,在我们讨论申请布道后,我想,我将提出一些多年来我对这一问题的看法。 我想指出一些陷阱 你可能想记住 当你训练R. 我了解他们的唯一原因 就是自己花太多时间在他们身上 多年来,我一直以来都在自责自悔。 第一种想法是,太多时候(即使在一些关于布道的好书中),我们听到文字驱动布道. 这是半个事实。 一个潜在的危险 半真相。 我见过一个男人如此有意地公开他的文字(他做得非常好),他似乎没有注意到或关心房间里有三分之一的人在他完成布道之前就离开,因为他走了这么长一段时间,会议的最后一餐是用来应付当地火车时间的限制。 错误地注重案文及其解释会使我们忘记案文所要为的人。 一位挺身而出进行传道的传道者,在一周里,他90%的布道准备时间都集中在圣经文本上,但是他没有充分意识到实际的传道内容。 在他们所著的"沿着路"(Letrys A. A. Carson)和"约翰·伍德布里奇"(John Woodbridge)一书中这样写道: 传福音的宣讲之所以如此之多,实在是无趣而无关紧要的一个主要原因是,传道人花费了大量的不相称的准备时间来解剖和提纲,在思考"上帝之道"是怎样去伤口和愈合(使用"霍西"的语言)时却很少考虑. 1个 故传道以人为事. 意义在于上帝要对人们说 他们的生活 讲道的文字是上帝要对人们说的话。 所以布道的文字就像菜谱。 一个好厨师永远也不会把注意力集中在一个配方上,以至于她不禁意识到这根本不是客人需要或欣赏的食物类型. 她一开始就想着她的客人 毕竟,一个好厨师的目标不仅仅是一个菜谱或某种菜肴的问题. 它在给人们提供食物和盛宴。 人们驱使布道。 人们是上帝给我们圣经文本中的信息的原因。 圣经文本将传道人引向人们需要从上帝那里听到的. 但圣经文本只是一个手段。 目标是人们,把他们带到上帝要他们去的地方去。 为了启蒙他们,改变他们,帮助他们,安慰他们,矫正他们,训练他们去崇拜并服务于上帝. 以人为中心的布道来自以上帝为中心, 以文字为取向的传道可能只是来自传道者对传道、开教或神学的热爱。 医生可能因治疗而着迷。 但好医生的真正兴趣不是治疗,而是那些遭受痛苦需要治疗的人。 所以,真正的传道是关于人的。 这让我想到另一个相关的想法。 我们经常被告知,在准备布道时,关键在于找到案文的主要想法。 将此视为关键不是以人民为导向的观点,也不产生好传道. 它产生许多强调思想的布道,很少强调应用。 准备布道的关键不是找到文本的主要想法. 它是为了找到案文的主要目标。 而非"圣经主要说些什么?" 但更确切地说,“这个文本主要是为了什么?” 案文主要打算如何影响人们的生活? 这个文字的目的是要促使人们相信,去做,变成什么? 申请! A. T. 皮尔逊,i

featured.title: Spoiled for Choice: Two New Graphic Novels of Pilgrim’s Progress
featured.summary: Two new graphic novel adaptations of Pilgrim’s Progress have arrived within weeks of each other. Here's how they are similar and different, and my recommendation of which one to buy. See Also A La Carte (July 27) The Puritans: John Bunyan A La Carte (6/3)
featured.summary_zh: 两部《天路历程》的全新漫画改编作品在相隔数周的时间内相继面世。以下是它们的异同之处，以及我对于购买哪一本的建议。另见《A La Carte》（7月27日）《清教徒：约翰·班扬》《A La Carte》（6月3日）
featured.title_zh: 选择多多：两部全新《天路历程》绘本小说
featured.content: I have often expressed how spoiled Christian readers are today. As if we needed more proof of this, how about the fact that in a single month, publishers released not one but two major graphic novel adaptations of Pilgrim’s Progress ? Both are well-written, beautifully illustrated, and faithful to Bunyan’s story. Let me help you understand their similarities and differences and tell you which one might be best to add to your library. Christian’s Quest is written by Tyler Van Halteren and illustrated by Manuel Zepic. It is published by Lithos Kids, which has already released the three-part Little Pilgrim’s Big Journey , an illustrated adaptation of Pilgrim’s Progress for young readers, and The Mansoul Chronicles , which is based on Bunyan’s Holy War . It is a 220-page 7×10.63 inch hardcover that targets children aged 8+, though it is meant to be enjoyed by teens and adults as well. Its illustrations are what I might describe as a clean, polished YA style. The lines are thin and tidy and much of the form comes from shading. The colors tend to maintain a soft, muted, painted look. It lightly updates some antiquated language so that Bunyan’s Slough of Despond becomes the Bog of Despond. Christian is youthful and fresh-faced, and his burden is a bulging pack on a frame. It includes some bonus material: a behind-the-scenes look at how a graphic novel is made, and a study guide that explains and applies each of the stages of Christian’s quest. It also indicates that a sequel, Christiana’s Crown , will be released in 2028. Pilgrim’s Progress: The Graphic Novel is written by Jeremy Patenaude, illustrated by Brent McKee, colored by Matt Wilson, and lettered by Taylor Esposito. It is published by Crossway as what I believe is the company’s first graphic novel, though it has a long history of publishing books for young readers. It is a 256-page 7×10.25 inch paperback that targets readers aged 14+. Its illustrations are what I might describe as gritty and stylized and perhaps a bit more indie than mainstream. It uses heavy brush ink, dark shadows, and vivid colors. It does not update Bunyan’s antiquated language. Christian is a gaunt, tormented, weathered adult whose burden is a huge stone roped to his back. Its bonus material includes a lexicon of the key characters and locations and reflections on each of the chapters. There is no indication of a sequel that will cover Christiana’s quest. While these two graphic novels tell the same story and tell it faithfully using dialogue and illustration rather than narration, they tell it using different visual language largely because Christian’s Quest is meant to be accessible to a younger demographic. You might say that Christian’s Quest is a bit more kid-friendly and Pilgrim’s Progress is a bit more adult-friendly, though both could easily be enjoyed by kids and adults alike. After all, who doesn’t enjoy reading the occasional graphic novel? Another key difference is that Pilgrim’s Progress is a paperback where Christian’s Quest is being sold as more of an heirloom object that features cloth binding, gold foil, and a ribbon marker. Let me show you a few examples of the art from each book. Christian’s Quest These are drawn from the publisher’s preview images. Pilgrim’s Progress These are drawn from the sample chapter on Crossway’s site. My Recommendation Which do I recommend? Either! Both! If your readers are younger, Christian’s Quest is the more obvious choice, and if they are older—teenagers and up—they may prefer Pilgrim’s Progress . But you couldn’t go wrong with either, and you couldn’t go wrong with picking up both. Where to Buy Christian’s Quest Lithos Kids · clothbound hardcover · ages 8+ Buy at Amazon Westminster Books Pilgrim’s Progress: The Graphic Novel Crossway · paperback · ages 14+ Buy at Amazon Westminster Books See Also A La Carte (July 27) The Puritans: John Bunyan A La Carte (6/3)

我经常表达基督教读者今天是多么的被宠坏。 似乎我们需要更多的证据, 在一个月里, 出版商只发行了两部关于朝圣者进步的重要小说改编。 他们都写得很好,

让我来帮助你理解它们之间的相似之处和差异,并告诉你,哪一个可能最好加入你的图书馆. 由泰勒·范·哈特伦(英语:Tyler Van Halteren)撰写,曼努埃尔·泽皮奇(英语:Manuel Zepic)作画.

由Lithos Kids出版, 已经发行了三部曲小朝圣者大旅, 这是一项220页的7x10.63英寸硬盖,针对的是8岁以上儿童,但青少年和成年人也享受。

它的插图是我可以描述的 一种干净,光泽的YA风格。 线条细而整齐,形式大多来自阴影. 颜色倾向于保持柔软,沉默,绘画的外观. 它轻而易举地更新了一些古老的语言,使邦扬的"Despond的Slough"成为了Despond的Bog. 克里斯蒂安年轻又新面孔,他的担子是架子上的膨胀包.

包括一些奖品:一幅幕后小说是如何制作的,一幅研究指南解释并应用了基督教的追求的每个阶段。 这部续集《克里斯蒂安娜的王冠》将于2028年发行。

朝圣者的进步:图画小说由Jeremy Patenaude写作,布伦特·麦基(Brent Mckee)饰演,马特·威尔逊饰演,泰勒·埃斯波西托(Taylor Esposito)饰演. 由Crossway出版, 我认为这是公司的第一部平面小说, 它有256页7x10.25英寸的纸质背面,针对14岁以上读者。

它的插图是我可以说的 粗糙和结构化, 可能比主流多一点。 它使用重笔墨,暗影,以及生动的色彩. 它不会更新Bunyan的过时语言。 克里斯蒂安是一个胆小, 受折磨,风化的成年人, 他的负担是一个巨大的石头绑在背上。

它的奖金材料包括关键人物和地点的词汇表以及对每一章的思考. 没有迹象表明会续集克里斯蒂安娜的追求。

虽然这两部图画小说讲述了同一个故事,忠实地用对话和插图来讲述,而不是用不同的视觉语言讲述,这主要是因为克里斯蒂安的Quest本意是让年轻人口能够接触到.

基督教徒的追问更适合孩子, 朝圣者的进步更适合成年人, 毕竟,谁不喜欢偶尔读那本图画小说?

另一个关键区别是,朝圣者的进步是一个纸质的回扣,在那里,基督教的Quest被作为更多的继承物出售,该物的特点是布装、金瓦和丝带标志。 让我给你们看看每本书中的一些艺术例子。 基督教的追问 这些照片来自出版商的预览图像。

朝圣者的进步 照片来自Crossway网站的样本章节。 我的建议 我推荐哪个? 也没有! 都一样! 如果你的读者年轻,基督教的“追问”是更明显的选择,如果他们是年长的年轻人,他们可能更喜欢朝圣者的进步。 但你也不可能出错,

featured.title: Midlife Is a Crossroads, Not a Crisis
featured.summary: In ‘Good News for Midlife,’ Jared Wilson reminds us to embrace our midlife crossroads, find new meaning in service to others, and let this season be an opportunity to discover grace upon grace in Jesus.
featured.summary_zh: 在《中年好消息》（ Good News for Midlife ）一书中，贾里德·威尔逊（ Jared Wilson ）提醒我们要拥抱中年十字路口，寻找为他人服务的新意义，让这个季节成为在耶稣身上发现恩典的机会。
featured.title_zh: 中年是一个十字路口，而不是危机
featured.content: Last year, I was sitting with an early twentysomething grad student in our church. He said he was looking for an older man to mentor him, and I started thinking through our godly, wise men in their 50s and 60s. He stopped me and clarified: He was asking me to mentor him. “Wait, you think I’m old?!” I’m 42, and to be fair, I’ve been told I’m an “old soul” my whole life. Some have wondered aloud if I was born old. While I still don’t feel old, I’ll admit this new and strange season has spurred me to go looking for wisdom. I’ll tell you, reading about midlife is depressing. According to studies, happiness in life follows a U-shaped curve. Our self-reported happiness starts high in childhood, then decreases into adolescence and further into early adulthood. It bottoms out somewhere around age 46—smack in the center of middle age—before beginning to rise again and steadily increasing into our twilight years. Further, studies have shown that depression and anxiety also are highest around the age of 45. Despite all the bad news, Good News for Midlife: Navigating Middle Age with Guts and Grace was encouraging. Writing from his early 50s, Jared Wilson, associate professor of pastoral ministry at Midwestern Baptist Theological Seminary, understands the challenges of midlife but also provides refreshing hope for those of us finding our own way through. Understand Midlife Most definitions place “middle age” as 40 to 60, but it’s probably more accurate to describe midlife in terms of its demands and responsibilities. For me, it looks something like this: I still feel energetic, but it takes far longer to recover from lost sleep, injuries, and travel. My kids are now teenagers, and some days, I only see them for a half hour. Our grocery bill is three times our first mortgage. Our parents are in their 70s and now need more support from us than we need from them. I think I’m still in touch with modern culture, but my kids assure me I’m not. I may have 40-plus years left, but it sure feels like most of my life is now behind me. Most deeply, I’m frequently reflecting on life’s disappointments and griefs, wondering if I should have done this or that differently. This is middle life. We’re too young to feel old. But we’re also too old to feel young. Wilson, who writes specifically for men entering or inhabiting these decades, acknowledges all these challenges. “But,” he writes, “while this season presents unique challenges . . . midlife also presents exciting opportunities to trust Jesus for personal, marital, and spiritual flourishing” (xi). Thankfully, Wilson helps us reframe the demands and opportunities of middle age not as a necessary crisis but as a critical crossroads . Crossroads, Not Crisis For almost 60 years, pop culture has made “midlife” nearly synonymous with “crisis.” The phrase comes from psychoanalyst Elliott Jaques’s 1965 essay “ Death and the Mid-Life Crisis ” and has been repeated across dozens of books ever since. (There’s even a board game called Mid-Life Crisis, where players aim to accumulate wealth and avoid landing on bankruptcy, divorce, and nervous breakdown.) This is middle life. We’re too young to feel old. But we’re also too old to feel young. Fortunately, recent studies suggest fewer than 20 percent of Americans experience a full-on crisis in these middle decades. Despite this, many of us face a unique temptation to flee from responsibility or forge some entirely new life. Wilson puts it poignantly: “Whether you’re in a crisis or not, at midlife you’re at a crossroads” (16). At this crossroads, we see down one path the allure of individualism and freedom from responsibility. We might simply call this path the road of empty promises. As the proverbs say, it seems right, but in the end, it leads to death (Prov. 14:12). The second path is one of embracing reality, stepping deeper into relationship, and trusting the goodness of God. This road offers no promises other than the hardships of real life. But it’s also where

featured.title: Avoid the Trap of Bitterness
featured.summary: Joseph avoids the trap of bitterness. And you can too, if you follow these three steps.
featured.summary_zh: 约瑟避免了痛苦的陷阱。如果你遵循这三个步骤，你也可以这样做。
featured.title_zh: 避开苦涩的陷阱
featured.content: Imagine the people closest to you betray you. It’s your trust in them that lets them get close enough to hurt you so terribly. Now, imagine that this betrayal completely upends your life for years . Everything that made your life good—your family, your home, your safety—is violently taken from you. Now imagine years bleed into decades. Your life spirals into ever more pain and isolation. And every jab of hurt leads you to agonize over the initial wound: None of this would have happened if it weren’t for them. How could they do this? However, in the last few years, your fortunes have turned around. From the slums, you’re suddenly lifted to a vaulted position of power. People no longer take advantage of you but try to stay in your good graces. It doesn’t wash all the bitter memories away, but it’s something. And then, lo and behold, who happens to come before you but them . Your cruel betrayers are there, groveling, asking you for help. How would you feel? What would you do? If you haven’t picked up on it yet, this is the story of Joseph from Genesis. Sold into slavery by his brothers, Joseph walks through much injustice and suffering before being catapulted into the most powerful office in Egypt, second only to Pharaoh. And when his brothers come cringing toward him in the end, certain that Joseph will use his power to pay them back, Joseph responds with unexpected mercy, generosity, and warmth (Gen. 50:15–21) . How? Joseph avoids the trap of bitterness. And you can too, if you follow these three steps. 1. Understand Bitterness Bitterness is revealed in our emotions (coldness, anger, resentment, suspicion, revulsion), but it begins in our will. We choose bitterness when we believe that for justice or fairness to be preserved, the offender must be punished in some way. We may even claim to forgive, but in our heart of hearts, we fear that forgiveness comes at the expense of justice. So, you give your spouse the silent treatment, you cut your parents off, you make life difficult for your kids. Joseph avoids bitterness by trusting that God is the One who takes care of justice. When his brothers beg for mercy, Joseph replies, “Do not fear, for am I in the place of God?” (Gen. 50:19). Joseph knows it isn’t his place to deal out the judgment only God can give. The first step in avoiding bitterness is letting God take care of final justice (Rom. 12:14–21). Bitterness feels like a solution to the problem, but it isn’t. It’s trying to solve one sin with another sin. Which is why we’re commanded unequivocally to repent of bitterness, full stop (Eph. 4:31). We’re never told bitterness is an acceptable method to coerce repentance or pursue justice, or is permissible until the other person apologizes and makes restitution. Reconciliation requires two people who are willing. But to repent of bitterness only requires one. Bitterness feels like a solution to the problem, but it isn’t. It’s trying to solve one sin with another sin. Bitterness isn’t the path to justice—only to more bitterness. Using bitterness to pursue justice is like using a hatchet to build a house, confident it’ll work just like a hammer. 2. Unmask Bitterness We’re called to be so absolute and unqualified in rejecting bitterness because of its penchant to spread. It’s a “root” (Heb. 12:15) that will only grow and become more difficult to uproot as time goes on. Plucking up a sapling is easy; removing an oak tree isn’t. Soon, the bitterness you feel toward Person A will make you more prone to taking offense at Person B and more sensitive to Person C. Soon, you become an angry person who holds grudges. It’s a root that “defiles many.” Bitterness is hard to detect initially because it hides so effectively behind a mask of morality. The bitter person “blesses himself in his heart, saying, ‘I shall be safe, though I walk in the stubbornness of my heart’” (Deut. 29:19). In other words, “I’m not wrong, they are! They’re the ones who hurt me!” It not only immediately puts you into a

featured.title_zh: 神圣欢乐的味道
featured.content: Audio Transcript We like to think in simple categories. It’s easier that way, and easier to be clear in explaining things. So, if I ask, “How are you doing?” you will probably respond in terms of “good” or “bad,” and then explain why you are feeling good or bad. By default, we are doing fine until we are doing bad, but it’s normally one or the other, up or down like a light switch: We’re good. We’re bad. Then along comes the apostle Paul and pulls this on-off switch off the wall and breaks it into pieces to teach us that the very good and the very bad coexist in this life. Today on Ask Pastor John: the many flavors of holy joy. It’s a question from an anonymous listener to the podcast. “Pastor John, you have been writing and speaking for decades about the importance of joy in the life of God and the life of a Christian. You have made the case that joy in God — not only in his gifts but in his person — is essential to glorifying God. You have argued that the reason that God’s God-centeredness, his pursuit of his own glorification in all he does, is not megalomania is precisely because he magnifies his glory through our enjoyment of him. You have pointed out that the apostle Paul not only spoke of being ‘sorrowful, yet always rejoicing,’ but that he also said, ‘In all our affliction, I am overflowing with joy’ (2 Corinthians 6:10; 7:4). That last statement seems staggering. If it can be present in such different circumstances, can you help me even begin to imagine what true joy is?” Joy in All Circumstances That very statement from 2 Corinthians 7:4 has arrested my attention for a little over a year (since I taught 2 Corinthians last year) and just wouldn’t let me go, because it seems to demand that we dig into the nature of joy to figure out what he could possibly mean by calling his experience joyful in the light of so many different sufferings. He mentions 26 sufferings, different kinds of affliction in 2 Corinthians 11:23–28. It’s not just Paul’s experience of joy in all those afflictions that drives me, but many, many different circumstances in the Bible are the circumstances in which we are told to rejoice. It’s just incredible how many there are. Here are a few. - Rejoice in your future inheritance (1 Peter 1:3–6). - Rejoice that your names are written in heaven (Luke 10:20). - Rejoice in the plundering of your property for love’s sake (Hebrews 10:34). - Rejoice in being poured out for others (Philippians 2:17–18). - Rejoice in spending and being spent for souls (2 Corinthians 12:15). - Rejoice in your weakness for Christ’s sake (2 Corinthians 12:9–10). - Rejoice in being slandered and persecuted and rejected (Matthew 5:11–12; Luke 6:22–23). - Rejoice in being shamed for Christ’s name (Acts 5:41). - Rejoice in contributing to others’ needs (2 Corinthians 9:7). - Rejoice in the partnership of other believers (Philippians 1:4–5). - Rejoice in people being converted (1 Thessalonians 2:19–20). - Rejoice in the unity of believers (Philippians 2:2). - Rejoice in truth (1 Corinthians 13:6). - Rejoice in the law of God (Psalm 119:14, 111, 162). - Rejoice in the Lord (Philippians 4:4). - Rejoice in the hope of the glory of God (Romans 5:2). - Rejoice in God (Romans 5:11). That’s for starters. The variety of circumstances in which we are told to rejoice demands this: Joy is not a static emotion but one that changes in intensity. That’s pretty obvious for everybody, but also — this is what I’m drawing out now that feels fresh to me — it varies in quality. So, what do I mean by quality? I mean the nature or the kind of experience joy is — not just how intense it is but how different it is, or how it can feel so different from one kind of experience to the next. And yet, all of them could be called joy, which I think means a positive emotion that we really want to have. That would be my kind of bottom-line definition of joy. 音频记录 我们喜欢简单思考 这样比较容易, 因此,如果我问到“你在做什么?” 你可能会回答“好”或“坏”,然后解释你为什么感觉好或坏。 默认情况下,我们做得很好,直到我们做坏事为止,但通常它是一个或另一个,上或下像一个开关:我们很好。

我们是坏人。 然后使徒保罗来了 把这个关上 然后把它拆成碎片 教我们 生活中的善恶共存 今天在"问约翰牧师"(Ask Pastor John):许多圣乐的口味. 这是匿名听众对播客的提问。

“约翰神父,几十年来你一直在写作和谈论欢乐在上帝生活中的重要性和基督徒的生活。 你已说明,上帝的喜悦——不仅是他的礼物,而且是他个人的喜悦——对颂扬上帝至关重要。

你们认为,上帝的以神为本,他追求自己的美德,并不是因为大浪漫通过我们享受他的光荣。

你已指出使徒保罗不仅说出"悲伤而总是欢喜",他还说:"在我们所有的苦难中,我充满了欢快" (2 Corinthians 6: 10; 7: 4). 刚才的发言令人吃惊。

如果在这样不同的情况下它能够存在,你能帮助我开始想象真正的快乐是什么吗?” 所有情况下的欢乐 2个哥林多人7: 4的言论让我的注意力 一年多一点(因为去年我教过2个哥林多人),

在如此多不同痛苦的光芒下 称他的经历很快乐 他提到26起痛苦, 不仅仅是保罗在所有这些苦难中所经历的快乐, 这真是不可思议。

这里有一些。 - 享受你未来的遗产(1 Peter 1: 3-6) - 很高兴你们的名字写在天上(公爵10:20) - 在为爱而掠夺你的财产(赫布鲁斯10:34)中欢欣鼓舞. - 欢呼为他人倒出(菲利浦2:17-18)。 - 享受为灵魂而花和花的快乐(2科林斯人12:15).

- 为基督欢呼你的软弱(2科林斯人12:9-10). 被诽谤、迫害和拒绝(马修5:11–12;卢克6:22–23)。 - 乐于满足他人的需要(2科林斯9:7)。 - 与其他信徒合作欢呼(菲利浦1:4-5)。

- 很高兴有人被改造(1 Thessalonians 2:19-20)。 - 欢呼信徒的团结(菲利浦2:2). - 真理快乐(1科林斯13:6). - 在"上帝之法"中取悦("诗经"119:14,111,162). - 欢乐于主(菲利浦4:4). - 为上帝的荣耀而欢呼(罗马人5:2). - 享受上帝(罗马人5:11). 这首先要说明,

我们被告知欢乐的环境多种多样,这就要求我们:欢乐不是一种静态的情感,而是一种强度变化的情感. 这对每个人都是显而易见的,但同样——这是我现在所画的,我觉得很新鲜——它的质量也各不相同。 那么,我是什么意思 质量?

我指的是快乐的本质或体验类型——不仅仅是它有多强烈,而是它有多不同,或者它能有什么感觉,从一种体验到另一种体验如此不同. 然而,所有它们都可以叫做快乐, 我认为这意味着我们真正想要有一种积极的情感。 那就是我对快乐的底线定义

featured.content: Let me take a moment to remind you of some of the features of this site you may not know about. I have a growing page of Liturgies meant to help the local church in its worship. I also offer Book Recommendations across many categories and a list of the Best Commentaries for each book of the Bible. And if you like the quote graphics I share day by day, you can find them all at SquareQuotes.church where they are free to download. Sales & Deals Today’s Kindle deals include several of the “Heart Talks” mini books that are meant to help women with common concerns: feeling like failures in parenting, husbands who lead poorly, doubt, and so on. You’ll also find Greg Gifford’s Lies My Therapist Told Me and several other titles. Recommended Reading Beer, Beef and Player’s Navy Cut. This is a brilliant article about C.S. Lewis and the vices that dogged him throughout his life—a three-pack-a day smoking habit, eating habits that bordered on gluttony, and far more alcohol than anyone should consume. “In case you really are new here and you mostly know Lewis from the kid’s books, let’s state the obvious: the man we universally honor as one of the 20th Century’s great saints smoked, ate and drank like he was a sponsored athlete of consumption. He sinned frequently through overindulgence. What do we do with this information?” How to Graciously Say No. You have probably run into the same conclusion I have: it’s often far harder to say no than to say yes. Yet sometimes the best thing we can do for ourselves and for others is to say no. Reagan Rose offers some thoughts on that (for those who have the ability to say no, of course, since in many occupations saying no isn’t an option). Can’t You Let Me Just Attend? “We live in a chronically noncommittal society. No wonder, then, that this has been dubbed the age of anxiety. Surely, covenant relationships aren’t the only cure, but it might surprise us how much stability of soul comes from deep, reliable, unflighty fellowship.” David Mathis explains why commitment to a particular church is so important, even if it’s extremely countercultural. When Morningness Is Confused With Godliness. I always enjoy an article that provides an alternate view of something we almost take for granted. That’s the case with this one from Cole Mizel, who is concerned that we may be too quick to imply that the best Christians do their daily devotions in the morning. “But is it really more virtuous to be a morning person than a night owl?” Everyone Doesn’t React the Same Way. J.V. Fesko makes a simple but wise point here: everyone doesn’t respond to preaching the same way. Because that’s the case, we should not assume that those who display a lot of emotion are necessarily being impacted more than those who do not. “Tears are not the sacrament of a changed heart, the visible sign and seal of an anguished and healed soul.” Evangelising With a Dog. featured.content: Good morning. Grace and peace to you. Sales & Deals Today’s Kindle deals include several excellent biographies from Crossway. Each of them is good, but I’m partial to the one on R.C. Sproul. Note that these biographies are typically priced between $22 and $40. In case you missed it on the weekend, Westminster Books is offering a deep discount on the new graphic novel adaptation of Pilgrim’s Progress . Recommended Reading Christianity Under the Progressive Gaze. Kyle Borg: “What interests me more than politics is the apparent cultural strength and growing respectability of progressive Christianity. In fact, a headline in The Guardian boldly declared: ‘A progressive understanding of Christianity won in the US elections.’ In a society where historic Christian convictions — and I don’t just mean Reformed confessionalism but basic creedal Christianity — is often treated with suspicion, if not hostility, some expressions of ‘Christianity’ seem to be enjoying a rather warm reception.” Counterfeit Providence: Why Christians Must Reject the Conspiratorial Mind. Mitchell Bahnsen explores the conspiratorial mind and explains why it’s so important for Christians to reject it. “None of this requires Christians to become gullible or naive. Psalm 2 describes kings taking counsel together against the Lord, and the crucifixion itself was a conspiracy carried out jointly by religious and governmental authorities. True connivance does occur, and wisdom to discern the truth is necessary in a complex and fallen world. However, we must defend against a totalizing hermeneutic of suspicion, lest it become its own form of faith.” Wise People Strive To Be Wiser. Justin Huffman discusses a principle that may be obvious, but is also important. “The wise person is always seeking to become wiser still. The truly spiritual person recognizes his or her constant need for spiritual growth.” The Pro-Life Movement’s Midterm Reckoning. First Things allows everyone to access several free articles per month, and this one from Jonathon Van Maren is worth one of the quota. He considers how the battle against abortion is likely to look very different after the midterm elections. “‘It’s impossible to sugarcoat it,’ Marjorie Dannenfelser of Susan B. Anthony Pro-Life America wrote in a memo issued on November 3. The 2026 midterm election results ‘are a disaster for the unborn, for their mothers, and for the country as a whole. Democrats are on track to control two of the three pieces they need to legalize taxpayer-funded abortion on demand, up until birth, in all fifty states—something they promise to start pushing as soon as they take office in January.'” How Evil Works. John Piper helpfully explains how evil works. “At the center of Satan’s purpose is to deceive on earth and to accuse in heaven. If he can deceive you about God and Christ, you will perish. If he can successfully accuse you of unforgiven sin in heaven, you will perish. And Jesus calls him ‘a murderer from the beginning’ (John 8:44). So, the deception and the accusation and the eternal death that results from unforgiven sin is a way of destroying people and opposing God.” Preaching in Paragraphs. This may be helpful for preachers to read as they let last week’s sermon fade into the past and begin to think about the next one. “Every preacher knows the terror of a blank screen. It is Tuesday morning—or even worse, Saturday afternoon—and the preacher sits and stares at his laptop. He has opened a new document in his word processor, and now the cursor stands idling on the page, patiently blinking. And the words aren’t coming.” Reader Recommendations Once a week, I like to ask what you enjoy and recommend. What books, products, videos, sites, or other experiences do you recommend to others who read this blog/newsletter? Let me know, and I’ll share a collection on Saturday. (If you’re reading this via email, you’ll need to visit my site to fill out the form. Go here to read last week’s recommendations.) Submit

featured.title_zh: 对那些厌倦了头条新闻的人来说，圣诞节是个好消息
featured.content: Read Go on up to a high mountain, O Zion, herald of good news; lift up your voice with strength, O Jerusalem, herald of good news; lift it up, fear not; say to the cities of Judah, “Behold your God!” (Isa. 40:9) Reflect When I first started writing for The Gospel Coalition, my editor told me we were going to report good news. We were going to tell stories of where Christians were helping and the kingdom was advancing. We were going to say, “Behold, church, how God is at work in the world!” Neither of us had a lot of confidence it’d work. We have education and experience in journalism, and we know there’s a reason joy, peace, and cooperation aren’t often featured in articles. Nobody reads those stories. There’s a reason joy, peace, and cooperation aren’t often featured in articles. Nobody reads those stories. That’s not because humans are insensitive monsters. It’s because when we read bad news, our bodies react with fight or flight instincts— studies show our hearts beat faster and our skin begins to perspire. We want to understand or process what’s going on, so we click on the link and read past the headline. When we read good news, on the other hand, we have no physiological response. Heart rates and perspiration levels stay the same. Researchers say it’s the same nonresponse we have when we look at a blank screen. For a long time, I was frustrated with God for creating us this way. Why didn’t he make us able to absorb bad news calmly and react to good news with wild, enthusiastic joy? Wouldn’t that be better? Wouldn’t that make Isaiah’s job easier? And John the Baptist’s? And Jesus’s? Wouldn’t that make the church’s job easier? “Behold your God!” we could say to the world. “Isn’t he amazing? Isn’t it wonderful what he has done for us?” And the secular world would shout back, “Hooray! Praise the Lord!” But that’s not how God did it. And only recently did I begin to spot the beauty in his way. First, it’s right that human bodies react with stress and anxiety to news of sin and brokenness in the world. That’s a sign we were made for another world, one that isn’t steeped in corruption and sadness. It’s a testimony that God himself, the One we image, doesn’t ignore evil. The tension we feel is a tiny shadow of God’s reaction when he sees depravity unfolding across space and time. Second, just because we stay relaxed when reading good reports or stories doesn’t mean we’re unaffected. Studies show that when we hear positive news, we’re not only happier but more likely to take action —to respond with compassion and energy to the world around us. There’s no better news than the gospel—the message that God sent his Son to die on a cross for our sins and open a way for us to be reconciled to him. Our good God offers us not only salvation from our past but purpose for our present and hope for our future. Our good God offers us not only salvation from our past but purpose for our present and hope for our future. This good news changed, and continues to change, the world. Out of grateful joy, Christians have become missionaries, started schools, and adopted children. They’ve moved to broken places, given away their time and money, and forgiven those who sinned against them. They’ve preached the gospel, made countercultural choices, and kept doggedly working long before they saw any fruit. Behold, our God! What marvelous things he has done in us, is doing through us, and has planned for us. Respond Consider your news diet. If good news energizes us, how can you limit your bad news intake or find more good news? How can you keep reminding yourself of the good news of the gospel?

featured.title_zh: 邮政父母：传教士儿童的经历
featured.content: Faith Cook’s Troubled Journey narrates her early experiences as the daughter of OMF missionaries to China. Honouring the faith, courage, and self-sacrifice of her parents, she also shines a compassionate light on the family deprivations brought about by long periods of separation from them. The excerpt below is Chapter 11 of the book in question, which cover Faith’s childhood between the ages of fourteen and eighteen. A passage on the P & O Carthage was booked for Stanley and Norah [Faith’s parents—Ed.] in early January 1952, only eight months after our family had first arrived back from China. It was a subdued Christmas we spent together that year, the last for some years to come. Frantic packing followed, purchasing school uniform and preparing for the long outward journey back to the Far East, this time by sea. A round of speaking engagements filled the days for my parents and seemingly eased the ache of the forthcoming separation. As the day of parting drew ever nearer, I noticed a new tenderness in their attitude towards me – a tenderness that only added to my distress. And at last came the day of departure. It would be four years before we would see them again. Photographs were taken on the steps of the mission headquarters, as all joined to wish the departing missionaries well. Norah’s expression told a story, as did fifteen-year-old Christopher’s forced smile, for in reality, the boy’s spirit was at breaking point. On we went to the station where our parents would board a train to Southampton. A large contingent of missionary personnel followed, for this departure was highly significant for the entire future of the mission, urgently seeking a new role for its operations now the door to China was closed. I found myself thrust to the back of the crowd as the train slowly moved off. Suddenly one more thoughtful friend spotted the irony of the situation and pushed me to the front to catch the last glimpse of my parents as they stood waving at the window of the train, my mother looking tense and tearful, and my father strained. Back at the mission home once more, we were at a loose end. No guardian had yet been appointed to care for us, although one or two kindly adults helped out if I asked for assistance. The Spring term would soon begin and I was glad. Some of my new clothes were too long and needed altering, and I discovered with alarm that the shoe repairer considered my school shoes beyond his skills to patch up. Never handy with a needle, I tried my best to turn up the hems myself. At last the third week of January arrived and I was on the train back to my well-loved school – a place I now regarded as home. Although soon immersed once more in all the trivia of boarding school life, I found time each week to write a letter to my parents. The first few letters were addressed to ports en route for Malaysia where the P & O Carthage would call: Aden, Penang and then to Singapore to await their arrival. Stanley and Norah treasured these schoolgirl epistles, storing them all up, until at last my father would present his married daughter with a shoe box crammed with letters dating from January 1952 until the time that he and my mother finally retired from missionary service in Malaysia more than twenty years later. These letters form a unique commentary on the development of a postal relationship with my parents that would form the bedrock of my security and development from a young teenager to womanhood and beyond. Faithfully my parents replied to each letter, commenting on my progress, chiding when they could sense my behaviour was becoming erratic, and offering advice as well as they were able. Not long after arriving back at the mission headquarters in London at the end of the spring school term, I discovered that a middle-aged couple had been appointed as guardians for the children of the missionaries: Louis and Nancy Gaussen. featured.content_zh: Faith Cook的"麻烦之旅"讲述了她作为OMF传教士去中国的女儿的早期经历. 她以对父母的信仰、勇气和自我牺牲的敬意,也为长期与父母分离所带来的家庭贫困而发出同情之光。 下面的节录是该书第11章,其中涵盖了费斯14至18岁的童年. 1952年1月初,我们一家刚从中国回来才八个月,为斯坦利和诺拉(Faith的父母——Ed.)预订了P & O迦太基号上的一段。 那年是我们一起度过的圣诞 几年来的最后一天 紧随其后的弗朗克包装,购买了校服并准备了远东的漫长出行旅程,这次是海上出行. 一轮的演讲为我父母提供了时间,似乎缓解了即将到来的分居的痛苦。 随着离别日的临近,我注意到他们对我的态度出现了新的温柔,这种温柔只会使我更加痛苦。 终于到了出发之日 四年后我们才能再见到他们 对特派团总部的步骤进行了拍照,因为所有人都希望离开的传教士们一切顺利。 Norah的言论讲述了一个故事,15岁的Christopher被迫微笑也讲述了一个故事,因为实际上,这名男孩的精神正在崩溃。 我们去了车站 在那里,我们的父母 会登上火车到南安普顿。 随即派出了大批传教人员,因为这次出走对传教团的整个未来都具有重大意义,因此紧急寻求为传教团的行动起新的作用,现在中国的大门已经关闭了。 我发现自己被推倒 在人群的后部 当火车慢慢地离开。 突然又有一位深思熟虑的朋友发现情况具有讽刺意味,把我推到前面,以抓住我父母站在火车窗前挥手的最后一眼,我母亲看起来紧张而泪流满面,而我父亲也感到紧张. 回到了任务之家, 我们处在一个松散的结局。 目前还没有指定监护人来照顾我们,不过,如果我想得到帮助,一两个成年人会帮助我们。 春季学期即将开始 我很高兴 一些我的新衣服太长,需要更换,我惊恐地发现,修鞋者认为我的校鞋超出了他的能力来补补补. 我从不用针指手画脚,我尽力自己把螺丝弄大 终于在一月的第三个星期抵达, 我坐上火车回到我深爱的学校, 虽然我很快再次沉浸在寄宿学校生活的三难之中,但我发现每周都有时间写信给我的父母。 最初的几封信是寄给前往马来西亚的港口,P&O迦太基会称这些港口为:亚丁,槟城,再到新加坡等他们到达. 斯坦利和诺拉珍藏了这些女学生的表皮, 把它们全部储存起来, 直到最后我父亲会向他的已婚女儿展示一个鞋盒, 里面塞有1952年1月的信件, 直到他和我妈妈20多年后终于从马来西亚的传教士退休。 这些信件构成了关于与我父母发展邮政关系的独特评论,这将构成我从青少年到妇女时代及以后的安全和发展的基石。 诚然,我的父母每一封信都回信,评论我的进展,当他们能感觉到我的行为变得不规则时,他们就会发号施令,并尽可能地提供建议。 在春季学期结束回到伦敦的使团总部不久后,我发现一对中年夫妇被指定为传教士子女监护人:路易和南希·高森. 理解和友善,他们很适合照顾孩子。 高森夫妇

featured.title_zh: 特朗普、习近平和普京在宗教自由状况恶化之际会晤
featured.content: U.S. President Donald Trump, Chinese President Xi Jinping, and Russian President Vladimir Putin met Thursday in Shenzhen, China, for an unprecedented trilateral summit, projecting an image of cooperation among three of the world’s most powerful nations but offering few concrete agreements on the conflicts and international issues facing them. The roughly 80-minute meeting produced a joint statement addressing United Nations reform, energy production, international legal authority, and nuclear risks. However, the statement offered no clear breakthroughs on the wars in Ukraine or Iran and made no public reference to religious freedom or the persecution of religious communities in China and Russia. The gathering underscored the importance of direct engagement among world leaders as they seek to manage competing interests, global conflicts, and questions about the future of international order. The summit also offered an opportunity to address concerns affecting millions of people who face persecution for their faith, particularly in countries governed by authoritarian regimes. A Summit Focused on Global Stability The three leaders presented themselves as sharing responsibility for maintaining international peace and security. Their joint statement called for United Nations reform, increased production and supply of petroleum products, and further dialogue on reducing nuclear risks. The leaders also emphasized state sovereignty and the immunity of government officials, declaring that the International Criminal Court and similar bodies should not abuse their authority. The language reflects a shared interest among the three governments in limiting the reach of international institutions, although their respective political, economic, and security priorities remain distinct. Concerningly, this language is similar to that used by China in pushing back on American calls to respect human rights and ensure citizens can freely practice religion. Claiming that these are internal affairs, China rejects what it considers to be overly zealous policing by the U.S. and continues on its path of persecution. Putin described the summit as a new chapter in diplomatic history and praised the opportunity for direct engagement with Trump and Xi. The Russian president also invoked the 1945 Yalta Conference, which helped shape the postwar European order, arguing that international conflicts eventually require countries to recognize realities on the ground. While the leaders expressed interest in dialogue and international stability, their meeting did not produce publicly announced agreements to resolve major conflicts or address underlying tensions between their governments. Religious Freedom Remains a Global Concern For religious freedom advocates, high-level diplomatic meetings represent an important opportunity to raise the plight of prisoners of conscience and religious communities facing government persecution. China, in particular, continues to impose severe restrictions on religious practice. Christians in unregistered churches face surveillance, detention, church closures, and pressure to submit to government oversight. The Chinese Communist Party’s campaign to bring religious institutions under its control has affected Protestant house churches, Catholic communities, Tibetan Buddhists, Uyghur Muslims, and other religious minorities. In recent months, international advocates have urged the Trump administration to raise the cases of imprisoned religious leaders with Xi. Earlier this year, Trump raised the case of Pastor Ezra Jin Mingri, founder of Beijing’s Zion Church, during a meeting with Xi. Chinese authorities subsequently released Jin, who later relocated to the United States. However, other Zion Church leaders arrested during the same crackdown remain detained, and no such direct advocacy seems to have occurred at this most recent meeting. featured.content_zh:
美国总统唐纳德·特朗普,中国国家主席习近平,俄罗斯总统弗拉基米尔·普京星期四在中国深圳举行前所未有的三边峰会,展现出世界三大强国之间合作的形象,但很少就它们面临的冲突和国际问题达成具体协议.

大约80分钟的会议产生了关于联合国改革、能源生产、国际法律权威和核风险的联合声明。 然而,该声明对于乌克兰或伊朗的战争没有提出明确的突破,也没有公开提及中国和俄罗斯的宗教自由或对宗教团体的迫害.

会议强调了世界领导人直接参与的重要性,因为他们寻求管理相互竞争的利益、全球冲突和有关国际秩序未来的问题。 首脑会议还提供了一个机会,解决影响到数百万因信仰而面临迫害的人的关切,特别是在专制政权统治的国家。

以全球稳定为重点的首脑会议 三位领导人自称分担维护国际和平与安全的责任。 他们的联合声明呼吁联合国改革、增加石油产品的生产和供应,以及就减少核风险进一步进行对话。

各国领导人还强调国家主权和政府官员的豁免权,宣布国际刑事法院和类似机构不应滥用其权力。 其措辞反映了三国政府对限制国际机构的影响力的共同利益,尽管它们各自的政治、经济和安全优先事项仍然不同。

关于这一点,这种语言类似于中国在抵制美国尊重人权和确保公民可以自由信奉宗教的呼声时所使用的语言。 中国声称这是内政,反对美国过于狂热地维持治安,继续走迫害的道路。

普京将峰会描述为外交史上的新篇章,并称赞与特朗普和习近平直接接触的机会. 俄罗斯总统还援引了1945年雅尔塔会议,会议帮助塑造了战后的欧洲秩序,认为国际冲突最终需要各国承认当地的实际情况.

虽然领导人对对话和国际稳定表示兴趣,但他们的会议没有达成公开宣布的协议,以解决重大冲突或解决政府之间的紧张关系。

宗教自由仍然是全球关注的问题 对于宗教自由倡导者来说,高级别外交会议是一个重要的机会,可以提高良心犯和宗教界面临政府迫害的困境。 特别是中国继续严格限制宗教活动.

在未登记的教堂的基督徒面临监视,拘留,教堂关闭,以及服从政府监督的压力. 中国共产党将宗教机构置于其控制之下的运动影响了新教住宅教堂,天主教社区,藏传佛教,维吾尔穆斯林等宗教少数派.

最近几个月,国际倡导者敦促特朗普政府向习近平提出被囚禁宗教领袖的案件. 今年早些时候,特朗普在北京锡安教会创始人伊兹拉·金明里牧师会见习近平时提出这个案例. 中国当局随后释放了后来移居美国的金.

然而,在同一次镇压中被捕的其他锡安教会领导人仍然被拘留,在最近的这次会议上似乎没有进行这种直接的宣传。 该案表明,总统直接参与会如何影响局势

featured.title_zh: 在持续冲突的背景下，东盟继续将缅甸军政府排除在外
featured.content: Southeast Asian leaders reaffirmed their opposition to Myanmar’s military government at the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) summit in Manila on Nov. 15, extending restrictions on the country’s political representation after concluding that its military leadership had made insufficient progress toward ending the country’s civil war. The decision came as leaders from the 11-member regional bloc gathered in the Philippines for three days of discussions on international conflicts, regional security, and economic stability. Myanmar’s continuing violence and humanitarian crisis featured prominently, alongside disputes in the South China Sea and the broader consequences of conflicts in the Middle East and Ukraine. In a statement following their review of Myanmar’s implementation of a five-point peace plan adopted in 2021, ASEAN leaders expressed deep concern over the continuing conflict. They denounced attacks against civilians and public infrastructure. They called on all parties to halt indiscriminate violence, protect civilian populations, and allow humanitarian assistance to reach those in need. The leaders also agreed to maintain the restriction preventing Myanmar’s military leader and foreign minister from attending ASEAN summits and foreign ministers’ meetings until meaningful progress is made toward implementing the peace plan. Myanmar will continue to be represented at those meetings by lower-level diplomatic officials. The decision represents a positive continuation of ASEAN’s effort to pressure Myanmar’s military leadership while preserving diplomatic channels with the country. A Peace Plan with Little Progress Myanmar has been embroiled in a nationwide civil war since February 2021, when the military overthrew the elected government of Aung San Suu Kyi. The coup prompted widespread protests and a violent crackdown by security forces. Armed resistance subsequently emerged across the country, with longstanding ethnic armed organizations also intensifying their campaigns against the military. In April 2021, ASEAN developed a five-point consensus intended to address the crisis. The agreement called for an immediate cessation of violence, constructive dialogue among all parties, mediation by an ASEAN special envoy, humanitarian assistance, and engagement between the envoy and relevant stakeholders. Despite repeated diplomatic efforts, the plan has produced little meaningful progress toward ending the conflict. ASEAN has struggled to balance its traditional policy of noninterference in member states’ domestic affairs with the need to respond to the increasingly severe humanitarian and political crisis in Myanmar. The bloc has maintained contact with the military government while withholding full political recognition at its highest-level meetings. In May 2025, ASEAN attempted to strengthen its approach by making the special envoy position permanent rather than replacing the representative annually. The change was intended to provide greater continuity in diplomatic engagement and improve the prospects for negotiations. However, continued military operations and widespread abuses have undermined those efforts. According to the Assistance Association for Political Prisoners, an independent monitoring organization, more than 8,600 people had been killed and 32,406 arrested by Myanmar’s security forces as of this week. The figures reflect the extensive human cost of the conflict and the government’s continued repression of opposition. Myanmar’s military leadership has also attempted to restore its international standing. Military chief Min Aung Hlaing became president in April following elections conducted in phases in December and January. Opposition groups and international observers criticized the elections as an effort to consolidate military control rather than restore genuine civilian government. featured.content_zh:
东南亚领导人在11月15日于马尼拉举行的东南亚国家联盟(东盟)首脑会议上重申反对缅甸军政府,认为缅甸的军事领导在结束该国内战方面进展不足后,延长了对该国政治代表权的限制.

这项决定是11个成员的区域集团领导人在菲律宾聚集一堂,讨论国际冲突、区域安全和经济稳定问题,为期三天。 缅甸的持续暴力和人道主义危机与南中国海的争端以及中东和乌克兰冲突的更广泛后果一道,占据了显著地位。

东盟领导人在审查缅甸执行2021年通过的五点和平计划后发表声明,对持续冲突深表关切. 他们谴责对平民和公共基础设施的袭击。 他们呼吁所有各方停止不分青红皂白的暴力,保护平民,允许人道主义援助送达需要援助的人。

领导人还同意继续限制缅甸的军事领导人和外交部长出席东盟首脑会议和外交部长会议,直到在执行和平计划方面取得有意义的进展。 缅甸将继续派低级外交官员出席这些会议。

这一决定是东盟在保持与缅甸的外交渠道的同时向缅甸军事领导人施压的努力的积极继续。 自2021年2月军方推翻昂山素季当选政府以来,与小进步缅甸的和平计划卷入全国内战.

政变引发了广泛的抗议和安全部队的暴力镇压. 武装抵抗随后在全国各地出现,长期存在的族裔武装组织也加强了对军队的进攻。 2021年4月,东盟达成了旨在应对危机的五点共识.

协定要求立即停止暴力,所有各方进行建设性对话,由东盟特使进行调解,提供人道主义援助,特使与相关利益攸关方进行接触。 尽管一再作出外交努力,但该计划在结束冲突方面没有取得什么有意义的进展。

东盟努力在不干涉成员国内政的传统政策与应对缅甸日益严重的人道主义和政治危机的必要性之间取得平衡。 该集团与军政府保持联系,同时拒绝在最高级别会议上给予充分的政治承认。

2025年5月,东盟试图加强其做法,使特使的职位永久化,而不是每年更换代表。 这一变化旨在增加外交接触的连续性,改善谈判前景。 然而,持续的军事行动和普遍的侵权行为破坏了这些努力。

据独立监督组织政治犯援助协会称,截至本周,缅甸安全部队已杀害8 600多人,逮捕32 406人。 这些数字反映了冲突给人带来的巨大代价以及政府继续镇压反对派。

缅甸的军事领导人也试图恢复其国际地位。 在12月和1月分阶段举行选举之后,军事长官敏昂·赫莱于4月成为总统。 反对派团体和国际观察员批评选举是为了巩固军事控制而不是恢复真正的文职政府。

尽管访问了东盟的几个成员国,敏昂莱仍然被排除在集团最高领导层之外。

featured.title: Judge adjourns Kyra Backs so defense can review autopsy photos
featured.summary: Article content The Kyra Renee Backs trial was adjourned following an argument from the defence that a lack of disclosure from the Crown could have a detrimental impact on the former day-home operator
featured.content: Article content The Kyra Renee Backs trial was adjourned following an argument from the defence that a lack of disclosure from the Crown could have a detrimental impact on the former day-home operator’s trial. Missing from the disclosure were photos discussed on Nov. 13, defence lawyer Danielle Boisvert said. Recommended Videos “The reason being, sir, is that these photographs are first-party disclosure that are essential to this case as disclosure could possibly get.” Backs, now 33, ran an unlicensed day-home in High Prairie. She was charged with second-degree murder following the October 6, 2022, death of a child in her care — seven-month-old Oaklan Cunningham. The deceased as well as witnesses and any identifiable information were previously included in a publication ban at the beginning of the trial. Justice Peter B. Michalyshyn lifted the ban before hearing arguments for the adjournment. Her trial began in Peace River in January, and adjourned to review disclosure and resumed in July. The midsummer session included days of testimony from police, EMS and witnesses before the trial adjourned again. At that time the court would be setting dates for an Edmonton courtroom to accommodate expert witnesses and resumed in November. The photos given to the defence varied from those the Crown had. That the brain is reportedly the criminally injured organ, photos submitted into evidence that included the infant’s brain, eyes and spinal cord had not been provided to the defence, Boisvert said. “What came about in preparation for this case was a concern by defence, of the photographs that had not been provided of the dissection and cutting of the brain by the neurologist,” she added. Given that expert testimony would relate to those procedures, the defence’s strategy with the Crown witnesses could be compromised. Furthermore, Boisvert said previous questions to witnesses were based on the disclosure they had. Those witnesses may need to be recalled. Crown prosecutor Jeff Rudiak responded saying the Crown didn’t intend to use the photos. Instead, they would be presenting the testimony of the expert who took the photos. Michalyshyn found there was reason to grant the request. During the January voir dire, testimony by a Crown witness highlighted the importance of the photos, Michalyshyn said. The relevance and materiality of the photographs are still unknown, he added. The defence counsel very fairly said in her submission that she doesn’t yet know how material they are and requires more information. “I agree with the submissions of Ms. Boisvert, that I cannot be satisfied that the trial will be fair, if this early relevant and potentially material evidence is not available to the court through properly prepared expert witnesses.” Allowing the trial to continue as requested by the Crown has the potential to impact the expert testimony if interrupted, Michalyshyn said. The information should be presented and considered in a conventional rather than unconventional, truncated and piecemeal fashion. Moving the trial’s venue from Peace River was made because of the intricacy of the evidence. “It was likely that the expert evidence in this trial would be complex, closely contested, and critical with regard to the ultimate verdict in the case, and there’s no reason to think that that’s changed.” The trial is scheduled to resume Nov. 27 at Court of King’s Bench in Edmonton. featured.title: Batalha do Salado ( figuraes na historiografia medieval )
featured.summary: A celebração dos novecentos anos de Portugal convoca uma reflexão sobre os momentos inaugurais em que o registo histórico se funde não só com o imaginário lendário, como com o cruzamento de presciênci
featured.content: A celebração dos novecentos anos de Portugal convoca uma reflexão sobre os momentos inaugurais em que o registo histórico se funde não só com o imaginário lendário, como com o cruzamento de presciências tornando-se alicerce da identidade coletiva também através de matrizes simbólicas. Este cruzamento corrobora dimensões factuais essenciais para a compreensão do percurso civilizacional, evidenciando, segundo Mircea Eliade (1907-1986), que a dimensão racional do logos não extingue relatos míticos e emocionais, antes os absorve e valida enquanto testemunhos antropológicos. A Batalha do Salado Travada a 30 de outubro de 1340, junto ao Rio Salado, nas proximidades de Tarifa, Espanha, constitui um dos marcos mais decisivos da geopolítica ibérica do século XIV. O confronto colocou lado a lado os reinos cristãos de Castela e Portugal (com apoio de Aragão) contra as forças muçulmanas do Sultanato Merínida de Marrocos e do Emirado de Granada, traduzindo-se no confronto direto entre a coligação cristã, liderada por Afonso XI de Castela e D. Afonso IV de Portugal, e a contraofensiva islâmica encabeçada pelo referido Sultanato Merínida de Abu al-Hassan, em aliança com o Reino Nacérida de Granada. Do ponto de vista estritamente militar, a intervenção do contingente português revelou-se um elemento de crucial importância estratégica. A coordenação tática entre as forças peninsulares permitiu neutralizar a superioridade numérica adversária e estancar a última grande tentativa de expansão magrebina no ocidente europeu, fixando de forma definitiva o controlo cristão sobre as margens do Estreito de Gibraltar. Dimensões Em termos historiográficos e simbólicos, o desfecho da Batalha transcendeu a imediata vitória territorial, assumindo uma profunda dimensão de legitimação política e dinástica para a Coroa de Portugal. Numa época marcada por tensões intermonárquicas latentes, a solidariedade militar prestada por D. Afonso IV consolidou a soberania portuguesa face ao expansionismo castelhano, ao mesmo tempo que elevou o prestígio internacional do monarca, doravante cognominado “o Bravo”. Adicionalmente, o conflito foi instrumentalizado através duma retórica de cruzada fortemente enraizada na mentalidade medieval. A cronística coeva e a tratadística posterior sacralizaram o acontecimento, convertendo-o num pilar da identidade nacional fundado na defesa da Cristandade, o que conferiu à dinastia de Borgonha uma renovada autoridade moral e um papel central no xadrez diplomático europeu. Cronística medieval A cronística medieval portuguesa – cronicões, crónicas e nobiliários – enquanto género literário-historiográfico, não atua apenas como um mero registo de factos, mas como um poderoso instrumento de legitimação política e de construção da memória dinástica. No século XIV, a escrita da História servia de palco à afirmação da soberania de Portugal no complexo tabuleiro geopolítico peninsular. O tratamento textual da Batalha do Salado nas letras revela uma intencionalidade clara: monumentalizar a intervenção de D. Afonso IV e fixar um modelo de realeza fundado na valentia militar e na piedade cristã. Destarte, abandona a frieza do relato factual para adotar uma retórica de teor épico, contrariando a natural tendência da cronística castelhana em menorizar o papel dos contingentes lusos. D. Afonso IV presentifica-se sob o prisma da necessitas – o rei não age por ambição territorial, mas sim para acudir à Cristandade e responder ao apelo de auxílio do seu genro, Afonso XI de Castela. Tal construção projeta no imaginário a imagem de um Portugal autónomo, cuja força militar é indispensável para a sobrevivência dos restantes reinos hispânicos. featured.title: Adiós Leon XIV : la miniserie de 4 caps sobre los misterios de la fe que conquista Netflix
featured.summary: (BUENOS AIRES).- Netflix tiene disponible Misterios de la fe, una miniserie documental de cuatro episodios sobre algunas de las reliquias más sagradas del cristianismo. La producción recorre las histo
featured.content: (BUENOS AIRES).- Netflix tiene disponible Misterios de la fe, una miniserie documental de cuatro episodios sobre algunas de las reliquias más sagradas del cristianismo. La producción recorre las historias, creencias y controversias que rodean a esos objetos. Las piezas que aparecen en la serie estuvieron vinculadas con Jesús y con momentos importantes de la historia cristiana, según la tradición religiosa. El recorrido muestra cómo atravesaron los siglos y se convirtieron en símbolos de devoción para millones de creyentes. Para reconstruir esas historias, la miniserie combina investigaciones, testimonios y reconstrucciones. Uno de los episodios aborda la Corona de Espinas, que, según la tradición, fue colocada sobre la cabeza de Jesús durante la crucifixión. El documental también recuerda el incendio de la catedral de Notre Dame, en París, ocurrido en 2019. En ese contexto, repasa el operativo que permitió rescatar la reliquia de las llamas. El Santo Grial, la copa asociada con la Última Cena, aparece entre los grandes interrogantes de la producción. La serie explora distintas teorías sobre su posible paradero y presenta las versiones que rodean a esa reliquia. El objeto forma parte de un recorrido que combina la historia con las creencias vinculadas a los símbolos cristianos. La miniserie también se detiene en el Velo de Manoppello, una tela conservada en Italia. Algunos fieles le atribuyen una representación del rostro de Cristo. La producción incorpora esa creencia a su recorrido por objetos venerados y por las historias que se formaron alrededor de ellos. Otro tramo sigue la Vera Cruz, vinculada con la crucifixión de Jesús, y llega hasta Río de Janeiro, donde se conserva un fragmento de la reliquia. Las historias presentadas abren preguntas sobre la autenticidad de esos objetos y el lugar que ocupan dentro de la fe. La propuesta combina historia, investigación y espiritualidad para abordar esas cuestiones. La llegada del papa León XIV a Argentina el 8 de noviembre de 2026 volvió a poner a la Iglesia Católica y sus tradiciones en el centro de la atención. El pontífice tenía una agenda de encuentros y celebraciones hasta el miércoles 11. En ese marco, la miniserie aparece como una propuesta para quienes buscan profundizar en los símbolos y las historias del cristianismo, incluso fuera de las comunidades religiosas.

featured.title: Cementerio judío de Mostar : huella sefardí en los Balcanes
featured.summary: Por Ricardo Angoso El cementerio judío de Mostar, situado en el barrio de Sutina, es uno de los testimonios más interesantes de la presencia histórica de los judíos en Herzegovina y, fundamentalmente,
featured.content: Por Ricardo Angoso El cementerio judío de Mostar, situado en el barrio de Sutina, es uno de los testimonios más interesantes de la presencia histórica de los judíos en Herzegovina y, fundamentalmente, de los sefardíes en los Balcanes. Tiene una particularidad: aunque la comunidad judía de Mostar se remonta al siglo XVI, el cementerio que hoy podemos visitar es bastante posterior. Sin embargo, existe cierta controversia sobre su antigüedad, ya que algunas fuentes locales hablan de un origen en el siglo XVII, mientras que los estudios patrimoniales documentan la existencia del cementerio actual a finales del siglo XIX. Como dato práctico para quienes quieran visitarlo, conviene señalar que se encuentra en la carretera M-17, frente a una gasolinera y muy cerca de la ciudad, en una zona que se asemeja a una especie de polígono industrial poco poblado. Es fácil pasar por alto su ubicación si se circula en coche. Los orígenes de la comunidad judía de Mostar La presencia judía en Mostar está documentada desde 1570, durante el dominio del Imperio otomano. Los primeros judíos conocidos fueron sefardíes, descendientes de aquellos que habían abandonado España después de la expulsión de 1492 y que encontraron refugio en los territorios otomanos. Se conocen dos antiguos sefardíes prominentes establecidos en Mostar: Daniel Rodríguez, comerciante que mantenía relaciones comerciales con Venecia, Dubrovnik y otros centros del Mediterráneo, y Moše Koen, también citado en algunas fuentes con variantes de su apellido. Los judíos contribuyeron al desarrollo comercial y artesanal de Mostar. La ciudad ocupaba una posición estratégica entre el interior de los Balcanes y la costa adriática, entre el mundo veneciano, el entonces Imperio otomano y los flujos comerciales procedentes de Occidente. Posteriormente, durante el siglo XIX, especialmente después de la ocupación austrohúngara de Bosnia en 1878, llegaron también judíos asquenazíes procedentes de Europa central. Ambas comunidades convivieron y terminaron constituyendo una comunidad judía organizada, aunque el elemento sefardí siempre fue predominante. Otro pequeño grupo de judíos asquenazíes había llegado a esta ciudad después de la caída de Budapest en manos cristianas, en 1686, cuando la ciudad, hasta entonces ocupada por los turcos, pasó a manos de los Habsburgo. Paradójicamente, el entorno otomano había resultado más tolerante hacia los judíos que el que ofrecieron posteriormente las autoridades cristianas. En lo que respecta a la evolución demográfica de la comunidad, hemos encontrado algunos datos de interés: en 1879 había aproximadamente 35 judíos; en 1885, unos 98; en 1895, 164; en 1910, 254; y en 1930, alrededor de 300. La población aumentó ligeramente durante los años posteriores, hasta 1939, cuando comenzó la Segunda Guerra Mundial y se puso en marcha la maquinaria criminal del Holocausto. Tras la contienda, ya en plena Yugoslavia socialista, quedaban algo menos de 70 judíos viviendo en Mostar. Hoy, seguramente, no quedan ni tres decenas de miembros de la comunidad judía en la ciudad. ¿Cuántos años tiene el cementerio? Existen dos versiones sobre su antigüedad. La primera sitúa su origen en el siglo XVII, aunque no quedan rastros materiales de aquel supuesto recinto. Al parecer, Zoran Mandlbaum, antiguo dirigente de la comunidad judía de Mostar, escribió que el cementerio se fundó entre 1630 y 1650, mediante la adquisición de unos 1.850 metros cuadrados de terreno. Según este testimonio, habría tumbas de más de 350 años de antigüedad. Sin embargo, no hay constancia material de las mismas y tampoco está claro que aquel camposanto estuviera situado en el mismo lugar que ocupa el actual. La segunda versión sitúa su fundación en el siglo XIX y resulta mucho más creíble, sobre todo en lo referente al recinto que hoy podemos visitar. El estudio patrimonial de Samuel D.
